verses.sanskrit: ततो ह्येकार्णवं सर्वं विभज्य परमेश्वरः । विस्तीर्णोपलतोयौघां सरित्सरविवर्धिताम्
verses.transliteration: tato hyekārṇavaṃ sarvaṃ vibhajya parameśvaraḥ / vistīrṇopalatoyaughāṃ saritsaravivardhitām
verses.translation: They have abundant purity and have attained mental Repeating it ten times, they go to the worlds calle Svar and- Tafias. After staying there for ten Kalpas, they proceed to the world called Satya. The residents of the Kalpa go
verses.hindi: ततोड़ व्य क्षिति देवो जगतः स्थापनेचछया । पूथिव्याः प्रविभागाय मनश्चक़ 5स्बुजेक्ष गः
verses.wordMeaning: They have abundant purity and have attained mental Repeating it ten times, they go to the worlds calle Svar and- Tafias. After staying there for ten Kalpas, they proceed to the world called Satya. The residents of the Kalpa go
verses.commentary: Sense: They have abundant purity and have attained mental Repeating it ten times, they go to the worlds calle Svar and- Tafias. After staying there for ten Kalpas, they proceed to the world called Satya. The residents of the Kalpa go

verses.sanskrit: पश्यते मेदिनीं देवः सवृक्षौषधिपल्वलाम् । हिमवन्तं गिरिश्रेष्ठं श्वेतं पर्वतमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration: paśyate medinīṃ devaḥ savṛkṣauṣadhipalvalām / himavantaṃ giriśreṣṭhaṃ śvetaṃ parvatamuttamam
verses.translation: Thus thousands ofYugas according to the calculations Verses 21-30 describe how Devas proceed from heaven to still higher regions in the order: Mahar->Svar->Tapas—>Brahma.
verses.hindi: पृथिवीं तु समीकृत्य पृथिव्यां सोडचिनोदिगरीन्। प्राक्सग द्यममानास्तु तदा संवत काप्निना ॥ तेनायिना विशीर्णास्ते पता भुचि सवंशः । शैत्यादेकार्णवे तस्मिन्वायुना55पस्तु संहताः २८
verses.wordMeaning: Thus thousands ofYugas according to the calculations Verses 21-30 describe how Devas proceed from heaven to still higher regions in the order: Mahar->Svar->Tapas—>Brahma.
verses.commentary: Sense: Thus thousands ofYugas according to the calculations Verses 21-30 describe how Devas proceed from heaven to still higher regions in the order: Mahar->Svar->Tapas—>Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: शृङ्गवन्तं महाशैलं ये चान्ये कुलपर्वताः । जंबुद्वीपं कुशं क्रौञ्चं सगोमेदं सशाल्मलम्
verses.transliteration: śṛṅgavantaṃ mahāśailaṃ ye cānye kulaparvatāḥ / jaṃbudvīpaṃ kuśaṃ krauñcaṃ sagomedaṃ saśālmalam
verses.translation: Except overlordship (on the world), thcybecome equal to Brahma in affluence, glory, form (appearance) and objects (of enjoyment of senses) 1. There they stay happily due to their close contact with Brahma. Acquiring the bliss of Brahma, they become liberated along with Brahma.
verses.hindi: परम द्यतिमान वे नाना दीक्षाओं से दीक्षित थे ।१५-१६। महायज्ञ मयविभु योगी का दक्षिणा हृदय था उपाकर्म, रुचिर इष्टि और प्रवग्यं ही वैभव था, ताना छन्द गतिपथ और रहस्यमय उपनिषद् आसन थे। पत्नी छाया के सहित वे मणिमय शुद्ध (सुमेर) के समान ऊंचे थे। इस प्रकार प्रभु यज्ञवाराह बनकर उस जलरासि में घुस गए। उस प्रजाप्रति ने जल से आवृत पृथ्वी के समीप जाकर उसको
verses.wordMeaning: Except overlordship (on the world), thcybecome equal to Brahma in affluence, glory, form (appearance) and objects (of enjoyment of senses) 1. There they stay happily due to their close contact with Brahma. Acquiring the bliss of Brahma, they become liberated along with Brahma.
verses.commentary: Sense: Except overlordship (on the world), thcybecome equal to Brahma in affluence, glory, form (appearance) and objects (of enjoyment of senses) 1. There they stay happily due to their close contact with Brahma. Acquiring the bliss of Brahma, they become liberated along with Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: पुष्करान्ताश्च ये द्वीपा ये च सप्तमहार्णवाः । लोकालोकं महाशैलं सर्वं च पुरतः स्थितम्
verses.transliteration: puṣkarāntāśca ye dvīpā ye ca saptamahārṇavāḥ / lokālokaṃ mahāśailaṃ sarvaṃ ca purataḥ sthitam
verses.translation: In view of the inevitability in matters pertaining to Prakfti; they remain boundin their separateness produced at that time. When the differences of those 'whose energies are of different nature, are restrained and withdrawn, their effects
verses.hindi: दाँतों से पकड़कर जल के ऊपर स्थापित कर दिया ।२०-२४ इतना कर चुकने के बाद समुद्र जल को समुद्रों में, नदी जल को नदियों में बॉट दिया । पृथ्वी के उद्धार कर्ता उस हरि ने पृथ्वी को अपने निर्दिष्ट स्थान पर रख कर पहले मन में भविष्य की रूप रेखा निश्चित कर उनको जल तल प्र छोड़ दिया । उस जलराशि के ऊपर पृथ्वी बहुत बड़ी नाव के समान स्थित हुई जो कि
verses.wordMeaning: In view of the inevitability in matters pertaining to Prakfti; they remain boundin their separateness produced at that time. When the differences of those 'whose energies are of different nature, are restrained and withdrawn, their effects
verses.commentary: Sense: In view of the inevitability in matters pertaining to Prakfti; they remain boundin their separateness produced at that time. When the differences of those 'whose energies are of different nature, are restrained and withdrawn, their effects

verses.sanskrit: चतुःप्रकृतिसंयुक्तं जगत् स्थावरजंगमम् । युगान्ते तु विनिष्क्रान्तम् अपश्यत्स महेश्वरः
verses.transliteration: catuḥprakṛtisaṃyuktaṃ jagat sthāvarajaṃgamam / yugānte tu viniṣkrāntam apaśyatsa maheśvaraḥ
verses.translation: Here those persons who have attained liberation have not to go by the (same) path of Samsdra. There is the non- recurrence (non-existence) of these like the blazing flames of fire which has been extinguished 2. Cf. the concept of Brahma-nirvana in BG V. 24-26.
verses.hindi: अपने आकार की विपुलता और भगवान के प्रभाव से डूबती नहीं है । कमलनेन्न देव पृथ्वी का उद्धार करने के अनन्तर संसार स्थापन के उद्देश्य से प्रथ्वी को कई भागों में विभक्त करने को सोचने लगे । पहले भूतत को समतल कर उस पर पहाड़ों को स्थापित क़िया। पूर्व सृष्टि में जो संवतको अग्नि से गल गए थे और घरातल पर चारों ओर जल कर बिखर गए थे, वे उस जलप्लावन में
verses.wordMeaning: Here those persons who have attained liberation have not to go by the (same) path of Samsdra. There is the non- recurrence (non-existence) of these like the blazing flames of fire which has been extinguished 2. Cf. the concept of Brahma-nirvana in BG V. 24-26.
verses.commentary: Sense: Here those persons who have attained liberation have not to go by the (same) path of Samsdra. There is the non- recurrence (non-existence) of these like the blazing flames of fire which has been extinguished 2. Cf. the concept of Brahma-nirvana in BG V. 24-26.

verses.sanskrit: विप्रकीर्णशिलाजालामपश्यत्स वसुंधराम् । कूर्मपृष्ठोपगां देवीं महार्णवगतां प्रभुः
verses.transliteration: viprakīrṇaśilājālāmapaśyatsa vasuṃdharām / kūrmapṛṣṭhopagāṃ devīṃ mahārṇavagatāṃ prabhuḥ
verses.translation: There are classes of beings from Gandharvas toPisacas, Brahmanas and other human beings, animals and birds, the immobile ones and reptiles. While they (the beings mentioned in v. 40) stand there as the residents of the surface of the earth, at that time the thousand rays that emanate from the sun (gettingcombined and concentrated) become seven rays of the sun and each ray (out of those seven rays) becomes a sun.
verses.hindi: शीतलता के कारण, वायु के द्वारा जल इकट्ठा हो जाने से पहले जहाँ जहाँ स्थित थे वहाँ वहाँ इस बार भी अचल हो गए ।२५-२६४। पहले पिघल कर वे अचल (स्थित) हुए, इसलिये पतों का नाम अचल पड़ा, पे
verses.wordMeaning: There are classes of beings from Gandharvas toPisacas, Brahmanas and other human beings, animals and birds, the immobile ones and reptiles. While they (the beings mentioned in v. 40) stand there as the residents of the surface of the earth,…
verses.commentary: Sense: There are classes of beings from Gandharvas toPisacas, Brahmanas and other human beings, animals and birds, the immobile ones and reptiles. While they (the beings mentioned in v. 40) stand there as the residents of the surface of the earth,…

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिन् विशीर्णशैलाग्रे सरित्सरोविवर्जिते । नानातरंगभिन्नोद आवर्तोद्वर्तसंकुले
verses.transliteration: tasmin viśīrṇaśailāgre saritsarovivarjite / nānātaraṃgabhinnoda āvartodvartasaṃkule
verses.translation: Rising up gradually, they burn the three worlds, mobile and immobile beings, rivers and all mountains. They had al¬ ready been dried up by drought and are now burnt by the suns. Then all these—the mobile and immobile, both the pious and impious who are burnt by the rays of the sun, settle down and rest.
verses.hindi: धनुदिचिह्वान्तगंतग्रन्थो घ. पुस्तके नास्ति ।
verses.wordMeaning: Rising up gradually, they burn the three worlds, mobile and immobile beings, rivers and all mountains. They had al¬ ready been dried up by drought and are now burnt by the suns. Then all these—the mobile and immobile,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Rising up gradually, they burn the three worlds, mobile and immobile beings, rivers and all mountains. They had al¬ ready been dried up by drought and are now burnt by the suns. Then all these—the mobile and immobile,…

verses.sanskrit: नानौषधिप्रज्वलिते नानोत्पलशिलातले । नानाविहंगसंघुष्टां मत्स्यकूर्मसमाकुलाम्
verses.transliteration: nānauṣadhiprajvalite nānotpalaśilātale / nānāvihaṃgasaṃghuṣṭāṃ matsyakūrmasamākulām
verses.translation: At the end of the sinful age, they go away with their bodies burnt. But they are not freed from bodies derived from their pious or impious activities. They are united with the people of Jana Loka having the same form as they have. Abounding in purity they attain mental perfection. Having stayed there for the period of the night of Brahma of unmanifest birth, they are born again as the mental sons of Brahma, at the beginning of the creation (of the world). When the residents of the three worlds thus function in Janaloka, and the three worlds are burnt down by the seven suns, when the earth is flooded with rain, when all abodes are scattered, the oceans, clouds and the earthly waters form a vast watery mass called ' Salila n.
verses.hindi: .गिरयोइन्तनिंगीणेत्वाच्चयनाउ्च शिलोच्चयाः  ततस्तेषु विशीणंषु लोकोद्धिगिरिष्चथ
verses.wordMeaning: At the end of the sinful age, they go away with their bodies burnt. But they are not freed from bodies derived from their pious or impious activities. They are united with the people of Jana Loka having the same form as they have.…
verses.commentary: Sense: At the end of the sinful age, they go away with their bodies burnt. But they are not freed from bodies derived from their pious or impious activities. They are united with the people of Jana Loka having the same form as they have.…

verses.sanskrit: दिव्यमायामयीं देवीम् उत्कृष्टाम्बुदसन्निभाम् । नदीमपश्यद्देवेशो ह्यनौपम्यजलाशयाम्
verses.transliteration: divyamāyāmayīṃ devīm utkṛṣṭāmbudasannibhām / nadīmapaśyaddeveśo hyanaupamyajalāśayām
verses.translation: It (water) followed (one flood after another). When that enormous flood of water covered the earth (in one vast sheet of water) it is called Arnava (sea). The word (root )bha is used in the sense of spreading ( vydpli) and shining ( dipti ), as- water shines and spreads. It floods on all sides and hence water is known as Ambhas.
verses.hindi: विश्वकर्मा विभजते कव्पादिषु पुनः पुन। ससमुद्रामिर्मा पृथ्वी सप्तद्वीपाँ सपर्वताम ॥
verses.wordMeaning: It (water) followed (one flood after another). When that enormous flood of water covered the earth (in one vast sheet of water) it is called Arnava (sea). The word (root )bha is used in the sense of spreading ( vydpli) and shining ( dipti ), as- water shines and spreads.…
verses.commentary: Sense: It (water) followed (one flood after another). When that enormous flood of water covered the earth (in one vast sheet of water) it is called Arnava (sea). The word (root )bha is used in the sense of spreading ( vydpli) and shining ( dipti ), as- water shines and spreads.…

verses.sanskrit: मध्ये तस्याम्बुदश्यामां पीनोरुजघनस्तनीम् । वस्त्रैरनुपमैर्दिव्यैर्नानाभरणभूषिताम्
verses.transliteration: madhye tasyāmbudaśyāmāṃ pīnorujaghanastanīm / vastrairanupamairdivyairnānābharaṇabhūṣitām
verses.translation: The root/Tan means c to cover', 'to expand.' Since waters Verses 47-52 give the popular etymologies of salila, arnava, ambhas, tanu and nard. Cf. Bd. P. I. 2. 6. 51-56 for similar derivation of these words. The learned say that the particle c Aram' denotes quick¬ ness. In the vast ocean the waters are not quick. (Hence) they are called 'Maras'.
verses.hindi: भूरायांश्चतुरों लोकान्पुनः सो5थ प्रकल्पयत्  लोकान्प्रकल्पयित्वा च प्रजासग ससर्ज हा
verses.wordMeaning: The root/Tan means c to cover', 'to expand.' Since waters Verses 47-52 give the popular etymologies of salila, arnava, ambhas, tanu and nard. Cf. Bd. P. I. 2. 6. 51-56 for similar derivation of these words. The learned say that the particle c Aram' denotes quick¬ ness.…
verses.commentary: Sense: The root/Tan means c to cover', 'to expand.' Since waters Verses 47-52 give the popular etymologies of salila, arnava, ambhas, tanu and nard. Cf. Bd. P. I. 2. 6. 51-56 for similar derivation of these words. The learned say that the particle c Aram' denotes quick¬ ness.…

verses.sanskrit: सनूपुररवोद्दामां हारकेयूरमण्डिताम् । तादृशीं नर्मदां देवीं स्वयं स्त्रीरूपधारिणीम्
verses.transliteration: sanūpuraravoddāmāṃ hārakeyūramaṇḍitām / tādṛśīṃ narmadāṃ devīṃ svayaṃ strīrūpadhāriṇīm
verses.translation: At the end of a thousand.Yugas, when Brahma's day comes to an end, when, during the night everything is covered up with water, when the earth destroyed by the fire disappears in water, when the wind is calm and motionless, and darkness spreads around and there is no ray of light, Brahma, the Lord Purusa who presides over all these, desires to make the apportionment of this world once again. When the mobile and immobile beings are destroyed and lost in that vast ocean, Brahma becomes (a god) endowed with a thousand i.e. innumerable feet and thousand eyes.
verses.hindi: ब्रह्मा स्वयंभूभंगवान्सिसुकुविधचिधाः प्रजा: । ससर्ज सूष्टि तद्गपां कल्पादिषु यथा पुरा
verses.wordMeaning: At the end of a thousand.Yugas, when Brahma's day comes to an end, when, during the night everything is covered up with water, when the earth destroyed by the fire disappears in water, when the wind is calm and motionless,…
verses.commentary: Sense: At the end of a thousand.Yugas, when Brahma's day comes to an end, when, during the night everything is covered up with water, when the earth destroyed by the fire disappears in water, when the wind is calm and motionless,…

verses.sanskrit: योगमायामयैश्चित्रैर्भूषणैः स्वैर्विभूषिताम् । अव्यक्ताङ्गीं महाभागामपश्यत्स तु नर्मदाम्
verses.transliteration: yogamāyāmayaiścitrairbhūṣaṇaiḥ svairvibhūṣitām / avyaktāṅgīṃ mahābhāgāmapaśyatsa tu narmadām
verses.translation: The thousand-headed Purusa, of golden complexion, who is beyond the ken of senses, who is Brahma called Narayana, goes to sleep in the water. When he wakes up due to the predominance of Sattva guna, he sees the world a void. They cite this verse about Narayana. Waters are called Nara. We have thus heard that the name of waters is Tarns. He stays there with waters coming up- to his umbilicus. So he is called Narayana.
verses.hindi: तस्यार्भिध्यायतः सग॑ सदा वै बुद्धिपू्वकम्। प्रध्यानसमकालं वैप्राडुभू तस्तमोमयः १५५४
verses.wordMeaning: The thousand-headed Purusa, of golden complexion, who is beyond the ken of senses, who is Brahma called Narayana, goes to sleep in the water. When he wakes up due to the predominance of Sattva guna, he sees the world a void. They cite this verse about Narayana.…
verses.commentary: Sense: The thousand-headed Purusa, of golden complexion, who is beyond the ken of senses, who is Brahma called Narayana, goes to sleep in the water. When he wakes up due to the predominance of Sattva guna, he sees the world a void. They cite this verse about Narayana.…

verses.sanskrit: अर्धोद्यतभुजां बालां पद्मपत्रायतेक्षणाम् । स्तुवन्तीं देवदेवेशमुत्थितां तु जलात्तदा
verses.transliteration: ardhodyatabhujāṃ bālāṃ padmapatrāyatekṣaṇām / stuvantīṃ devadeveśamutthitāṃ tu jalāttadā
verses.translation: In the Vedas he is called the first patriarch, the Purusa with good mind, thousand (i.e. inumerable) heads, thousand feet, thousand eyes, thousand faces, thousand hands 1 and de¬ vouring thousands. He has the colour of Adifya (sun). He is the protector of the world. He is the single unprecedented and the first over- powerer of the mighty. He is the golden-wombed Purusa. He is the noble soul who is beyond darkness.
verses.hindi: 'बहिरन्तःप्रकाशश्व शुद्धो निःसेश एव च । तस्मात्तः संत्रत्ता बुद्धिमुख्यानि करणानि च
verses.wordMeaning: In the Vedas he is called the first patriarch, the Purusa with good mind, thousand (i.e. inumerable) heads, thousand feet, thousand eyes, thousand faces, thousand hands 1 and de¬ vouring thousands. He has the colour of Adifya (sun). He is the protector of the world.…
verses.commentary: Sense: In the Vedas he is called the first patriarch, the Purusa with good mind, thousand (i.e. inumerable) heads, thousand feet, thousand eyes, thousand faces, thousand hands 1 and de¬ vouring thousands. He has the colour of Adifya (sun). He is the protector of the world.…

verses.sanskrit: विस्मयाविष्टहृदयो ह्यहमुद्वीक्ष्य तां शुभाम् । स्नात्वा जले शुभे तस्याः स्तोतुमभ्युद्यतस्ततः
verses.transliteration: vismayāviṣṭahṛdayo hyahamudvīkṣya tāṃ śubhām / snātvā jale śubhe tasyāḥ stotumabhyudyatastataḥ
verses.translation: At the beginning of the Kalpas, Rajas predominates in him. He becomes Brahma and creates the subjects. At the end of the Kalpas, Tamas predominates in him. He becomes Kala and swallows them again. Cf. the Purusa Sukta (RV X. 90) He who is designated as Narayana with the Sattva Guna predominant, sleeps in the vast ocean. Dividing himself into three forms, he abides in the three worlds.
verses.hindi: तस्मात्ते संवृतात्मानों नगा मुख्याः प्रकीरतिताः। मुख्यसर्गतथा भूत ब्रक्काइष्ट्वा छसाधकम्
verses.wordMeaning: At the beginning of the Kalpas, Rajas predominates in him. He becomes Brahma and creates the subjects. At the end of the Kalpas, Tamas predominates in him. He becomes Kala and swallows them again. Cf. the Purusa Sukta (RV X.…
verses.commentary: Sense: At the beginning of the Kalpas, Rajas predominates in him. He becomes Brahma and creates the subjects. At the end of the Kalpas, Tamas predominates in him. He becomes Kala and swallows them again. Cf. the Purusa Sukta (RV X.…

verses.sanskrit: अर्चयामास संहृष्टो मन्त्रैर्वेदांगसंभवैः । सृष्टं च तत्पुरा राजन्पश्येयं सचराचरम्
verses.transliteration: arcayāmāsa saṃhṛṣṭo mantrairvedāṃgasaṃbhavaiḥ / sṛṣṭaṃ ca tatpurā rājanpaśyeyaṃ sacarācaram
verses.translation: Through the three forms he creates, surveys and swallows them. When the mobile and immobile world is de¬ stroyed in that vast ocean, at the end of thousand sets of four Yugas, when everything is covered up with water all round, Brahma called Narayana sleeps in the dark, deep waters. The great sages see from Maharloka, Kala who, after swallowing four types of creation, is slumbering in the great (cosmic) ocean during the night of Brahma.
verses.hindi: (गाँ5) होने के कारण वे पर्बत कहे गये । जल के भीतर निगले जाने के कारण गिरि और शझिलाओं के चयत (चुनना) के कारण पव॑तों का नाम हिलोच्चय पड़ा। उन लोक-समुद्र ओर पव॑तों के नष्ठ हो जाने पर विश्वस्रष्टा हरि कल्प के आदि में बार-बार पृथ्वी का विभाग और निर्माण करते हैं। इस नियम के अनुसार इस बार भी उन्होंने समुद्र, सप्तदीप और पवतों से युक्त इस पृथ्वी, भू आदि चारों लोकों
verses.wordMeaning: Through the three forms he creates, surveys and swallows them. When the mobile and immobile world is de¬ stroyed in that vast ocean, at the end of thousand sets of four Yugas, when everything is covered up with water all round, Brahma called Narayana sleeps in the dark,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Through the three forms he creates, surveys and swallows them. When the mobile and immobile world is de¬ stroyed in that vast ocean, at the end of thousand sets of four Yugas, when everything is covered up with water all round, Brahma called Narayana sleeps in the dark,…

verses.sanskrit: सदेवासुरगन्धर्वं सपन्नगमहोरगम् । पश्याम्येषा महाभागा नैव याता क्षयं पुरा
verses.transliteration: sadevāsuragandharvaṃ sapannagamahoragam / paśyāmyeṣā mahābhāgā naiva yātā kṣayaṃ purā
verses.translation: The great sages like Bhrgu and others as in seven Kalpas, so in this Kalpa, surrounded this immense being. That immense being is surrounded by the seven sages Bhrgu and others. The word c Rsi 3 is derived from the root «s/Rs, c to go 5. 1 They existed from the beginning hence they are called Rsis. The word Mahat indicates 'greatness 3. Because they are great, they are called Makar sis. The sleeping Kala was then observed by them while staying in Maharloka. In the past Kalpa there were seven sages beginning with Satya.
verses.hindi: की सृष्टि की ।३०-३२३। लोकसृष्टि के अनन्तर प्रजासृष्टि की । जिस समय ध्यानावस्थित होकर उन्होंने बुद्धिपूवेक सह्टि की इच्छा की उसी समय ध्यान के साथ ही तमोमोह, तामिस्न और अन्ध नामक पाँच प्रकार की तमोमय सुष्टि हुई  उस महात्मा के ध्यान मात्र से पाँच पर्वों (श्रेणी) वाली यह अविद्या उत्पन्न हुई। उस अभिमानोी ध्यानस्थ देव का यह सर्ग पाँच भागों में विभक्त था ।३३-३६२॥। वह सर्ग चारों ओर से अन्धकार
verses.wordMeaning: The great sages like Bhrgu and others as in seven Kalpas, so in this Kalpa, surrounded this immense being. That immense being is surrounded by the seven sages Bhrgu and others. The word c Rsi 3 is derived from the root «s/Rs, c to go 5.…
verses.commentary: Sense: The great sages like Bhrgu and others as in seven Kalpas, so in this Kalpa, surrounded this immense being. That immense being is surrounded by the seven sages Bhrgu and others. The word c Rsi 3 is derived from the root «s/Rs, c to go 5.…

verses.sanskrit: महादेवप्रसादाच्च तच्छरीरसमुद्भवा । भूयो भूयो मया दृष्टा कथिता ते नृपोत्तम
verses.transliteration: mahādevaprasādācca taccharīrasamudbhavā / bhūyo bhūyo mayā dṛṣṭā kathitā te nṛpottama
verses.translation: Thus, during these nights of Brahma that had passed in thousands, the great sages (Satya and others) saw the sleeping Kala (during the period of his slumber). Brahma is called Kala (the destroyer) because at the beginning of a Kalpa, he fashioned fourteen forms of des¬ truction.
verses.hindi: से ढका ऐसा जान पड़ता था मानो घड़े से ढका दीपक हो। वह सर्ग बाहर और भीतर से प्रकाशमान, शुद्ध और निःसंज्ञ (अचेतन) था ।: ७३। अतः उन पांचों से बुद्धि और मुख्य कारण (इन्द्रियाँ) ढकी हुई थीं इसलिये वे संवत्तात्मा 'नग” नामक मुख्य सर्ग कहलाए।३६९। ब्रह्मा अपने मुख्य से को इस प्रकार सुष्टिकाय॑ में अवरोधक देखकर असंतुष्ट हो गए। उस सर्ग से विरक्त हो वे अन्य सृष्टि के लिये ध्यान करने लगे। उनके
verses.wordMeaning: Thus, during these nights of Brahma that had passed in thousands, the great sages (Satya and others) saw the sleeping Kala (during the period of his slumber). Brahma is called Kala (the destroyer) because at the beginning of a Kalpa, he fashioned fourteen forms of des¬ truction.
verses.commentary: Sense: Thus, during these nights of Brahma that had passed in thousands, the great sages (Satya and others) saw the sleeping Kala (during the period of his slumber). Brahma is called Kala (the destroyer) because at the beginning of a Kalpa, he fashioned fourteen forms of des¬ truction.

verses.sanskrit: प्रादुर्भावमिमं कौर्म्यं ये ऽधीयन्ते द्विजोत्तमाः । ये ऽपि शृण्वन्ति विद्वांसो मुच्यन्ते ते ऽपि किल्बिषैः
verses.transliteration: prādurbhāvamimaṃ kaurmyaṃ ye 'dhīyante dvijottamāḥ / ye 'pi śṛṇvanti vidvāṃso mucyante te 'pi kilbiṣaiḥ
verses.translation: He creates living beings at the beginning of each Kalpa again and again. He, the great lord, is both manifest and unmanifest. This entire universe is his creation. Thus the period of transition between the two Kalpas—the one that is current and the other that has passed— has been described to you briefly. The conditions that existed in previous Kalpas have also been mentioned briefly. Now I shall explain the present Kalpa. Listen to that. A correct etymology.
verses.hindi: ध्यान करने से वहाँ तियंक् (तिरछा) स्रोत नामक सं उत्पन्न हुआ ।३८-४०। यतः उस समय के उत्पन्न पदार्थ तियंक (उलटा) व्यवहार और व्यापार करने वाले थे इसलिये उनका नाम तियेक स्रोत पड़ा । वे सभी तमोगुण की अधिकता के कारण अज्ञानी हुये ॥४१॥ द द
verses.wordMeaning: He creates living beings at the beginning of each Kalpa again and again. He, the great lord, is both manifest and unmanifest. This entire universe is his creation.…
verses.commentary: Sense: He creates living beings at the beginning of each Kalpa again and again. He, the great lord, is both manifest and unmanifest. This entire universe is his creation.…

verses.sanskrit: ॥ इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्ये कूर्मकल्पसमुद्भवो नाम सप्तमो ऽध्यायः ॥ र्क्व् अध्याय ८ मार्कण्डेय उवाच: नष्टे लोके पुनश्चान्ये सलिलेन समावृते । महार्णवस्य मध्यस्थो बाहुभ्यामतरं जलम्
verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmye kūrmakalpasamudbhavo nāma saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 8 mārkaṇḍeya uvāca: naṣṭe loke punaścānye salilena samāvṛte / mahārṇavasya madhyastho bāhubhyāmataraṃ jalam
verses.translation: When the mobile and immobile beings had already perished, Brahma assumed the form of wind and moved about in the water, (enveloped) in darkness. When the surface of the earth had been completely covered by the water, when the elements remained undivided and undifferentiated, the self-born lord, surveying everything, moved about like the glowworm at night during the rainy season. 1 Seeking a means for putting it back in position after knowing that the earth is immersed in water, he became enlightened by means of inference (as to the way) of.lifting up the earth. He created another body which he recollected (as having been assumed) in the previous Kalpas. On seeing the earth fully engulfed in waters, he entered the waters after assuming the form of a Boar.
verses.hindi: ४२ द वायुपुराणम्
verses.wordMeaning: When the mobile and immobile beings had already perished, Brahma assumed the form of wind and moved about in the water, (enveloped) in darkness. When the surface of the earth had been completely covered by the water, when the elements remained undivided and undifferentiated,…
verses.commentary: Sense: When the mobile and immobile beings had already perished, Brahma assumed the form of wind and moved about in the water, (enveloped) in darkness. When the surface of the earth had been completely covered by the water, when the elements remained undivided and undifferentiated,…

verses.sanskrit: दिव्ये वर्षशते पूर्णे श्रान्तो ऽहं नृपसत्तम । ध्यातुं समारभं देवं महदर्णवतारणम्
verses.transliteration: divye varṣaśate pūrṇe śrānto 'haṃ nṛpasattama / dhyātuṃ samārabhaṃ devaṃ mahadarṇavatāraṇam
verses.translation: After lifting up the earth from the waters, he deposited the waters of the oceans in the oceans, of the rivers in the rivers and of the earth on the earth. Then he collected the mountains. When the previous creation was being burnt by the Samvartaka, fire of dissolution, the mountains lay destroyed and (scattered) all over the earth. In that one vast ocean, the (solidified) waters tossed by wind got collected together due to cold. Wherever they were (thus) stuck (heaped) together, there they became immovable.
verses.hindi: (अहंऊूता अहँमाना अश्ञााविशद्विधात्मका: । एकादशेन्द्रियचिधा नवधा चोदयस्तथा
verses.wordMeaning: After lifting up the earth from the waters, he deposited the waters of the oceans in the oceans, of the rivers in the rivers and of the earth on the earth. Then he collected the mountains. When the previous creation was being burnt by the Samvartaka, fire of dissolution,…
verses.commentary: Sense: After lifting up the earth from the waters, he deposited the waters of the oceans in the oceans, of the rivers in the rivers and of the earth on the earth. Then he collected the mountains. When the previous creation was being burnt by the Samvartaka, fire of dissolution,…

verses.sanskrit: ध्यायमानस्ततः काले अपश्यं पक्षिणं परम् । हारकुन्देन्दुसंकाशं बकं गोक्षीरपाण्डुरम्
verses.transliteration: dhyāyamānastataḥ kāle apaśyaṃ pakṣiṇaṃ param / hārakundendusaṃkāśaṃ bakaṃ gokṣīrapāṇḍuram
verses.translation: The mountains are called Acalas because they become motionless after being dried up and solidified. Because they have knots and joints they are called Parvatas. They are called Cf. Supra 6. 7-11. A repetition of verses. Then, after lifting up the earth from within the waters, the Lord established it in its position again and made division in it.
verses.hindi: अष्ठों च तारकायाश्र तेषां शक्तिविधाः स्मताः। अन्तःप्रकाशास्ते सर्व आछ्ूताश्व बहिः पुनः
verses.wordMeaning: The mountains are called Acalas because they become motionless after being dried up and solidified. Because they have knots and joints they are called Parvatas. They are called Cf. Supra 6. 7-11. A repetition of verses. Then, after lifting up the earth from within the waters,…
verses.commentary: Sense: The mountains are called Acalas because they become motionless after being dried up and solidified. Because they have knots and joints they are called Parvatas. They are called Cf. Supra 6. 7-11. A repetition of verses. Then, after lifting up the earth from within the waters,…

verses.sanskrit: ततो ऽहं विस्मयाविष्टस्तं बकं समुदीक्ष्य वै । अस्मिन् महार्णवे घोरे कुतो ऽयं पक्षिसंभवः
verses.transliteration: tato 'haṃ vismayāviṣṭastaṃ bakaṃ samudīkṣya vai / asmin mahārṇave ghore kuto 'yaṃ pakṣisaṃbhavaḥ
verses.translation: In each of its seven continents, 2 he made seven Varsas (sub-continents). He levelled the uneven places and collected the mountains, with (heaps of) rocks. There are forty(?) Varsas in all the continents together. There are as many mountains also stationed at the extremities of the Varsas. They were assembled there at the beginning of creation according to their nature and not otherwise. The seven continents and the (seven) oceans encircle each other. They are in contiguity with.each others, surround¬ ing each other naturally.
verses.hindi: ते सुखप्रीतिबहुला बहिरन्तश्व संब्ृता:। प्रकाशा बहिरन्‍्तश्च ऊध्वस्तोतोक्षचाः स्म्ताः
verses.wordMeaning: In each of its seven continents, 2 he made seven Varsas (sub-continents). He levelled the uneven places and collected the mountains, with (heaps of) rocks. There are forty(?) Varsas in all the continents together.…
verses.commentary: Sense: In each of its seven continents, 2 he made seven Varsas (sub-continents). He levelled the uneven places and collected the mountains, with (heaps of) rocks. There are forty(?) Varsas in all the continents together.…

verses.sanskrit: तरन्बाहुभिरश्रान्तस्तं बकं प्रत्यभाषिषि । पाक्षरूपं समास्थाय कस्त्वमेकार्णवीकृते
verses.transliteration: taranbāhubhiraśrāntastaṃ bakaṃ pratyabhāṣiṣi / pākṣarūpaṃ samāsthāya kastvamekārṇavīkṛte
verses.translation: Even at the outset, Brahma created all these stations, the four worlds, viz. Bhilh etc., the sun, the moon and planets, Formerly at the beginning of this Kalpa 3, Brahma created the Sthdniiis (presiding deities or occupants of these posts). verses.transliteration: bhramase divyayogātmanmohayanniva māṃ prabho / etatkathaya me sarvaṃ yo 'si so 'si namo 'stu te
verses.translation: These are semantic etymologies i.c. those based on the meaning of the word. The derivations of acala or giri are understandable but others are doubtful. The Sapta-dvipi conception (division of the earth into seven continents) has superseded the Catur-dvipi concept( division of the earth into four parts) of old Puranas. The figure seven was then popular. Thus the earth is divided into seven continents. Each continent has seven sub-continents; each sub-con¬ tinent has seven mountain ranges (Kula Parvatos ), seven big rivers etc. For their description vide infra Chapters 40-49. Verses 17 ff. describe the process of re-creation of the Universe. Due to the inexorable law of Karma, every being has to re-start his or her life accord¬ ing to one's Karma in the new Kalpa. There is no automatic Mok$a even after the complete annihilation of the Universe at the end of a Kalpa.
verses.hindi: विपरीत मार्ग पर चलने वाले ध्यान और अध्यान पर कुछ भी विचार करने वाले न थे। उस तियेक स्रोत सगे को देखकर ईइ्वर ने पुनः दूसरे प्रकार की सृष्टि की । वह सुष्टि अहंकार भाव वाली और अद्ठाइस प्रकार की है । एकादश इन्द्रिय वाले उस सर्ग का नवविध उदय बताया गया है ।४२-४३॥ तारक आदि की संख्या आठ है, जिनकी शक्ति भिन्न भिन्न प्रकार की हैं। उनका अन्तस् प्रकाशमान परन्तु बाहर से वे ढके हुये हैं  ४४।

verses.sanskrit: सो ऽब्रवीन्मां महादेवो ब्रह्माहं विष्णुरेव च । जगत्सर्वं मया वत्स संहृतं किं न बुध्यसे
verses.transliteration: so 'bravīnmāṃ mahādevo brahmāhaṃ viṣṇureva ca / jagatsarvaṃ mayā vatsa saṃhṛtaṃ kiṃ na budhyase
verses.translation: They are Kna, Treta, Dvapara and Kali. In the beginning of the Kalpa, during the first Kytayuga, he created the subjects (beings). The subjects of the previous ages who have been men¬ tioned to you by me, were burnt by the Sarhvartaka fire then in the Kalpa that was coning to an end. Those who could not reach Tapoloka, had resorted to the Janaloka. They began to function as seeds for the future creation.
verses.hindi: (वे तियंक् व्यवहार वाले हैं अतः तियंक् स्लोत उनका नाम है। इस तियंक् स्रोत वाली सृष्टि को देख कर भी ईइवर ने तृतीय सृष्टि की इच्छा की क्योंकि पूर्व की दो सृष्टियों को देखकर उनके हृंदय में अन्य प्रकार की सृष्टि करने की इच्छा हुई थी)। उनके नित्य ध्यान से सात्त्विक सर्ग उत्पन्न हुआ ।४५-४६। वह तीसरा स्ग ऊर्घ्वस्लोत हुआ जो कि ऊध्वे दिशा की ओर ही व्यवस्थित रहा। यतः उसके ऊपर की ओर ही गति थी

verses.sanskrit: तव माता पिताहं वै विश्वस्य च महामुने । कारुण्यं मम संजातं दृष्ट्वा मग्नं महार्णवे
verses.transliteration: tava mātā pitāhaṃ vai viśvasya ca mahāmune / kāruṇyaṃ mama saṃjātaṃ dṛṣṭvā magnaṃ mahārṇave
verses.translation: Abiding there, in the form of seeds for the subsequent creation, they, on being let loose (scattered) serve the purpose of progeny. The subjects, Dcvas, Pitys, sages and Manus are those who accomplish (the four Purusarihas viz.) virtue (Dharma), wealth (Artha), pleasure (Kama), and salvation (Moksa). Being endowed with Penance thereafter, they fill up (occupy) the stations. As the mental sons of Brahma, they work as accomplished souls.
verses.hindi: इसलिये उस सर्ग का नाम ऊध्वेस्रोत पड़ा । उस सर्ग के जीव सुखी और प्रेमी थे। उनका अन्तः और बाह्य दोनों प्रकाशभान और समान रूप से व्यवस्थित था। ऐसे ऊध्वेत्नोत सर्ग से उत्पन्न सभी ऊध्वेस्रोत ही कहे जाते हैं ।४७-४८। उसी सर्ग के अन्तर्गत जीवों में प्राण संचार करने वाले वायु आदि सम्मिलित हैं । उध्वं प्रवृत्ति होने के कारण ही वह सर्गे ऊरध्वत्नोत कहा गया है ४६। उस समय ऊध्वंस्रोत देवों की सृष्टि हो जाने के

verses.sanskrit: पक्षिरूपं समास्थाय अतो ऽत्राहं समागतः । किम् अर्थमातुरो भूत्वा भ्रमसीत्थं महार्णवे
verses.transliteration: pakṣirūpaṃ samāsthāya ato 'trāhaṃ samāgataḥ / kim arthamāturo bhūtvā bhramasītthaṃ mahārṇave
verses.translation: The created beings who have attained heaven through subversive rites are reborn (repeatedly) in every Yuga. Due to the residue of the fruits of their actions, they become well-known with their souls inclined in that manner. They descend from the Janaloka due to the bondage of the Karmans. It is the intention, the feelings of the mind that should be regarded as the cause, in regard to the activities. The people descend from Janaloka due to their good and bad acti¬ vities (in their previous lives).
verses.hindi: अनन्तर प्रभु ब्रह्मा अत्यन्त प्रसन्‍न हुएं। तदनन्तर उन्होंने अब दूसरे प्रकार की सृष्टि करने का विचार किया ।५०। उस प्रभु ईश्वर ने अन्य साधक (इच्छानुकूल) सगे की सृष्टि की। उस समय सत्य-चिन्तन करने वाले ब्रह्मा के चिन्तन से अव्यक्त से अव्यक्त स्रोत तामक सर्ग उत्पन्न हुआ जो कि प्रभु के इच्छानुकूलस था।
verses.wordMeaning: The created beings who have attained heaven through subversive rites are reborn (repeatedly) in every Yuga. Due to the residue of the fruits of their actions, they become well-known with their souls inclined in that manner.…

verses.sanskrit: शीघ्रं प्रविश मत्पक्षौ येन विश्रमसे द्विज । एवमुक्तस्ततस्तेन देवेनाहं नरेश्वर
verses.transliteration: śīghraṃ praviśa matpakṣau yena viśramase dvija / evamuktastatastena devenāhaṃ nareśvara
verses.translation: They take up different forms of bodies in different wombs (species) from Devas to immobile beings. They are born of one another successively. Being created again and again, they pursue those activities which they had been pursuing before. They pursue violent or non-violent, soft or ruthless, virtuous or evil, truthful or false activities on being urged by those previous innate feelings which appeal to them.

verses.sanskrit: ततो ऽहं तस्य पक्षान्ते प्रलीनस्तु भ्रमञ्जले । काले युगसाहस्रान्ते अश्रान्तो ऽर्णवमध्यगः
verses.transliteration: tato 'haṃ tasya pakṣānte pralīnastu bhramañjale / kāle yugasāhasrānte aśrānto 'rṇavamadhyagaḥ
verses.translation: Whatever names and forms (these beings have) in the past Kalpa, they mostly receive the same in the future Kalpas. They assume those very names and forms again and again. They are born in the different Kalpas with the same names and forms. When Brahma who was desirous of creation got his creative activity obstructed. He, of truthful contemplation, began to contemplate on the subjects. He created a thousand pairs from his mouth. With the quality of Sattva predominant, they, of good mind, were suitable for the task.
verses.hindi: तै च प्रकाशबेहुलास्तमःसच्व रजो घिकाः । तस्मात्ते दुःखबहुला भूया भूयश्च कारिणुः
verses.wordMeaning: Whatever names and forms (these beings have) in the past Kalpa, they mostly receive the same in the future Kalpas. They assume those very names and forms again and again. They are born in the different Kalpas with the same names and forms.…

verses.sanskrit: ततः शृणोमि सहसा दिक्षु सर्वासु सुव्रत । किंचिन्नूपुरसंमिश्रम् अद्भुतं शब्दमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration: tataḥ śṛṇomi sahasā dikṣu sarvāsu suvrata / kiṃcinnūpurasaṃmiśram adbhutaṃ śabdamuttamam
verses.translation: He created another thousand pairs from his chest. These had the quality of passion (Rajas) predominant and were fiery and impatient. He created another thousand'couples from his thighs. Passion (Rajas) and Ignorance (Tamas) were predominant in them. They were ambitious and aspirant. He created another thousand couples from his feet. They had ignorance (Tamas) predominant in them. They were inglorious and deficient in brilliance.
verses.hindi: प्रकाशा बहुरन्‍्तश्च मनुष्याः साधकाश्च ते। लक्षणेस्तारकायस्ते अष्टचथा च व्यचस्थिता:
verses.wordMeaning: He created another thousand pairs from his chest. These had the quality of passion (Rajas) predominant and were fiery and impatient. He created another thousand'couples from his thighs. Passion (Rajas) and Ignorance (Tamas) were predominant in them.…

verses.sanskrit: तदार्णवजलं सर्वं संक्षिप्तं सहसाभवत् । किमेतदिति संचिन्त्य दिशः समवलोकयम्
verses.transliteration: tadārṇavajalaṃ sarvaṃ saṃkṣiptaṃ sahasābhavat / kimetaditi saṃcintya diśaḥ samavalokayam
verses.translation: The living beings born of these pairs were passion¬ ate. Being lustful, they began to copulate with one another. Thenceforward procreation from pairing originated in this Kalpa. Women did not have their menstrual courses month by month. Then they did not conceive, even when copulated. They brought forth pairs of children once at the end of life. They gave birth to crooked offspring (?), when they had desire for death. From that time onward pairing originated in this Kalpa. Even by contemplating once mentally, the subjects had created for them, the five objects of senses such as sound, each of which was of five characteristics in the pure form. 1
verses.hindi: सिद्धात्मानों मनुष्यास्ते गन्धवंसहधर्मिणः । इस्येष तेजसः सर्गों ह्थावस्रोताः प्रकीर्तितः
verses.wordMeaning: The living beings born of these pairs were passion¬ ate. Being lustful, they began to copulate with one another. Thenceforward procreation from pairing originated in this Kalpa. Women did not have their menstrual courses month by month. Then they did not conceive,…

verses.sanskrit: दश कन्यास्ततो दिक्षु आगताश्च महार्णवे । वस्त्रालंकारसहिता दिग्भ्यो नूपुरभूषिताः
verses.transliteration: daśa kanyāstato dikṣu āgatāśca mahārṇave / vastrālaṃkārasahitā digbhyo nūpurabhūṣitāḥ
verses.translation: In this way the previous creation by god Brahma was through his mind (mental activity). Those who were born in his race have filled the world. Verses 44-63 paint a glowing picture of the Krta age. They depict the ideal state of society from Puraijic point of view—a classless society with perfect equality and full liberty. The people in that age resorted to rivers, lakes, oceans and mountains. The waters in that Yuga were neither too hot nor too cold.
verses.hindi: विद्वत्त वर्तमान च तेडर्थ जानन्ति तक्त्चतः  भूतादकानां सत्त्वानां षष्ठः सं: स उच्यते
verses.wordMeaning: In this way the previous creation by god Brahma was through his mind (mental activity). Those who were born in his race have filled the world. Verses 44-63 paint a glowing picture of the Krta age.…

verses.sanskrit: काचिच्चन्द्रसमाभासा काचिदादित्यसप्रभा । काचिदंजनपुञ्जाभा काचिद्रक्तोत्पलप्रभा
verses.transliteration: kāciccandrasamābhāsā kācidādityasaprabhā / kācidaṃjanapuñjābhā kācidraktotpalaprabhā
verses.translation: They usually took the diet of the juicy food of the earth. They moved about wherever they pleased. They had acquired mental Siddhis. In that Krta age, there was neither virtue nor evil. The human beings were non-differentiated. They had equal longevity, happiness and beauty (form). In the beginning of the Kalpa, in the Krta age, neither virtue (Dharma) nor evil (Adharma) existed. The people were born with their respective authority and rights.
verses.hindi: (८ ते परिशभ्रहिणः सर्व संविभागरत।: पुनः । खादुनाश्चाप्यशीलाश्च शेया भूतादिकास्तु ते)

verses.sanskrit: नानारूपधरा सौम्या नानाभरणभूषिता । अर्घ्यपाद्यादिभिर्माल्यैर्बकमभ्यर्च्य सुव्रताः
verses.transliteration: nānārūpadharā saumyā nānābharaṇabhūṣitā / arghyapādyādibhirmālyairbakamabhyarcya suvratāḥ
verses.translation: The first Krta age consisted of four thousand divine Even when thousands of human beings spread they had no obstruction, no clash and no order. They had no fixed abode or place of resort. They wandered about mountains and oceans. They were free from sorrow. They had abundant goodness. They were happy in solitude.
verses.hindi: तन्माआणां द्वितीयस्तु भूतस्गः स उच्यते । वेकारिकस्तृतीयस्तु सर्व ऐेन्द्रियकः स्स्ृतः

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तं पर्वताकारं गुह्यं पक्षिणमव्ययम् । प्रविवेश महाघोरं पर्वतो ह्यर्णवं स्वराट्
verses.transliteration: tatastaṃ parvatākāraṃ guhyaṃ pakṣiṇamavyayam / praviveśa mahāghoraṃ parvato hyarṇavaṃ svarāṭ
verses.translation: They moved about as they pleased. They were always joyous in their minds. There were no animals, birds or reptiles then. There were no trees or plants nor hellish beings born of evil. There were neither roots nor fruits nor flowers nor the seasons nor the years. Time was always pleasant when peoples' desires were fulfilled. There were no extremes in heat or cold. Whatever object they desired in their minds was available everywhere and at all times.
verses.hindi: तियेक्स्नोताश्च यः सर्ग स्तियंग्योनि: स पश्चमः । तथोध्चस्नोतर्सा षष्ठो देवसर्ग सस्‍्तु स स्मुतः॥
verses.wordMeaning: They moved about as they pleased. They were always joyous in their minds. There were no animals, birds or reptiles then. There were no trees or plants nor hellish beings born of evil. There were neither roots nor fruits nor flowers nor the seasons nor the years.…

verses.sanskrit: योजनानां सहस्राणि तावन्त्येव शतानि च । त्रिंशद्योजनसाहस्रं यावद्भूमण्डलं त्विति
verses.transliteration: yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi tāvantyeva śatāni ca / triṃśadyojanasāhasraṃ yāvadbhūmaṇḍalaṃ tviti
verses.translation: Whatever juices they meditated upon, grew up from the earth. Their achievements were conducive to strength, fair complexion and destructive of ailments. With their bodies requiring no decoration (or beauti¬ fication), the subjects had eternal youth. Pairs of children were born from their pure mental conception. They were born alike and they died together. They had similar forms and features. At that time, there was truth, absence of greed, forbearance, contentment, happiness and restraint.
verses.hindi: अतः वह सर्ग अर्वाक् (मध्यगत) प्रवृत्ति वाला था इसलिए वह अवकि स्रोत कहा गया है।५१-५२! उसे सर्ग के जीव प्रकाश, सत्त्व, रज और तमभ तीनों गुणों से यथ्रेष्ट रूप से पूर्ण थे। इसलिये उनमें दुःख की मात्रा अधिक थी और वे बार बार कर्म करने वाले हुए । वे मनुष्य अन्तः बाह्य सभी ओर से प्रकाशपूर्ण और सृष्टि के सहायक हुए। वे तारक आदि लक्षणों से आठ रूपों में स्थित हैं ।५१-५४। वे सिद्धात्मा
verses.wordMeaning: Whatever juices they meditated upon, grew up from the earth. Their achievements were conducive to strength, fair complexion and destructive of ailments. With their bodies requiring no decoration (or beauti¬ fication), the subjects had eternal youth.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Whatever juices they meditated upon, grew up from the earth. Their achievements were conducive to strength, fair complexion and destructive of ailments. With their bodies requiring no decoration (or beauti¬ fication), the subjects had eternal youth.…

verses.sanskrit: ततो भूमण्डलं दिव्यं पञ्चरत्नसमाकुलम् । दिव्यस्फटिकसोपानं रुक्मस्तंभमनोरमम्
verses.transliteration: tato bhūmaṇḍalaṃ divyaṃ pañcaratnasamākulam / divyasphaṭikasopānaṃ rukmastaṃbhamanoramam
verses.translation: They had no distinguishing marks in their forms and features, longevity, conduct and activity. Their actions were spontaneous and voluntary, without the intercession of intellect. In the Krtavuga, there was no inclination towards performance, of good or evil actions. There was no classification of castes or differentiation in stages of life. Nor was there inter¬ mixture of castes. In their mutual dealings they behaved without being impelled by desire or hatred. All of them, had equal forms, features and longevity. There was neither superior nor inferior class of people.
verses.hindi: मानव गन्धर्वों के सहधर्मी हैं। इस प्रकार यह सर्ग तैजस और अर्वाक् स्रोत कहा गया है ।५४५। पाँचवाँ सर्ग अनुग्रह के नाम से विख्यात है, जिसकी व्यवस्था शक्ति, तुष्टि एवं सिद्धि के विपयंय (उलटे) क्रम से की गई हैं ।५६। उस सृष्टि के प्राणी (ब्रह्म के) विवंत रूप एवं उसके वरतंमान अर्थ को तात्त्विक रूप से जानते हैं, इस प्रकार भूतादि (पञ्चभूत आदि) जीवों का वह सर्ग छठां सर्य कहा जाता है ।५५७। उनमें
verses.wordMeaning: They had no distinguishing marks in their forms and features, longevity, conduct and activity. Their actions were spontaneous and voluntary, without the intercession of intellect. In the Krtavuga, there was no inclination towards performance, of good or evil actions.…
verses.commentary: Sense: They had no distinguishing marks in their forms and features, longevity, conduct and activity. Their actions were spontaneous and voluntary, without the intercession of intellect. In the Krtavuga, there was no inclination towards performance, of good or evil actions.…

verses.sanskrit: योजनानां सहस्रं तु विस्तराद्द्विगुणायतम् । वापीकूपसमाकीर्णं प्रासादाट्टालकावृतम्
verses.transliteration: yojanānāṃ sahasraṃ tu vistarāddviguṇāyatam / vāpīkūpasamākīrṇaṃ prāsādāṭṭālakāvṛtam
verses.translation: Only those who were mostly happy and devoid of sorrow were born in the Krta Yuga. They were highly power¬ ful, very strong and perpetually delighted in the mind. They had neither gain nor loss; neither friends nor foes; neither likes nor dislikes, since they were devoid of desires. The objects functioned according to their minds. They neither desired to possess nor favoured one another. It has been said that in the Krta age meditation was the highest; in Treta it was knowledge; in Dvapara it was sacrifice, while charity (donation) is excellent m Kali age.
verses.hindi: जो संचय तथा समान विभाग करने वाले और भक्षणशील एवं कठोर प्रवृत्ति के हैं, उन्हें भूत सर्ग नामक छठा सगे जानना चाहिए ।५८। विपयेय के क्रम से उत्पन्न वह भूतादि सर्ग, छक्तिहंन रूप से स्थित है। प्रथम उत्पन्न होने के नाते इसको महत् सर्ग कहा गया है, इसीलिए उसे मह॒त् सर्ग जानना चाहिए ।५६। पज्चतन्मात्रा का दूसरा रूप भूतसर्ग कहा जाता है, और विकार जनित होने के नाते उसके
verses.wordMeaning: Only those who were mostly happy and devoid of sorrow were born in the Krta Yuga. They were highly power¬ ful, very strong and perpetually delighted in the mind. They had neither gain nor loss; neither friends nor foes; neither likes nor dislikes,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Only those who were mostly happy and devoid of sorrow were born in the Krta Yuga. They were highly power¬ ful, very strong and perpetually delighted in the mind. They had neither gain nor loss; neither friends nor foes; neither likes nor dislikes,…

verses.sanskrit: कल्पवृक्षसमाकीर्णं ध्वजषष्टिविभूषितम् । तस्मिन्पुरवरे रम्ये नानारत्नोपशोभितम्
verses.transliteration: kalpavṛkṣasamākīrṇaṃ dhvajaṣaṣṭivibhūṣitam / tasminpuravare ramye nānāratnopaśobhitam
verses.translation: In accordance with practice obtaining in the different ages, goodness (Sattva) predominates in Krta, passion fRajas) in Treta, passion (Rajas) and Ignorance (Tama.) m Dvapara and only ignorance (Tamas) in the Kali Yuga. As for the duration of Krta age, know that four thou¬ sand divine years constitute its duration. In the Krta age, when the interim period (between
verses.hindi: तीसरे रूप को वेकारिक कहते हैं इन्हें ऐन्द्रियक (इन्द्रिय द्वारा जनित) भी कहा जाता हैं ।६०। इस प्रकार बुद्धिपृवंक यह प्राकृत सर्ग उत्पन्न हुआ। चौथा मुख्य सर्ग है, जिसमें मुख्य स्थावर सर्म का होना बताया गया है ।६१। तियंक् स्लोत वाले उस पाँचवें सगे को तियंक योनि कहा गया है और ऊध्व ज्रोत वाले उस छठे
verses.wordMeaning: In accordance with practice obtaining in the different ages, goodness (Sattva) predominates in Krta, passion fRajas) in Treta, passion (Rajas) and Ignorance (Tama.) m Dvapara and only ignorance (Tamas) in the Kali Yuga. As for the duration of Krta age,…

verses.sanskrit: तथान्यच्च पुरं रम्यं पताकोज्ज्वलवेदिकम् । शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं तावद्द्विगुणमायतम्
verses.transliteration: tathānyacca puraṃ ramyaṃ patākojjvalavedikam / śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ tāvaddviguṇamāyatam
verses.translation: When the period of junction is over at the end of the age, 1 the Dharma of the period of junction remains but one- fourth. When the Krta age lapses completely without any remnant, the spiritual achievement (of Krta age) too vanishes. When the mental Siddki (of Krta age) is lost, another comes into being in the Treta Yuga. The eight mental perfections in the beginning of the creation, mentioned by me, decline gradually and are lost.
verses.hindi: घनुद्चिल्वान्त्गंत नास्ति क. पुस्तके ।
verses.wordMeaning: When the period of junction is over at the end of the age, 1 the Dharma of the period of junction remains but one- fourth. When the Krta age lapses completely without any remnant, the spiritual achievement (of Krta age) too vanishes.…
verses.commentary: Sense: When the period of junction is over at the end of the age, 1 the Dharma of the period of junction remains but one- fourth. When the Krta age lapses completely without any remnant, the spiritual achievement (of Krta age) too vanishes.…

verses.sanskrit: पुरमध्ये ततस्तस्मिन्नदी परमशोभना । महती पुण्यसलिला नानारत्नशिला तथा
verses.transliteration: puramadhye tatastasminnadī paramaśobhanā / mahatī puṇyasalilā nānāratnaśilā tathā
verses.translation: In the beginning of the Kalpa, in the Krta age, this attainment is only mental. In all the Manvantaras in accord¬ ance with the division of the four Yugas, the attainment is due to the holy rites, due to the pursuit of the conduct of life of the respective castes and stages of life. When the Krta age passes off thus, one-fourth of the Dharma is lost in the first junction, another one-fourth When water becomes subtle, cloud is formed The
verses.hindi: ४४ । वायुपुराणम्
verses.wordMeaning: In the beginning of the Kalpa, in the Krta age, this attainment is only mental. In all the Manvantaras in accord¬ ance with the division of the four Yugas, the attainment is due to the holy rites,…

verses.transliteration: tasyāstīre mayā dṛṣṭaṃ taḍitsūryasamaprabham / indranīlamahānīlaiścitaṃ ratnaiḥ samantataḥ
verses.translation: When the surface of the earth is drenched with rain Versts 77-88 humo "dipt " d Trc,i I '"'" All the necessary objects of enjoyments emanated from them (the trees). In the beginning of Treta, people subsisted on them (i.e. the products of trees). Then after the lapse of a long time, due to their own perversity the emotions of lust and greed possessed them suddenly.

verses.sanskrit: क्वचिद्वह्निसमाकारं क्वचिदिन्द्रायुधप्रभम् । क्वचिद्धूम्रं क्वचित्पीतं क्वचिद्रक्तं क्वचित्सितम्
verses.transliteration: kvacidvahnisamākāraṃ kvacidindrāyudhaprabham / kvaciddhūmraṃ kvacitpītaṃ kvacidraktaṃ kvacitsitam
verses.translation: The menstrual flow that used to take place only at the end of life in the case of women then (in Krta Yuga), ceased to be so due to the power of the (new, Treta) Yuga. In their case, the menstruation began to take place every month. As a consequence thereof, they indulged in copulation the same way. When the flow took this turn and when they copulat¬ ed every month, the untimely menstrual flow and conception began to happen.
verses.hindi: विस्ताराजुप्रह सर्ग कीर्त्यमानं निबोधत । चतु्धांउबस्थितः सोड्थ सवभूतेषु कृ्स्नशः
verses.wordMeaning: The menstrual flow that used to take place only at the end of life in the case of women then (in Krta Yuga), ceased to be so due to the power of the (new, Treta) Yuga. In their case, the menstruation began to take place every month. As a consequence thereof,…

verses.sanskrit: नानावर्णैः समायुक्तं लिङ्गमद्भुतदर्शनम् । ब्रह्मविष्ण्विन्द्रसाध्यैश्च समन्तात्परिवारितम्
verses.transliteration: nānāvarṇaiḥ samāyuktaṃ liṅgamadbhutadarśanam / brahmaviṣṇvindrasādhyaiśca samantātparivāritam
verses.translation: On account of their perversity and due to what was destined to happen in course of time, all the trees in their house (or which were like their houses) perished. When these were destroyed, the people became excited and agitated in all their senses. They, of truthful thought, began to meditate on that mental Siddhi. The trees manifested in their houses again. They yielded clothes, fruits and ornaments. Invigorating honey without the bees, possessing sweet taste, scent and colour, exuded in them in every leafeup.
verses.hindi: सर्गा; परस्परस्याथ प्रंकारा बहव:ः स्म्बृताः। अग्ने ससर्ज वे ब्रह्मा मानसानात्मनः समान

verses.sanskrit: नन्दीश्वरगणाध्यक्षैश्चेन्द्रादित्यैश्च तद्वृतम् । पश्यामि लिङ्गमीशानं महालिङ्गं तमेव च
verses.transliteration: nandīśvaragaṇādhyakṣaiścendrādityaiśca tadvṛtam / paśyāmi liṅgamīśānaṃ mahāliṅgaṃ tameva ca
verses.translation: They maintained themselves with that honey at the beginning of the Treta age. They were delighted and contented with that Siddhi. They were free from ailments. As time elapsed, they were overcome with greed once again. They forcibly took possession of trees and extracted from them the nectar (of flowers) and honey. Due to this misdemeanor committed by the people, the wish-yielding trees perished at some places along with honey.
verses.hindi: सननन्‍द्नं च सनक॑ विद्वांसे च सनातनम् । विज्ञानेन निवृत्तास्ते वेवतन महोजसः ॥
verses.wordMeaning: They maintained themselves with that honey at the beginning of the Treta age. They were delighted and contented with that Siddhi. They were free from ailments. As time elapsed, they were overcome with greed once again.…
verses.commentary: Sense: They maintained themselves with that honey at the beginning of the Treta age. They were delighted and contented with that Siddhi. They were free from ailments. As time elapsed, they were overcome with greed once again.…

verses.sanskrit: परिवार्य ततस्तं तु प्रसुप्तान्देवदानवान् । निमीलिताक्षान्पश्यामि दिव्याभरणभूषितान्
verses.transliteration: parivārya tatastaṃ tu prasuptāndevadānavān / nimīlitākṣānpaśyāmi divyābharaṇabhūṣitān
verses.translation: When the period of junction remained but little, due to the passage of time, there arose extremes of climate (e.g. scorching heat and extreme cold). They were terribly distressed by the extremes of biting winds and scorching sunshine. Being afflicted by these they made shelters. Warding off Dvandvas (pairs of opposites) of heat and cold, they resorted to abodes. Formerly, they had been roaming about as they pleased, without a fixed habitation. Now according to circumstances and their liking, they stayed in abodes, wildernesses, deserts, deep chasms, on hills, mountains or riversides. They resorted to fortresses, dry soils and waste lands with perpetual supply of water.
verses.hindi: तदा तेषु व्यतीतेषु तदान्यान्साथकांश् तान  मानसानखज दुशह्मा पुनः स्थानाभिमानिनः+
verses.wordMeaning: When the period of junction remained but little, due to the passage of time, there arose extremes of climate (e.g. scorching heat and extreme cold). They were terribly distressed by the extremes of biting winds and scorching sunshine.…
verses.commentary: Sense: When the period of junction remained but little, due to the passage of time, there arose extremes of climate (e.g. scorching heat and extreme cold). They were terribly distressed by the extremes of biting winds and scorching sunshine.…

verses.sanskrit: ततस्ताः पद्मपत्राक्ष्यो नार्यः परमसंमताः । नद्यास्तस्या जले स्नात्वा दिव्यपुष्पैर्मनोरमैः
verses.transliteration: tatastāḥ padmapatrākṣyo nāryaḥ paramasaṃmatāḥ / nadyāstasyā jale snātvā divyapuṣpairmanoramaiḥ
verses.translation: In order to ward off heat and cold, they made habita¬ tions in level and rugged lands in accordance with the availa¬ bility and their taste. Then they set up hamlets, villages and towns with due alignment and built harems loo. The measure of their length and diameter was fixed by them. * 1 Ihey built houses on this basis just as tlicy thought fit. A unit was termed PradeSa —a distance between the (ex¬ tended) thumb and the (outstretched) forefinger. The distance between the thumb and the middle finger (when both are stretched) was Tala and that between the thumb and the ring figer was Gokarna.
verses.hindi: आधभूतसंधक्षवावस्थाश्षामतस्ताक्षिबोघत । आपोउद्निः पृथिवत वायुरन्तरिक्ष॑ द्शिरुतथा
verses.wordMeaning: In order to ward off heat and cold, they made habita¬ tions in level and rugged lands in accordance with the availa¬ bility and their taste. Then they set up hamlets, villages and towns with due alignment and built harems loo.…
verses.commentary: Sense: In order to ward off heat and cold, they made habita¬ tions in level and rugged lands in accordance with the availa¬ bility and their taste. Then they set up hamlets, villages and towns with due alignment and built harems loo.…

verses.transliteration: dattvārghapādyaṃ vidhivalliṃgasya saha pakṣiṇā / arcayantīrvarārohā daśa tāḥ pramadottamāḥ
verses.translation: The distance between the thumb and the little finger (when both are stretched) was called Vitasli. It contained Verses 97-102 give the units of measurement of distance as follows The first unit 'Angula * means 'Finger-breadth* Four Hastas or two Nalikas made one Dhanus or Danda. Two thousand Dlianus or Pandas made one Gavyuti. Eight thousand Dhanus constituted a Tojana. It is on the basis of the Yojana calculation that the sites were fixed then.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्त्वभ्यर्च्य तल्लिङ्गं तस्मिन्नेव पुरोत्तमे । सर्वा अदर्शनं जग्मुर्विद्युतो ऽभ्रगणेष्विव
verses.transliteration: tatastvabhyarcya talliṅgaṃ tasminneva purottame / sarvā adarśanaṃ jagmurvidyuto 'bhragaṇeṣviva
verses.translation: Of the four types of fortifications, three occur naturally. The fourth kind of fortress is artificial. I shall describe the mode of its construction. 1 Huge mansions, lofty ramparts and fort-walls are built around. There is a principal gate called Svastika and there is a gynaeceum in which maidens are kept ( Kumaripura ). The (main) gate is close to a moat with flowing water current. The width of the moat is the best if (it is) eight or ten hands. Others-opine that nine or eight hands (in width) is the best.
verses.hindi: को देवसर्ग ।६२। इसो प्रकार अवांक स्रोत वाले को सातवाँ मानुष सर्ग कहा जाता है एवं अनुग्रह सर्ग को आठवाँ जा कि सात्त्विक और तामस के संमिश्रण से प्रादुर्भूत है ।६३। इसी प्रकार पाँच प्रकार के विकृंत और तीन प्रकार के प्राकृत सर्ग बताये गये है। उन्हीं बिकृत तथा प्राकृत सर्गों के समेत नवें कौमार सगे का व्याख्या की गई है (इनमें तीन प्रकार के इस प्राकृत सर्ग की बुद्धिपूवंक सृष्टि की गई है) इस प्रकार ब्रह्म
verses.wordMeaning: Of the four types of fortifications, three occur naturally. The fourth kind of fortress is artificial. I shall describe the mode of its construction. 1 Huge mansions, lofty ramparts and fort-walls are built around.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Of the four types of fortifications, three occur naturally. The fourth kind of fortress is artificial. I shall describe the mode of its construction. 1 Huge mansions, lofty ramparts and fort-walls are built around.…

verses.sanskrit: न चासौ पक्षिराट् तस्मिन्न स्त्रियो न च देवताः । तदेवैकं स्थितं लिङ्गमर्चयन्विस्मयान्वितः
verses.transliteration: na cāsau pakṣirāṭ tasminna striyo na ca devatāḥ / tadevaikaṃ sthitaṃ liṅgamarcayanvismayānvitaḥ
verses.translation: (I shall mention the dimensions) of hamlets, cities and villages and three types of forts, viz. mountains, waters (rivers) and constructed (artificially by) men. The diameter shall be half a Yojana. Its length should be one and one-eighth of a Yojana. A city that extends to the east or north is the most excellent. 2 3 Its extent shall be half or one-fourth of the maximum length. It should be divided into a hypotenuse and segments and be laid out in the shape of a fan. A city planne circularly or merely lengthwise (with little breadth) or deficient in (amenities) is not recommeiidable. A city set up in e form of,a square with straight rows of houses in all the eight quarters is desirable. Verses 103-107 refer to construction of forts. __- nr, Verses 108-117 explain the ancientideas B.lt crudeness fr
verses.hindi: की ये छहों सृष्टियाँ बुद्धि परवक ही भ्रवृत्त होती है ।६५-६५। अब मैं वर्णनीय उस अनुग्नरह वामक सर्गे की जो समस्त प्राणियों में चार प्रकार से पूर्ण रूपेण स्थित है, विस्तृत व्याख्या बता रहा हूँ, तुम लोग सुनो ६६। शक्ति, तुष्ठि एवं सिद्धि के विपयं य क्रम से स्थावर सृष्टि में विपयेय और तियेक् योतियों में शक्ति का संचार हुआ है ।६: अतः मनुष्यों में सिद्धि और देवों में तुष्टि पूर्ण रूप से निहित है। पुनः इस प्रकार
verses.wordMeaning: (I shall mention the dimensions) of hamlets, cities and villages and three types of forts, viz. mountains, waters (rivers) and constructed (artificially by) men. The diameter shall be half a Yojana. Its length should be one and one-eighth of a Yojana.…

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽहं दुःखमूढात्मा रुद्रमायेति चिन्तयन् । ततः कन्याः समुत्तीर्य दिव्यांबरविभूषणाः
verses.transliteration: tato'haṃ duḥkhamūḍhātmā rudramāyeti cintayan / tataḥ kanyāḥ samuttīrya divyāṃbaravibhūṣaṇāḥ
verses.translation: The reading Vyajana from Bd. P. I. 2. 7. 107 is accepted as Vyaana, The minimum width of a dwelling is twenty-four Hastas and the maximum is eight hundred Hastas. But they praise a middle one which is neither too narrow nor too wide. Important dwellings shall be constructed in a site eight hundred Kifkus wide. A hamlet has half the diameter of the city and a village is bigger than that.
verses.hindi: प्राकृत तथा विक्ृत सर्ग नव प्रकार के बताये गये हैं ।६८। परस्पर संबद्ध इन सर्गों के बहुत से भेद कहे गये हैं । सबसे पहले बह्मा ने अपने ही समान विद्वानू सनक, सननन्‍्दन और सनातन नामक तीन मानस पुत्रों को उत्पन्न किया । वे तीनों महातेजस्वी अपने सृष्टिविज्ञान के भ्रभाव से निवत्ति मार्ग पर अल रहे ।६६-७०। नानात्व के रहस्य को जानकर वे ज्ञान सम्पन्न हो गए और पिता की आज्ञा न मानकर प्रजोत्पत्ति से विभुख हो अन्य
verses.wordMeaning: The reading Vyajana from Bd. P. I. 2. 7. 107 is accepted as Vyaana, The minimum width of a dwelling is twenty-four Hastas and the maximum is eight hundred Hastas. But they praise a middle one which is neither too narrow nor too wide.…

verses.sanskrit: भासयन्त्यो जगत्सर्वं विद्युतो ऽभ्रगणानिव । पद्मैर्हिरण्मयैर्दिव्यैरर्चयित्वा शुभाननाः
verses.transliteration: bhāsayantyo jagatsarvaṃ vidyuto 'bhragaṇāniva / padmairhiraṇmayairdivyairarcayitvā śubhānanāḥ
verses.translation: A hamlet shall be situated a Tojana away from a city and a village shall be half a Tojana away from a hamlet. Two Krosas is the maximum boundary. The boundary of a field is four Dhantis. The highway shall be twenty Dhanus wide. The main road in the village shall also be twenty Dhanus wide. But the road in the border-land shall be only ten Dhanus wide. The main road shall be excellent if it is ten Dhanus wide. The movement of the traffic of people (pedestrians), horses, elephants and chariots should be without hindrance. Branch roads should be four Dhanus wide. The roads connecting dwelling houses and side roads shall be two Dhanus wide.
verses.hindi: चले गए ।७१। इस प्रकार उन कुमारों के चले जाने पर ब्रह्मा ने पुनः अपने पद का अभिमान करने वाले अन्य मानस पुत्रों को उत्पन्न किया जिन्होंने सृष्टि काय॑ में पूरा सहयोग दिया ।७२! प्रलय तक स्थित रहने, वाले स्थानाश मानी देवों के नामों को गिना रहा हूँ सुनो-- जल, अग्नि, पृथिवी, वाझु, अन्तरिक्ष, दिद्लायें स्वर्ग, दिव, समुद्र, नंद, शेल, वनस्पतियाँ, ओषधियाँ, आत्मा, मन, दुृक्ष, वीरुघ, (छोटे वृक्ष), लव, काष्ठ,
verses.wordMeaning: A hamlet shall be situated a Tojana away from a city and a village shall be half a Tojana away from a hamlet. Two Krosas is the maximum boundary. The boundary of a field is four Dhantis. The highway shall be twenty Dhanus wide.…
verses.commentary: Sense: A hamlet shall be situated a Tojana away from a city and a village shall be half a Tojana away from a hamlet. Two Krosas is the maximum boundary. The boundary of a field is four Dhantis. The highway shall be twenty Dhanus wide.…

verses.sanskrit: विविशुस्तज्जलं क्षिप्रं समंताद् वरभूषणाः । तस्मिन्पुरवरे चान्ये तामेवाहं पुनःपुनः
verses.transliteration: viviśustajjalaṃ kṣipraṃ samaṃtād varabhūṣaṇāḥ / tasminpuravare cānye tāmevāhaṃ punaḥpunaḥ
verses.translation: The "bell-road", i.e. the main road in a village, should be four steps wide j the space between two dwellings shall con¬ sists of three steps or paces. The side roads shall be half a pace wide. The way to the sacrificial room shall be a pace wide. The dust-bin shall be a pace wide. The gutters on either side of the road shall be a pace wide. They made a lay¬ out and built houses afterwards. Thinking and recollecting again and again they
verses.hindi: + बनुश्चह्वान्तगंतग्रन्थो ग. पुस्तके नास्ति

verses.sanskrit: पश्यामि ह्यमरां कन्याम् अर्चयन्तीं महेश्वरम् । ततो ऽहं तां वरारोहामपृच्छं कमलेक्षणाम्
verses.transliteration: paśyāmi hyamarāṃ kanyām arcayantīṃ maheśvaram / tato 'haṃ tāṃ varārohāmapṛcchaṃ kamalekṣaṇām
verses.translation: The trees had branches going upwards and apreading They observed carefully how the branches had gone. They constructed the apartments in accordance with the growth of the branches (Sakhas). 1 Hence they had been called Salas. Thus Salas (apartments) became well known from branches; so also the abodes. Hence they are remembered as 'Salas'. Thus is explained their state of being Salas ( Sdlatva ). The mind is delighted in them. They delight the mind. Hence the houses, halls and mansions are duly termed as prdsadas.
verses.hindi: लवा: काछाः कलाश्चैच मुहर्ताः संधिराज्यहाः । अधमासाध्य मासाश्य अयनाब्द्युगानि च
verses.wordMeaning: The trees had branches going upwards and apreading They observed carefully how the branches had gone. They constructed the apartments in accordance with the growth of the branches (Sakhas). 1 Hence they had been called Salas.…
verses.commentary: Sense: The trees had branches going upwards and apreading They observed carefully how the branches had gone. They constructed the apartments in accordance with the growth of the branches (Sakhas). 1 Hence they had been called Salas.…

verses.sanskrit: का त्वमस्मिन्पुरे देवि वससे शिवमर्चती । ताश्चागताः स्त्रियः सर्वाः क्व गतास्ते गणेश्वराः
verses.transliteration: kā tvamasminpure devi vasase śivamarcatī / tāścāgatāḥ striyaḥ sarvāḥ kva gatāste gaṇeśvarāḥ
verses.translation: After warding off the Dvandvas (the pairs of mutual opposites, viz. heat and cold), they began to think of the means of their sustenance (such as agriculture). When the Kalpa-trees had perished along with the honey, they were over¬ whelmed by hunger and thirst and became bewildered and dejected. Thereafter, in the Treta age, a Siddhi (accomplishment) appeared before them. The means ofagriculture that could meet their ends came as they desired. 1 The waters showered (from the sky) which flowed downwards became srotas (river, stream). And waters flowing in ditches or excavated places are known as Nimnagas (down flowing).
verses.hindi: वक्‍त्नायस्य ब्राह्मणाः संप्रसूतास्तद्वक्षस्तः क्षत्रियाः पूर्व भागे । वैश्याश्वोवर्यिस्य पदूम्यां च शुद्धाः सर्वे चर्णा गात्रतः संप्रसूताः ।
verses.wordMeaning: After warding off the Dvandvas (the pairs of mutual opposites, viz. heat and cold), they began to think of the means of their sustenance (such as agriculture). When the Kalpa-trees had perished along with the honey,…
verses.commentary: Sense: After warding off the Dvandvas (the pairs of mutual opposites, viz. heat and cold), they began to think of the means of their sustenance (such as agriculture). When the Kalpa-trees had perished along with the honey,…

verses.sanskrit: नमो ऽस्तु ते महाभागे ब्रूहि पुण्ये महेश्वरि । तव प्रसादाद्विज्ञातुमेतदिच्छामि सुव्रते । दयां कृत्वा महादेवि कथयस्व ममानघे
verses.transliteration: namo 'stu te mahābhāge brūhi puṇye maheśvari / tava prasādādvijñātumetadicchāmi suvrate / dayāṃ kṛtvā mahādevi kathayasva mamānaghe
verses.translation: Thus in the second creation through rain, the rivers came into being. What little of water remained on the surface of the earth thereafter, became mixed with earth and grew into plants and herbs. Plants began to put forth flowers, fruits and roots. Fourteen kinds of trees and bushes which grew up in the villages and forests without ploughing or burning, put forth seasonal flowers and fruit. It was in the Treta age that vegetation manifested first and the medicinal plants appeared. The people in the Treta age maintained themselves on the products of agriculture. Then again all of them were overwhelmed with lust and greed as a result of unavoidable fate or due to the Treta age.
verses.hindi: नारायण: परोड्व्यक्तादण्डमव्यक्तसंभचम् । अण्डाउजल्षे पुनत्नह्मा लोकास्तेन रूताः स्वयम् ॥ एच: व कथितः पादः समासान्नतु विस्तरात्  अनेना55श्येन पादेन पुराणं संप्रकीतितम् ।
verses.wordMeaning: Thus in the second creation through rain, the rivers came into being. What little of water remained on the surface of the earth thereafter, became mixed with earth and grew into plants and herbs. Plants began to put forth flowers, fruits and roots.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Thus in the second creation through rain, the rivers came into being. What little of water remained on the surface of the earth thereafter, became mixed with earth and grew into plants and herbs. Plants began to put forth flowers, fruits and roots.…

verses.sanskrit: श्र्युवाच: विस्मृताहं कथं विप्र दृष्ट्वा कल्पे पुरातने । मा ते ऽभूत्स्मृतिविभ्रंशः सा चाहं कल्पवाहिनी
verses.transliteration: śryuvāca: vismṛtāhaṃ kathaṃ vipra dṛṣṭvā kalpe purātane / mā te 'bhūtsmṛtivibhraṃśaḥ sā cāhaṃ kalpavāhinī
verses.translation: Verses 124-137 show that in the Treta Age man developed agriculture and for division of labour the society was divided into different arnas (Classes). The credit of introducing Agriculture is given to Brahma. They then forcibly occupied the rivers, fields, moun¬ tains, trees, clusters and medicinal plants. While describing the Prdkrta Sarga, I have spoken about the accomplished souls. These were born as human beings according to Brahma's plan.
verses.hindi: इति महापुराणे वायु्रोक्ते प्रक्रियापादे सृश्टिकरणं नाम षष्ठोड्ष्यायः
verses.wordMeaning: Verses 124-137 show that in the Treta Age man developed agriculture and for division of labour the society was divided into different arnas (Classes). The credit of introducing Agriculture is given to Brahma. They then forcibly occupied the rivers, fields, moun¬ tains, trees,…

verses.sanskrit: नर्मदा नाम विख्याता रुद्रदेहाद् विनिःसृता । यास्ताः कन्यास्त्वया दृष्टा ह्यर्चयन्त्यो महेश्वरम्
verses.transliteration: narmadā nāma vikhyātā rudradehād viniḥsṛtā / yāstāḥ kanyāstvayā dṛṣṭā hyarcayantyo maheśvaram
verses.translation: They were quiescent, powerful, active and distressed. Then, thus functioning they were born again in the Treta age. Urged by the auspicious and inauspicious activities of the previous births they were born as Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas, Sudras and Dasyus. Those who were truthful, non-violent, devoid of greed and self-controlled lived therein. There were others de¬ ficient in brilliance, who served these in return for the gifts they received from them. Thus there was mutual dependence. Due to their fault, the medicinal plants disappeared while they were looking on helplessly. They vanished as sand particles in handfuls. The earth, due to the power of the Yuga, swallowed the fourteen kinds of plants both in villages and forests—the plants which bore fruit through flowers and flowers with leaves.
verses.hindi: प्रनत्तिस्लंध्यिव्की से ल्वस्त्

verses.sanskrit: याभिस्त्विह समानीतः पक्षिराजसमन्विताः । दिशस्ता विद्धि सर्वेशाः सर्वास्त्वं मुनिसत्तम
verses.transliteration: yābhistviha samānītaḥ pakṣirājasamanvitāḥ / diśastā viddhi sarveśāḥ sarvāstvaṃ munisattama
verses.translation: When these were destroyed, the people became be¬ wildered. On being overwhelmed by hunger they approached Lord Svayambhu, Prajapati. (It was) at the beginning of Treta Yuga. The self-born lord Brahma, knowing that they wanted the means of sustenance, considered what was proper by observing directly. Realising that the medicinal plants were swallowed by the earth he milked them out again (from the earth). 1 Making mount Meru as the calf, he milked the earth. The earth-cow yielded the seeds on its surface.
verses.hindi: कला, मुह॒त्त, सन्धि, रात्रि, दिन, पक्ष, मास, अयन, वर्ष, युग, ये सभी स्थानाभिमानी और स्थान के नाम से प्रसिद्ध हैं ।9३-७६। जिसके मुख से ब्राह्मण, वक्ष:स्थल से क्षत्रिय, ऊर से वेश्य और जिसके पैर से शूद्र, इस प्रकार जिसके शरीर से सब वर्ण उत्पन्न हुए वे नारायण अव्यक्त से परे हैं। उत्त अव्यक्त से अण्ड की उत्पत्ति हुई और अण्ड से ब्रह्मा उत्पन्न हुए. जिन्होंने स्वयं लोकों को उत्पन्न किया । यह प्रक्रियापाद आप लोगों से संक्षेप में

verses.sanskrit: तिर्यक्पक्षिस्वरूपेण महायोगी महेश्वरः । एभिः शिवपुराद्विप्र आनीतः स महेश्वरः
verses.transliteration: tiryakpakṣisvarūpeṇa mahāyogī maheśvaraḥ / ebhiḥ śivapurādvipra ānītaḥ sa maheśvaraḥ
verses.translation: This is the Puranic development of the ancient Vcdic concept of 25 Vararuci became the milker and the science of Dramaturgy {Mtya Veda) was the milk. The seeds grew into wild and cultivated plants yielding ripe fruits. They comprised seventeen classes. Rice, barley, wheat, the minute gingelly seeds, the Priyangus, Udams,Kdrusas, Tinakas (different kinds of pulse etc.), black gram, green gram, Masuras (a pulse), Mspdvas, horse grams, Adhakis (the pulse cajanus Indicus spreng ), and other grams. These are the seventeen varieties of rural medicinal plants ( Grdmya osadhi ). Then there are fourteen kinds of plants used in sacrifices.
verses.hindi: कहा गया है। इस प्रकार इस आद्य पांद के द्वारा यह पुराण कहा गया है
verses.wordMeaning: This is the Puranic development of the ancient Vcdic concept of 25 Vararuci became the milker and the science of Dramaturgy {Mtya Veda) was the milk. The seeds grew into wild and cultivated plants yielding ripe fruits. They comprised seventeen classes. Rice, barley, wheat,…

The seeds grew into wild and cultivated plants yielding ripe fruits. They comprised seventeen classes. Rice, barley, wheat,…

verses.sanskrit: सैष देवो महादेवो लिङ्गमूर्तिर्व्यवस्थितः । अर्च्यते ब्रह्मविष्ण्विन्द्रैः सुरासुरजगद्गुरुः
verses.transliteration: saiṣa devo mahādevo liṅgamūrtirvyavasthitaḥ / arcyate brahmaviṣṇvindraiḥ surāsurajagadguruḥ
verses.translation: They are: rice, barley, black gram, wheat, anus (panicum Miliaccum), gingelly seeds, Priyahgu the seventh among them and horse-gram the eighth. Syajnakas (a variety of rice), Nivaras (another variety of rice), Jariilas (wild sesamum), Gavedhukas, Kurudndas (a kind of barley), Venuyavas (bamboo seeds) and Markatakas (a species of grain) —these are the fourteen varieties of wild and cultivated plants. They were originally produced in the beginning of the Treta age. All these medicinal plants, trees, hedges, creepers and grasses grew in villages and forests without the fields being ploughed.
verses.hindi: श्री वायुपुराण का सृष्टि-प्रमाणनामक छठाँ अध्याय समाप्त
verses.wordMeaning: They are: rice, barley, black gram, wheat, anus (panicum Miliaccum), gingelly seeds, Priyahgu the seventh among them and horse-gram the eighth. Syajnakas (a variety of rice), Nivaras (another variety of rice), Jariilas (wild sesamum), Gavedhukas, Kurudndas (a kind of barley),…
verses.commentary: Sense: They are: rice, barley, black gram, wheat, anus (panicum Miliaccum), gingelly seeds, Priyahgu the seventh among them and horse-gram the eighth. Syajnakas (a variety of rice), Nivaras (another variety of rice), Jariilas (wild sesamum), Gavedhukas, Kurudndas (a kind of barley),…

verses.sanskrit: लयमायाति यस्माद्धि जगत्सर्वं चराचरम् । तेन लिङ्गमिति प्रोक्तं पुराणज्ञैर् महर्षिभिः
verses.transliteration: layamāyāti yasmāddhi jagatsarvaṃ carācaram / tena liṅgamiti proktaṃ purāṇajñair maharṣibhiḥ
verses.translation: The seeds that were milked from the earth at the outset by the self-born god Brahma grew into various fruits and flowers. They grew into plants yielding seasonal flowers and fruits. When they let go (the seasonal product once) they did not grow again. The self-born Brahma then devised for the livelihood of the people by means of agriculture. From that time onwards the plants began to grow on being (ploughed and) cultivated. Thus when agriculture came into vogue the self-born lord established conventions for their mutual hel Those who were masters (powerful ones) had (to follow) prescribed conventions and established them (as) Ksattriyas for the protection of others.
verses.hindi: सूतजी बोलें--यह पहला प्रक्रिया पाद कह दिया गया, जिसको सुनकर सनातन काश्यपेय प्रसन्न
verses.wordMeaning: The seeds that were milked from the earth at the outset by the self-born god Brahma grew into various fruits and flowers. They grew into plants yielding seasonal flowers and fruits. When they let go (the seasonal product once) they did not grow again.…
verses.commentary: Sense: The seeds that were milked from the earth at the outset by the self-born god Brahma grew into various fruits and flowers. They grew into plants yielding seasonal flowers and fruits. When they let go (the seasonal product once) they did not grow again.…

verses.sanskrit: तेन देवगणाः सर्वे संक्षिप्ता मायया पुरा । प्रलीनाश्चैव लोकेश न दृश्यन्ते हि सांप्रतम्
verses.transliteration: tena devagaṇāḥ sarve saṃkṣiptā māyayā purā / pralīnāścaiva lokeśa na dṛśyante hi sāṃpratam
verses.translation: Verses 154-164 show the evolution of Varnas or Classes in an agrarian society and the duties of each class. Verses 166-168 state the region to which Ptous members of these classes go. Those who worship (or respect or obey) those (Ksatriyas) are free from fear. Those who averred that Brahman is the truth and spoke according to facts (the truth) are Brahmanas. Those who were weak were assigned the duty of Vaisyas. They became the cultivators of the soil. Formerly they used to destroy things in the earth. They are called Vaisyas as they maintain their livelihood by soil and cultivation.
verses.hindi: +- इदं नास्ति क. पुस्तके ।
verses.wordMeaning: Verses 154-164 show the evolution of Varnas or Classes in an agrarian society and the duties of each class. Verses 166-168 state the region to which Ptous members of these classes go. Those who worship (or respect or obey) those (Ksatriyas) are free from fear.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Verses 154-164 show the evolution of Varnas or Classes in an agrarian society and the duties of each class. Verses 166-168 state the region to which Ptous members of these classes go. Those who worship (or respect or obey) those (Ksatriyas) are free from fear.…
