verses.transliteration: kīdṛśaṃ darśanaṃ tasyāḥ phalaṃ sparśe 'thavā vibho / snāne jāpye 'thavā dāna upavāse tathā mune
verses.translation: Pavamana is the fire which is obtained after churning (the Arani). Suci is remembered as the solar fire. Pavaka is the fire originating from the lightning. These are their (specific) abodes.
verses.hindi: एवं तत्र शयानेन विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना । आत्मारामेण क्रौडार्थ सुष्ट नाभ्यां तु पडूजम् १२ शतयोजनविस्तीर्ण तदणादित्यवर्चसम् । वज्ञ्रदण्ड महोत्सेधं लीलया प्रभविष्णुना १३ तस्येवं क्ीडमानस्य समीप देवमीदुषः । हेमब्रह्माण्डजो ब्रह्म रक्‍्सवर्णो ह्यतीन्द्रियः ॥ द
verses.wordMeaning: Pavamana is the fire which is obtained after churning (the Arani). Suci is remembered as the solar fire. Pavaka is the fire originating from the lightning. These are their (specific) abodes.
verses.commentary: Sense: Pavamana is the fire which is obtained after churning (the Arani). Suci is remembered as the solar fire. Pavaka is the fire originating from the lightning. These are their (specific) abodes.

verses.sanskrit: कथयस्व महाभाग कावेरीसङ्गमे फलम् । धर्मः श्रुतो ऽथ दृष्टो वा कथितो वा कृतो ऽपि वा
verses.transliteration: kathayasva mahābhāga kāverīsaṅgame phalam / dharmaḥ śruto 'tha dṛṣṭo vā kathito vā kṛto 'pi vā
verses.translation: In this chapter fortyninc ritualistic functions of Fire are represen¬ ted as so many Fire-gods and the correlation of these is arranged in a genealogical form. In fact it is a Vedic conception presented here in a popular form. Probably this formed a part of the original Purana as it is found in the Mblu Vana chs. 217-222, £</. P. I. 2.12, Ml. , VP. I.
verses.hindi: श्रिया युक्तेन नव्येन सुप्रभेण सुगन्धिना । त॑ क्रीडमानं पद्मेन दृष्ट्वा ब्रह्मा तु भेजिवान
verses.wordMeaning: In this chapter fortyninc ritualistic functions of Fire are represen¬ ted as so many Fire-gods and the correlation of these is arranged in a genealogical form. In fact it is a Vedic conception presented here in a popular form.…
verses.commentary: Sense: In this chapter fortyninc ritualistic functions of Fire are represen¬ ted as so many Fire-gods and the correlation of these is arranged in a genealogical form. In fact it is a Vedic conception presented here in a popular form.…

verses.sanskrit: अनुमोदितो वा विप्रेन्द्र पुनातीति श्रुतं मया । यथा धर्मप्रसङ्गे तु मुने धर्मो ऽपि जायते
verses.transliteration: anumodito vā viprendra punātīti śrutaṃ mayā / yathā dharmaprasaṅge tu mune dharmo 'pi jāyate
verses.translation: to mention a few. V. S. Agrawal regards Va. P. account as the original [Ml. P.: A study, ). Pargiter did not know the Vedic back¬ ground when he condemned it as 'imaginary genealogy' (AIHT, ) for it is no 'genealogy' at all.
verses.hindi: स विस्मयमथा55गम्य शस्यसंपुर्णया गिरा । प्रोवाच को भवाज्शेते आश्षितो मध्यमस्भसाम्
verses.wordMeaning: to mention a few. V. S. Agrawal regards Va. P. account as the original [Ml. P.: A study, ). Pargiter did not know the Vedic back¬ ground when he condemned it as 'imaginary genealogy' (AIHT, ) for it is no 'genealogy' at all.
verses.commentary: Sense: to mention a few. V. S. Agrawal regards Va. P. account as the original [Ml. P.: A study, ). Pargiter did not know the Vedic back¬ ground when he condemned it as 'imaginary genealogy' (AIHT, ) for it is no 'genealogy' at all.

verses.sanskrit: स्वर्गश्च नरकश्चैव इत्येवं वैदिकी श्रुतिः
verses.transliteration: svargaśca narakaścaiva ityevaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ
verses.translation: The relations of the following fires will be clear from the following genealogical table:
verses.hindi: करते हैं। यह जो सप्तम कल्प बीत गया है, उसे हमने आप लोगों को बताया है। इस कल्पावशेष में सातों सागर मिलकर एक हो जाते हैं। घोर अन्धकार छा जाता है। इस एक समुद्र में कहीं भी विभाग नहीं रहता है ।७-८। उस एका्णव में शद्धु-चक्र-्गदा धारण करनेवाले मेघतुल्य, कमलनयन, किरीटधारौ, श्रीपति, नारायण के मुख से उत्पन्न, अष्टम पुरुषोत्तम, अष्टबाहु, विशालवक्ष, लोकसमूह के उत्पत्तिस्थान
verses.wordMeaning: The relations of the following fires will be clear from the following genealogical table:
verses.commentary: Sense: The relations of the following fires will be clear from the following genealogical table:

verses.sanskrit: श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: साधु साधु महाभाग यत्पृष्टो ऽहं त्वयाधुना । शृणुष्वैकमना भूत्वा कावेरीफलम् उत्तमम्
verses.transliteration: śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: sādhu sādhu mahābhāga yatpṛṣṭo 'haṃ tvayādhunā / śṛṇuṣvaikamanā bhūtvā kāverīphalam uttamam
verses.translation: Atharvan shall be known as Bhrgu and Angiras as the son of Atharvan. Hence it is that the worldly fire Dadhyan was Atharvan's son.
verses.hindi: योगात्मा हरि माया द्वारा किसी अचिन्त्य योग को ग्रहण करके महान् नागराज के सहस्न फणों से युक्त
verses.wordMeaning: Atharvan shall be known as Bhrgu and Angiras as the son of Atharvan. Hence it is that the worldly fire Dadhyan was Atharvan's son.
verses.commentary: Sense: Atharvan shall be known as Bhrgu and Angiras as the son of Atharvan. Hence it is that the worldly fire Dadhyan was Atharvan's son.

verses.sanskrit: अस्ति यक्षो महासत्त्वः कुबेरोनाम विश्रुतः । सो ऽपि तीर्थप्रभावेन राजन्यक्षाधिपो ऽभवत्
verses.transliteration: asti yakṣo mahāsattvaḥ kuberonāma viśrutaḥ / so 'pi tīrthaprabhāvena rājanyakṣādhipo 'bhavat
verses.translation: The group from Vaidyuta fire is arranged as follows: Vaidyuta (Fire)
verses.hindi: अत्युन्नत अनृपम कान्ति वाले और सुबर्ण की तरह चमकीले शरीर रूपी पये डू को बिछा कर सोते हैं
verses.wordMeaning: The group from Vaidyuta fire is arranged as follows: Vaidyuta (Fire)
verses.commentary: Sense: The group from Vaidyuta fire is arranged as follows: Vaidyuta (Fire)

verses.sanskrit: तच्छृणुष्व विधानेन भक्त्या परमया नृप । सिद्धिं प्राप्तो महाभाग कावेरीसङ्गमेन तु
verses.transliteration: tacchṛṇuṣva vidhānena bhaktyā paramayā nṛpa / siddhiṃ prāpto mahābhāga kāverīsaṅgamena tu
verses.translation: This is a reference to RVvi. 16. 12 where Agni is said to have been churned out of Puskara. Thus Puskara = Waters ( Apo vai Pufkaram Sal. Br. VI. 4. 2.2). Sat. Br.'VII. 4.1-13 further explains that when Indra became frightened after killing Vrtra, he resorted to waters. They (waters) offered their sap ( apdm rasaft) to him and created a city {pur) f° r him. Hence water came to be called Puskara ( asmai puram akurvans tasm&d pufkaram ha vai tat pufkaram dcaksate par ok jam.
verses.hindi: आत्माराम प्रभविष्ण ने सोते हये ही कौतुकवबश नाभिदेश से एक कमल को उत्पन्न किया । उस कमल का विस्तार सौ योजन का था और वह तरुण सूर्य की तरह कान्तिमान् था। वह व की तरह दण्डवाला अत्युन्नत कमल प्रभविष्ण की लीला से उत्पन्न हुआ था। उस कमल से विष्णु क्रीड़ा कर रहे थे कि उनके समीप स्वर्णमय ब्रह्माण्ड से उत्पन्न अतएव स्वणंवर्ण, अतीन्द्रिय, विशालाक्ष, चतुर्मखी ब्रह्मा इच्छानुसर उन्हें
verses.wordMeaning: This is a reference to RVvi. 16. 12 where Agni is said to have been churned out of Puskara. Thus Puskara = Waters ( Apo vai Pufkaram Sal. Br. VI. 4. 2.2). Sat. Br.'VII. 4.1-13 further explains that when Indra became frightened after killing Vrtra, he resorted to waters.…
verses.commentary: Sense: This is a reference to RVvi. 16. 12 where Agni is said to have been churned out of Puskara. Thus Puskara = Waters ( Apo vai Pufkaram Sal. Br. VI. 4. 2.2). Sat. Br.'VII. 4.1-13 further explains that when Indra became frightened after killing Vrtra, he resorted to waters.…

verses.sanskrit: कावेर्या नर्मदायास् तु सङ्गमे लोकविश्रुते । तत्र स्नात्वा शुचिर्भूत्वा कुबेरः सत्यविक्रमः
verses.transliteration: kāveryā narmadāyās tu saṅgame lokaviśrute / tatra snātvā śucirbhūtvā kuberaḥ satyavikramaḥ
verses.translation: Dadhyan is etymologically related with dadhi which according to Sat. Br. 7.5-1 is a symbol of the earth or Matter ( dadhi haivasya lokasya rupam ). Probably it is related to Dak?iriagni.
verses.hindi: ढूँढ़ते हुये वहाँ आ गये । श्रीसम्पन्न, प्रभावान्,. सुगन्धित नवीन पदुम से विष्ण की खेलते हुये देखकर ब्रह्मा उनके और समीप पहुँच गये । वहाँ जाने पर ब्रह्मा विस्मित हो गये। वे गम्भीर स्वर में बोले-- “आप कौन हैं जो इस जल के बीच सो रहे हैं ?”१२-१६। ब्रह्मा के उस शुभ वचन को सुनकर ब्रह्मज्न अच्युत
verses.wordMeaning: Dadhyan is etymologically related with dadhi which according to Sat. Br. 7.5-1 is a symbol of the earth or Matter ( dadhi haivasya lokasya rupam ). Probably it is related to Dak?iriagni.
verses.commentary: Sense: Dadhyan is etymologically related with dadhi which according to Sat. Br. 7.5-1 is a symbol of the earth or Matter ( dadhi haivasya lokasya rupam ). Probably it is related to Dak?iriagni.

verses.sanskrit: विधिवन्नियमं कृत्वा शास्त्रयुक्त्या नरोत्तम । आराधयन्महादेवमेकचित्तः सनातनम्
verses.transliteration: vidhivanniyamaṃ kṛtvā śāstrayuktyā narottama / ārādhayanmahādevamekacittaḥ sanātanam
verses.translation: Now the fire Pavamana 1 which is remembered by the wise as Nirmanlha (one generated by churning) should be known as Garhapatya fire from whom were born two sons.
verses.hindi: अथ तस्याच्युतः श्रत्वा ब्रह्मज्स्तु शुभं बचः । उदतिष्ठत पयड्ूाद्विस्मयोत्फुलललोचनः
verses.wordMeaning: Now the fire Pavamana 1 which is remembered by the wise as Nirmanlha (one generated by churning) should be known as Garhapatya fire from whom were born two sons.
verses.commentary: Sense: Now the fire Pavamana 1 which is remembered by the wise as Nirmanlha (one generated by churning) should be known as Garhapatya fire from whom were born two sons.

verses.sanskrit: एकाहारो वसन्मासं तथा षष्ठाह्नकालिकः । पक्षोपवासी न्यवसत् कंचित् कालं नृपोत्तम
verses.transliteration: ekāhāro vasanmāsaṃ tathā ṣaṣṭhāhnakālikaḥ / pakṣopavāsī nyavasat kaṃcit kālaṃ nṛpottama
verses.translation: Sabhya and Avasalliya were the two sons of the fire Samsya. Samsya Havyavahana which is known as the Ahavaniya fire by the Brahmanas loved sixteen rivers. 2
verses.hindi: तमेवमुक्त्वा भगवान्विष्णु: पुनरथाब्रवीत् । कस्त्वं खलु समायातः समीप भगवान्कुतः॥॥
verses.wordMeaning: Sabhya and Avasalliya were the two sons of the fire Samsya. Samsya Havyavahana which is known as the Ahavaniya fire by the Brahmanas loved sixteen rivers. 2
verses.commentary: Sense: Sabhya and Avasalliya were the two sons of the fire Samsya. Samsya Havyavahana which is known as the Ahavaniya fire by the Brahmanas loved sixteen rivers. 2

verses.sanskrit: मूलशाकफलैश्चान्यं कालं नयति बुद्धिमान् । किंचित्कालं वसंस्तत्र तीर्थे शैवालभोजनः
verses.transliteration: mūlaśākaphalaiścānyaṃ kālaṃ nayati buddhimān / kiṃcitkālaṃ vasaṃstatra tīrthe śaivālabhojanaḥ
verses.translation: They were Kaverl, KrsnavenI, Narmada, Yamuna, Godavari, Viiasta, Candrabhaga, Iravatl, Vipasa, KausikI, Satadru, Sarayu, Sita, Sarasvatl, Hradini and Pavanl. 3
verses.hindi: यथा भवांस्तथा चाह॒मादिकर्ता प्रजापति: । नारायणसमाख्यातः सर्व वे मयि तिष्ठति ..
verses.wordMeaning: They were Kaverl, KrsnavenI, Narmada, Yamuna, Godavari, Viiasta, Candrabhaga, Iravatl, Vipasa, KausikI, Satadru, Sarayu, Sita, Sarasvatl, Hradini and Pavanl. 3
verses.commentary: Sense: They were Kaverl, KrsnavenI, Narmada, Yamuna, Godavari, Viiasta, Candrabhaga, Iravatl, Vipasa, KausikI, Satadru, Sarayu, Sita, Sarasvatl, Hradini and Pavanl. 3

verses.sanskrit: पराकेणानयत्कालं कृच्छ्रेणापि च मानद । चान्द्रायणेन चाप्यन्यमन्यं वाय्वम्बुभोजनः
verses.transliteration: parākeṇānayatkālaṃ kṛcchreṇāpi ca mānada / cāndrāyaṇena cāpyanyamanyaṃ vāyvambubhojanaḥ
verses.translation: He divided himself into separate sixteen parts among them and deposited himself in those dhisnis.
verses.hindi: सविस्मयं पर श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मणा लोककतु णा। सोनुज्ञातो भगवता बेकुप्ठो विश्वसंभव: १२२ कोौतृहलान्महायोगी प्रविष्ठो ब्रह्मणो मुखम्। इमानष्टादश द्वोपान्सससुद्रान्सपवंतान्
verses.wordMeaning: He divided himself into separate sixteen parts among them and deposited himself in those dhisnis.
verses.commentary: Sense: He divided himself into separate sixteen parts among them and deposited himself in those dhisnis.

verses.sanskrit: एवं तत्र नरश्रेष्ठ कामरागविवर्जितः । स्थितो वर्षशतं साग्रं कर्षयन्स्वं तथा वपुः
verses.transliteration: evaṃ tatra naraśreṣṭha kāmarāgavivarjitaḥ / sthito varṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ karṣayansvaṃ tathā vapuḥ
verses.translation: Dhisnis move about in the sky. Those that are born in them are called Dhisiiis. They are proclaimed as Dhisnis as they are born in Dhisnis.
verses.hindi: प्रविश्व स महातेजाश्चातुरवंण्येंसमाकुलान् । ब्रह्मादिस्तस्वपयन्तान्सप्तलोकान्सनातनान्
verses.wordMeaning: Dhisnis move about in the sky. Those that are born in them are called Dhisiiis. They are proclaimed as Dhisnis as they are born in Dhisnis.
verses.commentary: Sense: Dhisnis move about in the sky. Those that are born in them are called Dhisiiis. They are proclaimed as Dhisnis as they are born in Dhisnis.

verses.sanskrit: ततो वर्षशतस्यान्ते देवदेवो महेश्वरः । तुष्टस्तु परया भक्त्या तमुवाच हसन्निव
verses.transliteration: tato varṣaśatasyānte devadevo maheśvaraḥ / tuṣṭastu parayā bhaktyā tamuvāca hasanniva
verses.translation: Hence these sons of the rivers were born in Dhisnis. Out of them some fires are Viharaniya (portable) and some
verses.hindi: ब्रह्मणस्तुदरे दृष्ट्वा सर्वान्विष्णुमंहायशा: । अहोष्स्य तपसो बीरय॑ पुनः पुनरभाषत
verses.wordMeaning: Hence these sons of the rivers were born in Dhisnis. Out of them some fires are Viharaniya (portable) and some
verses.commentary: Sense: Hence these sons of the rivers were born in Dhisnis. Out of them some fires are Viharaniya (portable) and some

verses.sanskrit: भोभो यक्ष महासत्त्व वरं वरय सुव्रत । परितुष्टो ऽस्मि ते भक्त्या तव दास्ये यथेप्सितम्
verses.transliteration: bhobho yakṣa mahāsattva varaṃ varaya suvrata / parituṣṭo 'smi te bhaktyā tava dāsye yathepsitam
verses.translation: This is a poetic way of describing the spread of 5 ajrni-cu the geographical area from Central Asia from the river Sita or the (AGP 100-102) down to the Kaveri in South India. Modern po i
verses.hindi: पर्यटन्विविधाँललोकान्विष्णर्नानाविधाश्रमान् । ततो वर्षसहस्रान्ते नान्‍तं हि ददुशे तदा
verses.wordMeaning: This is a poetic way of describing the spread of 5 ajrni-cu the geographical area from Central Asia from the river Sita or the (AGP 100-102) down to the Kaveri in South India. Modern po i
verses.commentary: Sense: This is a poetic way of describing the spread of 5 ajrni-cu the geographical area from Central Asia from the river Sita or the (AGP 100-102) down to the Kaveri in South India. Modern po i

verses.sanskrit: यक्ष उवाच: यदि तुष्टो ऽसि देवेश उमया सह शङ्कर । अद्यप्रभृति सर्वेषां यक्षाणामधिपो भवे
verses.transliteration: yakṣa uvāca: yadi tuṣṭo 'si deveśa umayā saha śaṅkara / adyaprabhṛti sarveṣāṃ yakṣāṇāmadhipo bhave
verses.translation: The following are the modern names m the in vv. 13-14: K r?na-Veni (the Krishna), Vnasta
verses.hindi: 'तदाषस्य वक्‍त्रान्निष्क्रम्य पन्नगेरद्रादिकितनः । अजातशत्रगर्भगवान्पितामहमथान्रवीत् १२७ भगवदनज्नादिमध्यं व अन्तः कालदिशे न च। नाहमस्त॑ प्रपश्यामि हा दरस्य तवानघ २८
verses.wordMeaning: The following are the modern names m the in vv. 13-14: K r?na-Veni (the Krishna), Vnasta
verses.commentary: Sense: The following are the modern names m the in vv. 13-14: K r?na-Veni (the Krishna), Vnasta

verses.sanskrit: अक्षयश्चाव्ययश्चैव तव भक्तिपुरःसरः । धर्मे मतिं च मे नित्यं ददस्व परमेश्वर
verses.transliteration: akṣayaścāvyayaścaiva tava bhaktipuraḥsaraḥ / dharme matiṃ ca me nityaṃ dadasva parameśvara
verses.translation: Rtu, Pravahana and Agnidhra arc the Dhisnis in front. Otliers are ordained in accordance with their seats in the order of sacrifice on the day when Soma juice is extracted.
verses.hindi: विस्मय से बड़ी-बड़ी आँखें तचा कर पलंग पर से उठ बैठे । उन्होंने उत्तर दिया--'जो कार्य, कारण, अन्तरिक्ष, भूमि, स्वर्ग आदि हैं, उनका प्रभु मैं हूँ । मै ही परम पद हूं ।” इस तरह कहकर भगवान् विष्णु ने फिर कहा--हे भगवन् ! आप कौन हैं ? कहाँ से आप हमारे समीप आये हैं? फिर कहाँ जायेंगे ? आपका आश्रम कहाँ है ? विश्वमूर्ति धारण करनेवाले आप कौन हैं? हम आपका कौन सा कारयय करें?”
verses.wordMeaning: Rtu, Pravahana and Agnidhra arc the Dhisnis in front. Otliers are ordained in accordance with their seats in the order of sacrifice on the day when Soma juice is extracted.
verses.commentary: Sense: Rtu, Pravahana and Agnidhra arc the Dhisnis in front. Otliers are ordained in accordance with their seats in the order of sacrifice on the day when Soma juice is extracted.

verses.sanskrit: ईश्वर उवाच: यत्त्वया प्रार्थितं सर्वं फलं धर्मस्य तत्तथा । इत्येवमुक्त्वा तं तत्र जगामादर्शनं हरः
verses.transliteration: īśvara uvāca: yattvayā prārthitaṃ sarvaṃ phalaṃ dharmasya tattathā / ityevamuktvā taṃ tatra jagāmādarśanaṃ haraḥ
verses.translation: Listen to the order of fires, the names of which are not mentioned before. 2 3 4 5 6 The fire Samrat is the fire stationed on the second Uttara-vedi.
verses.hindi: वेकुण्ठविहारी विष्णु के इस प्रकार कहने के बाद पितामह ने कहा ।१७-२०। “जिस तरह आप हैं उसी तरह हम भी आदिकर्ता प्रजापति हैं। मेरा नाम नारायण है और मुझमें ही सब प्रतिष्ठित है” ।३१। लोक- कर्ता ब्रह्मा से इस प्रकार सुनकर विश्वसम्भव वंकुण्ठविहारी भगवनू अत्यन्त विस्मित हो गये और उनसे आज्ञा लेकर महायोगी विष्णु ब्रह्मा के मुख में बंठ गये । महायशस्वी और तेजस्वी विष्णु ने वहाँ प्रवेश करके
verses.wordMeaning: Listen to the order of fires, the names of which are not mentioned before. 2 3 4 5 6 The fire Samrat is the fire stationed on the second Uttara-vedi.
verses.commentary: Sense: Listen to the order of fires, the names of which are not mentioned before. 2 3 4 5 6 The fire Samrat is the fire stationed on the second Uttara-vedi.

verses.sanskrit: सो ऽपि स्नात्वा विधानेन संतर्प्य पितृदेवताः । आमन्त्रयित्वा तत्तीर्थं कृतार्थश्च गृहं ययौ
verses.transliteration: so 'pi snātvā vidhānena saṃtarpya pitṛdevatāḥ / āmantrayitvā tattīrthaṃ kṛtārthaśca gṛhaṃ yayau
verses.translation: The Samrat fire is proclaimed as eight (fold in form?). Brahmanas worship them. Beneath it is the second Parsad lire.
verses.hindi: देखा कि सागर पव॑तों के साथ आठो द्वीप और ब्रह्मा से लेकर स्तम्बपयंन्त चतुराश्रम में विभक्त सातों सनातन लोक यहाँ विद्यमान हैं ।२२-२४ यह देखकर वे आप ही आप बोलने लगे--अहो  इनकी तपस्या का प्रभाव अद्भुत है! ।२५। विष्णु वहाँ नाना प्रकार के आश्रमों और लोकों में घूमने लगे; किन्तु हजार वर्ष के बीत जाने पर भी उन्होंने अन्त नहीं देखा । तब अजातकत्रु गंरुड़ध्वज भगवान् ब्रह्मा के मुँह से निकल
verses.wordMeaning: The Samrat fire is proclaimed as eight (fold in form?). Brahmanas worship them. Beneath it is the second Parsad lire.
verses.commentary: Sense: The Samrat fire is proclaimed as eight (fold in form?). Brahmanas worship them. Beneath it is the second Parsad lire.

verses.sanskrit: पूजितस्तत्र यक्षैस्तु सो ऽभिषिक्तो विधानतः । चकार विपुलं तत्र राज्यमीप्सितमुत्तमम्
verses.transliteration: pūjitastatra yakṣaistu so 'bhiṣikto vidhānataḥ / cakāra vipulaṃ tatra rājyamīpsitamuttamam
verses.translation: A fire having no association with the celestial or the sacrificial fires has an abode in the cremation ground. The terrestrial fire of the ocean is said to abide in Brahma's region. The lustrous fire Rtudhama lives in the Uduriibara wood. (Line
verses.hindi: कर बोले---'हे भगवन् ! है निष्पाप ! आपके उदर का आदि अन्त, मध्य, नहीं, काल, दिशा और अन्त
verses.wordMeaning: A fire having no association with the celestial or the sacrificial fires has an abode in the cremation ground. The terrestrial fire of the ocean is said to abide in Brahma's region. The lustrous fire Rtudhama lives in the Uduriibara wood. (Line
verses.commentary: Sense: A fire having no association with the celestial or the sacrificial fires has an abode in the cremation ground. The terrestrial fire of the ocean is said to abide in Brahma's region. The lustrous fire Rtudhama lives in the Uduriibara wood. (Line

verses.sanskrit: तत्र चान्ये सुराः सिद्धा यक्षगन्धर्वकिंनराः । गणाश्चाप्सरसां तत्र ऋषयश्च तथानघ
verses.transliteration: tatra cānye surāḥ siddhā yakṣagandharvakiṃnarāḥ / gaṇāścāpsarasāṃ tatra ṛṣayaśca tathānagha
verses.translation: The author classifies Dhisnya fires into (1) Viharapiya and (2) Upastheya. The Dhifpya was a side-altar of a heap of earth covered with sand. Fire was placed on the altar. In soma sacrifices, these fires were placed between the altar ( Vedi ) of the Srauta Yajna and the Uttara-Vedi meant for soma sacrifice. The designation Upastheya is given to these fires as they were to he approached at their fixed places on the Uttara Vedi. The Viharapiya fires were so called as they could be taken to any spot con¬ sidered necessary on the day of the Yajna.
verses.hindi: प्रबिश्य लोकान्पश्येताननौपस्यान्द्रिजोत्तम
verses.wordMeaning: The author classifies Dhisnya fires into (1) Viharapiya and (2) Upastheya. The Dhifpya was a side-altar of a heap of earth covered with sand. Fire was placed on the altar. In soma sacrifices,…
verses.commentary: Sense: The author classifies Dhisnya fires into (1) Viharapiya and (2) Upastheya. The Dhifpya was a side-altar of a heap of earth covered with sand. Fire was placed on the altar. In soma sacrifices,…

verses.sanskrit: कावेरीसङ्गमं तेन सर्वपापहरं विदुः । स्वर्गाणामपि सर्वेषां द्वारमेतद्युधिष्ठिर
verses.transliteration: kāverīsaṅgamaṃ tena sarvapāpaharaṃ viduḥ / svargāṇāmapi sarveṣāṃ dvārametadyudhiṣṭhira
verses.translation: Verses 19-24 give the list of Upastheya fires as follows:
verses.hindi: तानेब लोकान्गर्भस्थः पश्यन्सोडचिन्त्यविक्र मः । पर्यटित्वा5डदिदेवस्थ ददर्शान्त न वे हरे: ,..
verses.wordMeaning: Verses 19-24 give the list of Upastheya fires as follows:
verses.commentary: Sense: Verses 19-24 give the list of Upastheya fires as follows:

verses.sanskrit: ते धन्यास्ते महात्मानस्तेषां जन्म सुजीवितम् । कावेरीसङ्गमे स्नात्वा यैर्दत्तं हि तिलोदकम्
verses.transliteration: te dhanyāste mahātmānasteṣāṃ janma sujīvitam / kāverīsaṅgame snātvā yairdattaṃ hi tilodakam
verses.translation: Samrdd agni also called Ktfdnu.
verses.hindi: ज्ञात्वा5घगर्मं तस्य पितामहस्य द्वाराणि सर्वाणि विधाय विष्णु:
verses.wordMeaning: Samrdd agni also called Ktfdnu.
verses.commentary: Sense: Samrdd agni also called Ktfdnu.

verses.sanskrit: दश पूर्वे परे तात मातृतः पितृतस्तथा । पितरः पितामहास्तेन उद्धृता नरकार्णवात्
verses.transliteration: daśa pūrve pare tāta mātṛtaḥ pitṛtastathā / pitaraḥ pitāmahāstena uddhṛtā narakārṇavāt
verses.translation: Parsad (but Mt. P. names it Parjanya) [ Mt. P. mentions Samuhya fires but our text omits it].
verses.hindi: पद्मसुत्रानुमागंण ह्ानुगम्य पितामहः । उज्जहारा5ध्त्मनो रूप पुष्कराच्चतुरानन: ॥।
verses.wordMeaning: Parsad (but Mt. P. names it Parjanya) [ Mt. P. mentions Samuhya fires but our text omits it].
verses.commentary: Sense: Parsad (but Mt. P. names it Parjanya) [ Mt. P. mentions Samuhya fires but our text omits it].

verses.sanskrit: तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन तत्र स्नायीत मानवः । अर्चयेदीश्वरं देवं यदीच्छेच्छाश्वतीं गतिम्
verses.transliteration: tasmātsarvaprayatnena tatra snāyīta mānavaḥ / arcayedīśvaraṃ devaṃ yadīcchecchāśvatīṃ gatim
verses.translation: Samitra: The reading in Mt. P. sado is also called Samitra and Assamrjjya.
verses.hindi: विरराजारविन्दस्थः पद्मगर्भसमझतिः ३४
verses.wordMeaning: Samitra: The reading in Mt. P. sado is also called Samitra and Assamrjjya.
verses.commentary: Sense: Samitra: The reading in Mt. P. sado is also called Samitra and Assamrjjya.

verses.sanskrit: कावेरीसङ्गमे राजन्स्नानदानार्चनं नरैः । कृतं भक्त्या नरश्रेष्ठ अश्वमेधाधिकं फलम्
verses.transliteration: kāverīsaṅgame rājansnānadānārcanaṃ naraiḥ / kṛtaṃ bhaktyā naraśreṣṭha aśvamedhādhikaṃ phalam
verses.translation: Ajaikapada also called Salamukhiya.
verses.hindi: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे ताभ्यामेकंकस्य तु कात्स्न्यंतः । प्रवतंभाने संहरें भध्ये तस्थाणंवस्थ तु..
verses.wordMeaning: Ajaikapada also called Salamukhiya.
verses.commentary: Sense: Ajaikapada also called Salamukhiya.

verses.sanskrit: होमेन चाक्षयः स्वर्गो जपादायुर्विवर्धते । ध्यानतो नित्यमायाति पदं शिवकलात्मकम्
verses.transliteration: homena cākṣayaḥ svargo japādāyurvivardhate / dhyānato nityamāyāti padaṃ śivakalātmakam
verses.translation: Ahirbudhnya also called AnuddeSya.
verses.hindi: ततो ह्यपरिमेयात्मा भुतानां प्रभुरीश्वरः। शुलपाणिमंहादेवों हैमचोराम्बरच्छुद: ॥
verses.wordMeaning: Ahirbudhnya also called AnuddeSya.
verses.commentary: Sense: Ahirbudhnya also called AnuddeSya.

verses.sanskrit: अग्निप्रवेशं यः कुर्यात् तस्मिंस् तीर्थे नरेश्वर । अग्निलोके वसेत्तावद्यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम्
verses.transliteration: agnipraveśaṃ yaḥ kuryāt tasmiṃs tīrthe nareśvara / agniloke vasettāvadyāvadābhūtasamplavam
verses.translation: Variations from Mt. P are noted in the notes.
verses.hindi: का भी चुछ पता नहीं चलता । ऐसा कहकर भगवान् हरि ने पितामह से फिर कहा- है द्विजोत्तम ! आप भी इसी प्रकार हमारे शाश्वत उदर में प्रवेश कर अनृपम लोकों को देखें ।३६-२९। पितामह ने जब मन को प्रसन्न करनेवाली ऐसी बाणी को सुना, तो वे श्रीपति विष्णु का अभिनन्दन कर उनके उदर में बैठ गये । अत्यन्त पराक्रमी गर्भस्थ ब्रह्मा ने घूम-फिर कर उन्हीं लोकों को देखा, किन्तु विष्णु देवता के उदर का अन्त
verses.wordMeaning: Variations from Mt. P are noted in the notes.
verses.commentary: Sense: Variations from Mt. P are noted in the notes.

verses.sanskrit: अनाशकं तु यः कुर्यात् तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नराधिप । तस्य पुण्यफलं यद्वै तच्छृणुष्व नरोत्तम
verses.transliteration: anāśakaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāt tasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa / tasya puṇyaphalaṃ yadvai tacchṛṇuṣva narottama
verses.translation: Ajaikapat is the Upaslheya fire. Its place is in front of the sacrificial hall. Ahirbudhnya is th cAnuddesya (not kindled?). That fire is proclaimed as Grhapati.
verses.hindi: नहीं पा सके ।३०-३१। इधर विष्ण ने जब उदर के भीतर पितामह के आगमन को समझा तब उन्होंने सब द्वारों को बन्द कर उस महाजल राशि में सुखपूर्वक सो जाने की इच्छा की !३२। ब्रह्मा ने जब सब द्वारों को बन्द देखा, तब उन्होंने सक्षम रूप धारण किया और नाभिदेश में द्वार पकर कमलनाल के सहारे निकल कर अपने रूप का उद्धार कर लिया । उस समय चतुरानन ब्रह्मा पद्मगर्भ के समान द्यतिमान् होकर कमल
verses.wordMeaning: Ajaikapat is the Upaslheya fire. Its place is in front of the sacrificial hall. Ahirbudhnya is th cAnuddesya (not kindled?). That fire is proclaimed as Grhapati.
verses.commentary: Sense: Ajaikapat is the Upaslheya fire. Its place is in front of the sacrificial hall. Ahirbudhnya is th cAnuddesya (not kindled?). That fire is proclaimed as Grhapati.

verses.sanskrit: गन्धर्वाप्सरःसंकीर्णे विमाने सूर्यसन्निभे । वीज्यमानो वरस्त्रीभिर्दैवतैः सह मोदते
verses.transliteration: gandharvāpsaraḥsaṃkīrṇe vimāne sūryasannibhe / vījyamāno varastrībhirdaivataiḥ saha modate
verses.translation: All the sons of Sarhsya fire are regarded as Upaslheya by Brahmanas.
verses.hindi: के बीच जा बंठे। इसी प्रकार उन दोनों का आपस में कोौतुक-व्यापार उस जलाणंव में चलने लगा ।
verses.wordMeaning: All the sons of Sarhsya fire are regarded as Upaslheya by Brahmanas.
verses.commentary: Sense: All the sons of Sarhsya fire are regarded as Upaslheya by Brahmanas.

verses.sanskrit: षष्टिवर्षसहस्राणि षष्टिवर्षशतानि च । क्रीडते रुद्रलोकस्थस्तदन्ते भुवि चागतः
verses.transliteration: ṣaṣṭivarṣasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭivarṣaśatāni ca / krīḍate rudralokasthastadante bhuvi cāgataḥ
verses.translation: Kratu, Pravahana and Agnldhra are the Dhisnis there. On the day when Soma juice is extracted, they are carried to their spots.
verses.hindi: सूसजी बोले--इसी समय जहाँ नाग-भोगपति हरि स्थित थे, वहाँ अपरिमेयात्मा भूतपति सुवर्ण चीराम्बरधारी शूलपाणि महादेव आये ।३६॥ वे बड़ी शीघत्रता और जोर-जोर से पेर पटक रहे थे, जिससे
verses.wordMeaning: Kratu, Pravahana and Agnldhra are the Dhisnis there. On the day when Soma juice is extracted, they are carried to their spots.
verses.commentary: Sense: Kratu, Pravahana and Agnldhra are the Dhisnis there. On the day when Soma juice is extracted, they are carried to their spots.

verses.sanskrit: भोगवान्दानशीलश्च जायते पृथिवीपतिः । आधिशोकविनिर्मुक्तो जीवेच्च शरदां शतम्
verses.transliteration: bhogavāndānaśīlaśca jāyate pṛthivīpatiḥ / ādhiśokavinirmukto jīvecca śaradāṃ śatam
verses.translation: The fire which is remembered as the sonof Pautra, that Havya-bearer is called fire Santi or Pracetas or Satya. It is the second fire.
verses.hindi: अस्मिन्स्थलेउ्ध्यायपरिसमाप्तिदू श्यते ख. घ. ड. पुस्तकेषु ।
verses.wordMeaning: The fire which is remembered as the sonof Pautra, that Havya-bearer is called fire Santi or Pracetas or Satya. It is the second fire.
verses.commentary: Sense: The fire which is remembered as the sonof Pautra, that Havya-bearer is called fire Santi or Pracetas or Satya. It is the second fire.

verses.sanskrit: एवं गुणगणाकीर्णा कावेरी सा सरिन्नृप । त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्याता नर्मदासङ्गमे सदा
verses.transliteration: evaṃ guṇagaṇākīrṇā kāverī sā sarinnṛpa / triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātā narmadāsaṅgame sadā
verses.translation: The fire Visvadeva is said to be at Brahma-sthana. Avaksu, the son of Acchavaka, is conceived to be at the position of the earth (Bhu ).
verses.hindi: शीघ्र' विक्रमतस्तस्य पद्भ्यामत्यन्तपीडिताः । उद्भुतास्तूर्णमाकाशे पृथुलास्तोयविन्दवः ॥ अत्युष्णाश्वातिशीताभ्र वायुस्तत्र बवो भृशम् द
verses.wordMeaning: The fire Visvadeva is said to be at Brahma-sthana. Avaksu, the son of Acchavaka, is conceived to be at the position of the earth (Bhu ).
verses.commentary: Sense: The fire Visvadeva is said to be at Brahma-sthana. Avaksu, the son of Acchavaka, is conceived to be at the position of the earth (Bhu ).

verses.sanskrit: जितवाक्कायचित्ताश्च ध्येयध्यानरतास् तथा । कावेरीसङ्गमे तात ते ऽपि मोक्षमवाप्नुयुः
verses.transliteration: jitavākkāyacittāśca dhyeyadhyānaratās tathā / kāverīsaṅgame tāta te 'pi mokṣamavāpnuyuḥ
verses.translation: The powerful fire Uslra is regarded as the son of Nesthiya. The eighth fire Vyaratti is proclaimed as the son of Marjali (?). Dhisnyas are Viharamyas (portable?) by Saumya(?) and another. Out of them that which is called Pavaka is the foetus of waters. 2
verses.hindi: तद्दृष्ट्वा महदाश्रर्य ब्रह्मा विष्मुमभभाषत । अब्बिन्दवो हि स्थलोष्णा: कम्पते चास्व्रुजं भूशम् ॥।
verses.wordMeaning: The powerful fire Uslra is regarded as the son of Nesthiya. The eighth fire Vyaratti is proclaimed as the son of Marjali (?). Dhisnyas are Viharamyas (portable?) by Saumya(?) and another. Out of them that which is called Pavaka is the foetus of waters. 2
verses.commentary: Sense: The powerful fire Uslra is regarded as the son of Nesthiya. The eighth fire Vyaratti is proclaimed as the son of Marjali (?). Dhisnyas are Viharamyas (portable?) by Saumya(?) and another. Out of them that which is called Pavaka is the foetus of waters. 2

verses.sanskrit: शृणु ते ऽन्यत्प्रवक्ष्यामि आश्चर्यं नृपसत्तम । त्रिषु लोकेषु का त्वन्या दृश्यते सरिता समा
verses.transliteration: śṛṇu te 'nyatpravakṣyāmi āścaryaṃ nṛpasattama / triṣu lokeṣu kā tvanyā dṛśyate saritā samā
verses.translation: That fire shall be known as " Avabhrtha " which is worshipped properly by oblations in the waters. The fire Hrcchaya is his son, it is the fire stationed in the belly of men.
verses.hindi: एत॑ मे संशय बृहि किचान्यत्वं चिकीर्षसि ३८ . एतदेवंविधं वाक्य पितामहमुखोज्भूवम् । श्रुत्वाउप्रतिमकर्मा55ह भगवानसुरान्तकृत् ३३६
verses.wordMeaning: That fire shall be known as " Avabhrtha " which is worshipped properly by oblations in the waters. The fire Hrcchaya is his son, it is the fire stationed in the belly of men.
verses.commentary: Sense: That fire shall be known as " Avabhrtha " which is worshipped properly by oblations in the waters. The fire Hrcchaya is his son, it is the fire stationed in the belly of men.

verses.sanskrit: लब्धं यैर् नर्मदातोयं ये च कुर्युः प्रदक्षिणम् । ये पिबन्ति जलं तत्र ते पुण्या नात्र संशयः
verses.transliteration: labdhaṃ yair narmadātoyaṃ ye ca kuryuḥ pradakṣiṇam / ye pibanti jalaṃ tatra te puṇyā nātra saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: Viharaniya fires are eight in number. But their lists in our text and in the Mt. P. are different. These portable (viharaniya) fires are regarded as the sons of the stationary fires. The list of Viharaniya fires in our text is as follows: Pravahana, 2. Santi or Pracetas or Satya, 3. Visvadeva, 4. Avaksu,
verses.hindi: कि नु खल्वत्र में नाभ्यां भुतमन्यत्कृतालयम् । बदति प्रियमत्यर्थ विप्रियेषपि च ते सया १४० इत्येब॑ मनसा ध्यात्वा प्रत्युवाचेदमुत्तरम् । कि न्वत्र भगवांस्तस्मिन्पुष्करे जातसंत्रमः ३४ १ कि मया यत्कृतं देव यन्‍्मां प्रियमनुत्तमम् । भाषसे पुरुषश्रेष्ठ किमर्थ ब्रृहि तत्त्वतः
verses.wordMeaning: Viharaniya fires are eight in number. But their lists in our text and in the Mt. P. are different. These portable (viharaniya) fires are regarded as the sons of the stationary fires. The list of Viharaniya fires in our text is as follows: Pravahana, 2.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Viharaniya fires are eight in number. But their lists in our text and in the Mt. P. are different. These portable (viharaniya) fires are regarded as the sons of the stationary fires. The list of Viharaniya fires in our text is as follows: Pravahana, 2.…

verses.sanskrit: न तेषां सन्ततिच्छेदो दश जन्मानि पञ्च च । तेषां पापं विलीयेत हिमं सूर्योदये यथा
verses.transliteration: na teṣāṃ santaticchedo daśa janmāni pañca ca / teṣāṃ pāpaṃ vilīyeta himaṃ sūryodaye yathā
verses.translation: Usira, 6. Vyaratti. Two more names are missing in this list, but Mt. gives only four names and cannot supply the missing names.
verses.hindi: एवं बुवाणं देवेशं लोकमात्रां तु तत्त्वगाम् । प्रत्युवाचाम्बुजाभास्कः ब्रह्मा वेदनिधि:ः प्रभु: ४३ योडसों तबोदरं पूर्व प्रविष्टो5हं त्वदिच्छेया । यथा ममोदरे लोकाः सर्वे दृष्टास्त्वया प्रभो ॥ तथव दुृष्टाः कारत्स््येन मया लोकास्तवोदरे ४४ ततो वर्षसहल्नान्त उपावत्तस्य सेइनघ । नून॑ मत्सरभावेन मां वशीकर्तुमिच्छता ॥
verses.wordMeaning: Usira, 6. Vyaratti. Two more names are missing in this list, but Mt. gives only four names and cannot supply the missing names.
verses.commentary: Sense: Usira, 6. Vyaratti. Two more names are missing in this list, but Mt. gives only four names and cannot supply the missing names.

verses.sanskrit: गङ्गायमुनसङ्गे वै यत्फलं लभते नरः । तत्फलं लभते मर्त्यः कावेरीस्नानमाचरन्
verses.transliteration: gaṅgāyamunasaṅge vai yatphalaṃ labhate naraḥ / tatphalaṃ labhate martyaḥ kāverīsnānamācaran
verses.translation: Verses 30-35 give the following 'descendants* of the fire Pavaka. The fire Suci, son of the Sun, was kindled by Gandhar- vas and Asuras by churning the Arani wood. 1
verses.hindi: खौलते हुये और अत्यन्त शीतल बड़े-बड़े जलबिन्दु आकाश की तरफ उड़ने लगे तथा वाशु भी जोर से बहने लगी ।३७। यह देखकर ब्रह्मा को बड़ा आश्चर्य हुआ और उन्होंने विष्णु से कहा--जल-बिन्दु स्थूल और उष्ण हो गये हैं, जिससे कमल काँप रहा है। हमारे मन में सन्‍न्देह हो रहा है कि, यह आप क्या करना चाह रहे हैं ।” ।३८। पितामह के मुख से निकली इस तरह की वाणों सुनकर असुरविनाशी और
verses.wordMeaning: Verses 30-35 give the following 'descendants* of the fire Pavaka. The fire Suci, son of the Sun, was kindled by Gandhar- vas and Asuras by churning the Arani wood. 1
verses.commentary: Sense: Verses 30-35 give the following 'descendants* of the fire Pavaka. The fire Suci, son of the Sun, was kindled by Gandhar- vas and Asuras by churning the Arani wood. 1

verses.sanskrit: भौमे तु भूतजायोगे व्यतीपाते च संक्रमे । राहुसोमसमायोगे तदेवाष्टगुणं स्मृतम्
verses.transliteration: bhaume tu bhūtajāyoge vyatīpāte ca saṃkrame / rāhusomasamāyoge tadevāṣṭaguṇaṃ smṛtam
verses.translation: Lord Ayus is the fire consecrated in the animal. Mahi- man was the son of Ayus and his son was Savana by name.
verses.hindi: अनृपम कार्यकर्ता भगवान् विष्णु ने कहा--क्या, मेरी नाभि में दूसरे जीव ने आकर आश्रय ग्रहण किया है ! ब्रह्मा ! मैंने आपके प्रति अनुचित व्यवहार किया है फिर भी आप हमारे प्रति सुन्दर वचन कह रहे हैं। इस तरह मन में ध्यान कर उन्होंने फिर कहा-क्या आपको इस कमल के सम्बन्ध में कुछ सन्देह हो गया है? पुरुषश्रेष्ठ ! मैंने क्या किया है, जो आप इस तरह प्रिय और उत्तम वचन मुझसे कह रहे हैं. यह आप
verses.wordMeaning: Lord Ayus is the fire consecrated in the animal. Mahi- man was the son of Ayus and his son was Savana by name.
verses.commentary: Sense: Lord Ayus is the fire consecrated in the animal. Mahi- man was the son of Ayus and his son was Savana by name.

verses.sanskrit: अशीतिश्च यवाः प्रोक्ता गङ्गायामुनसङ्गमे । कावेरीनर्मदायोगे तदेवाष्टगुणं स्मृतम्
verses.transliteration: aśītiśca yavāḥ proktā gaṅgāyāmunasaṅgame / kāverīnarmadāyoge tadevāṣṭaguṇaṃ smṛtam
verses.translation: The fire that identifies (itself with it) in cooking and sacrifices is known as Savana. The son of the fire Savana was the famous Adbhuta. Vivici is known as the great son of Adbhuta. It always swallows the offerings in expiatory rites of sinners.
verses.hindi: कहें । लोकयात्रा के तत्त्वगामी देवेश विष्णु के कहने पर कमलनिवासी वेदनिधि प्रभु ब्रह्मा ने उत्तर दिया--३६-४३। है प्रभु ! इसके पहले मैंने ही आपकी इच्छा से आपके उदर में प्रवेश किया था और आपने जिस प्रकार हमारे उदर में सब लोकों को देखा था, उसी प्रकार मैंने भी आपके उदर में सम्पूर्ण लोकों को देखा ।४४। है निष्पाप ! हजार वर्ष के बाद जब हम बाहर आने लगे, तब आपने मात्सय से शीघ्र
verses.wordMeaning: The fire that identifies (itself with it) in cooking and sacrifices is known as Savana. The son of the fire Savana was the famous Adbhuta. Vivici is known as the great son of Adbhuta. It always swallows the offerings in expiatory rites of sinners.
verses.commentary: Sense: The fire that identifies (itself with it) in cooking and sacrifices is known as Savana. The son of the fire Savana was the famous Adbhuta. Vivici is known as the great son of Adbhuta. It always swallows the offerings in expiatory rites of sinners.

verses.sanskrit: गङ्गा षष्टिसहस्रैस्तु क्षेत्रपालैः प्रपूज्यते । तदर्धैर् अन्यतीर्थानि रक्षन्ते नात्र संशयः
verses.transliteration: gaṅgā ṣaṣṭisahasraistu kṣetrapālaiḥ prapūjyate / tadardhair anyatīrthāni rakṣante nātra saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: Vivici's son was Arka and his sons are Anlkavan, Asjrjavan, Raksoha, Pitrkrt, Surabhi and Rukmavan. The latter abides in gold, jewels and other shining materials.
verses.hindi: सब इद्धिन्य-ह्वारों को बन्द कर दिया था। आप हमें वशीभूत करना चाहते थे । है महाभाग ! तब अपने
verses.wordMeaning: Vivici's son was Arka and his sons are Anlkavan, Asjrjavan, Raksoha, Pitrkrt, Surabhi and Rukmavan. The latter abides in gold, jewels and other shining materials.
verses.commentary: Sense: Vivici's son was Arka and his sons are Anlkavan, Asjrjavan, Raksoha, Pitrkrt, Surabhi and Rukmavan. The latter abides in gold, jewels and other shining materials.

verses.sanskrit: अमरेश्वरे तु सरितां ये योगाः परिकीर्तिताः । ते त्वशीतिसहस्रैस्तु क्षेत्रपालैस्तु रक्षिताः
verses.transliteration: amareśvare tu saritāṃ ye yogāḥ parikīrtitāḥ / te tvaśītisahasraistu kṣetrapālaistu rakṣitāḥ
verses.translation: The fourteen fires are the progeny of the fire Suci. These are called Vahnis. They are consecrated by reciting mantras in sacrifices. In the Manvantara called Svayambhuva, in the first Sarga (creation), these fires who were Abhimanins, had passed away along with the Yamas, the best of Devas.
verses.hindi: मा भूत्ते सनसो5ल्‍्पोषपि व्यघातो5यं कथंचन । इत्येषाइनुगतिविष्णो: कार्याणामौपसर्गिकी.
verses.wordMeaning: The fourteen fires are the progeny of the fire Suci. These are called Vahnis. They are consecrated by reciting mantras in sacrifices. In the Manvantara called Svayambhuva, in the first Sarga (creation), these fires who were Abhimanins, had passed away along with the Yamas,…
verses.commentary: Sense: The fourteen fires are the progeny of the fire Suci. These are called Vahnis. They are consecrated by reciting mantras in sacrifices. In the Manvantara called Svayambhuva, in the first Sarga (creation), these fires who were Abhimanins, had passed away along with the Yamas,…

verses.sanskrit: तथामरेश्वरे याम्ये लिङ्गं वै चपलेश्वरम् । द्वितीयं चण्डहस्ताख्यं द्वे लिङ्गे तीर्थरक्षके
verses.transliteration: tathāmareśvare yāmye liṅgaṃ vai capaleśvaram / dvitīyaṃ caṇḍahastākhyaṃ dve liṅge tīrtharakṣake
verses.translation: In the previous Manvantara, these fires were those who identified themselves with their abodes called Viharaniyas, both sentient and non-sentient.
verses.hindi: पन्‍्मया5ननन्‍्तरं कार्य मयाध्ध्यवसितं त्वयि  त्वां वा बाधितुकामेन क़ीडापुर्व यद्च्छया ॥।
verses.wordMeaning: In the previous Manvantara, these fires were those who identified themselves with their abodes called Viharaniyas, both sentient and non-sentient.
verses.commentary: Sense: In the previous Manvantara, these fires were those who identified themselves with their abodes called Viharaniyas, both sentient and non-sentient.

verses.sanskrit: शिवेन स्थापिते पूर्वं कावेर्याद्यभिरक्षके । लक्षेण रक्षिता देवी नर्मदा बहुकल्पगा
verses.transliteration: śivena sthāpite pūrvaṃ kāveryādyabhirakṣake / lakṣeṇa rakṣitā devī narmadā bahukalpagā
verses.translation: Verses 36-41 give the following descendants* of Suci (the Son of the Sun-god): These (fires) were assigned to the three types of Karmas, viz. Kamya (those depending on desire), Naimittika (occasional) and constant (JV itya). In the previous Manvantara they passed away along with the fair sens.
verses.hindi: न तेपन्यथाइवमन्तव्यों सान्यः पृज्यश्रव से भवान् । सर्वे सषेय कल्याण यन्मयाञ्थ कृतं तव ॥
verses.wordMeaning: Verses 36-41 give the following descendants* of Suci (the Son of the Sun-god): These (fires) were assigned to the three types of Karmas, viz. Kamya (those depending on desire), Naimittika (occasional) and constant (JV itya).…
verses.commentary: Sense: Verses 36-41 give the following descendants* of Suci (the Son of the Sun-god): These (fires) were assigned to the three types of Karmas, viz. Kamya (those depending on desire), Naimittika (occasional) and constant (JV itya).…

verses.sanskrit: धनुषां षष्ट्यभियुतैः पुरुषैरीशयोजितैः । ॐ कारशतसाहस्रैः पर्वतश्चाभिरक्षितः
verses.transliteration: dhanuṣāṃ ṣaṣṭyabhiyutaiḥ puruṣairīśayojitaiḥ / oṃ kāraśatasāhasraiḥ parvataścābhirakṣitaḥ
verses.translation: Thus the abodes and the abiders have been explained by me. Through them alone, the characteristics of the fires of the past and future Manvantaras have been enumerated. All of them are remembered as ascetics, those who performed Avabhjrtha bath, lords of subjects and luminous.
verses.hindi: नाहूं भवन्तं शवनोमि सोढुं तेजोमयं गुरुप् । स चोवाच वरं बृहि पद्मादबतराम्यहम् ५०
verses.wordMeaning: Thus the abodes and the abiders have been explained by me. Through them alone, the characteristics of the fires of the past and future Manvantaras have been enumerated. All of them are remembered as ascetics, those who performed Avabhjrtha bath, lords of subjects and luminous.
verses.commentary: Sense: Thus the abodes and the abiders have been explained by me. Through them alone, the characteristics of the fires of the past and future Manvantaras have been enumerated. All of them are remembered as ascetics, those who performed Avabhjrtha bath, lords of subjects and luminous.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यदेशकृतं पापम् अस्मिन् क्षेत्रे विनश्यति । अस्मिंस्तीर्थे कृतं पापं वज्रलेपो भविष्यति
verses.transliteration: anyadeśakṛtaṃ pāpam asmin kṣetre vinaśyati / asmiṃstīrthe kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ vajralepo bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: In the seven Manvantaras from Svarocisa to Savarni, they shall be known through their different forms and purposes in all the Manvantaras. The present fires exist with the present Devas and the future fires with the future Devas.
verses.hindi: पुत्रो में त्वं भव ब्रह्मन्सवंलोकाधिप प्रभो ५२ ततः स भगवान्त्रह्मा बरं गृह्म किरीटिनः । एवं भवतु चेत्युक्त्वा प्रीतात्मा गतसत्सरः ५३
verses.wordMeaning: In the seven Manvantaras from Svarocisa to Savarni, they shall be known through their different forms and purposes in all the Manvantaras. The present fires exist with the present Devas and the future fires with the future Devas.
verses.commentary: Sense: In the seven Manvantaras from Svarocisa to Savarni, they shall be known through their different forms and purposes in all the Manvantaras. The present fires exist with the present Devas and the future fires with the future Devas.

verses.sanskrit: एषा ते कथिता तात कावेरी सरितां वरा । रुद्रदेहसमुत्पन्ना तेन पुण्या सरिद्वरा
verses.transliteration: eṣā te kathitā tāta kāverī saritāṃ varā / rudradehasamutpannā tena puṇyā saridvarā
verses.translation: Thus the instruction about Fire-god has been imparted to you precisely. Now the account of Pitrs (manes) will be told in detail and in due order.
verses.hindi: मन में सोचा और नाभि में प्रवेश कर कमलनाल द्वारा बाहर निकल आया । है विष्णु! इससे आपके मन को जरा भो चोट न पहुंचे । कार्यों की परस्पर इसी प्रकार की स्वाभाविक गति होती है
verses.wordMeaning: Thus the instruction about Fire-god has been imparted to you precisely. Now the account of Pitrs (manes) will be told in detail and in due order.
verses.commentary: Sense: Thus the instruction about Fire-god has been imparted to you precisely. Now the account of Pitrs (manes) will be told in detail and in due order.

verses.sanskrit: ॥ इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे नर्मदामाहात्म्ये कावेरीसङ्गममाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकोनत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः ॥ र्क्व् अध्याय ३० श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: नर्मदोत्तरकूले तु दारुतीर्थमनुत्तमम् । यत्र सिद्धो महाभाग तपस्तप्त्वा द्विजोत्तमः
verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe narmadāmāhātmye kāverīsaṅgamamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 30 śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: narmadottarakūle tu dārutīrthamanuttamam / yatra siddho mahābhāga tapastaptvā dvijottamaḥ
verses.translation: While he thought upon Pitrs (lit. like Pitrs), the Pitrs (Manes) were born. Their creation has been described before. Its details are being narrated now. gdtratab (in Bd. 2. 13. 1 )'From the limbs' is a better reading. The six seasons (the spring etc.) are called the Pitj-s. The Vedic Sruti declares: "The seasons are the Pitr-Devas" 3 4 In all the Manvantaras, past and future (the same is repeated). Formerly these were born in the auspicious Man- vantara (called) Svayambhuva. Those (of the Pitrs) who performed sacrifices (and pressed Soma-juice) are the Pitrs called Soma-pithins. Those Pitrs who maintained the sacred fire (while on the earth) are remembered as Barhisad Pitrs. In the scriptures, the decision that seasons are the Pitr-devas is approved. The months of Madhu and Madhava (Caitra and Vaisakha) should be known as Rasas (juicy); those of Suci and Sukra (Jyestha and Asadha) are Susmins (lustrous). Those of Nabhas and Nabhasya (Sravana and Bhadrapada) are cited asjivas; those of Isa and Orja (Asvina and Kartika) are ambrosial; those of Saha and Sahasya (Margasirsa and Pausa) are called manyuman (angry) and those of Tapas and Tapasya (Magha and Phalguna) are terrible and cold. 5 abhyamanyala (Bd. P.I 1 2.13.3)'took pride in them'. upayakfitah in the text is obscure upapaksatah, 'from the flanks' in op. cit. is better. Pa andj>a in Devanagari script are always confused. The identification of seasons (Rtus) with Pitrs is as old as Tait. Br. (1.4.10.8) which states: For classification of Pitts see supra ch. 1, , note 2 also. The periods of time (called seasons) are six. In them are included (periods of time called) months. These seasons are said to be sentient and insentient. Through the change of their abodes, these Abhimanins (deities who identify) will be recognizable. Day, night, month, season, tropical transits of the sun (a half year) and year con¬ stitute the abodes of the deities. Nimesas, Kalas, Kasthas, Muhurtas, days and nights constitute the units of time. Since these are stationed in them or since these identify with them, they are known as identifiers. I shall explain them. Understand. The units of time are the Tithis of Parvans, the junctions, The sons of the season are five (viz. human beings, quadrupeds, birds, reptiles and trees). They are characterise by their seasonal changes. Since the mobile and immobile beings are born of Artavas (seasonal changes, menstruation etc.), the seasonal changes are their fathers and seasons are grandfathers. It is from Sumeka* (fixed period of time) that beings are born and die. Hence Sumeka isremembered as the great-gra father of the subjects. Due to their having the same name, the s *"' He who is known as Prajapati, is a year. A year Since they are born of Rta, the seasons are called *tus. The flowering period of bipeds, quadrupeds, birds, reptiles and immovable beings is called Kaldrlava (the seasonal change?). The state of being Rtu and Artava is declared as father¬ hood. Hence the seasons and Artavas should be known as Pitrs. Since beings are born of them through the ljUu-Kala (period favourable for conception, the Rtu period), these Artavas arc also Pitrs—So we have heard (it reported). The (deities) identifiers with Kala (period of time) continue to stay in all Manvantaras conditioned and regulated by their identification with their positions.

verses.translation: The Pitrs are of two types, the Agnisvattas and Barhi- sads. Two famous daughters were born of the Pitrs. The Barhisads, known as Somafiithins gave DharinI to Meru in marriage. • Agnisvattas gave Mena to Himalaya as wife Their ST Were ° Wn - N ° W *» < on the grand' The daughter of the Sea called Savarna 1 became the wife of Praclnabarhis. Savarna that daughter of the Sea (Sa- mudra) (married to Praclnabarhis) gave birth to ten Pracetas who were the masters of the science of archery. As a result of the curse of Siva, Daksa, the son of the self-born god Brahma, was reborn as their son 2 in the Caksusa Manvantara." On hearing this, Samsapayana asked Suta—"How was Daksa born in the Caksusa Manvantara formerly, as a result of the curse of Siva? Narrate this in detail to us who ask you." Thus requested, Suta narrated the episode of Daksa and the occasion of Siva's curse, after addressing Samsapayana. Daksa had eight daughters whom I have already mentioned to you. He invited them from their homes and welcomed them at his house. They stayed in their father's house duly honoured. But the eldest (of them) Satl, wife of Siva, was not invited by him out of hatred for Siva. Siva, the son-in-law, (being) stable (enveloped in his own brilliance) never bowed to his father-in-law Daksa. Knowing that her sisters had gone to their father's, Sati, though not invited, went to her father's house. Highly infuriated (with wrath), the goddess spoke to, Daksa: "O Lord! How is it that you have done this despicable act of dishonouring me by according greater honour to younger daughters? Iam the eldest and the most excellent daughter. It does not behove you to be discourteous to me". Thus addressed, Daksa, with his eyes reddened with anger retorted. "You are the most excellent of my daughters, foremost and most worthy of my respect for ever. Their husbands too are worthy of my respect always. The story of the second birth of Daksa is told here as in this birth These sons-in-law of mine, viz. Vasistha, Atri, Pula- stya, Angiras, Pulaha, Kratu, Bhrgu and Marici are very great. So said Daksa with the deluded mind, resulting in a curse to himself and to the great sages mentioned. Thus addressed, the infuriated Sati spoke to her father—"Since you insult me, who am pure in speech, mind and acts, I cast off this body, O father, born of you." Then goddess Sati, dejected and infuriated due to the insult, spoke after bowing mentally to Siva. "Wherever I am reborn with another refulgent body, I, undeluded and righteous, will attain the status of the righte¬ ous wife of Siva alone." She sat there itself with her Atman in Yogic commu¬ nion. She mentally retained the Agneyi Dharana. Fire came out of all limbs of her body and was blown by the wind, from the Agneyi Dkaraija. It reduced her to ashes. On hearing about the death of Sati, and on understand- ing their conversation precisely, the trident-bearing Siva be¬ came furious with Daksa and other sages. "O Daksa, since for my sake pure, sinless Sat! had been insulted and all other daughters were praised along with their husbands, they will die (attain Yama's region) and will be They will be there when Brahma will offer sour gruel in fire in the Caksusa Manvantara."

verses.translation: "O evil-minded one, I will be putting up obstacles to you, there also, again and again in the rites of virtue (Dbarma), wealth and love (Kama) • Since you spoke cruelly of the sages for my sake, the Brahmanas will never worship you in their sacrifice where they After offering Ahutis (to you) they will offer water (as "The earth is called the first among the worlds. At t e behest of Brahma, I shall sustain that world. Then thus cursed angrily by Rudra of unmeasured After realizing the Lord, the master of »" When the Vaivasvata Manvantara arrive, • It is said that as a result of Rudra's curse, he was born in Marsa by the tenth Pracctas in this second Manvantara. All the great sages, Bhrgu and others, were born former¬ ly in the first Treta Yuga. They assumed body from Varuna at the sacrifice of the great god. Thus the mutual enmity of Daksa Prajapati and Lord Siva continued from their previous existence. Hence, intense enmity should never be pursued even with enemies. Due to merits and demerits, a living being does not leave off (forget) the awareness of what was intensly concei¬ ved in the previous existence. Hence an intelligent person should use discretion in his actions. O Suta, how was the horse sacrifice of Daksa Praja¬ pati, son of Pracetas, destroyed in Vaivasvata Manvantara?. How did Daksa propitiate the lord who was enraged Similarly the ceWfoi The trees were in full bloom with the flowers of all seasons. The Vidyadharas, Siddhas, ascetics and other living beings (and goblins) assuming various forms began to worship the great lord Pasupati. Great and terrible Raksasas and.Pisacas were seen there assuming various forms and holding different kinds of weapons lifted up. The attendants of the lord who were as brilliant as Fire-god stood there. Lord Nandlsvara stood in the service of the lord, wielding the blazing trident shining with its brilliance. O excellent Brahmanas, Ganga the excellent river, the source of all sacred waters, assumed the form of a deity and worshipped him. Thus the great lord shining with his brilliance stayed there along with the celestial sages and the blessed Devas. Formerly on the top of Himavat in an auspicious place near Gangadvara, 1 resorted to by the sages and Siddhas, Daksa began his sacrifice. The Devas led by Indra gathered together and prepared to attend the sacrifice. It is reported that with the permission of the Lord (Siva), Devas who were resplendent like fire went to Ganga- dvara in their dazzling aerial cars. Folding their palms in reverence, the residents of earth, sky and heaven approached Daksa Prajapati, the foremost among sacrificers, who was surrounded by sages, Gandharvas and celestial* damsels at Gangadvara abounding in various trees and creepers. Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, Sadhyas arrived there for their share in the sacrifice along with Maruts and Indra. (Deities of the categories of) TJsmapas, Somapas, Ajyapas, Dhumapas (drinkers of hot offerings, soma, ghee and smoke), the two Asvin-gods and Pitrs came there along with god Brahma.

verses.translation: These and many other groups of living beings— Jarayujas (viviparous animals), Anfajas (born of eggs, birds) The same as modem Hara(i)dwar. The actual spot of Daksa's sacrifice is at a distance of a kilometer from modern Haridwar. Dcvas and their consorts were invoked through Mantras. Seated in their aerial chariots they shone like blazing fires. On seeing them Dadhlca became angry and said, "A man incurs sin by worshipping one unworthy of worship and not worshipping one who is worthy of worship. After saying thus, the sage spoke again to Daksa, "Why don't you invite lord Siva who is worthy of worship?. I have so many Rudras here armed with spears and having matted hair. They stay with eleven forms. I do not know any other great god. He who has invited Siva, has invited all gods. As I do not see (regard) any other'deity superior to Sankara, this vast and rich sacrifice of Daksa will not take place. "O heroic lord, in this sacrifice, I offer unto Visnu, the lord without an equal, all the Havis sanctified by Mantras, and invariably through the Ahavanlya fire, holding the Havis in a golden vessel". On knowing that Devas had gone, Parvatl, the chaste daughter of the king of mountains, spoke to Lord Siva (her husband). O Lord, where have these gone, led by Indra. O knower of truth, speak truly. There is my great doubt. O blessed lord, why have you not gone to this sacrifice? Wherefore is the departure thither prohibited? O blessed lady! All this has been done by Devas only. My share in all the sacrifices is not allotted (to me). O beautiful lady! By following the traditional proce¬ dure, the Devas do not give me my due share in sacrifice. "O Lord! You are the most brilliant among afl the Devas. You excel them in good qualities. You are invincible, unthwartable by your splendour, fame and glory. O blessed one, by this prohibition, I am much distressed. O sinless lord, my body heaves. What indeed is the religious gift I should give or penance I should perform whereby you, my husband, shall have a share of the sacirfice—half or a third of it." The unthinkable lord delightedly spoke to her who was so agitated. "O goddess of Devas, of slender belly and limbs, you do not know whether your statements are proper. O large-eyed goddess 1 I know that when men of good qualities speak, all of them do so attentively. But atpresent god Indra has fallen in delusion and the three worlds arc also deluded in every respect. They eulogise me in sacrifices. They sing appropriate Saman Rathamara.In the Brahmasatra, Brahmanas worship me. The Adhvaryus assign my share." "Undoubtedly my lord, though not born of Prakrti, you either eulogise or offer self-defence in this assembly of women." The Lord said: "O Goddess of Devas, I do not eulogise myself. O fair lady, O beautiful one,see and appro the person I create for the sake of.my share. After speaking thus to his wife, more beloved to him than his vital breath, the Lord created from his mouth a goblin that resembled the fury of fire. He had a thousand heads, a thousand feet and eyes. He held a thousand iron clubs, a thousand arrows in his hands. He held a conch, a discus, a mace, a blazing bow, an axe and a sword in his hands. He was terrible and awe-inspiring. He was blazing with a terrible form. Half a moon constituted his crest. He was clad in a tiger-skin dripping with blood.

verses.translation: He was terrible with his curved fangs. He was whirl¬ ing (?). He had wide mouth and big belly. His tongue was like lightning. His lips hung loose. His ears were long. He was inaccessible to all. A thunderbolt brightened his hands. His hair shone with splendour. He was surrounded by wreaths of flames. He was bedecked in pearl-strings. He blazed with brilliance like the fire of Dissolution. He had great strength and spendour. He was a great Purusa and lord. His huge body was capable of destroying the universe. It was as huge as the clustering banyan tree. He blazed like a hundred moons blazing simultaneously or like the fire that burnt Madana. He wore different flowers on his head. He had various kinds of scent and unguents. His limbs were decorated with different jewels. He was bedecked in ornaments. He wore a shining garland of Karnikara flowers. Due to anger his eyes were whirling and turning. At times he danced in different postures. At times he meditated with his soul in communion. At times he wiped off the gross matter. At times he sang and at times he cried over and over again. He was endowed with the basic attributes of know¬ ledge, detachment, lordship, penance, truthfulness, forbearance, fortitude, mastery and self-enlightenment. He knelt on his knees on the ground. He bowed with palms joined in reverence and stood still. Then he said, "O lord of Devas, command, what work shall I do for you?" The great lord spoke to him—"Destroy the sacrifice ofDaksa". On hearing the command of the lord, the powerful Vlrabhadra bowed at the feet of the lord, bending his head. Then he jumped ahead sportingly like a lion released from bondage. He considered that the sacrifice of Daksa was already destroyed by the fury of the goddess. The great goddess, highly fierce Bhadrakali accom¬ panied him wrathfully to reveal her omnipresence (to all). This is the infuriated lord, having his residence in the abodes of ghosts, who became known as Vlrabhadra. He dispelled the anger of the goddess. From the hair pores in his body he created the chiefs of Ganas named Raudras. They were the followers of Rudras who possessed great prowess and exploits ofRudra. They were the followers of Rudra. They had the splendour of Rudra. They started immediately in hundreds and thousands. There arose tumultuous roar that -filled the sky. By that loud noise, the heaven-dwellers became frightened. O Brahmanas, mountains crumbled, the earth shook. The Meru whirled round. The seas were agitated. They suppressed everything. They danced. Having the speed of the wind and the quickness of the mind, they ran here and there. They broke the sacrificial vessels to pieces. The sacri¬ ficial altar shattered utterly, appeared like the stars fallen from the sky. There were heaps of foodstuffs and beverages like mountains. Rivers of milk were flowing. Ghee and milk pudding formed muddy slushes. There was honey and gruel water. There were divine sugar candies, powdered like sands. Foodstuffs having all the six tastes flowed through the rivulets of jaggery, charming to the mind. There were meat dishes of several varieties. Whatever sweet foodstuffs they saw, they ate up. They squeezed the juice and licked up thelambatives. Their different faces exhibited different reactions. They rolled every¬ where. They sported about assuming different forms. They seized the celestial damsels and molested them. Urged byRudra's fury, the Ganas as furious as Rudra himself, destroyed the sacrifice, though it was well guarded by Devas. Others roared loudly terrifying all living beings. Others severed the head of sacrifice and roared. Daksa, the skilled Prajapati, and the lord of sacrifices began to flee through the sky in the form of a deer. Virabhadra of incomprehensible soul then gauged his strength. He cut off the' head* as he passed through the sky.

verses.transliteration: tasya nāmnā tu tattīrthaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam / tatra snātvā vidhānena arcayetpitṛdevatāḥ
verses.translation: Daksa Prajapati was confused and lost consciousness. The thirty-three crores of Devas of pure souls were bound with noose as strong as fire or lion. Then Devas went to the powerful noble being and said, "O Lord Rudra, be pleased. O Lord, do not be angry with your servants". Then Brahma and other Devas and Daksa Prajapati spoke with palms joined in reverence, "Please tell us who you are?". I am neither a Deva nor an Aditya, I have not come here to take meals, nor to visit the chiefs of Devas nor out of curiosity. Know me as one come here to destroy the sacrifice. I am known as Virabhadra and I have come out of the fur)' of Rudra. Bhadrakali has come out of the fury of the goddess (Parvati). Sent by the lord of Devas, she has come near the sacrifice. O Daksa, seek refuge in lord Siva. Even his fury is better than the gift of boons from a Deva." On hearing the words of Virabhadra, Daksa, the fore¬ most of the upholders of holy rites, propitiated the trident-bear¬ ing Siva, lord of Devas. When the premises of the sacrifice were defiled, when the Brahmanas fled, when the hideous and terrible great fire in the form of the constellation Mrgasiras blazed, when the servants whose faces were pierced by spears (screamed), when the uprooted sacrificial posts were scattered here and there, when the place was filled with vultures greedy of flesh rising up and flying, when the sound of hundreds of vixens by the flapping o wings (pervaded the quarters), the Lord of Devas, the conqueror of enemies* the lord having many visions, restrained his Prana and Apana strenuously in their places, directed his vision a round. Suddenly came out of the pit of fire the God of gods. His splendour was comparable to that of a thousand suns, moons and the Samvartaka fire. The lord laughed loudly and said again: "O Daksa, you are ruined due to ignorance. I hope you are well disposed towards me now". Smilingly he spoke again: "Tell me, what shall I "If you, my lord, are pleased, if I am your favo¬ urite, if I am to be blessed and if I am to be granted boon, I would choose this. The requisites of sacrifice are collected by me with strenuous efforts over long period. They have been swallowed, eaten, drunk, chewed, destroyed, powdered and scattered in this manner. Let them not go in vain." "So be it", said the lord, the destroyer of the eyes of Bhaga. After receiving the boon Prajapati Daksa knelt on the ground and eulogised the bull-bannered, three-eyed lord, the presiding deity of sacred rites, by - his thousand and eight names. 1 "Obeisance to you, the lord of the chiefs of Devas, O thousand-eyed one, O hideous-eyed one, O three- You arc the protector of Devas and Danavas, you are Brahma and Indra. O large-bodied one, you are. the lord of the deities. Obeisance (to you), you are the upholder of the waters in the ocean. Devas abide in your body as cows in the cow-shed. I see your body as the moon, fire and ocean. I sec you as Aditya, Visnu, Brahma and Brhaspati. You are the cause, becoming, being, agent and instrument. You are the non-existent, theexistent-cum-non-existent, the source of origin and the end of the universe. Obeisance to Bhava, Sarva, Rudra and the granter of boons. Obeisance to the lord of Pasus, the destroyer ofAnd- haka, Trijata (having matted hair in three plaits), the three- headed-and the wielder of excellent trident. Obeisance to Tryambaka (three-eyed), Trinetra (three¬ eyed), the destroyer of Tripuras, Canda (the fierce), Mun/jla (one with a shaven head), Pracanda (very fierce) and Dhara (the uplifter). Obeisance to one engaged in listening to Din<jima, Lord of Ardhadanda, Niska (body-less), Vikjrta (the deformed one). Salute to Vilohila (ruddy), Dliumra (coloured), blue¬ necked, Siva, who is without a compeer. Obeisance to the sun, the lord of the sun, the sun- bannered god, the lord of Pramathas, and the bull-shouldered archer.

verses.transliteration: satyavādī jitakrodhaḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ / sarvānkāmān avāpnoti rājannatraiva savarthā
verses.translation: Obeisance to Hiranyagarbha (the golden-wombed), one with golden coat of mail, the gold-crested and the lord of gold, Obeisance to the destroyer of sacrifice, Danfa i the staff), Parnapanaputa (one having a cup of leaves for drinking); one who is eulogised, one worthy of being praised, one being Bow to Saroa (the all); one who subsists on non-eatable Obeisance to worshipper, one worthy of worship; the Obeisance to the one who is stable; who is walking- who symbolizes a mystic sign, who is crooked, who is habitually dancing and making a musical instrument of his mouth. Obeisance to the one greedy of securing presents in dances; who is engaged in songs and musical instruments, who is the eldest, the excellent and the suppressor of foes. Obeisance to Kalana (creator), Kalpa, Ksaya (complete dissolution), Upakfaya (subsidiary dissolution), one laughino- terribly like the Dundubhi (wardrum), cherished by Bhlmat sena. Obeisance to Ugra (the fierce one); one having ten arms and a skull in his hand; obeisance to one fond of ashes from the funeral pyre. Obeisance to the terrible, the awe-inspiring one, one Obeisance to i r Obeisance to the one • Obeisance to one having a hundred thousand bells, one Fond of a garland of bells, to the rcstrainer of Prana, the renunciation (incarnate), and to Hilahila (a sport). Obeisance to one who makes the "Iiuihhum" sound, who takes us across, who is fond of Humhum sound. Obeis¬ ance to Sarhbhu who is fond of mountains, trees and their fruits. Obeisance to the jackal (fond of) embryo meal. Obeis¬ ance to Taraka (one who takes across), Tara (ferryboat), to the lord of sacrifices, the one who has fled (or rushed in). * Obeisance to the carrier of sacrifices, religious gifts, the goal of penance ( Tapya ) and the (scorching) Sun-god. Hail to the shore (of the ocean of Samsara?) and the excellent Lord of lightnings. Obeisance to the bestower of cooked food, Lord of cooked food, one born of cooked food, the thousand-headed and thousand-footed lord. Obeisance to him with thousand tridents lifted up, to the thousand-eyed, one in the form of a boy, or one assuming the form of a boy. Obeisance to the protector of children, one sporting with children, the pure and the enlightened, the agitator and the unwoundable. Obeisance to the one whose tresses are marked by waves, the one of unbound tresses, the one abiding by six pres¬ cribed rites, the one engaged in three-fold rites. Obeisance to the one who makes people of different castes and stages of life duly function separately. Obeisance to loud sound, one worthy of proclamation, who is Kalakala (the murmuring sound). Obeisance to the one with white and reddish brown eyes, the one with black and red eyes* the one bestower of virtue, wealth, love and salvation. Obeisance to slaughter and the slaughterer. Obeisance to Samkhya, to the master of Samkhya and Yoga. Obeisance to Rathya, Virathya and to one interested in crossroads. Obeisance to the one with a deer-skin for upper gar¬ ment; to the one wearing a serpent for sacred thread, O Tsana, O destroyer of Indra. O green-haired one, obeisance be to you. O Kama, bestower of desires, destroyer of the god of Love, slayer of the haughty and arrogant, Sarva (all in all), O bestower of all, omniscient and twilight red, obeisance be to

verses.sanskrit: यः कुर्याद् उपवासं च सत्यशौचपरायणः सौत्रामणिफलं चास्य सम्भवत्यविचारितम्
verses.transliteration: yaḥ kuryād upavāsaṃ ca satyaśaucaparāyaṇaḥ sautrāmaṇiphalaṃ cāsya sambhavatyavicāritam
verses.translation: O powerful, mighty-armed one, and highly powerful, lustrous, great cloud, excellent-visioned great Kala, obeisance be to you. (Obeisance to) perpetual ascetic with stout and worn out limbs and matted hair, to one wearing bark garments and deer-skin, to one with matted hair resembling blazing fire and the sun, to one clad in bark garments and deer skin. Obeisance be to one resembling a thousand suns. O one having hundreds of maddening revolutions, O one with tresses half filled with the waters of Gahga, O Candra- varta, Yugavarta, Meghavarta, obeisance be to you. You are the cooked food, the creator, the bestower, and the maker of food; you are the person cooking food. Obeis¬ ance to cook and enjoyer of the cooked food. O lord, you are the lord of chief of Devas and the four-fold living beings, viz. the viviparous, oviparous, the sweat- You are Brahma, the creator of the mobile and immo- The Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas, Sudras and people of inferior castes worship you alone. The clusters of clouds sing about you by their rattling and roaring thunder. You are the year, seasons, months, fortnights, Kalas, Kasthas, Nimcsas, Yugas, stars and planets. You are the hump of bulls, the peak of mountains, the lion among beasts, Tarksya (Garuda) among birds, and Ananta among serpents. You are the ocean of milk among oceans, bow among mechanical devices, thunderbolt among weapons, and truth among holy vows. You are desire, hatred, passion, delusion, infirmity, mental control, restraint of sense organs, enterprise, fortitude, greed, love, fury, success, and failure. You are the mace-bearer, the discharger of arrows, the wielder of Khatvanga, the holder of Jharjhara (drum or cymbols). You chop, pierce, strike, leak and annihilate. You are the holy rite (piety) with ten characteristics. You are wealth, love, Indra, oceans, rivers, puddles and lakes. You are the beginning, end and the middle; you are the Gayatri and Omkara mantra; you are green, red, black, blue, You are tawny-coloured, dove-coloured, dark-blue, and gold-semened; hence you are known as having good colour. You have names consisting of good letters; -you are fond of gold; You are, Indra, Yama, Varuna, Kubera and You arc well-winged Brahman; you are Satarudriya among Yajumantras. You are the holiest among holy, the most auspicious of the auspicious. You are the huge mountain, and the little one. You are the tree, the individual soul and atom. You are the Sattva Rajas and the Tamas Guna; you are the creation. You are (the vital airs such as) Prana, Apana Saman, Udana and Vyana; you arc the wink of the eyes; you are their expansion and stretching. You are of red-complcxioned body, wielder of a mace (gada) and have curved fangs; you have a huge face and huge belly. You are white-haired and green-moustached. You have three eyes and hair lifted up. You are the parts of dance, song and music; you are fond ofsinging and playing on instruments; you are Maty a (fish); you arc watery, water and conducive to watery life. You are speed, time, Kali and Kala. You are improper time, propitious period and bad (famine-like) time as well as ■ the destroyer of Kala. You are death, decline and end and the destroyer of the earth. You are the Samvartaka fire (annihilating the universe) and clouds of final dissolution. You are Ghat a (a duration of tmt) Ghatika (master of Ghata), Ghanfika (having small bells?), Cuddolabala (having the strength in swinging locks of hair). You You are Tar ana (one that takes across), Taraka (liber¬ ator), Sarvabhuta-Satarana (liberator of all living beings); you are Dha.tr (creator), Vidhdlr (dispenser of destiny) and the pre¬ server of living beings; you are the supporter of all. You are austerity, the Brahman, truth, celibacy, straight-forwardness, the Atman and the maker of all living be¬ ings, the living being, the spirit, the source of everything that was, is and will be.

verses.sanskrit: ऋग्वेदजापी ऋग्वेदी साम वा सामपारगः । यजुर्वेदी यजुर्जप्त्वा लभते फलम् उत्तमम्
verses.transliteration: ṛgvedajāpī ṛgvedī sāma vā sāmapāragaḥ / yajurvedī yajurjaptvā labhate phalam uttamam
verses.translation: You are Bhuh, Bhuvah, Svar, the origin (of the universe); you are the great Lord, liana, the surveyor. You are the quies¬ cent; hard to be subdued and the destroyer of teeth. You are Brahmavarta, Suravarta, and Kamavarta. Obeisance be to you. You are the destroyer of Kama's body; you are fond of the pollen powder of the Karnikara flower. You have a moon-like face and also a. terrible one. You are pleasant-faced, wry-faced, faceless, four-faced, multi¬ faced, and always face to face with the enemy in the battle. You are gold-wombed, a big bird (a vulture) andean ocean. You are the greatest and (the most) immense being. \ou are the destroyer of evil, chastiser of the wicked, the wielder of the rod of punishment and fond of battles. You are the best of bulls, the rider of a bull, the bull- vehicled one. You are the promulgator of Dharma, the creator of Dharma and foremost among the experts in Dharma. You are the protector of the worlds and the winner You are soft spoken (and of lovable traits), the moon, the subduer. You are chilliness and heat, an unquenchable thirst. You are the mental worries and physical ailments, the You are bearable, the sacrifice, the deer-hunter, the You are a holder of the rod (of chastisement), the wielder of a staff, adorned with staff, and tonsured head. You arc imbiber of poison, drinker of nectar, drinker of wine, drinker of milk and Soma juice. You are the imbiber of honey, ghee and everything; you are very powerful; you are carried by a horselike bull; you are the bull (strong person), with eves like those of a bull. You are known as Vrsabha (a bull); you are honoured by the people; the moon and the sun are your eyes; Brahma is your heart; you are fire and water; you are the lord achievable by pious rites. O Siva, neither Brahma nor Visnu nor the ancient sages can understand your greatness precisely. Your subtle forms do not come within the ken of my vision. Protect me with them as a father does to his son. The Lord is always sympathetic and favourable to his devotees. And I am always devoted to you. May that lord be always my protector—the Lord w o after devouring (withdrawing at the time of Pralaya) thousands of men, abides all alone at the bottom of the ocean. nii., ' ~ b f Isaace to the Yogic soul whom persons of impartial Obeisance to them all, for ever, who do not cry and who, stationed in the body, make the living beings cry. Obeis¬ ance be to them who are delighted and who delight all. Perpetual obeisance to them, whc arc stationed in the ocean, in the river, in the fort, on the mountains, in the caves, at the roots of trees, in the cowpens, in the dense forests, in crossroads, in the streets, in the quadrangular courtyards, in the assemblies and in the midst of the sun and the moon, in the rays of the sun and the moon, who have gone to the nether- worlds and beyond them. Perpetual obeisance to those who are subtle, gross, lean or short. O Lord, you are all in all; you pervade all; you are the lord and the inner soul of all living beings. Therefore you were not invited to the sacrifice. Since it is you alone who are worshipped with sacri¬ fices with various monetary gifts and since you alone are the doer of everything, you were not invited. O Lord, I was deluded by your subtle Maya that you were not invited. O Lord ofDevas, be pleased with me. You alone are my refuge, my goal, my foundation. I have no other goal or resort." After eulogising the great lord thus, the Prajapati stopped. The delighted lord spoke then to Daksa: "O Daksa of good rites, I am pleased with this hymn of vours; of what avail is much talk. You will come near me. Then the lord of the three worlds, conversant with the appropriate use of words spoke consoling words and said
