verses.hindi: पुष्कर द्वीप है। इसंके सम्बन्ध में भी कहते हैं, सुनिये । पुष्कर द्वीप से क्षीरतागर चारों ओर घिरा हुआ है । यह शाकद्वीप से दुगुना बड़ा है। इस द्वीप में शोभा सम्पन्न एक महाशिल नाम का पव॑त है, जिसके समुन्नत शलशिखर मणियों द्वारा चित्रित हैं। इस द्वीप के पूर्वार्द भाग में इसका एक विचित्र सानुदेश (चोटी) स्थित है, जिसका घेरा या विस्तार पचीस हजार योजन का है और ऊंचाई चौंतीस हजार योजन की। दीपाद्ध के परिमाण के बराबर एक उत्तम मानस पव॑त है ।१०४-१०५। जो समुद्र तट पर उगे हुए नवीन चन्द्रमा की भाँति वर्तमान है। यह पचास हजार थोजन ऊँचा है और इसका घेरा या विस्तार भी उतना ही है। इस द्वीप के पश्चात् अद्ध भाग में पृथ्वी को घारण करनेवाला मानस पव्व॑त है ।!०९-११०। यह एक ही विशालकाय शिखर है, जो देश भेद से दो भागों में विभक्त है। मीठे जलवालेसमुद्र से यह घिरा हुआ है।
verses.wordMeaning: He taught the first branch (compilation) to Bodha, the second to Agnimathara, the third to Parasara and the last to Yajnavalkya.
verses.commentary: Sense: He taught the first branch (compilation) to Bodha, the second to Agnimathara, the third to Parasara and the last to Yajnavalkya.

verses.sanskrit: ततः समीपगा वृद्धा तस्य वृन्दस्य भारत । स्वाध्यायनिरता विप्रा दृष्टास्तैः पापकर्मभिः
verses.transliteration: tataḥ samīpagā vṛddhā tasya vṛndasya bhārata / svādhyāyaniratā viprā dṛṣṭāstaiḥ pāpakarmabhiḥ
verses.translation: The excellent Brahmana Indrapramati taught the blessed and renowned Markandeya one of the Samhitas.
verses.hindi: पुष्करव्वीप के विस्तार के अनुरूप ही उसका भी विस्तार है। इस द्वीप में पवित्र और शुभकारक दो देश हैं । ये दोनों , देश मानस पर्वत के निम्नभाग में मण्डलाकार अवस्थित है। मानस के बाहर जो देश है वह महावीत कहलाता है ओर जो देश भीतर है, वह घातकी खण्ड के नाम से प्रसिद्ध है।१११-११३। वहाँ लोग दस हजार वर्ष तक जीते हैं। वहाँ के लोगों को मानसी सिद्धि प्राप्त है। वे सभी नीरोग तथा सुखी
verses.wordMeaning: The excellent Brahmana Indrapramati taught the blessed and renowned Markandeya one of the Samhitas.
verses.commentary: Sense: The excellent Brahmana Indrapramati taught the blessed and renowned Markandeya one of the Samhitas.

verses.sanskrit: ऊचुस्ते तु समूहेन ब्राह्मणांस्तपसि स्थितान् । अस्माकं स्वामिनः सर्वे तिष्ठन्ते तीर्थमध्यतः । ते प्रस्थाप्या महाभागाः सर्वथैव त्वरान्विताः
verses.transliteration: ūcuste tu samūhena brāhmaṇāṃstapasi sthitān / asmākaṃ svāminaḥ sarve tiṣṭhante tīrthamadhyataḥ / te prasthāpyā mahābhāgāḥ sarvathaiva tvarānvitāḥ
verses.translation: Markandeya of great fame, taught his eldest son Satyasravas. Satyasravas taught to Satyahita.
verses.hindi: हैं। उन दोनों देशों के लोग आयु तथा रूप में एक समान ही हैं ।११४-११५। वहाँ ऊँच-तीच का कोई भेंद नहीं है । रूपस्वभाव में सभी बराबर हैं। वंहाँन वंचकता है, न वंचना है, ह डाह, न चोरी, न भय, न एकोनपआशत्तमोश्च्यायः ३५७
verses.wordMeaning: Markandeya of great fame, taught his eldest son Satyasravas. Satyasravas taught to Satyahita.
verses.commentary: Sense: Markandeya of great fame, taught his eldest son Satyasravas. Satyasravas taught to Satyahita.

verses.sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तेषां सर्वे चैव त्वरान्विताः । जग्मुस्ते नर्मदाकक्षं दृष्ट्वा रेवां द्विजोत्तमाः
verses.transliteration: tacchrutvā vacanaṃ teṣāṃ sarve caiva tvarānvitāḥ / jagmuste narmadākakṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā revāṃ dvijottamāḥ
verses.translation: That master (of Vedic Lore) taught his son Satyasri who was truthful, noble-souled and eagerly devoted to truthful¬ ness and piety.
verses.hindi: सत्यानुतं न तत्रास्ति धर्माधमों तथेव च्। वर्णाअमाणां बार्ता वा पाशुपालयं वणिक्क्रिया.
verses.wordMeaning: That master (of Vedic Lore) taught his son Satyasri who was truthful, noble-souled and eagerly devoted to truthful¬ ness and piety.
verses.commentary: Sense: That master (of Vedic Lore) taught his son Satyasri who was truthful, noble-souled and eagerly devoted to truthful¬ ness and piety.

verses.sanskrit: ततः केचित्स्तुवन्त्यन्ये जय देवि नमो ऽस्तु ते
verses.transliteration: tataḥ kecitstuvantyanye jaya devi namo 'stu te
verses.translation: Satyairi had three very brilliant disciples. They were highly learned and very anxious to learn scriptures.
verses.hindi: न्रयी विद्या दण्डनीतिः शुक्षूषा शल्यमेव च । वर्षद्ये सर्वेमेतत्पुष्करस्य न बिद्यते न तत्र नयो वर्ष च शीतोष्णं वा न विद्यते  उज्हूज्जान्युदकान्यत्र गिरिप्रश्न (स्र) वणाति च
verses.wordMeaning: Satyairi had three very brilliant disciples. They were highly learned and very anxious to learn scriptures.
verses.commentary: Sense: Satyairi had three very brilliant disciples. They were highly learned and very anxious to learn scriptures.

verses.sanskrit: नमो ऽस्तु ते सिद्धगणैर् निषेविते नमो ऽस्तु ते सर्वपवित्रमङ्गले । नमो ऽस्तु ते विप्रसहस्रसेविते नमो ऽस्तु रुद्राङ्गसमुद्भवे वरे
verses.transliteration: namo 'stu te siddhagaṇair niṣevite namo 'stu te sarvapavitramaṅgale / namo 'stu te viprasahasrasevite namo 'stu rudrāṅgasamudbhave vare
verses.translation: Sakalya was the first among them. Another was Rathantara, The third was Bharadvaja, son of Baskala. The three were the expounders of the branches of that Veda.
verses.hindi: उत्तराणां कुरूणां तुल्यकालो जनः सदा । सर्वत्र सुसुखस्तत्र जराक्लमविवर्जित: १२० इत्येष धातकीखण्डे महावीते तथेव च । आनृपुर्व्याद्विधिः कृत्स्नः पुष्करस्य प्रकीतित।. ४१२१ स्वादृदकेनोदधिना पुष्करः परिवारितः । विस्तरान्मण्डलाच्चेव पुष्करस्थ तथेव च...
verses.wordMeaning: Sakalya was the first among them. Another was Rathantara, The third was Bharadvaja, son of Baskala. The three were the expounders of the branches of that Veda.
verses.commentary: Sense: Sakalya was the first among them. Another was Rathantara, The third was Bharadvaja, son of Baskala. The three were the expounders of the branches of that Veda.

verses.sanskrit: नमो ऽस्तु ते सर्वपवित्रपावने नमो ऽस्तु ते देवि वरप्रदे शिवे । नमामि ते शीतजले सुखप्रदे सरिद्वरे पापहरे विचित्रिते
verses.transliteration: namo 'stu te sarvapavitrapāvane namo 'stu te devi varaprade śive / namāmi te śītajale sukhaprade saridvare pāpahare vicitrite
verses.translation: In the horse-sacrifice of Janaka the Brahmana Sakalya (also known as) Devamitra, perished as he was too proud of his knowledge. 1
verses.hindi: एवं द्वीपसमुद्राणां वृद्धिज्षेंया परस्परात् । अपां चैव. समुद्रेकात्समुद्रा इति संज्ञिताः ऋषदइत्येव ऋषिणो वृष: शक्तिप्रबन्धने । रतिप्रबन्धनात्सिद्धं पर्षत्वं तेन तेषु तत् .
verses.wordMeaning: In the horse-sacrifice of Janaka the Brahmana Sakalya (also known as) Devamitra, perished as he was too proud of his knowledge. 1
verses.commentary: Sense: In the horse-sacrifice of Janaka the Brahmana Sakalya (also known as) Devamitra, perished as he was too proud of his knowledge. 1

verses.sanskrit: अनेकभूतौघसुसेविताङ्गे गन्धर्वयक्षोरगपाविताङ्गे । महागजौघैर् महिषैर् वराहैर् आपीयसे तोयमहोर्मिमाले
verses.transliteration: anekabhūtaughasusevitāṅge gandharvayakṣoragapāvitāṅge / mahāgajaughair mahiṣair varāhair āpīyase toyamahormimāle
verses.translation: How did that sage, too proud of his knowledge, perish? How did the argument arise in the horse-sacrifice of Janaka?
verses.hindi: बल-प्रयोग. न दण्ड, न लोभ हैं और न दान आदि की समस्‍्या। पुष्करद्वीप के दोनों देशों में सच झूठ, घ॒र्म-अधर्म, वर्णाश्रम विषयक बात, पशुपालन, क्रय-विक्रय, त्रयी विद्या, दण्डनीति, सेवावृत्ति और दुर्वाक्‍्य या शस्त्र प्रयोग की समस्या नहीं है। वहाँ न नदी है, न वर्षा होती है, न गमी-सर्दी है, न उन्द्धिज्ज, न जल और झरने हैं ।११६-११९ वहाँ का काल सदा उत्तर कुरे की तरह रहता है । वहाँ सवंत्र सुख है : लोगों को
verses.wordMeaning: How did that sage, too proud of his knowledge, perish? How did the argument arise in the horse-sacrifice of Janaka?
verses.commentary: Sense: How did that sage, too proud of his knowledge, perish? How did the argument arise in the horse-sacrifice of Janaka?

verses.sanskrit: नमामि ते सर्ववरे सुखप्रदे विमोचयास्मानघपाशबद्धान्
verses.transliteration: namāmi te sarvavare sukhaprade vimocayāsmānaghapāśabaddhān
verses.translation: Why did the argument arise at all and with whom? Narrate all this in the manner that happened, as far as you know.
verses.hindi: न थकाबट आती हैं ओर न बुढ़ापा ही  पुष्करद्दीप के महावीतर और धातकी खण्ड को इस श्रकार हमने क्रम से सम्पूर्ण वर्णण कर दिया। सुस्वाद दशध्ििसागर से यह पुष्कर सागर घिरा हुआ है। विस्तार और घेरे में यह पृष्कर द्वीप के ही बराबर है। १२० -१२२। इस प्रकार सातों द्वीप सात समुद्रों से घिरे हुए हैं। हीपों को जो समुद्र घेरे हुए हैं, वे उसीके बराबर हैं। ढीपों और समुद्रों की परस्पर वृद्धि या संस्थान इसी प्रकार का होता है। जल का समुद्रेक या वृद्धि होने के कारण सागरों का नाम समुद्र पढ़ा है !२३-१२४। चातुवंर्ण प्रजा और ऋषिगण देश में निवास करते हैं इसलिए देश को वर्ष कहते हैं। यह वंष प्रजाजन को सुख देनेवाला होता है। जिस प्रकार ऋष् धातु से ऋषि शब्द बना है, उसी प्रकार शक्ति प्रबन्धन बोधक बुध धातु से वर्ष पद सिद्ध होता है। वृष शब्द से ही “वर्ष” हुआ है।१२५-१२६! शुक्‍्लपक्ष में
verses.wordMeaning: Why did the argument arise at all and with whom? Narrate all this in the manner that happened, as far as you know.
verses.commentary: Sense: Why did the argument arise at all and with whom? Narrate all this in the manner that happened, as far as you know.

verses.sanskrit: भ्रमन्ति तावन्नरकेषु मर्त्या यावत्तवाम्भो नहि संश्रयन्ति । स्पृष्टं करैश्चन्द्रमसो रवेश्चेत् तद्देवि दद्यात् परमं पदं तु
verses.transliteration: bhramanti tāvannarakeṣu martyā yāvattavāmbho nahi saṃśrayanti / spṛṣṭaṃ karaiścandramaso raveścet taddevi dadyāt paramaṃ padaṃ tu
verses.translation: At the horse-sacrifice of Janaka there was a great congregation of sages. Thousands of sages, desirous of witness¬ ing the sacrifice of the saintly king Janaka, came there from various places.
verses.hindi: चन्द्रमा की वृद्धि के अनुसार समुद्र बढ़ता है और क्ृष्णपक्ष में जब चन्द्रमा क्षीण होते हैं, तब समुद्र भी घटता है। सम॒द्र स्वतः अपने को जल से भरता है और जब उनका जल घटता है, तब भी उसीपें
verses.wordMeaning: At the horse-sacrifice of Janaka there was a great congregation of sages. Thousands of sages, desirous of witness¬ ing the sacrifice of the saintly king Janaka, came there from various places.
verses.commentary: Sense: At the horse-sacrifice of Janaka there was a great congregation of sages. Thousands of sages, desirous of witness¬ ing the sacrifice of the saintly king Janaka, came there from various places.

verses.sanskrit: अनेकसंसारभयार्दितानां पापैरनेकैर् अभिवेष्टितानाम् । गतिस्त्वमम्भोजसमानवक्त्रे द्वन्द्वैरनेकैरभिसंवृतानाम्
verses.transliteration: anekasaṃsārabhayārditānāṃ pāpairanekair abhiveṣṭitānām / gatistvamambhojasamānavaktre dvandvairanekairabhisaṃvṛtānām
verses.translation: On seeing the Brahmanas assembled there, a desire to know more about them arose in him. "Who is the most excellent
verses.hindi: शश८ द बायुपुराणम् द्विरापत्वात्स्तृता दीपा: सर्वतश्योदकावुताः । उदकस्या55धान॑ यस्मात्तस्मादुदधिदच्यते ॥
verses.wordMeaning: On seeing the Brahmanas assembled there, a desire to know more about them arose in him. "Who is the most excellent
verses.commentary: Sense: On seeing the Brahmanas assembled there, a desire to know more about them arose in him. "Who is the most excellent

verses.sanskrit: नद्यश्च पूता विमला भवन्ति त्वां देवि सम्प्राप्य न संशयो ऽत्र । दुःखातुराणामभयं ददासि शिष्टैर् अनेकैर् अभिपूजितासि
verses.transliteration: nadyaśca pūtā vimalā bhavanti tvāṃ devi samprāpya na saṃśayo 'tra / duḥkhāturāṇāmabhayaṃ dadāsi śiṣṭair anekair abhipūjitāsi
verses.translation: He collected a thousand cows, more than a thousand gold pieces and gems, slaves and villages. He then announced to the sages: "O excellent and blessed ones, I bow to you all with my head.
verses.hindi: तस्मिन्निवसति ब्रह्मा साध्येः साथ प्रजापति: । उपासते तत्र देवास्त्रयस्त्रिशन्‍्मह्िभिः ॥ द
verses.wordMeaning: He collected a thousand cows, more than a thousand gold pieces and gems, slaves and villages. He then announced to the sages: "O excellent and blessed ones, I bow to you all with my head.
verses.commentary: Sense: He collected a thousand cows, more than a thousand gold pieces and gems, slaves and villages. He then announced to the sages: "O excellent and blessed ones, I bow to you all with my head.

verses.sanskrit: विण्मूत्रदेहाश्च निमग्नदेहा भ्रमन्ति तावन्नरकेषु मर्त्याः । महाबलध्वस्ततरङ्गभङ्गं जलं न यावत्तव संस्पृशन्ति
verses.transliteration: viṇmūtradehāśca nimagnadehā bhramanti tāvannarakeṣu martyāḥ / mahābaladhvastataraṅgabhaṅgaṃ jalaṃ na yāvattava saṃspṛśanti
verses.translation: O excellent Brahmanas, the wealth that is brought here is offered to the most excellent sage among you. It is offer¬ ed as the price of your learning".
verses.hindi: स तत्र पुज्यते चेव देवदेबोत्तमोत्तमः - १३६ जस्बूद्वीपात्म्रवंतन्ते रत्नानि विविधानि च। द्वीपेषु तेषु सर्वेषु प्रजानां हि क्रमात्विह... समाकर रह जाता है। वरतंनः में रखा हुआ जल आग पर चढ़ाये जाने से जेसे खौलकर बढ़ जाता है, उसी प्रकार समद्र का जल भी बढ़ता है। शुक्ल और कृष्णपक्ष में चन्द्रमा के उदय और अस्त के हिसाब से नियमपुवंक--न कम न. अधिक जल बढ़ा करता है। सारांश यह है कि, चन्द्रमा को क्षय-बृद्धि के अनुसार ही समुद्र के जल का:भी क्षय और बृद्धि होती है ।१२४-१३०। पर्वों में समद्र का जल एक सौ पनद्रह अंग्रुल
verses.wordMeaning: O excellent Brahmanas, the wealth that is brought here is offered to the most excellent sage among you. It is offer¬ ed as the price of your learning".
verses.commentary: Sense: O excellent Brahmanas, the wealth that is brought here is offered to the most excellent sage among you. It is offer¬ ed as the price of your learning".

verses.sanskrit: म्लेच्छाः पुलिन्दास्त्वथ यातुधानाः पिबन्ति ये ऽंभस्तव देवि पुण्यम् । ते ऽपि प्रमुच्यन्ति भयाच्च घोरात्किमत्र विप्रा भवपाशभीताः
verses.transliteration: mlecchāḥ pulindāstvatha yātudhānāḥ pibanti ye 'ṃbhastava devi puṇyam / te 'pi pramucyanti bhayācca ghorātkimatra viprā bhavapāśabhītāḥ
verses.translation: On hearing the words of Janaka, those sages, experts in the Vedas, saw and coveted the vast wealth. With full con¬ fidence in their knowledge, they began to challenge one
verses.hindi: तक बढ़कर घटा करता: है, ऐसा देखा गया है। दोनों ओर जल बहने के कारण और सभी तरफ जल से घिरे रहने के कारण द्वीपोंकी “द्वीप” संज्ञा पड़ी है। जिस कारण समुद्र में जल रहा करता है, इसीलिए उसे उदधि कहते हैं। बिना पर्व गाँठ या स्तर वाले गिरि कहलाते हैं और पर्ववाले पर्वत कहलाते हैं। इसी नियम के अनुसार प्लक्षद्वीप में जो गोमेद है, वह पर्वत है ।१३१०१३२। शाल्मलढ्वीप में शाल्मलि नामक
verses.wordMeaning: On hearing the words of Janaka, those sages, experts in the Vedas, saw and coveted the vast wealth. With full con¬ fidence in their knowledge, they began to challenge one
verses.commentary: Sense: On hearing the words of Janaka, those sages, experts in the Vedas, saw and coveted the vast wealth. With full con¬ fidence in their knowledge, they began to challenge one

verses.sanskrit: सरांसि नद्यः क्षयमभ्युपेता घोरे युगे ऽस्मिन्कलिनावसृष्टे । त्वं भ्राजसे देवि जलौघपूर्णा दिवीव नक्षत्रपथे च गङ्गा
verses.transliteration: sarāṃsi nadyaḥ kṣayamabhyupetā ghore yuge 'sminkalināvasṛṣṭe / tvaṃ bhrājase devi jalaughapūrṇā divīva nakṣatrapathe ca gaṅgā
verses.translation: With their minds hovering round the wealth, one said,
verses.hindi: महावक्ष पूज्य है। कुशद्वीप में कुछ नामक तृण है, अतः उसीके नाम पर वह द्वीप कुशद्वीप कहलाता है क्रौंच द्वीप के मध्यदेश में क्रॉंच नामक पहाड़ है। श्ाकद्वीप में शाकवुक्ष है, अतः वह छ्ाकद्वीप कहलाता है ।१३३-१३४। पुष्करद्वीप में एक बटव॒ुक्ष है, जिसकी, वन्दना सब किया करते हैं। यहाँ तरिभवनेश्बर महादेव और ब्रह्मा पूजित होते हैं। वहाँ साध्यों के साथ प्रजापति ब्रह्मा निवास करते हैं और तैंतीस :महर्षियों के साथ देवगण उपासना किया करते हैं । वहाँ. देवों के द्वारा देवाधिदेव ब्रह्मा पूणित होते हैं ।.३५-१३६। -जम्बूदीप में विविध. भाँति के रत्न उत्पन्न होते हैं। उस समस्त द्वीपों
verses.wordMeaning: With their minds hovering round the wealth, one said,
verses.commentary: Sense: With their minds hovering round the wealth, one said,

verses.sanskrit: तव प्रासादाद्वरदे विशिष्टे कालं यथेमं परिपालयित्वा । यास्याम मोक्षं तव सुप्रसादाद्वयं यथा त्वं कुरु नः प्रसादम्
verses.transliteration: tava prāsādādvarade viśiṣṭe kālaṃ yathemaṃ paripālayitvā / yāsyāma mokṣaṃ tava suprasādādvayaṃ yathā tvaṃ kuru naḥ prasādam
verses.translation: There was a great scholar Yajnavalkya, son of Brahmavaha. He was highly brilliant, a great saint. He was born of the very body of Brahma. The most excellent among the knowers of Brahman, he told his disciple clearly, O, take away this wealth. O dear one, take this p
verses.hindi: एकोनपश्चाशक्तमोष्ष्यायः क्‍ रे५र्द
verses.wordMeaning: There was a great scholar Yajnavalkya, son of Brahmavaha. He was highly brilliant, a great saint. He was born of the very body of Brahma. The most excellent among the knowers of Brahman, he told his disciple clearly, O, take away this wealth. O dear one, take this p
verses.commentary: Sense: There was a great scholar Yajnavalkya, son of Brahmavaha. He was highly brilliant, a great saint. He was born of the very body of Brahma. The most excellent among the knowers of Brahman, he told his disciple clearly, O, take away this wealth. O dear one, take this p

verses.sanskrit: त्वामाश्रिता ये शरणं गताश्च गतिस्त्वमम्बेव पितेव पुत्रान् । त्वत्पालिता यावदिमं सुघोरं कालं त्वनावृष्टिहतं क्षिपामः
verses.transliteration: tvāmāśritā ye śaraṇaṃ gatāśca gatistvamambeva piteva putrān / tvatpālitā yāvadimaṃ sughoraṃ kālaṃ tvanāvṛṣṭihataṃ kṣipāmaḥ
verses.translation: Thereupon that vast concourse of Brahmanas became agitated like the ocean at the time of dissolution. The cool and calm Yajnavalkya smilingly told them:
verses.hindi: सबंशो ब्रह्मचयेंण सत्येन च दमेन च । आरोग्यायु: प्रमाणाद्धि द्विगुणं च समन्‍्ततः . एतस्समिन्पुष्करद्वीपे यदुक्‍्त वर्षकद् यम । गोपायति प्रजास्तत्र स्वयं सज्जनमण्डिताः .. ॥
verses.wordMeaning: Thereupon that vast concourse of Brahmanas became agitated like the ocean at the time of dissolution. The cool and calm Yajnavalkya smilingly told them:
verses.commentary: Sense: Thereupon that vast concourse of Brahmanas became agitated like the ocean at the time of dissolution. The cool and calm Yajnavalkya smilingly told them:

verses.sanskrit: एवं स्तुता तदा देवी नर्मदा सरितां वरा । प्रत्यक्षा सा परा मूर्तिर् ब्राह्मणानां युधिष्ठिर
verses.transliteration: evaṃ stutā tadā devī narmadā saritāṃ varā / pratyakṣā sā parā mūrtir brāhmaṇānāṃ yudhiṣṭhira
verses.translation: "O learned ones, O speakers of truth, do not be angry. Trying to know one another, we shall argue in the proper manner".
verses.hindi: ईश्वरो दण्डसुथ्म्य ब्रह्मा त्रिभुवनेश्वरः । सविष्णुः सशिवो देवः स पिता स वितामहः..
verses.wordMeaning: "O learned ones, O speakers of truth, do not be angry. Trying to know one another, we shall argue in the proper manner".
verses.commentary: Sense: "O learned ones, O speakers of truth, do not be angry. Trying to know one another, we shall argue in the proper manner".

verses.sanskrit: श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: पठन्ति ये स्तोत्रमिदं नरेन्द्र शृण्वन्ति भक्त्या परया प्रशान्ताः । ते यान्ति रुद्रं वृषसंयुतेन यानेन दिव्याम्बरभूषिताङ्गाः
verses.transliteration: śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: paṭhanti ye stotramidaṃ narendra śṛṇvanti bhaktyā parayā praśāntāḥ / te yānti rudraṃ vṛṣasaṃyutena yānena divyāmbarabhūṣitāṅgāḥ
verses.translation: Then their arguments took various turns. They dis¬ cussed thousands of important topics on the subtle subject of philosophy. The secular, Vedic and spiritual topics were also discussed. All branches of leaning were touched. In the course of argument some cursed and some exhibited their excellent qualities. The kings were excluded from discussion. Thus the Brahmanas continued discussion for the sake of wealth.
verses.hindi: परेण पुष्करस्याथ आवुत्यायः (यं) स्थितो महान् । स्वादूदकः समुद्रस्तु समस्तात्परिवेष्टित: परेण तस्य महती दृश्यते लोकसंस्थितिः। का्चनी दविग्रुणा भुमिः सर्वा चेकशिलोपसा ..
verses.wordMeaning: Then their arguments took various turns. They dis¬ cussed thousands of important topics on the subtle subject of philosophy. The secular, Vedic and spiritual topics were also discussed. All branches of leaning were touched.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Then their arguments took various turns. They dis¬ cussed thousands of important topics on the subtle subject of philosophy. The secular, Vedic and spiritual topics were also discussed. All branches of leaning were touched.…

verses.sanskrit: ये स्तोत्रम् एतत् सततं जपन्ति स्नात्वा च तोयेन तु नर्मदायाः । तेभ्यो ऽन्तकाले सरिदुत्तमेयं गतिं विशुद्धामचिराद् ददाति
verses.transliteration: ye stotram etat satataṃ japanti snātvā ca toyena tu narmadāyāḥ / tebhyo 'ntakāle sariduttameyaṃ gatiṃ viśuddhāmacirād dadāti
verses.translation: The sages ranged on one side. Yajnavalkya stood on the other side. Thereafter, all those sages were individually questioned by the intelligent Yajnavalkya. They however failed to reply.
verses.hindi: “तस्मात्परेण शेलस्तु मर्यादान्ते तु मण्डलस् । प्रकाशश्राप्रकाशश्व लोकालोकः स उच्यते...
verses.wordMeaning: The sages ranged on one side. Yajnavalkya stood on the other side. Thereafter, all those sages were individually questioned by the intelligent Yajnavalkya. They however failed to reply.
verses.commentary: Sense: The sages ranged on one side. Yajnavalkya stood on the other side. Thereafter, all those sages were individually questioned by the intelligent Yajnavalkya. They however failed to reply.

verses.sanskrit: प्रातः समुत्थाय तथा शयानो यः कीर्तयेतानुदिनं स्तवेन्द्रम् । देहक्षयं स्वे सलिले ददाति समाश्रयं तस्य महानुभाव
verses.transliteration: prātaḥ samutthāya tathā śayāno yaḥ kīrtayetānudinaṃ stavendram / dehakṣayaṃ sve salile dadāti samāśrayaṃ tasya mahānubhāva
verses.translation: After defeating the sages in argument, the sage Yajna¬ valkya of great splendour, a repository of Brahmanic knowl- edge, spoke to Sakalya who had initiated discussion:
verses.hindi: आलोकस्तस्य चार्वाक्तु निरालोकस्ततः परम् । योजनानां सहस्नाणि दश तस्योच्छयः स्मृत: ताबांश्व विस्तरस्तस्य पृथिव्यां कामगश्च सः। आलोके लोकशब्दस्तु निरालोके सलोकता,॥ हु
verses.wordMeaning: After defeating the sages in argument, the sage Yajna¬ valkya of great splendour, a repository of Brahmanic knowl- edge, spoke to Sakalya who had initiated discussion:
verses.commentary: Sense: After defeating the sages in argument, the sage Yajna¬ valkya of great splendour, a repository of Brahmanic knowl- edge, spoke to Sakalya who had initiated discussion:

verses.sanskrit: पापैर् विमुक्ता दिवि मोदमानाः सम्भोगिनश्चैव तु नान्यथा च
verses.transliteration: pāpair vimuktā divi modamānāḥ sambhoginaścaiva tu nānyathā ca
verses.translation: "O Sakalya, speak out what you have to say. Why are you sitting meditating quietly? Full of sluggishness and false prestige, you are like a pair of bellows inflated by wind".
verses.hindi: “लोकार्थ संमतो लोकों निरालोकस्तु बाह्मतः . १ ४६ : लोकबिस्तारमात्रं तु आलोकः सर्वतो बहिः। परिच्छिन्न: समन्‍्ताच्च उदकेनाउः्वृतश्व सः॥ . निरालोकात्परश्रापि अण्डसाव॒त्य तिष्ठति
verses.wordMeaning: "O Sakalya, speak out what you have to say. Why are you sitting meditating quietly? Full of sluggishness and false prestige, you are like a pair of bellows inflated by wind".
verses.commentary: Sense: "O Sakalya, speak out what you have to say. Why are you sitting meditating quietly? Full of sluggishness and false prestige, you are like a pair of bellows inflated by wind".

verses.sanskrit: प्रसन्ना नर्मदा देवी स्तोत्रेणानेन भारत । जलेनाप्यायितान् विप्रान् दक्षिणापथवाहिनी
verses.transliteration: prasannā narmadā devī stotreṇānena bhārata / jalenāpyāyitān viprān dakṣiṇāpathavāhinī
verses.translation: On being attacked thus Sakalya with his face and eyes red like copper due to anger, spoke to Yajnavalkya harshly m the presence of all sages:
verses.hindi: “अण्डस्यान्तस्त्विसे लोकाः सप्तद्वीपा च मेदिनी । भूलेको5थ भुवलोकः स्वलोकोथ महस्तथा में प्रजागण क्रमशः: सर्वंशता धारण करके ब्ह्मचयं, सत्य और दम के द्वारा आरोग्य तथा द्विगुण आयु प्राप्त करते हैं। इस पुष्करद्ीप में हमने जिन दों-देशोंवको बताया “है, उनकी रक्षा बहाँ-के साधु स्वभाव प्रजागण स्वयं करते -हैं ।३७-१३६। विष्णु, - शिव; सूर्य, और पितरों के साथ स्वयं ब्रह्मा दण्डविधान से वहाँ का शासन :करते हैं। वहाँ:वाले बिसा प्रयत्न के ही पघड्रस और बलशाली भोजन प्राप्त
verses.wordMeaning: On being attacked thus Sakalya with his face and eyes red like copper due to anger, spoke to Yajnavalkya harshly m the presence of all sages:
verses.commentary: Sense: On being attacked thus Sakalya with his face and eyes red like copper due to anger, spoke to Yajnavalkya harshly m the presence of all sages:

verses.sanskrit: अमृतत्वं तु वो दद्मि योगिभिर्यन्न गम्यते । दुर्लभं यत्सुरैः सर्वैर् मत्प्रसादाल् लभिष्यथ
verses.transliteration: amṛtatvaṃ tu vo dadmi yogibhiryanna gamyate / durlabhaṃ yatsuraiḥ sarvair matprasādāl labhiṣyatha
verses.translation: "Ignoring (abandoning) us as well as these excellent rahmanashke blades o f grass } y° u W i s h to seize alJ b
verses.hindi: करते हैं। यह पुष्करद्दीप स्वादु जलवाले समुद्र से घिरा हुआ है ।१४०-१४२। इसके आगे. एक बड़ी भारी : कांचनपुरी है, जहाँ की भूमि एक शिला की तरह सम और घनी बसी हुई । इसके आगे. सीमान्‍्त में.एक पव॑त है, फिर मंण्डेल है। उँसके बाद लोकालोक है, जिसकी एक दिशा में प्रकाश और ूसरी दिशा में अन्धकार है ।१४३-१४४॥ आलोक प्रब की दिशा में और अन्धकार पदिचिम:दिद्ां में है। यह दस ह॒जाश
verses.wordMeaning: "Ignoring (abandoning) us as well as these excellent rahmanashke blades o f grass } y° u W i s h to seize alJ b
verses.commentary: Sense: "Ignoring (abandoning) us as well as these excellent rahmanashke blades o f grass } y° u W i s h to seize alJ b

verses.sanskrit: इति ते ब्राह्मणा राजंल्लब्धा वरमनुत्तमम् । गमिष्यन्तः प्रीतचित्ता ददृशुश्चित्रम् अद्भुतम्
verses.transliteration: iti te brāhmaṇā rājaṃllabdhā varamanuttamam / gamiṣyantaḥ prītacittā dadṛśuścitram adbhutam
verses.translation: This has been the condition laid down by the saintly kingjanaka. Hence the wealth is being taken by me".
verses.hindi: योजन ऊँचा है। इसका विस्तार भी उतना ही है। प्रृथ्वी के बीच यह प्रवंत इच्छाधीन गति वाला है। 'इसकी जिस दिल्या में आलोक है उसीको लक्ष्य कर लोक शब्द बना है: अन्धकारवाले भाग की ओर भी ” लोक हैं। आलोक के ही कारण लोक हुआ है। अन्धकार बाहर-है। बाहर.में श्री जहाँ तक आलोक हैं, बहाँ तक लोकों का विस्तार है। इसके बाद जल के द्वारा सब ढेँका हुआ. है।। :निरालोक के बाद जो भाग  है, ग्हु अण्ड लोक मण्डल ब्रह्मा को ढेंके हुए है ।१४५-१४७। अण्ड- के मध्य में यही सातों द्वीप .बाली
verses.wordMeaning: This has been the condition laid down by the saintly kingjanaka. Hence the wealth is being taken by me".
verses.commentary: Sense: This has been the condition laid down by the saintly kingjanaka. Hence the wealth is being taken by me".

verses.sanskrit: श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: दृष्टास्तैः पुरुषाः पार्थ नर्मदातटसंस्थिताः । स्नानदेवार्चनासक्ताः पञ्च एव महाबलाः
verses.transliteration: śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: dṛṣṭāstaiḥ puruṣāḥ pārtha narmadātaṭasaṃsthitāḥ / snānadevārcanāsaktāḥ pañca eva mahābalāḥ
verses.translation: ct Now tell me the answers to these questions precisely". Then a great debate ensued between.the two experts in Brahman.
verses.hindi: पृथ्वी है, इसके अतिरिक्त, भूलोंक, भुवलोंक, महलोंक, जनलोक, तपोलोक और सत्यलोक - भी हैं-।.लोकों
verses.wordMeaning: ct Now tell me the answers to these questions precisely". Then a great debate ensued between.the two experts in Brahman.
verses.commentary: Sense: ct Now tell me the answers to these questions precisely". Then a great debate ensued between.the two experts in Brahman.

verses.sanskrit: ते दृष्टा ब्राह्मणैः सर्वैर्वेदवेदाङ्गपारगैः । संपृष्टास्तैर्महाराज यथा तदवधारय
verses.transliteration: te dṛṣṭā brāhmaṇaiḥ sarvairvedavedāṅgapāragaiḥ / saṃpṛṣṭāstairmahārāja yathā tadavadhāraya
verses.translation: Sakalya asked him more than a thousand questions. Yajnavalkya answered those all even as the sages were listening.
verses.hindi: ३६० ... ऑयूपुराणम् . जनस्तपस्तथा सत्य एतावाल्लोकसंग्रहः  एतावानेव विज्ञेयो लोकान्तश्चेब तत्पर...
verses.wordMeaning: Sakalya asked him more than a thousand questions. Yajnavalkya answered those all even as the sages were listening.
verses.commentary: Sense: Sakalya asked him more than a thousand questions. Yajnavalkya answered those all even as the sages were listening.

verses.sanskrit: विप्रा ऊचुः । वनान्ते स्त्रीयुगं दृष्ट्वा महारौद्रं भयावहम् । वृद्धाश्च पुरुषास्तत्र पाशहस्ता भयावहाः
verses.transliteration: viprā ūcuḥ / vanānte strīyugaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāraudraṃ bhayāvaham / vṛddhāśca puruṣāstatra pāśahastā bhayāvahāḥ
verses.translation: When SaJcalya ceased arguing, Yajnavalkya said, <c O Sakalya, answer a single question of mine, which I willingly put to you. The stake for this argument is a curse. If you are unable to answer you will die".
verses.hindi: अण्डानामीदुशानां तु कोटदो ज्ञेयाः सहलशः । तियंगुध्व॑मधस्ताच्च कारणस्याव्ययात्मन: ॥
verses.wordMeaning: When SaJcalya ceased arguing, Yajnavalkya said, <c O Sakalya, answer a single question of mine, which I willingly put to you. The stake for this argument is a curse. If you are unable to answer you will die".
verses.commentary: Sense: When SaJcalya ceased arguing, Yajnavalkya said, <c O Sakalya, answer a single question of mine, which I willingly put to you. The stake for this argument is a curse. If you are unable to answer you will die".

verses.sanskrit: दुर्धर्षा दुर्निरीक्ष्याश्च इतश्चेतश्च चञ्चलाः । व्याहरन्तः शुभां वाचं न तत्र गतिरस्ति वै
verses.transliteration: durdharṣā durnirīkṣyāśca itaścetaśca cañcalāḥ / vyāharantaḥ śubhāṃ vācaṃ na tatra gatirasti vai
verses.translation: Urged by him, aquestion was asked by Yajfiavalkya. Unable to understand its answer, Sakalya died immediately.
verses.hindi: कारण प्राकृतेस्तत्र ह्ाव॒तं प्रतिसप्तभिः अयोगुडनिभो वह्निः समन्तान्मण्डलाकृतिः । समन्‍्ताउ्दनवातेन धार्यमाणः स तिष्ठति ॥ घनवायुस्तथा55काशं धारयाणस्तु तिष्ठति.. द १५५ भुताविश्र 'तथा5काशं भुतादं चाप्यसो महान् । महान्व्याप्तो हानन्तेन अव्यक्तेन तु धायंते
verses.wordMeaning: Urged by him, aquestion was asked by Yajfiavalkya. Unable to understand its answer, Sakalya died immediately.
verses.commentary: Sense: Urged by him, aquestion was asked by Yajfiavalkya. Unable to understand its answer, Sakalya died immediately.

verses.sanskrit: अपरस्परयोः सर्वे निरीक्षन्तः पुनःपुनः । तैस् तु यद्वचनं प्रोक्तं तत्सर्वं कथ्यताम् इति
verses.transliteration: aparasparayoḥ sarve nirīkṣantaḥ punaḥpunaḥ / tais tu yadvacanaṃ proktaṃ tatsarvaṃ kathyatām iti
verses.translation: Sakalya died being afflicted by inability to answer the question. Thus there was a great dispute between the sages covetous of wealth and Yajnavalkya.
verses.hindi: तम एवं मिरालोकम्मर्यादमदेशिकम् । देवानामप्यविदितं व्यवहरविवजितमू.
verses.wordMeaning: Sakalya died being afflicted by inability to answer the question. Thus there was a great dispute between the sages covetous of wealth and Yajnavalkya.
verses.commentary: Sense: Sakalya died being afflicted by inability to answer the question. Thus there was a great dispute between the sages covetous of wealth and Yajnavalkya.

verses.sanskrit: अस्माकं पुरुषाः पञ्च तिष्ठन्ति तत्र सत्तमाः । ते प्रस्थाप्या महाभागाः सर्वथैव त्वरान्विताः
verses.transliteration: asmākaṃ puruṣāḥ pañca tiṣṭhanti tatra sattamāḥ / te prasthāpyā mahābhāgāḥ sarvathaiva tvarānvitāḥ
verses.translation: Answering hundreds and thousands of questions put by all of them, Yajnavalkya, who had deep penetration into the essence of those questions took the entire wealth. He spread his fame everywhere. He, the sage of controlled senses, left for home along with his disciples and was quite happy.
verses.hindi: के विषय में इतना ही ज्ञान प्राप्त है, इसलिए इतने ही लोकों को समझाना चाहिए । इसके बाद कुछ भी नहीं है ।१४८५-१४६९६। पदिचम दिशा में जिस प्रकार शुक्लपक्ष - की प्रतिपंदा को चन्द्रमा कुम्भस्थायी होकर रहते हैं, उसी प्रकारे अण्ड का शरीर है। इस प्रकार से हजारों करोड़ों अण्ड हैं, जो अव्ययात्मा कारण के . ऊपर, नीचे और बीच में स्थित हैं। ये प्रत्येक सात-सात भ्रक्रत कारणों द्वारा आवृत हैं ।१५०-१५१। इनमें एक दूसरे से दस गुने बड़े हैं और हर एक दूसरे को धारण किये हुये और ढॉके हुए हैं; क्योंकि सभी एक दूसरे की सहायता से उत्पन्न हुए हैं। इन अण्डों के चारों ओर धनीभूत सागर इस प्रकार अवस्थित है कि उसके जल द्वारा हौ सभी धारण कर लिये गये हैं और इस घनीभूत जल का भी जो ऊँचा या तिरछा मण्डल है, वह बाहर की ओर से घनीभूत तेज के द्वारा धारण कर लिया गया है ।१५२-१५४ यहाँ क्यों
verses.wordMeaning: Answering hundreds and thousands of questions put by all of them, Yajnavalkya, who had deep penetration into the essence of those questions took the entire wealth. He spread his fame everywhere. He, the sage of controlled senses,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Answering hundreds and thousands of questions put by all of them, Yajnavalkya, who had deep penetration into the essence of those questions took the entire wealth. He spread his fame everywhere. He, the sage of controlled senses,…

verses.sanskrit: अथ ते पुरुषाः पञ्च श्रुत्वा वाक्यमिदं शुभम् । परस्परं निरीक्षन्तो वदन्ति च पुनःपुनः
verses.transliteration: atha te puruṣāḥ pañca śrutvā vākyamidaṃ śubham / parasparaṃ nirīkṣanto vadanti ca punaḥpunaḥ
verses.translation: Sakalya (otherwise known as) Devamitra, was a noble, excellent Brahmana. He was intelligent and excellent among those who know the implications of grammar. He had com¬ posed five Samhitas.
verses.hindi: लौहगोलक की तरह मण्डलाकार होकर अग्नि इसके चारों ओर है, जो घनीभूत वायु के आधार परे स्थित है। इसी घनीभूत वायु ने आकाश को भो धारण किया है ।१५५॥ आकाहय भूतादि महान् को और महान् भूतादि को धारण किये हुए है और यह महान् अव्यक्त अनन्त द्वारा ब्याप्त है। यह अपरिव्यक्त अनन्त दस प्रकार का है--सूक्ष्, अकृतात्मा अनादिनिधन, असीम, घोर, अनालम्ब, अनामय, बहु सहखे
verses.wordMeaning: Sakalya (otherwise known as) Devamitra, was a noble, excellent Brahmana. He was intelligent and excellent among those who know the implications of grammar. He had com¬ posed five Samhitas.
verses.commentary: Sense: Sakalya (otherwise known as) Devamitra, was a noble, excellent Brahmana. He was intelligent and excellent among those who know the implications of grammar. He had com¬ posed five Samhitas.

verses.sanskrit: क्व ते कस्य कुतो याताः किमुक्तं तैर्भयावहैः
verses.transliteration: kva te kasya kuto yātāḥ kimuktaṃ tairbhayāvahaiḥ
verses.translation: He had five disciples, viz. Mudgala, Golaka, Khaliya, Matsya and Saisireya (the fifth one).
verses.hindi: योजन दूरस्थ, अन्धकाराच्छन्न, अन्धकार की भाँति अदशेनीय, निःसीम, अदेशिक, देवों के द्वारा भी एकोनपञ्चाशत्तमोष्ध्याय: ३६१
verses.wordMeaning: He had five disciples, viz. Mudgala, Golaka, Khaliya, Matsya and Saisireya (the fifth one).
verses.commentary: Sense: He had five disciples, viz. Mudgala, Golaka, Khaliya, Matsya and Saisireya (the fifth one).

verses.sanskrit: पुरुषा ऊचुः । तीर्थावगाहनं सर्वैः पूर्वदक्षिणपश्चिमैः । उत्तरैश्च कृतं भक्त्या न पापं तैर् व्यपोहितम्
verses.transliteration: puruṣā ūcuḥ / tīrthāvagāhanaṃ sarvaiḥ pūrvadakṣiṇapaścimaiḥ / uttaraiśca kṛtaṃ bhaktyā na pāpaṃ tair vyapohitam
verses.translation: Sakapurna Rathxtara expounded (compiled) three Samhitas. This excellent Brahmana composed Nirukta as his fourth work.
verses.hindi: तमसोह5न्ते च विश्यातमाकाशान्ते च भास्वरम् । मर्थादायामतस्तस्य शिवस्थाइड्यतर्॑ महत्
verses.wordMeaning: Sakapurna Rathxtara expounded (compiled) three Samhitas. This excellent Brahmana composed Nirukta as his fourth work.
verses.commentary: Sense: Sakapurna Rathxtara expounded (compiled) three Samhitas. This excellent Brahmana composed Nirukta as his fourth work.

verses.sanskrit: निष्पापाश्चाथ संजातास्तीर्थस्यास्य प्रभावतः । शृण्वन्तु ऋषयः सर्वे वह्निकालोपमा द्विजाः
verses.transliteration: niṣpāpāścātha saṃjātāstīrthasyāsya prabhāvataḥ / śṛṇvantu ṛṣayaḥ sarve vahnikālopamā dvijāḥ
verses.translation: He had four disciples, viz. Ketava, Dalaki, DJiarma- sarman and Devasarman. They were Brahmanas who observed holy rites.
verses.hindi: त्रिदशानामगम्यं तु स्थान दिव्यमिति श्रुतिः। महतो देवदेवस्य सर्यादायां व्यवस्थितम्. ७१६१ चरद्रादित्यावतप्तास्तु ये लोकाः प्रथिता बुधेः । ते लोका इत्यभिहिता जगतश्रव न संशयः. रसातलतलात्सप्त सप्तेवोध्बंतला: क्षितो । सप्त स्कन्‍्धास्तथा वायो: सब्रह्मसदना द्विजा:.
verses.wordMeaning: He had four disciples, viz. Ketava, Dalaki, DJiarma- sarman and Devasarman. They were Brahmanas who observed holy rites.
verses.commentary: Sense: He had four disciples, viz. Ketava, Dalaki, DJiarma- sarman and Devasarman. They were Brahmanas who observed holy rites.

verses.sanskrit: पातकानि च घोराणि यान्यचिन्त्यानि देहिनाम् । पापिष्ठेन तु चैकेन गुरुदारा निषेविता
verses.transliteration: pātakāni ca ghorāṇi yānyacintyāni dehinām / pāpiṣṭhena tu caikena gurudārā niṣevitā
verses.translation: When Sakalya died those present there, incurred the sin of Brahmin-slaughter. Worried thus they approached Brahma.
verses.hindi: पृथिव्यां चाग्निवायूनां महतस्तमसस्तथा । ईश्वरस्थ तु देवस्य अनन्तस्य द्विजोत्तमाः .
verses.wordMeaning: When Sakalya died those present there, incurred the sin of Brahmin-slaughter. Worried thus they approached Brahma.
verses.commentary: Sense: When Sakalya died those present there, incurred the sin of Brahmin-slaughter. Worried thus they approached Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: हृतं चान्येन मित्रस्वं सुवर्णं च धनं तथा । ब्रह्महत्या महारौद्रा कृता चान्येन पातकम्
verses.transliteration: hṛtaṃ cānyena mitrasvaṃ suvarṇaṃ ca dhanaṃ tathā / brahmahatyā mahāraudrā kṛtā cānyena pātakam
verses.translation: On knowing mentally their situation, Brahma sent them to Pavana Purn. " All of you go there, your sin will be washed off immediately.
verses.hindi: तस्य चोकक्‍तं सया पूर्व तस्मिन्नामानुकीतंने . ॥श्दद य एव शिवनाम्ना हि तद्दः कात्स्थन कीतितम् । स एष सर्वत्र गतः सर्वस्थानेषु पूज्यते भुमौ रसातले चेब आकाशे पवने5नले । अ्णंवेषु स सर्वेषु दिवि चेव न संशयः १७०
verses.wordMeaning: On knowing mentally their situation, Brahma sent them to Pavana Purn. " All of you go there, your sin will be washed off immediately.
verses.commentary: Sense: On knowing mentally their situation, Brahma sent them to Pavana Purn. " All of you go there, your sin will be washed off immediately.

verses.sanskrit: सुरापानं तु चान्यस्य संजातं चाप्यकामतः । गोवध्या चाप्यकामेन कृता चैकेन पापिना
verses.transliteration: surāpānaṃ tu cānyasya saṃjātaṃ cāpyakāmataḥ / govadhyā cāpyakāmena kṛtā caikena pāpinā
verses.translation: After bowing to the twelve suns, the deity Valuka, the eleven Rudras and particularly the son of Vayu (Hanu- man) and after taking a dip in the four holy pools, you will sur¬ mount (expunge) the sin of Brahmana's slaughter".
verses.hindi: अविदित और व्यवहार-रहित ।१५६-१४९। अन्धकार के अन्त में और आकाश के शेष भाग में अर्थात् सीमा प्रान्त में शिव का एक देदीप्यमान-विख्यात आयतन या मन्दिर है। वह दिव्य स्थान है, जहाँ देवगण भी नहीं जा सकते हैं। देवाधिदेव महादेव के आयतन की सीमा में चन्द्र-सूयं की किरण से प्रतप्त जो लोक हैं, उन्हें पण्डित लोग जागतिक लोक कहते हैं ।१६०-१६ । द्विजगण ! प्रथ्वी में रसातल के ऊपर था नीचे
verses.wordMeaning: After bowing to the twelve suns, the deity Valuka, the eleven Rudras and particularly the son of Vayu (Hanu- man) and after taking a dip in the four holy pools, you will sur¬ mount (expunge) the sin of Brahmana's slaughter".
verses.commentary: Sense: After bowing to the twelve suns, the deity Valuka, the eleven Rudras and particularly the son of Vayu (Hanu- man) and after taking a dip in the four holy pools, you will sur¬ mount (expunge) the sin of Brahmana's slaughter".

verses.sanskrit: अकामतो ऽपि सर्वेषां पातकानि नराधिप । ब्राह्मणानां तु ते श्रुत्वा वाक्यं तद्विस्मयान्विताः
verses.transliteration: akāmato 'pi sarveṣāṃ pātakāni narādhipa / brāhmaṇānāṃ tu te śrutvā vākyaṃ tadvismayānvitāḥ
verses.translation: On hearing this, they hastened to that city. They per¬ formed holy ablution in accordance with injunctions and visited the deities.
verses.hindi: सात-सात लोक हैं । ब्रह्मसदन पयंनत वायु के सात स्कन्ध हैं। वहाँ पाताल से लेकर स्वगंपयंन्त वायु की गति पाँच प्रकार की है। यही जगत का प्रमाग है और यही संसार-सागर कहलाता है। अनेक जातियों की उद्धव-भूमि यह अनादि-अनन्त जगत्परम्परा इसी प्रकार चलती रहती है। जगत की यह अस्थिर प्रवृत्ति सचमुच विचित्र है। इसकी भौतिक सृष्टि का अत्यधिक विस्तार है, जिसे अतीन्द्रिय महाभाग सिद्धगेण भी नहीं जान सकते हैं १६३-१६६। इस जगत् में अग्नि, वायु, महान्, तम, ईइ्वर और देव अनस्त का क्षय, परिणाम या अन्त नहीं होता है। ये सभी स्थानों में अनन्तनाम से अभिहित हैं । नामों के वर्णन प्रसज्छ में हमने पहले ही इस सम्बन्ध में कह दिया है ।१६७ १६५। जो शिव नाम से श्रप्तिद्ध हैं. उनके नामानुकीतंन- प्रसड़ में हमनें विस्तार के साथ कह दिया है। ये ही स्वंगामी हैं और सभी स्थानों में अर्थात् भूमि,
verses.wordMeaning: On hearing this, they hastened to that city. They per¬ formed holy ablution in accordance with injunctions and visited the deities.
verses.commentary: Sense: On hearing this, they hastened to that city. They per¬ formed holy ablution in accordance with injunctions and visited the deities.

verses.sanskrit: सद्य एव तदा जाताः पापिष्ठा गतकल्मषाः । तीर्थस्यास्य प्रभावेन नर्मदायाः प्रभावतः
verses.transliteration: sadya eva tadā jātāḥ pāpiṣṭhā gatakalmaṣāḥ / tīrthasyāsya prabhāvena narmadāyāḥ prabhāvataḥ
verses.translation: They bowed to Uttaresvara. By the grace of Vadavas they became free from sins and attained the solar region.
verses.hindi: रसातल आकादह्य, पवन, अभ्नि, समुद्र ओर स्वर्ग में पूजित होते हैं, इसमें कुछ संगय नहीं है। ऐसा जावा
verses.wordMeaning: They bowed to Uttaresvara. By the grace of Vadavas they became free from sins and attained the solar region.
verses.commentary: Sense: They bowed to Uttaresvara. By the grace of Vadavas they became free from sins and attained the solar region.

verses.sanskrit: न क्वचित्पातकानां तु प्रवेशश्चात्र जायते । एवं संचित्य ते सर्वे पापिष्ठाश्च परस्परम्
verses.transliteration: na kvacitpātakānāṃ tu praveśaścātra jāyate / evaṃ saṃcitya te sarve pāpiṣṭhāśca parasparam
verses.translation: Ever since that time, that holy centre became a destroyer of sins. This holy city of Vayu had been built by the Wind-god formerly.
verses.hindi: ३६२ . वायुपुराणम् ह सर्वलोकेषु लोकेश इज्यते बहुधा प्रभुः द ११७१ एवं परस्परोत्पन्ना धाय॑न्ते च परस्परान् । आधाराधेयभावेन विकारास्ते विकारिणः १७२ द पृथ्व्यादयों विकारास्ते परिच्छिन्नाः परस्परम् । परस्पराधिकाश्चैव प्रविष्ठाश्व परस्परमू ४१७२
verses.wordMeaning: Ever since that time, that holy centre became a destroyer of sins. This holy city of Vayu had been built by the Wind-god formerly.
verses.commentary: Sense: Ever since that time, that holy centre became a destroyer of sins. This holy city of Vayu had been built by the Wind-god formerly.

verses.sanskrit: चित्रभानुः स्मृतस्तैस्तु विचिन्त्य हृदये हरिम् । स्नात्वा रेवाजले पुण्ये तर्पिताः पितृदेवताः
verses.transliteration: citrabhānuḥ smṛtastaistu vicintya hṛdaye harim / snātvā revājale puṇye tarpitāḥ pitṛdevatāḥ
verses.translation: When Hanuman, the son of the Wind-god, born of (the womb of) Anjana, the great god of truthful exploits was born, this holy centre was created by Vayu, the son of god Brahma.
verses.hindi: मुतेम्यः परतस्तेभ्यो ह्यालोकः परतः स्मृतः । मृतान्यालोक आकाशे परिच्छिन्नानि सर्वशः
verses.wordMeaning: When Hanuman, the son of the Wind-god, born of (the womb of) Anjana, the great god of truthful exploits was born, this holy centre was created by Vayu, the son of god Brahma.
verses.commentary: Sense: When Hanuman, the son of the Wind-god, born of (the womb of) Anjana, the great god of truthful exploits was born, this holy centre was created by Vayu, the son of god Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: नत्वा तु भास्करं देवं हृदि ध्यात्वा जनार्दनम् । प्रदक्षिणं तु तं भक्त्या ज्वलन्तं जातवेदसम्
verses.transliteration: natvā tu bhāskaraṃ devaṃ hṛdi dhyātvā janārdanam / pradakṣiṇaṃ tu taṃ bhaktyā jvalantaṃ jātavedasam
verses.translation: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person, a wine addict or the defiler of one's preceptor's bed becomes free from all sins after bowing to Vadaditya.
verses.hindi: पात्रे महति पात्राणि य्थवान्तर्गतानि तु । भवन्त्यन्योन्यहीनानि परस्परसमाभ्षयात् ॥ तथा ह्यालोक आकाशे भेदास्त्वन्तगंता मताः १७७ कृत्स्नान्येतानि चत्वारि अस्योन्यस्थाधिकानि तु । यावदेतानि भृतानि तावदुत्पत्तिरच्यते।.
verses.wordMeaning: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…

verses.sanskrit: पतिताः पाण्डवश्रेष्ठ पापोद्विग्ना महीपते । सात्त्विकीं वासनां कृत्वा त्यक्त्वा रजस्तमस्तथा
verses.transliteration: patitāḥ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭha pāpodvignā mahīpate / sāttvikīṃ vāsanāṃ kṛtvā tyaktvā rajastamastathā
verses.translation: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person, a wine addict or the defiler of one's preceptor's bed becomes free from all sins after bowing to Vadaditya.
verses.hindi: जन्तुनामिह संस्कारों भूतेष्बन्तर्गतो मतः। प्रत्यास्याय च भूतानि कार्योत्पत्तिन विद्यते
verses.wordMeaning: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…

verses.sanskrit: हतं तैः पावके सर्वं रेवाया उत्तरे तटे । विमानस्थास् तदा दृष्टा ब्राह्मणैस्ते युधिष्ठिर
verses.transliteration: hataṃ taiḥ pāvake sarvaṃ revāyā uttare taṭe / vimānasthās tadā dṛṣṭā brāhmaṇaiste yudhiṣṭhira
verses.translation: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person, a wine addict or the defiler of one's preceptor's bed becomes free from all sins after bowing to Vadaditya.
verses.hindi: तस्मात्परिसिता भेदाः स्पृताः कार्यात्मकास्तु ते । करणात्मकास्तथेव स्युभेंदा ये सहदादयः १८० जाता है कि, ये तपस्या में रत हैं और महाद्यति-सम्पन्न हैं। ये ही महायोगी प्रभु महेश्वर अनेक रूपों में विभक्त होकर सभी लोकों में लोकेश नाम से पूजित होते हैं ।१६६-१७१। जिस प्रकार विकार विकारी को घारण करता है, उसी प्रकार आधाराधेय भाव से परस्पर उत्पन्न लोक एक दूसरे को धारण करता है। पृथ्वी आदि वंकारिक पदार्थ परस्पर परिच्छिन्न अर्थात् अलग-अलग हैं; किन्तु एक दूसरे से महात् होने पर
verses.wordMeaning: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…

verses.sanskrit: आश्चर्यमतुलं दृष्टम् ऋषिभिर् नर्मदातटे । तदाप्रभृति ते सर्वे रागद्वेषविवर्जिताः
verses.transliteration: āścaryamatulaṃ dṛṣṭam ṛṣibhir narmadātaṭe / tadāprabhṛti te sarve rāgadveṣavivarjitāḥ
verses.translation: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person, a wine addict or the defiler of one's preceptor's bed becomes free from all sins after bowing to Vadaditya.
verses.hindi: भी आपस में मिले हुए हैं। जिस कारण वे परस्पर मिले हुए हैं; उसी कारण से उन्होंने स्थिरता भी पाई है। पहले ये सामान्य रूप से वर्तमान थे, पीछे परस्पर संनिवेश करने के लिये अर्थात् मिलने के लिये वे विशेष भाव से स्थिर हुये । पृथ्वी से लेकर वायुपय॑ंन्त तीनों विकार पृथक् हैं ।७२-१७४। इन तीनों का पार्थक्य परस्पर गुणों के अपचय के अनुसार है। शेष विकारों का पार्थक्य सूक्षष्ता के कारण नहीं जाता जाता
verses.wordMeaning: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…

verses.sanskrit: रवितीर्थं द्विजा हृष्टाः सेवन्ते मोक्षकाङ्क्षया । तीर्थस्यास्य च यत्पुण्यं तच्छृणुष्व नराधिप
verses.transliteration: ravitīrthaṃ dvijā hṛṣṭāḥ sevante mokṣakāṅkṣayā / tīrthasyāsya ca yatpuṇyaṃ tacchṛṇuṣva narādhipa
verses.translation: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person, a wine addict or the defiler of one's preceptor's bed becomes free from all sins after bowing to Vadaditya.
verses.hindi: है । उन भूतों से परे एक आलोक है। आलोकमय आकाश में सभी भूत उसी प्रकार भेदभाव से स्थित हैं, जँसे बड़े पात्र में छोटा पात्र ढेंक जाता है और दूसरे की अपेक्षा एक हीन मालूम पड़ता है। उसी प्रकार आलोकमय आगकाझ्ष में प्रृथ्वी आदि भूतों का भेद जाना जाता है। ये चारों भूत परस्पर एक दूसरे से क्रमशः अधिक हैं। जितने भूत हैं या प्राणी हैं, उतनी ही सृष्टि है। १७४-१७७। जत्तुओं का संस्कार स्थल भूत के ही अनुसार कहा गया है। पंचभूत के बिना कार्यों की उत्पत्ति नहीं होती है। इसलिये महदा दि जितने कार्यात्मक भेद देखे जाते हैं वे सभी कारणात्मक हैं। कार्य और कार्यात्मक भेदों को परिच्छिन्न
verses.wordMeaning: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…

verses.sanskrit: पीडितो वृद्धभावेन भक्त्या प्रीतो नरेश्वर । उद्देशं कथयिष्यामि द्विक्रोशाभ्यन्तरे स्थितः
verses.transliteration: pīḍito vṛddhabhāvena bhaktyā prīto nareśvara / uddeśaṃ kathayiṣyāmi dvikrośābhyantare sthitaḥ
verses.translation: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person, a wine addict or the defiler of one's preceptor's bed becomes free from all sins after bowing to Vadaditya.
verses.hindi: एकोनपञ्चाशत्तमोध्ध्याय: ॥ रेध्शे
verses.wordMeaning: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…

verses.sanskrit: कुरुक्षेत्रं यथा पुण्यं रवितीर्थं श्रुतं मया । ईश्वरेण पुरा ख्यातं षण्मुखस्य नराधिप
verses.transliteration: kurukṣetraṃ yathā puṇyaṃ ravitīrthaṃ śrutaṃ mayā / īśvareṇa purā khyātaṃ ṣaṇmukhasya narādhipa
verses.translation: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person, a wine addict or the defiler of one's preceptor's bed becomes free from all sins after bowing to Vadaditya.
verses.hindi: एतावान्संनिवेशस्तु मया शक्यः प्रभाषितुम् । एतावदेव श्रोतव्यं संनिवेशे तु पाथिव ३१८४ तारकासंनिवेशश्व यावहिव्यं तु मण्डलम् । मर्यादासंनिवेशस्तु भुमेस्तदनुमण्डलम् ॥ क्‍
verses.wordMeaning: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…

verses.sanskrit: श्रुतं रुद्राच्च तैः सर्वैर् अहं तत्र समीपगः । ईश्वर उवाच: मार्तण्डग्रहणे प्राप्ते ये व्रजन्ति षडानन । रवितीर्थे कुरुक्षेत्रे तुल्यमेतत्फलं लभेत्
verses.transliteration: śrutaṃ rudrācca taiḥ sarvair ahaṃ tatra samīpagaḥ / īśvara uvāca: mārtaṇḍagrahaṇe prāpte ye vrajanti ṣaḍānana / ravitīrthe kurukṣetre tulyametatphalaṃ labhet
verses.translation: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person, a wine addict or the defiler of one's preceptor's bed becomes free from all sins after bowing to Vadaditya.
verses.hindi: दति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते भुवनविन्यासों नामंकोनपच्चाशोर्ष्याय:
verses.wordMeaning: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…

verses.sanskrit: स्नाने दाने तथा जप्ये होमे चैव विशेषतः । कुरुक्षेत्रे समं पुण्यं नात्र कार्या विचारणा
verses.transliteration: snāne dāne tathā japye home caiva viśeṣataḥ / kurukṣetre samaṃ puṇyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
verses.translation: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person, a wine addict or the defiler of one's preceptor's bed becomes free from all sins after bowing to Vadaditya.
verses.hindi: समझना चाहिए ॥१७५-१८०। ब्राद्मणो ! इस प्रकार हमने सातों द्वीपों और समुद्रोंवाली पृथ्वी का विभाग और संनिवेश (कैसे बसी हुई है) यथार्थ रूप से बता दिया। विस्तार और मंडल की परिसंख्या से विश्वरूपिणी प्रकृति का यह भांशिक परिमाण हुआ। यह समस्त जगत्'उसी जगत् को उत्पन्न करनेवाले ईदवर का निवास-स्थान है। इस प्रकार भूतगण इन सातों लोकों में परस्पर आश्रित हैं। १६१-१८३॥ लोक-सल्नलिवेश के विषय में इतना ही कहने की शक्ति रखता हूँ  पाथिव ! आप भी मुझसे इतना ही सुनने की इच्छा करें। जिन सातों प्रकृतिओं ने परस्पर एक. दूसरे को धारण किया है और जो ऊपर, नीचे या बीच में अनेकानेक प्रक्तियाँ हैं, उनमें से कुछ का थोझ सा वर्णन मैं यहाँ करता हूं। ताराओं का सन्निवेश और जितने दिव्य मंडल हैं तथा सीमाप्रान्त में जितने भूमि के अनुमंडलों के सन्निवेदद
verses.wordMeaning: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…

verses.sanskrit: ग्रामे वा यदि वारण्ये पुण्या सर्वत्र नर्मदा । रवितीर्थे विशेषेण रेवा पुण्यफलप्रदा
verses.transliteration: grāme vā yadi vāraṇye puṇyā sarvatra narmadā / ravitīrthe viśeṣeṇa revā puṇyaphalapradā
verses.translation: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person, a wine addict or the defiler of one's preceptor's bed becomes free from all sins after bowing to Vadaditya.
verses.hindi: हैं, उन सबके सम्बन्ध में मैं अब आगे कहुँगा ।१८४-१८६॥।
verses.wordMeaning: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…

verses.sanskrit: षष्ठ्यां सूर्यदिने भक्त्या व्यतीपाते च वै धृतौ । संक्रान्तौ ग्रहणे ऽमायां ये व्रजन्ति जितेन्द्रियाः
verses.transliteration: ṣaṣṭhyāṃ sūryadine bhaktyā vyatīpāte ca vai dhṛtau / saṃkrāntau grahaṇe 'māyāṃ ye vrajanti jitendriyāḥ
verses.translation: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person, a wine addict or the defiler of one's preceptor's bed becomes free from all sins after bowing to Vadaditya.
verses.hindi: ३६४ वायुपुराणम्र् अधः प्रमाणमुध्व॑ च वण्यंमानं निबोधत । प्रथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्व पत्चमम् !। अनन्तधातयो ह्व ते व्यापकास्तु प्रकीतिता
verses.wordMeaning: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. In this manner, the great administration of the Brahmanas took root here. Even a slayer of cow, an ungrateful person,…

verses.sanskrit: कामक्रोधैर्विमुक्ताश्च रागद्वेषैस् तथैव च । उपोष्य परया भक्त्या देवस्याग्रे नराधिप
verses.transliteration: kāmakrodhairvimuktāśca rāgadveṣais tathaiva ca / upoṣya parayā bhaktyā devasyāgre narādhipa
verses.translation: Here the Sudras born in the world and dedicated to the Brahmanas were taxed heavily for their livelihood and for the performance of Brahma Yajha. verses.translation: Bharadvaja, Yajnavaikya, Galaki, Salaki, the intelli¬ gent Satabalaka, the excellent Brahmana Naigama and Bhara- He had three noble-souled disciples endowed with good qualities. They were the intelligent Nandayanlya, the wise Pannagari and the third one Aryava (Arjava in Bd. P.). They were of praise-worthy, holy observances due to their penance. They were devoid of passions, endowed with very great splend¬ our and masters of the knowledge of Samhitas. Hence they were called Bahvrcas by whom Samhitas were propagated., The sage of the spiritual lineage of Vaisampayana composed Yajurveda. Eightysix auspicious Samhitas of Yajus (r) Mantras had been composed by him. 2 He passed them over to his disciples. They grasped them in accordance with the in¬ junctions. The sage Yajnavalkya of great penance alone was left out. But he too composed eightysix alternative Samhitas. Each of these three had three subdivisions. Thus there arose nine different schools. The three main schools are Udlcyas (the northerners), MadhyadeSas (those of the middle countries) and Pracyas (the easterners). Syamayani became the chief of the nort ern These are the three regional heads. 3 Arum was eulogised as the first and foremost of those who had been established in the MadhyadeSa. Alambi was the first among the easterners. verses.translation: O Brahmanas, then he meditated and worshipped the Sun-god. What was vomited rose up in the sky and stood near the Solar Brahman. The delighted Sun handed over the Yajur-Mantras which had gone up to the solar disc. The Sun-god gave them to the intelligent Brahmarati (in Bd. P.) Yajnavalkya who had assumed the form of a horse. Thenceforth, the Brahmanas who began the study of the Yajus handed over to Yajnavalkya in the form of a horse ( Vajin ) became known as Vajins. Those by whom the expiatory rite for Brahma-hatya (Brahmana-slaughter) was performed are remembered as Carakas 1 because of their performance of atonement (for Brahmana 5 s slaughter). The disciples of Vaisarhpayana are call¬ ed Carakas. These were called Carakas. Now understand the Vajins, the disciples of Yajnavalkya. They were 2 * *: Kanva, Vai- dheya, Salin, Madhyandina, Sapeyl, Vidigadha, Apya, Uddala, Tamrayana, Vatsya, Galava, Saisiri, Atavl, ParnI, Vlranl and Samparayana. These fifteen are known as Vajins. Thus there are hundred and one alternative Samhitas. A popular etymology of Caraka (SKD ) derives it from y/car c to go,' 'to know* and hence caraka is a knower of Vedas and medical science* and quotes from Bhava Prakasa how Sesa espied diseases and sufferings on the earth and composed a medical treatise out of compassion. Here it means c a follower of a branch of Black Yajurveda who follow.' fecial practices and rites different from those in SatapathaBr. (vide MW. 389). Cf. The list of disciples of Yajnavalkya in CVS, It differs in Jaimini taught his son Sumantu. 1 * 3 * 5 6 Sumantu taught his son Sutavan. Sutavan taught his son Sukarman. After learning in a short while a thousand Samhitas, Sukarman, expounded them to his thousand disciples having the brilliance of the Sun. Verses 27-48 give the genealogy of Sama Veda teachers. It differs much from the list of Sama Veda teachers in CVS p -40. The Bd. P. list (in 1.2.35. 31-55) is also somewhat different from our Purana, Our text gives following genealogy. Indra killed all of them because they pursued their studies even on prohibited days. Then Sukarman performed a fast unto death, for the sake of his disciples. On seeing him infuriated, Indra granted him a boon: "Two disciples of great prowess and brilliance of fire you will have. They will be highly intelligent and will study all the thousand Samhitas. They will be blessed. O excellent Brah- mana, do not be angry." After saying this to the renowned Sukarman and see¬ ing him mollified, the glorious Indra vanished there itself. O excellent Brahmanas, the intelligent Pausyanjin was his first disciple and king Hiranyanabha of Kusika race was the second. Pausyanjin taught five hundred Samhitas. The auspi¬ cious disciples of Pausyanjin were generally the northerners.

verses.translation: The powerful Kausikya taught five hundred Samhitas. The disciples of Hiranyanabha arc known as the easterners and the Samagas. LokaksI, Kuthumi, Kusltl and Langali were the four disciples of Pausyanjin. Now know their divisions (branches). Ranayaniya, son of Tandi, the highly learned Mula- carin, Kaitiputra and Satyaputra—know these to be the dis¬ ciples of different branches of Lokaksin. Kuthumi had three sons, viz. Aurasa, Rasapasara and the brilliant Bhagavitti. These three were famous as Kaulhumas. The two sages Sauridyu and Srrigiputra performed holy rites. Ranayaniya and Saumitri were experts in Samaveda. Sfngiputra of great penance expounded three Sam¬ hitas, O excellent Brahmanas, to Caila, Pracinayoga, Surala. Parasarya, disciple of Kuthumi, expounded six Sam¬ hitas. Asurayana, Vaisakhya, Vedavrddha, Parayana, Pracina- yogaputra and intelligent Patanjali are known as the six dis¬ ciples of Parasarya, the disciple of Kuthumi. Langali and Sali- hotra expounded six Samhitas each. Bhaluki, Kamahani, Jaimini, Lomagayina, Kantfa and Kolaha—these six are known as Langalas. These were the dis¬ ciples of Langali and they popularised these Samhitas. Hiranyanabha, who was the son of a king who had dis¬ ciples [ or who had as his disciple Krta, the son of a king] and who was the most excellent among men, composed twenty- four Samhitas. Listen and understand the names of those dis¬ ciples whom he taught. Rada, Mahavirya, Pancama, Vahana, Talaka, Pandaka, Kalika, Rajika, Gautama, Ajabasta, Somaraja, Pfsthaghna, Parikrsta, UIukhalaka,YavIyasa, Vaisala, Angullya, Kausika, Salimahjarisatya, Kaplya, Kanlka and the righte¬ ous Parasara—all these were ancient singers of Saman. Two sages, the most excellent among the Saman-sing- ers, are said to be Pausyanji and Krti. They are the composers of Samhitas. verses.translation: Saindhava gave it to Munjakesa. The Samhita was lvided again into two. The alternative Samhitas of the Atharva Veda are five * 1, viz. Naksatrakalpa, Vaitana, (the third) Samhitavidhi, the fourth Angiras-kalpa and the fifth Santi- alpa. O excellent sages, the Purana too was expounded by me after dividing it into six. The composers of the Samhitas were Kasyapa, Savarni The divisions of the Atharva Veda are five (1) Naksatra Kalpa, (2) Vaitana (prob. Vidhana Kalpa as in CVS.), (3) Samhita Vidhi (prob. Samhita Kalpa of CVS p.*46), (4) Ahgiras Kalpa, (5) Santi Kalpa. Verses 56-61 state the position of the Puranic lore: Although Loma- harsana had eleven disciples, only three of.them—Kasyapa, Savarni and Samsapayana composed Puraria Samhitas in addition to their Guru's work. There Samhitas had four pddas (parts) and 4000 verses. Only Samsapayana*s Samhita contained 8600 veises. All of them have four Padas. All of them expound the same matter. Tlicy were distinguished by separate readings like the recensions of the Vedas. Excepting Samsapayana's Samhita each contains four thousand verses. The Samhitas of Lomaharsana are original, then come the Saiiihitas of Kasyapa. The third are theSarhhitas of Savarni. All these can be readily understood by the scholars of Yajur Veda. The Samhitas of Sarhsapayana are embellished by the topics of exhortation. There are eight thousand six hundred verses. There are additional fifteen and ten along with ten (Rks?) known as Valakhilyas, Sarnapraikhas along with Savarnas. 1 The Saman Mantras are eight thousand fourteen (intheSama Veda) including Aranyaka along with Homa. Samagas (Sama-singers) sing them. The Adhvaryava Veda consists of twelve thousand Man¬ tras including the Yajur (Veda) and Brahraanas as compiled (classified) by Vyasa. It includes the Gramya, Aranyaka and the Mantrakarana. Henceforth the narratives will be known as Puroa-kalhas (former or ancient narratives). The Rk, Brahmana and Yajus are remembered to have Gramya, Aranyaand Mantra (Sections). There are additional compilations (Khila) and supplementary ones ( Upakhila ) of Haridravlya as also the Paraksudras of Taittiriyas. Verses 62-73 give the number'of Mantras in Vedic Text. But after comparing the figures stated in this Purana and those in CVS (Saunaka's Carapa-Vyiiha-Sutra) and the published editions of Vedic texts, I am constrai¬ ned to repeat what I said about the author of Bd. P. (Bd. 2.35, , Footnote 2): The Rk verses in ihc Vajasancyl Sariihita are a hundred less than two thousand. The Brahmana portion contains four times that number. The total number of Yajur Mantras and Rks is eight thousand eight hundred eighty plus a quarter more along with Sukriya (Samans belonging to Pravargya) and Khila (additional) Mantras (according.to) Yajnavalkya. Similarly listen to the extent of the Samhita ofCarana 1 - Vidyas (sections of Vedic School—of Atharva?). They contain six thousand twenty-six Rks. Yajur Mantras, it is said, are some¬ what more than this.

verses.translation: There are eleven thousand twenty Rks (in Yajus). In the Samhita of Bhrgu, there are ten thousand three hundred and eighty Rks and a thousand Mantras. The number of Rks in Atharva Veda is more. These are mentioned as five thousand. Some sages add nine hundred and eighty Rks. This is mentioned by Angiras who includes the Aranyaka portion. Thus the number of Rks and the different recensions have been enumerated. The composers of Rks are the cause of the differences in recensions. In all the Manvantaras, the recensional differen¬ ces are the same. The Vedic text which is the creation of Prajapati is eternal. These variations are due to the non-eternal nature of Devas. Creation of Mantras takes place again and again 2 (in every Manvantara). The determination of the names of the Devas takes place in each Manvantara. The divisions of Sruti in the Dva- para Yuga have been narrated. Thus, afrer handing over the Vedas and other mantras to his disciples, the holy lord, the excellent sage Vyasa went to the forest for performing penance. These different recensions have been made by his disciples and their disciples. The fourteen lores are the (six) Angas (ancillary sub¬ jects), the four Vedas, MImarasa,Nyaya-vistara(logic),Dharma- sastra and Puranas. Bd. P. (1.2.35.78) reads Carapa —a school of the Atharva Veda. Puranic writer believed that Devas are not eternal but Man ras are so and they manifest themselves again and again m the new world order, after the new creation of the world. (If four more lores viz.) Ayurveda (Science of Medi¬ cine), Dhanur Veda (Science of Archery), Gandharva-Veda (i.e. Musicology) and the fourth Arthasastra (Science of Economics and Politics) (are added) the number (of lores) be¬ comes eighteen. 1 It should be known that Brahmarsis are the earliest ones, thereafter come Devarsis and then Rajarsis. 2 Thus the sources of origin of Rsis are three. It is through sages of well- disciplined observances, that Rsis were born. Expounders of Brahman are born in the five Gotras viz. among the descendants of Kasyapa, Vasistha, Bhrgu, Angi- ras and Atri. They are called Brahmarsis because they can go to (approach) Brahma. Devarsis (Celestial Sages) are the sons of Dharma, Pulastya, Kratu, Pulaha, Pratyusa, Prabhasa and Kas'yapa. Listen to the enumeration of their names. The Celestial Sages, Kara and Narayana are the two sons of Dharma. Valakhilyas are the sons of Kratu; Kardama is the son of Pulaha. Kubera is the son of Pulastya and Acala is known as the son of Pratyusa. Parvata and Narada are the sons of Kasyapa. They are remembered as Devarsis (Celestial Sages), because they ap- proach Devas. Kings born in the race of Manu and in the dynasty of Atla (Pururavas), viz. Ailas, Aiksvakas (descendants of Iksvaku) and Nabhagas should be known as Rajarsis (Royal Sages).

verses.translation: Verses 80-93 define the i, m. <n u. Economics > Administration) They are called Rajar$is because they have attained ( Rsanti ) the Prajas (subjects) through delighting them [Rahjandt). Brahmarsis are considered to be established in Brahmaloka. The auspicious Devarsis (Celestial Sages) should be known as established in Devaloka. The Celestial Sages (Devarsis) andRajarsis are proclaim¬ ed as Brahmarsis on account of their nobility of birth, penance, ability to utter (compose and recite) Mantras. I shall now mention the characteristics of Devarsis and others. They have the knowledge of the past, present and future. They always speak the truth. They are enlightened and they are united to (their) self. They are well-known through their penance. Even while in the womb, the darkness of igno¬ rance has been dispelled by them. They practise the repetition of Mantras. Due to their Supreme Power, they are omnipresent. Devas, Brahmanas and Kings are in communion with the sages. Those who study and practise the above are considered to be Rsis. Seven of them with the following seven traits are remem¬ bered as Saptarsis (the Seven Sages), x They are long-lived; they compose Mantras; they arc possessed of noble qualities; they are endowed with divine visions; they are enlightened; they practise virtue directly and make their lineage function. Everyday they observe the six rites; they are flourishing householders; they believe in Adrsta (the Unseen Principle), the cause of Karmans, and act accordingly. They maintain their lives without rustic vulgarities; they prepare their own tasty dishes.; they maintain families; they are prosper¬ ous externally and internally. The arrangement of castes and stages of life in the Krta and other Yugas is made at the outset by them in each and every Age. When.the Treta Yuga begins again, these seven sages again establish the castes and stages of life entirely. In their family heroes are born again and again. Veises 94-98 describe the special qualifications, duties etc. of the Saptarsis (Seven Sages) who arc credited with a very long life. When a son is born to a father, and when the son turns into a father, the line of sages continues without a break. The sages thus live till the end of the Yuga. The number of sages who are householders is said to be eightyeight thousand. Those who resort to the Pitryana to the south of Aryaman (the Sun god), take wives unto themselves and per¬ form AgnihoPa (domestic sacrifices). They are known as the cause of progeny. Householders are innumerable. They resort to cremation ground. Eightyeight thousand of them are in the northern path. Those sages of sublimated sexuality who are reported to have attained heaven, arc reborn at the end of the Yuga as the composers of Mantras and Brahmanas. Thus they are repeatedly reborn in Dvapara Ages. They are the composers of Kalpa -Texts (Ritualistic Texts), propounders of commentatorial literature on diiTerent sciences at the end of the Yuga. When this Dvapara is over, in the further Dvapara Asvatthaman, the son of Drona, will be the Vedavyasa of great penance. 1

verses.sanskrit: शक्रेश्वरं नृपश्रेष्ठ ये प्रपश्यन्ति भक्तितः । तेषां जन्मकृतं पापं नश्यते नात्र संशयः
verses.transliteration: śakreśvaraṃ nṛpaśreṣṭha ye prapaśyanti bhaktitaḥ / teṣāṃ janmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ naśyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: In the future times the different recensions of the Vedas will be composed by him. By virtue of his great penance, he will attain eternal Brahman. Karman is attained by penance; through Karman fame is attained; through fame truth is attained; and through truth eternal Brahman is attained. From the eternal immortality is attained and from immortality essence of every object is attained. This eternal one-syllabled ( Om) Brahman, is established in the Self {Atman). It is called Brahman due to its greatness or (inconceivable) vastness. It remains in the form of Pranava and is known as Bhuh, Bhuvak, Svak. Obeisance to theBrahman of the form of Rk Yajus, Saman and Atharvan. Obeisance to that excellent Brahman that is known as the cause of the annihilation and origination of the Uni¬ verse and that is the esoteric secret beyond Maliat. It is unfathomable, unlimited and inexhaustible or imperishable. It is the source of the delusion of the Universe. It is the cause of the realization of human aims through enlight¬ enment and activity. It is the culminating point of those who adhere to the tenets of the Sankhya philosophy, the goal which gives its asso¬ ciation (?) It is the unmanifest, immortal, eternal Brahman, the cause of Prakrti. It is called Pradhana, self-bom, the secret and Sattva. It is indivisible, the essence of everything (Sukra), imperishable and multiformed. In the Krta Yuga (as) there are no religious rites, how can there be a rite not done? In this world whatever is once done or whatever is committed or omitted, whatever has been heard or should be heard, whether good or bad, what should be known, pondered over, touched or enjoyed, seen, heard or realized (is so by Brahman). Whatever has been shown by Him is the (only) know¬ ledge of Devarsis. Who can scrutinize that which He (Brahman) has pointed out*.It is the Lord alone who has declared all things to all. When anything is done by anyone, he gets identified with it. What is done by one, is previously conceived by another (i.e. by Brahman). When (even) a verbal effort ( vanmayam) by anyone is made anywhere that is done by Him (Brahman) only. The act (merely) appears to be done by the doer. Absence of passion, over-attachment, knowledge, igno¬ rance, pleasure, displeasure, dharma and adharma (good and evil), happiness, sorrow, death, immortality, the state of being above, below or at the sides—all these are due to the unseen (Adrsfa, destiny). In every Treta Age Svayambhuva (Manu),the eldest son of Brahma, the Supreme God, is the only knower of all lores which he classifies in the Dvapara Age. In the Vai- vasvata Manvantara, it is Brahma who teaches that lore at the outset. Being born frequently in the revolving cycles of the Yugas, the sages compose and propagate Samhitas. It is mentioned before that there are eighty-eight thousand Srutarsis. They propagate these (Vedic) Samhitas again and again.

verses.transliteration: agamyāgamane caiva avāhye caiva vāhite / svāmimitravighāte yannaśyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: Those branches (of the Vedic lore) are rearranged again and again in every Yuga by them who, following the Southern Path, resorted to cremation grounds ( = died). It should be known that the composition of all the different branches (of the Vedas) in the past and future Man- vantaras takes place in a similar way. (The composition of the branches of Veda) of the past (Manvantaras) have elapsed, those of the present (Man¬ vantara) exist, and those of the future (Manvantara) will be described in the future. The later Manvantara shall be understood through the earlier Manvantara. Both of them shall be understood through the present (Manvantara). The decision of the Man¬ vantara is on this-basis. Thus Devas, Rt|sf Sages and Manus jo up and return along with the Mantras. For Pain Kalpa of the Text Bd. 2.35.153 1 1I- 1 45 But till they see through this defective nature of these successive rebirths, they continue. The rebirths continue for ten Celestial Yugas before they stop. ' From Janaloka they go to Tapoloka from whence they do not return. Thus thousands of Celestial Yugas have elapsed. In Brahmaloka they meet death along with sages. It is impossible to describe in detail and in the proper order, the Manvantaras of the previous Kalpas that have gone before, because time is beginningless and they are innume¬ rable. Hundreds and thousands of Manvantaras and Kalpas have gone along with the Pitjrs, Sages, Devas and sets of Seven Sages that are the creatures of time. Dissolution at the end of a Manvantara and crea¬ tion at the end of dissolution, of Devas, Rsis, Pitrs and Manus cannot be described in detail and in proper order even in hun¬ dreds of years. The details of creation and annihilation cannot be stated. Now understand the duration of a Manvantara, according to the human calculation. The duration of a Manvantara according to the celes¬ tial calculation is eight hundred fiftytwo thousand years. Fourteen times this period constitute the Abhutasam - plava (the period of final dissolution). A thousand sets of four Yugas constitute a day of Brahma. All the living beings will be scorched by the rays of the Sun. Keeping Brahma at the head, and accompanied by Devas, Sages and Danavas, they will enter lord Mahesvara, the most excellent among Devas. (The period) what is called Yuga has been already That which includes Krta and Treta, Dvapara and Kali is known as Caturyuga (set of four Yugas). When it revol¬ ves into seventyone cycles, it is the period of a Manvantara. Thus the lord has ordained.
