verses.transliteration: gopradānaṃ prakartavyaṃ śubhaṃ brāhmaṇapuṃgave / dhuryaṃ vā dāpayet tasmin sarvāṅgaruciraṃ nṛpa
verses.translation: The characteristics of the Manvantaras of the past or of the future are explained through (those of) the present one. Thus the mode of creation of Svayambhuva Manu has been narrated. I shall now mention the interim period which links it with the following Manvantara. The Manvantaras in the future will also pass as in the previous period along with Devas and sages through the inevitabi¬ Those who have been the lords of the three worlds in this Manvantara, the Seven Sages, Devas, Pitrs and Manus are known as Sadhakas throughout the period of this Manvantara. Realising the expiry of their tenure and the fall from authority, they eagerly turn to go to Maharloka. The deities who decline in this Manvantara survive Krta Yuga in the course of their life time. In the meanwhile the future lords of Manvantaras, Dei¬ ties, Pitrs, Sages and Manus are born similarly. In every Manvantara it is the surviving subjects at the end of Kaliyugas who constitute the earlier subjects of the Krta Yugas. Just as the continuity of Krta Yuga is remembered as preceded by Kali Yuga by learned men, so also the beginning of Manvantaras is preceded by the end of (the previous) Manvantara. When the earlier Manvantara declines and the later one begins to function, those who survive in the beginning of the Krta Yuga, viz. the Seven Sages and Manu, remain biding their time (performing penance). When the creation of rain begins, they function actively for the proper working of the Manvantara and for the Verses 145-176 describe Pratisandhi —transition from one Yuga or Manvantara to another. Even as they perform penance extremely difficult to be performed for the Devas, Asuras, Pitrs, Sages, Serpents, Ghosts and Goblins, Gandharvas, Yaksas andRaksasas are born as before on the death of the earlier persons. The good people who have survived, begin to teach and propagate the good conduct of life. In the beginning of the Manvantaras, Manu and the Seven Sages initiate the holy rites. Human beings along with the Devas also perform those rites. At the beginning of a Manvantara as in the begin¬ ning of the Treta Yuga, when Devas and men become stabilised in Dharma, they absolve themselves from the idebtedness to Rsis (sages) by observing celibacy, to Pitrs by procereation and to the Devas by performance of sacrifices. After remaining in the practice of virtue pertaining to the castes and stages of life for a hundred thousand years, and after establishing the set of three Vedas, agricultural and other occupations for livelihood, maintenance of law and order and the virtuous practice of the discipline of castes and stages of life,

verses.transliteration: dātavyaṃ parayā bhaktyā svarge vāsamabhīpsatā / etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ śakreśvaraphalaṃ nṛpa
verses.translation: After they have set out for heaven, they at the outset At the end of the Manvantara, they abandon their abodes and go to Maharloka which is free from ailments, Free from aberrations, endowed with mental Siddhis, these people of self-control, stay till the final dissolution, observ- When all these have passed all the abodes become vacant everywhere Among the Seven Sages, Manu, Devas and Pitrs those who had been before die along with the future ones (?) Their final dissolution takes place at the close of (all) Manvantaras. They continue endlessly in the same order in all the Manvantaras, till the final dissolution of all beings. Thus the characteristics of the inter-link of the past Manvantaras and future have been declared by Svayambhuva Manu. The sequence of the Manvantaras of the past and future is snapped entirely through the final dissolution. After the lapse of the Manvantaras, these attain Maharloka; from Maharloka they go to Jana, Tapah and Satya Lokas. As observed by those who have that sort of mystic experience and as proved by manifold testimony, they stay in Satya Loka, but when aberrations set in at the hour of dissolution of Manvantara, they lerve off Satya Loka and with devotion they enter the body of lord Narayana, of vast incomprehensible size. In all the changes of Manvantaras that have been functioning for a long time, the world of living beings does not remain (the same) even for a moment. Due to the nature of destiny, it (the world) undergoes changes by way of decrease or increase. It is highly meritorious to eulogise the lords born It is conducive to the attainment of heaven. It is very holy, highly esoteric, capable of granting progeny. It should be recited during great parvan days. It is conducive to the removal of the effects of bad dreams and is conducive to longevity. Resort to the great principle Sumahesa for attaining Siddhis. Resort to this Purana which contains the narratives of Prajapatis, Devas, Sages, the well-known yet sacred origination of the unborn Lord and for the fulfilment of my narration. Thus I have described the Svayambhuva Manvantara in detail and in the proper order. What more shall I describe to you?

verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe śakreśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 62 śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: tato gacchettu rājendra karoḍīśvaram uttamam / yatra vai nihatāstāta dānavāḥ sapadānugāḥ
verses.translation: I wish to know precisely the order of Manvantaras 1 and all the respective deities pertaining to the different Manvan¬ taras. Listen to and understand as I recount succinctly and in detail, the Manvantaras which have gone and which are yet to come. The first Manu was Svayambhuva and then there was Svarocisa Manu. Thereafter the Manus wereAuttama, Tamasa, They arc the five Savarnas, Raucya, Bhautya and Vai- vasvata. I shall explain them after Vaivasvata Manu. Know the five Manus who have passed away to be Manavas. The Manvantara of Svayambhuva Manu which lias already passed has been described by me. Henceforth, I shall describe briefly the activity of crea¬ tion by Svarocisa, the second Manu of noble soul." In the Svarocisa Manvantara, there were the Devas called Tusitas and the learned scholars called Paravatas. Only these two are remembered as the groups of Devas.
verses.hindi: अत ऊध्वं प्रवक्ष्यासि सूर्याचन्द्रमसोगंतिम् । सुर्याचन्द्रमसावेतो भ्रमन्‍्तौ यावदेव तु
verses.wordMeaning: I wish to know precisely the order of Manvantaras 1 and all the respective deities pertaining to the different Manvan¬ taras. Listen to and understand as I recount succinctly and in detail, the Manvantaras which have gone and which are yet to come.…
verses.commentary: Sense: I wish to know precisely the order of Manvantaras 1 and all the respective deities pertaining to the different Manvan¬ taras. Listen to and understand as I recount succinctly and in detail, the Manvantaras which have gone and which are yet to come.…

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्रादिदेवैः संहृष्टैः सततं जयबुद्धिभिः । तेषां ये पुत्रपौत्राश्च पूर्ववैरम् अनुस्मरम्
verses.transliteration: indrādidevaiḥ saṃhṛṣṭaiḥ satataṃ jayabuddhibhiḥ / teṣāṃ ye putrapautrāśca pūrvavairam anusmaram
verses.translation: They were born of Tusita as the sons of Kralu, the Svarocisa (Manu). The Paravatas and the remaining ones—these two Ganas (groups) consist of twelve each. (Thus) all these Devas together are remembered as chandajas and they are twen¬ ty-four (in number). Dhaivasyasa, Vamanya, Gopa, Devayata, lord Aja, the powerful lord Durona, Apa of powerful arms, the vigorous Mahaujas, C.ikitvan, Nibhrta, Viryavan, and Amsa: these were the sons of Kratu. They were then the imbibers of Soma. Lord Pracetas, Visvedeva, Samanja who was well known, Ajihma the suppressor of enemies, Ajihmana and Mahl- yana endowed with learning, the blessed Aja and Usa, Yavxya of great strength, Hotr and Yajva were the Paravatas of great exploit. These all were the deities whofunctioned in the Svaro¬ cisa Manvantara. At that time these twenty-four Devatas (deities) were the imbibers of Soma. Their Indra (ruler and leader) was Vaidha who was world-famous. The Saptarsis (the Seven Sages) were Orja the son of Vasistha, Stambha the son ofKasyapa, Drona the sonofBhrgu, There are some variations in the names of future Manus in some Puranas. Our Purana gives some different names (such as Raucya and Bhautya) of future Manus. Verses 6-22 enumerate and describe the fuiicuonaries (gods, Indra etc.) during the second Manvantara.
verses.hindi: प्रकाशतः स्वभाभिस्तों मण्डलाभ्यां समास्थितौ जिह्वाओं से ज्वाला-माला को फेंकते रहने के कारण कलास की तरह दीख पड़ते है ।४३-४८। चिकने शरीर से कूंडली बाँध हुए) नागराज बाल सूय की तरह ताम्रबर्ण वाले अपने दो हजार नेत्रों से वहाँ सुशोभित हो रहे हैं । कुन्द ओर इन्दु के समान उज्ज्वल नागराज के नयनों की पंक्ति उसी तरह बिराजती है, जैसे इबेत पवेत के मस्तक पर तरुण सूय की पंक्ति । जिस समय ये सोते या बैठते हैं, उस समय द्यतिमात नागराज
verses.wordMeaning: They were born of Tusita as the sons of Kralu, the Svarocisa (Manu). The Paravatas and the remaining ones—these two Ganas (groups) consist of twelve each. (Thus) all these Devas together are remembered as chandajas and they are twen¬ ty-four (in number). Dhaivasyasa, Vamanya,…

verses.sanskrit: क्रुद्धैर्देवसमूहैश्च दानवा निहता रणे । तेषां शिरांसि संगृह्य सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः
verses.transliteration: kruddhairdevasamūhaiśca dānavā nihatā raṇe / teṣāṃ śirāṃsi saṃgṛhya sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ
verses.translation: Caitra, Kaviruta,Krtanta, Ravi, Brhat, Guha, Nava and Subha 1: these nine are rememberd as the sons of Svarocisa Manu who established his race. They have been enumerated in the Purana. Such is the second Manvantara. The Seven Sages, Manu, Devas and Pitrs—these four constitute theroot (and foundation)of a Manvantara. All the subjects are subsidiary to them. Deities are the sons of Sages, Pitrs are the sons of Devas and the Sages are the sons of Devas—This is the conclusion of the Sastras (Scriptures). Ksatriyas and Vaisyas were born of Manu and Brahmanas were born of the Seven Sages. Thus the Manvan¬ tara has been described in brief, not in details. The detailed description of the Svarocisa Manvantara should be understood through (thatof) Svayambhuva Manvan¬ tara. It is impossible to describe it in detail even in hundreds of years, since the progenies are many in every family and they are oft-repeated. The Manvantara of Auttama is the third among the Manvantaras. 2 There are five Ganas. I shall recount them. Under¬ stand them. The Devas are Sudhamans, Vasavartins, Pratardanas, Sivas, and Satyas. Each of these groups (< Ganas ) consists of twelve (Devas).
verses.hindi: जटाओं के द्वारा अत्यन्त भयज्भूर मालूम पड़ते है। उस समय ऐसा जान पड़ता है कि, मानो हजार शिखरवाला विदश्ञाल पव॑त पृथ्वी पर पड़ा है ।४६-४१॥। विशालशरीर, महाभाग्य अतुलबल ओर महानाग होने के कारण वह महातेजस्त्री महानागपतिं सबके द्वारा पूजित हो रहे हैं। सभी नागों के राजा वे महाद्यतिमान् शेषनाग हैं। यह विष्णु का ही सपंरूषी शरीर है, जो पृथ्वी की सीमा पर स्थित है। देव, असुर महानाग और राक्षसों

verses.sanskrit: निक्षिप्य नर्मदातोये बन्धुभावम् अनुस्मरम् । तत्र स्नात्वा सुराः सर्वे स्थापयित्वा उमापतिम्
verses.transliteration: nikṣipya narmadātoye bandhubhāvam anusmaram / tatra snātvā surāḥ sarve sthāpayitvā umāpatim
verses.translation: The names of the twelve constituting Sudhamans are Satya, Dhrti, Dama, Danta, Ksama, Ksama, Dhrti (Dhvani— Bd.P.), Suci, Isa, Orjas, Jyestha and Vapusman the twelfth. The Vamsakarin Devas (Vasavartins) were Sahasra- dhara, Visvatman, Samitara, Brhadvasu, Visvadha, ViSvakarma Manasvanta, Virad. Yasas, Jyotis, Vibhavya and Klrtiman. Pramardana (Pratardana) gods are glorified. They As per A. Verses 23-36 describe the Auttama or Uttama's Manvantara. As noted in v. 36 the activities of creation etc. are the same as in the previous Man¬ vantara. The reading anyanaradhito dtvo c God not worshipped by others' is mean¬ ingless, as this is a list of Pratardana gods.— c Pramardana * in the text is an Understand the names of those constituting the Satya category of Devas, as agreed (by sages of yore). They are Dikpati, Vakpati, Visva, Sarnbhu, Svamrdika, Adhi- pa, Varcodhas, Muhyasarvas'a (?), Vasava, Sadasva, Ksema and Ananda. These are those sacrifice-worthy other twelve (Devas) famous as Satyas. These are the deities who lived in the Manvantara of Auttama.
verses.hindi: के निवास से युक्त व्यावहारिक सातों रसातलों का ऐसा ही वर्णन है ।५२-५४। इसके आगे ऐसे स्थान हैं जहाँ पर न तो साधु ही जा सकते हैं, न तो देवता । यहाँ तक कि वे अब तक न तो एिद्धों द्वारा देखे ही गए हैं और न तो देवता ही उनको जान पाये हैं । ब्राह्मणो ! महषिगण पृथ्वी, अग्नि. जल, वायु और आकाश का महत्त्व इसी प्रकार बताते हैं, इसमें सन्देह नहीं ।५५०५६। इसके आगे अब हम सूयं और चन्द्र की गति बतलाते हैं। ये चन्द्र और सूर्य अपने मण्डल (कक्षा) में वतेमान रहकर सदा घूमते रहते हैं और अपनी प्रभा
verses.wordMeaning: The names of the twelve constituting Sudhamans are Satya, Dhrti, Dama, Danta, Ksama, Ksama, Dhrti (Dhvani— Bd.P.), Suci, Isa, Orjas, Jyestha and Vapusman the twelfth. The Vamsakarin Devas (Vasavartins) were Sahasra- dhara, Visvatman, Samitara, Brhadvasu, Visvadha,…

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्रेण सहिताः सर्वे ऽपूजयंल्लोकसिद्धये । हृष्टचित्ताः सुराः सर्वे जग्मुराकाशमण्डलम्
verses.transliteration: indreṇa sahitāḥ sarve 'pūjayaṃllokasiddhaye / hṛṣṭacittāḥ surāḥ sarve jagmurākāśamaṇḍalam
verses.translation: Aja, Parasu, Divya, Divyausadhi, Naya, the un¬ equalled Devanuja, Mahotsaha, Ausija, Vinlta, Suketu, Sumitra, Subala and Suci—these thirteen were the noble-souled sons of the Manu Auttama. These were the progenitors of the race of Ksatriyas and made them flourish. Such is the third Manvan- tara. The activity of creation etc. in the course of the Auttama Manvantara has been explained through (that of) Svarocisa Manvantara. Now listen and understand the creation etc. in the Tamasa Manvantara in detail and in the proper order. In the fourth period of Manvantara * 1 2 of the Manu Tamasa, the Ganas were four, viz. Satyas, Svarupas, Sudhls and Haris. In the Manvantara of Tamasa, the gardsons of Pulastya (manifested themselves). Each of these Devaganas consisted of twentyfive (gods). If Vitta, Kratu and Rathormi from the readings in Bd. P. is accepted, the list will have twelve names (the expected number of this group of Devas). Verses 37-43 deal with Tamasa Manvantara. The hundred Indriyas (sense-organs) and the eighth Tamas (Darkness) which the top-most sages who value truth as life, enunciate, are remembered as the Devas in that Manvan- tara.
verses.hindi: बट्पञचासतमइलोकास्तेथध्यायसमाप्ति. ख. पुस्तके वरतंते ।
verses.wordMeaning: Aja, Parasu, Divya, Divyausadhi, Naya, the un¬ equalled Devanuja, Mahotsaha, Ausija, Vinlta, Suketu, Sumitra, Subala and Suci—these thirteen were the noble-souled sons of the Manu Auttama. These were the progenitors of the race of Ksatriyas and made them flourish.…

verses.sanskrit: दानवानां महाभाग सूदिता कोटिरुत्तमा । तदा प्रभृति तत्तीर्थं करोडीति महीतले
verses.transliteration: dānavānāṃ mahābhāga sūditā koṭiruttamā / tadā prabhṛti tattīrthaṃ karoḍīti mahītale
verses.translation: Sibi the lord of (great) exploit, was the Indra of those Devas. O excellent ones, understand the seven sages of that Manvantara. Harsa, the son of Kavi; Pfthu, the son of Kasyapa; Agni, the son of Atri; Jyotirdhaman, the son of Bhrgu; Vanapltha, the son of Pulaha, Gotra, the son ofVasistha; and Caitra, the son ofPulastya were the (seven) sages in theTamasa Manvan¬ tara. Janughanda, Santi, Nara: Khyati, Bhaya, Priyabhrtya, Avaksi, Prstalodha, Drdhodyata, Rta and Rtabandhu were the sons of Tama sa Manu. In the fifth cycle of Manvantara of Carisnava Manu, 1 the groups of Devatas are well enumerated. Understand them. Amrtabha, Abhutarajas, Vikunthaand Sumedhas were the auspicious sons of Carisnu alias Vasistha, the Prajapati. Their shining and glorious Ganas were fourteen and four (i.e. eighteen) (or fourteen for each of the four Ganas). Svatra (Svapna in A.), Vipra, Agnibhas, Pratyetistha, Amrta, Sumati, Vavirava, Vacinoda, Srava, PravirasI, Vadaand Prasa were the fourteen (?) Amrtabhas remembered as the devas in the Carisnava Manvantara. Mati, Sumati, Rta, Satya, Avrti, 2 Vivrti, Mada, Vinaya, Jeta, Jisnu, Sahas, Dyutiman and Sravasa—these are the names of Abhutarajas Ganas as (they) know.
verses.hindi: पर्यासपारिमसाण्य॑ तु चर्द्रादित्यौं प्रकाशतः । पर्यासपारिसाण्येन भूमेस्तुल्य॑ दिवं॑ स्मृतम् अवति त्रीनिमांल्‍्लोकॉन्यस्मात्सूयें: परिश्रमन् । अवधातुः प्रकाशार्यों ह्यवनात्स रविः स्मृतः
verses.wordMeaning: Sibi the lord of (great) exploit, was the Indra of those Devas. O excellent ones, understand the seven sages of that Manvantara. Harsa, the son of Kavi; Pfthu, the son of Kasyapa; Agni, the son of Atri; Jyotirdhaman, the son of Bhrgu; Vanapltha, the son of Pulaha, Gotra,…

verses.sanskrit: विख्यातं तु तदा लोके पापघ्नं पाण्डुनन्दन । अष्टम्यां च चतुर्दश्याम् उभौ पक्षौ च भक्तितः । उपोष्य शूलिनश्चाग्रे रात्रौ कुर्वीत जागरम्
verses.transliteration: vikhyātaṃ tu tadā loke pāpaghnaṃ pāṇḍunandana / aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyām ubhau pakṣau ca bhaktitaḥ / upoṣya śūlinaścāgre rātrau kurvīta jāgaram
verses.translation: Vrsa, Bhetta, 3 Jaya, Bhima, §uci, Danta,Yasa, Dama, Natha, Vidvan, Ajeya, Krsa, Gaura and Dhruva are glorified as Vikunthas. Uunderstand the Sumedhas. Verses 44-55 describe the fifth Manvantara which the text calls Caris¬ nava i.e. of Manu Carisnu but calls the same Manu as Raivata in verses 54, 55 and 56. Manus from Svarocisa to Raivata belonged to the lineage of Priyaviata. Bd.P. ibid v. 56 adds c Edhana * here and makes up the number fourteen. Reading in Bd. P. accepted to make up the number (14). Medha, Medhatithi, Satyamedha, Prsnimcdha, Al- pamedha, Bhuyomedha and others (?), the lord Dlptimedha, Yasomedha, Sthiramedha, Sarvamedha, Asvamedha, Pratime- dha, Medhavan and Medhaharta are glorified as Sumedhas. Vibhu of well known exploits and manliness was their Indra. Then the (seven) sages in the fifth Manvantara of Raivata Manu were: Vedabahu, son (descedant) of Pulastya; the sage called Yaju, the son of Kafyapa; Hiranyaroma, son of Angiras; Vedasri, son of Bhrgu; Ordhvabahu, son of Vasistha; Parjanya, son of Pulaha; and Satyanetra, son of Atri. Mahapuranasambhavya, Pratyangaparaha, Suci, Bala- bandhu, Niramitra, Ketubhrnga and Drdhavrata were the sons of Carisnava. Such is the fifth Manvantara.
verses.hindi: अस्य भारतवर्षस्य विष्कम्भ तु सुविस्तरम् । सण्डलं भास्केरस्थाथ योजनानां निबोधत

verses.sanskrit: सत्कथापाठसंयुक्तो वेदाध्ययनसंयुतः । प्रभाते विमले प्राप्ते पूजयेत् त्रिदशेश्वरम्
verses.transliteration: satkathāpāṭhasaṃyukto vedādhyayanasaṃyutaḥ / prabhāte vimale prāpte pūjayet tridaśeśvaram
verses.translation: Svarocisa, Auttama, Tamasa and Raivatas—these four Manus belong to the family of Priyavrata. In the sixth cycle of Caksusa Manvantara 1 the Devas are remembered as consisting of five Ganas (classes), viz. Adyas, Prasutas, Bhavyas, the heaven-dwelling Prthukas and the Lekhas of great dignity. This creation of heaven-dwellers is mentioned in accor¬ dance with the names of their mothers. The Ganas of those Devas are the great-grandsons of Aranya, the Prajapati, the son of Atri. Each of these groups is remembered as comprising of eight Devas. Antariksa, Vasu, Haya, Atithi, Priyavrata, Srota, Manta and Sumanta—these are glorified as Adyas. Syenabhadra, Pasya, Pathyanetra of great fame. Suma- nas, Suvetas, Raivata, Supracetas and Dyuti of great prowess— these are mentioned as Prasutas. Vijaya, Sujaya,Mana, Udyana, Sumati, Supari,Vijnata and Arthapati—these Devas are remembered as Bhavyas. Now listen and understand the Prthuka gods. Ajista, the Lord Sakyana, Vanaprstha, Sankara, Satya- dhrsnu,Visnu, Vijaya and the highly blessed Ajita are the heaven¬ dwelling Prthukas. Verses 57-69 describe the Caksu§a Manvantara.
verses.hindi: नवयोजनासाहस्रो विस्तारों भास्करस्य तु । विस्तारात्त्रियुणाश्चास्य परिणाहोथ मण्डलम् निष्कम्भो सण्डलस्थेव भास्कराद्दिगुण: शशी ्््ि ।

verses.sanskrit: पञ्चामृतेन संस्नाप्य श्रीखण्डेन च गुण्ठयेत् । शस्तैः पल्लवपुष्पैश्च पूजयेत्तु प्रयत्नतः
verses.transliteration: pañcāmṛtena saṃsnāpya śrīkhaṇḍena ca guṇṭhayet / śastaiḥ pallavapuṣpaiśca pūjayettu prayatnataḥ
verses.translation: I shall now describe Lekhas. Understand as I recount them. Manojava, Praghasa, Pracetas of great fame, Vata, Dhru- vaksiti, Adbhuta of great virility, Avanaand Brhaspati are glori¬ fied as Lekhas. Manojava of great virility and prowess became their Indra then. The seven sages in the Caksusa Manvantara were: Unnata, son (descendant) of Bhrgu; Havisman, son of Angiras; Sudhaman, son of Kasyapa; Virajas, son of Vasistha; Atimana, son of Pulastya; Sahisnu, son of Pulaha, and Madhura, descendant of Atri. Oru, Puru, Satadyumna, Tapasvin, Satyavak, Krti, Agnistut, Atiratra and Sudyumna—these nine and the tenth one Abhimanyu; these were the sons of Caksusa Manuborn of Nad- vall. Such is the six'h Manvantara. O Bramanas, the creation of that noble soul is explain¬ ed through (that of) Vaivasvata Manvantara and it has been explained by me in detail and in the proper order. The successors and heirs of Caksusa Manu were born in the family of Kasyapa. Please mention (enumerate) to us all those others who were born in his family. It behoves you to hear the creative activity of Caksusa Manu in brief. Prthu, the valorous son of Vena, was born in his family. Other Prajapatis and Daksa, son of Pracetas, too were born (of that family). Atri, the Prajapati, adopted Uttanapada as his son.
verses.hindi: इत्येतदिह संख्यातं पुराणं परिमाणतः । तद्वक्ष्यामि प्रसंख्याय सांप्रतरभिमानिभिः
verses.wordMeaning: I shall now describe Lekhas. Understand as I recount them. Manojava, Praghasa, Pracetas of great fame, Vata, Dhru- vaksiti, Adbhuta of great virility, Avanaand Brhaspati are glori¬ fied as Lekhas. Manojava of great virility and prowess became their Indra then.…
verses.commentary: Sense: I shall now describe Lekhas. Understand as I recount them. Manojava, Praghasa, Pracetas of great fame, Vata, Dhru- vaksiti, Adbhuta of great virility, Avanaand Brhaspati are glori¬ fied as Lekhas. Manojava of great virility and prowess became their Indra then.…

verses.sanskrit: बहुरूपं जपन्मन्त्रं दक्षिणाशां व्यवस्थितः । यथोक्तेन विधानेन नाभिमात्रे जले क्षिपेत्
verses.transliteration: bahurūpaṃ japanmantraṃ dakṣiṇāśāṃ vyavasthitaḥ / yathoktena vidhānena nābhimātre jale kṣipet
verses.translation: The son of Daksaka, the Prajapati,became a king. He was given in adoption to Atri for some reason by Svayambhuva Manu after the advent of the sixth (Manvantara). O Brahma- nas, having reached the future Manvantara Caksusa, I shall now explain it by way of introduction. The very clever daughter of Dharma and his wife LaksmI, the lady of sparkling smiles named Sunrta (Suniti), the lady who could produce wealth, bore to Uttanapada a son named Dhruva and became his auspicious mother. Uttanapada begot of her Dhruva, Kirtiman, Ayasman and Vasu and also two daughters of sparkling smiles, Manasvini and Svara. Their sons have been already mentioned. The valorous Dhruva, praying for (desirous of) exten¬ sive fame, performed penance for ten thousand divine years observing fast. In the first Tretayuga, he (Dhruva), the grandson of Svayambhuva Manu, controlled himself by means of Yoga in his desire to win great fame. The delighted Brahma granted him the excellent abode among luminaries. It is pleasing and lasting till the final dissolution of the Universe. It is devoid of setting and rising. On seeing his unlimited glory and greatness, Usanas, the preceptor ofDaityas and Asuras, sang this Sloka (verse). "How wonderful is the prowess of his penance! How commendable is his learning! Wonderful is his Huta (Holy rite) that the seven sages have kept Dhruva above themselves. The firmament depends on Dhruva. He is the controller and the lord of the firmament". Bhumibore to Dhruva two kings (as sons), viz. Pusti and Bhavya. The powerful lord Pusti told his shadow, "Be a woman".
verses.hindi: अभिमानिव्यतीता ये तुल्यास्ते सांप्रतेरिह। देवा ये वे ह्मयतीतास्ते रूपर्नॉमभिरेव च तस्मात्तु सांप्रतेदेवेबंक्यासि वसुधातलम्। दिवस्तु संनिवेशो वे सांप्रतेरेव ऋत्स्नशः (६७ शतार्धकोटिविस्तारा पृथिवी क्ृत्स्नतः स्मृता । तस्या बाधप्रमाणेन मेरोवें चातुरन्तरम् 0६८ पृथिव्या बाधविस्तारों योजनाप्रात्प्रकीतितः  मेदसध्यात्प्रतिदिशं कोठिरेका तु सा स्‍्पृता.
verses.wordMeaning: The son of Daksaka, the Prajapati,became a king. He was given in adoption to Atri for some reason by Svayambhuva Manu after the advent of the sixth (Manvantara). O Brahma- nas, having reached the future Manvantara Caksusa, I shall now explain it by way of introduction.…
verses.commentary: Sense: The son of Daksaka, the Prajapati,became a king. He was given in adoption to Atri for some reason by Svayambhuva Manu after the advent of the sixth (Manvantara). O Brahma- nas, having reached the future Manvantara Caksusa, I shall now explain it by way of introduction.…

verses.sanskrit: तिलाञ्जलिं तु प्रेताय दक्षिणाशाम् उपस्थितः । श्राद्धं तत्रैव विप्राय कारयेद् विजितेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration: tilāñjaliṃ tu pretāya dakṣiṇāśām upasthitaḥ / śrāddhaṃ tatraiva viprāya kārayed vijitendriyaḥ
verses.translation: At his truthful utterance, the shadow of divine body became a woman immediately. She was bedecked in divine ornaments. Pusti begot of his Chaya five sinless sons, viz. Pracinagarbha, Vrsaka, Vrka,Vrkala and Dhrti. The wife of Pracinagarbha named Bhuvarca gave birth to a son who became a king by the name of Udaradhi. In his previous birth, he had been Indra. He used to take food but once at the end of every thousand years. Thus the lord secured Indra-hood which lasted a Manvantara. Bliadra bore to Udaradhi the son Divaiijaya. Varangi bore to Divaiijaya the son Ripu, the conqueror of foes. From Ripu, Brhati, bore a son Caksusa endowed with aU types of brilliance. Caksusa begot Manu of Puskarini, a descendant of Varuna and the daughter of the noble-souled Prajapati Aranya. O blessed one, Manu begot ten auspicious sons of Nadvala, the daughter of Vairaja, the Prajapati.
verses.hindi: से प्रकाश किया करते हैं ५७। सातों समुद्रों और द्वीपों का वही विस्तार है, जो पृथ्वी का है। चन्द्र सूय बहिर्भागस्थ परिधि परिमाण में प्रकाश करते हैं । यह आकाशमण्डल भूमि के परिधि परिमाण के समात है। घूमते हुए सूथ॑ जिस कांरण तीनों लोकों को प्रकाशित करते हैं; इस कारण प्रकाशाथ्थेंक “अव' धातु से प्रकाश करने के कारण “रवि” शब्द बना है ।५८-६०। इसके आगे अब हम चरद्र-सूयं के प्रमाण को कहते
verses.wordMeaning: At his truthful utterance, the shadow of divine body became a woman immediately. She was bedecked in divine ornaments. Pusti begot of his Chaya five sinless sons, viz. Pracinagarbha, Vrsaka, Vrka,Vrkala and Dhrti.…
verses.commentary: Sense: At his truthful utterance, the shadow of divine body became a woman immediately. She was bedecked in divine ornaments. Pusti begot of his Chaya five sinless sons, viz. Pracinagarbha, Vrsaka, Vrka,Vrkala and Dhrti.…

verses.sanskrit: विषमैरग्रजातैश्च वेदाभ्यसनतत्परैः । गोहिरण्येन सम्पूज्य ताम्बूलैर्भोजनैस्तथा
verses.transliteration: viṣamairagrajātaiśca vedābhyasanatatparaiḥ / gohiraṇyena sampūjya tāmbūlairbhojanaistathā
verses.translation: The sons of Manu and Nadvala were Oru, Puru, Sata- dyumna, Tapasvin, Satyavak, Kavi, Agnistut, Atiratra and Sudyumna—these nine as well as the tenth son Abhimanyu. Agneyi bore to Oru six sons of great brilliance, viz. Anga, Sumanas, Svati, Kratu, Angiras and Siva. To Anga, Sunltha bore a single child Vena. Due to the misdemeanour of Vena, there was a great indignant commotion. For the sake of progeny, the sages (churned) his right hand. When the hand of Vena was pressed, a great king was born. The royal descendant of Vena was glorified as Prthu. Prthu, the son of Vena, was the foremost of Ksatriyas. He was born with a bow and a coat of mail. He appeared blazing with his splendour. He protected all the worlds. He was the first among kings who had been crowned in the Rajasuya sacrifice. He was the ruler of the Earth. In order to eulogise him, the clever Suta and Magadha (Bards) were born. For the sake of his subjects desirous of livelihood the Earth in the form of a cow was milked, yielding all sorts of plants, along with the Devas, groups of Sages, Pitrs, Danavas, Gandharvas, Apsaras-s, all Punyajanas, creepers and mountains. Being milked in different vessels, the Earth (Vasundhara —that which contains rich deposits) yielded milk as much as they desired. Thereby, he sustained the world.
verses.hindi: हैं। इस भारतवषं में मही शब्द 'महितत्वात्' अर्थात् पृज्यत्व के कारण निपातन से सद्ध हुआ है। इस भारतवर्ष का विस्तार सूर्य के विस्तृत मण्डल के समान है। अब इसके बाद इनके विस्तार का प्रमाण सुनिये ।६१-६२। सूर्य का विस्तार नो हजार योजन है । इस विस्तार से इनके मण्डल की विशञालता तीन गुनी अधिक है एवं सूर्य से चन्द्रमंडल का विस्तार दुगुना अधिक है। अब हम सातों द्वीपों और मसमुद्रों वाली प्रृथ्वी का विस्तार और मंडल-प्रमाण योजनों में कहते हैं। वतंमान अभिमानी देवों द्वारा संख्यात और पुराणानुमोदित जो परिमाण है उसे ही हम कह रहे हैं। वर्तमान कालिक देवगण रूपों और नामों में अतीत अभिमानी देवों के ही समान हैं। इसलिये वर्तमान कालिक देवों के साथ पृथ्वीतल और आकाश के संनिबेश को पूर्ण रूप से कह रहे हैं ।६३-६७। मेरुमध्य से चारों ओर इस सम्पूर्ण प्रथ्वी का विस्तारप्रमाण
verses.wordMeaning: The sons of Manu and Nadvala were Oru, Puru, Sata- dyumna, Tapasvin, Satyavak, Kavi, Agnistut, Atiratra and Sudyumna—these nine as well as the tenth son Abhimanyu. Agneyi bore to Oru six sons of great brilliance, viz. Anga, Sumanas, Svati, Kratu, Angiras and Siva. To Anga,…
verses.commentary: Sense: The sons of Manu and Nadvala were Oru, Puru, Sata- dyumna, Tapasvin, Satyavak, Kavi, Agnistut, Atiratra and Sudyumna—these nine as well as the tenth son Abhimanyu. Agneyi bore to Oru six sons of great brilliance, viz. Anga, Sumanas, Svati, Kratu, Angiras and Siva. To Anga,…

verses.sanskrit: भूषणैः पादुकाभिश्च ब्राह्मणान्पाण्डुनन्दन । भवेत्कोटिगुणं तस्य नात्र कार्या विचारणा
verses.transliteration: bhūṣaṇaiḥ pādukābhiśca brāhmaṇānpāṇḍunandana / bhavetkoṭiguṇaṃ tasya nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
verses.translation: O highly intelligent one, narrate in detail the story of the birth of Prthu and how the Earth ( Vasundhara ) was milked formerly by that noble-souled (king) along with Devas, serpents, Brahmanas, Sages, Yaksas, Gandharvas and Apsaras-s. To us who solicit (the information) describe their special forms of vessels, the milker, the milk and the different calves (used for milking). Please mention everything to us, for what reason the hand of Vena was pressed formerly by the infuriated sages. O Brahmanas, I shall describe the origin of Prthu, the son of Vena. O excellent Brahmanas, listen attentively with minds purified by austerities. I shall not describe- this holy narrative to an impure person, nor to a sinful one, nor to one who is not a disciple, nor to one who is malevolent and never to (by no means to) one who does not observe holy rites. This story is conducive to fame, longevity and attainment of heaven. It is holy and on a par with the Vedas. It is esoteric as the sages, have said. He who is not malicious shall hear it. The man who recounts this narrative of the birth of Prthu, the son of Vena' to Brahmanas after bowing to them shall not bewail errors of commission and omission. This king (i.e. Pfthu) was a defender of faith. He was equal to Atri. The Prajapati named Ahga was born in the family of Atri. Vena was his son. He was not very pious or faithful.
verses.hindi: पच्रास करोड़ योजन है। प्रथ्वी का बाध विस्तार मेरुमध्य से एक योजन आगे से कहा गया है और मेर के
verses.wordMeaning: O highly intelligent one, narrate in detail the story of the birth of Prthu and how the Earth ( Vasundhara ) was milked formerly by that noble-souled (king) along with Devas, serpents, Brahmanas, Sages, Yaksas, Gandharvas and Apsaras-s.…
verses.commentary: Sense: O highly intelligent one, narrate in detail the story of the birth of Prthu and how the Earth ( Vasundhara ) was milked formerly by that noble-souled (king) along with Devas, serpents, Brahmanas, Sages, Yaksas, Gandharvas and Apsaras-s.…

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिंस् तीर्थे तु यः कश्चित् त्यजेद् देहं विधानतः । तस्य भवति यत्पुण्यं तच्छृणुष्व नराधिप
verses.transliteration: tasmiṃs tīrthe tu yaḥ kaścit tyajed dehaṃ vidhānataḥ / tasya bhavati yatpuṇyaṃ tacchṛṇuṣva narādhipa
verses.translation: The Prajapati was born of Sunitha, the daughter of Mrtyu. Vena was the son of the daughter of Kala. Hence on account of the (hereditary) evil trait of his maternal grandfather, Vena (was cruel). He turned his back on Dharma; he indulged in covet¬ ousness as he pleased. He established institutions devoid of Dharma (Virtue and Piety). Disregarding the Vedas and Sastras he was engrossed in sinful and evil activities. While he reigned the subjects were devoid of Vedic study and utterance of Vasatkaras. The deities did not partake of the sacrificial offerings nor did they drink the Soma juice. "No Yajna should be performed. No offerings should be oblated to fire". This was the cruel, solemn declaration of that Prajapati when his (utter) ruin was imminent. He proclaimed: "In all sacrifices, I deserve to be offered sacrifice (sacrificial oblations) and worship, by all twice- born castes. Yajnas should be performed unto me. I should be invoked while (performing) Homas." "We are going to be initiated (into a rite last¬ ing) for many hundreds of years. O Vena, do not perform un¬ righteous acts. This is not the eternal Dharma. In the (family of the God of) Death you are undoubtedly born as a Prajapati. It has been promised by you formerly: T shall protect the sub¬ jects. While they talked thus, Vena spoke to the Brahmarsis: The evil-minded but eloquent Vena laughingly said thus: "Who else is the creator of Dharma? Whose words aie needed by me? Who is there on the Earth equal to me in prowess, learning, penance and truthfulness? You all know precisely that I am inferior to none, that I am a noble soul. I am the source of origin of all the worlds and particularly of all Dharmas. If I wish I can burn the entire Earth or make it flood¬ ed with water. I can create it or swallow (annihilate) it. No doubts or suspicions need be entertained in this matter." When the king Vena who was utterly deluded by stubbornness and sense of false prestige, could not be dissuaded, the great sages became infuriated.
verses.hindi: ३७०  वायुपुराणम् तथा शतसह्नाणि एकोननवतिः पुनः । पत्चाशच्च सहल्लाणि पृथिव्याबाधविसतरर..
verses.wordMeaning: The Prajapati was born of Sunitha, the daughter of Mrtyu. Vena was the son of the daughter of Kala. Hence on account of the (hereditary) evil trait of his maternal grandfather, Vena (was cruel). He turned his back on Dharma; he indulged in covet¬ ousness as he pleased.…
verses.commentary: Sense: The Prajapati was born of Sunitha, the daughter of Mrtyu. Vena was the son of the daughter of Kala. Hence on account of the (hereditary) evil trait of his maternal grandfather, Vena (was cruel). He turned his back on Dharma; he indulged in covet¬ ousness as he pleased.…

verses.sanskrit: यावदस्थीनि तिष्ठन्ति मर्त्यस्य नर्मदाजले । तावद्वसति धर्मात्मा शिवलोके सुदुर्लभे
verses.transliteration: yāvadasthīni tiṣṭhanti martyasya narmadājale / tāvadvasati dharmātmā śivaloke sudurlabhe
verses.translation: They caught hold of that mighty one even as he was dazzling like fire. Highly infuriated, they twisted and churned his left hand. O Brahmanas, from his hand that was being twisted and churned, a man black in colour and very short in stature, was born. Formerly it was heard so (by us). He was agitated in all his sense-organs. Frightened, he stood there with palms joined in reverence. On seeing him confused and deject¬ ed, (the sages) said: ''JVisida (Sit down). He, of infinite valour, became the founder of the dynasty of Nisadas (a hill tribe). He created Dhivaras too (the fishermen) born of the sins and defects of Vena. All those others (hill tribes) residing on the Vindhya mountains such as Tumburas, Tuvaras and Khasas and persons interested in evil actions were born of the sins of Vena. Becoming indignant again, the great sages pressed and churned the right hand ol Vena in great fury as though it were the Arani (a pice of wood used to kindle sacred fire by attrition) - From the splendid brilliance originating from the pressure exerted on the right hand, Prthu was born. Since he He wielded the primordial bow of loud report, named Ajagava. Then he took up the arrows and the coat of mail of great lustre for the sake of protection. When he was born, all the living beings became high¬ ly delighted. When the great king was born, Vena went to heaven.
verses.hindi: पृथिव्या बिस्तर कृत्स्नं योजनेस्तन्निबोधत । तित्र: कोटचस्तु विस्तार: संख्यातः स चतुदिशम्ु
verses.wordMeaning: They caught hold of that mighty one even as he was dazzling like fire. Highly infuriated, they twisted and churned his left hand. O Brahmanas, from his hand that was being twisted and churned, a man black in colour and very short in stature, was born.…
verses.commentary: Sense: They caught hold of that mighty one even as he was dazzling like fire. Highly infuriated, they twisted and churned his left hand. O Brahmanas, from his hand that was being twisted and churned, a man black in colour and very short in stature, was born.…

verses.sanskrit: ततः कालाच्च्युतस्तस्मादिह मानुषतां गतः । कोटिधनपतिः श्रीमाञ्जायते राजपूजितः
verses.transliteration: tataḥ kālāccyutastasmādiha mānuṣatāṃ gataḥ / koṭidhanapatiḥ śrīmāñjāyate rājapūjitaḥ
verses.translation: Due to the birth of that intelligent noble-souled son, he (Vena) was (elevated as) a Rajarsi (a royal sage). The tiger among men (Prthu) then protected him from the hell called Put (by being born as a son). All the rivers and oceans brought gems and jewels and came there. They crowned the son of Vena as the king. With a great royal kingdom, he became an Emperor of great splendour. That Emperor was coronated by the Devas, the sons of Arigiras. The valorous son of Vena, Prthu, became the first king and a great Emperor. The subjects who had been antagonised by his father were won over by him. Hence thanks to his Anurdga (love and affection) he got the name Raja (king). When he rushed against the ocean, the waters stood steady and motionless, and mountains crumbled before him. He never experienced the breakage of his banner. The Earth yielded food-grains without being cultivat¬ ed. All edible things were achieved on mere thought. Cows yielded whatever one desired. Honey was obtained in every leaf-cup (cluster of flowers?) At that time, in the auspicious Yajna of Pitamaha, the highly intelligent Suta was born of suti (the extraction of Soma juice) on the day intended for the extraction of Soma juice. The intelligent Magadha was also born in the same great Yajna. Our text gives a number of popular etymologies, vide that of Nisada (in v. 123) and ofPrthu here.
verses.hindi: तथा शतसह्नाणामेकोनाशी तिरुच्यते । सप्तद्वीपसमुद्रायाः प्रथिब्यास्त्वेष घिस्तरः विस्तरात्त्रिगुणं चेव प्रथिव्यन्तस्य मण्डलम् । गणितं योजनाग्रं तु कोटचस्त्वेकादश स्मृताः
verses.wordMeaning: Due to the birth of that intelligent noble-souled son, he (Vena) was (elevated as) a Rajarsi (a royal sage). The tiger among men (Prthu) then protected him from the hell called Put (by being born as a son). All the rivers and oceans brought gems and jewels and came there.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Due to the birth of that intelligent noble-souled son, he (Vena) was (elevated as) a Rajarsi (a royal sage). The tiger among men (Prthu) then protected him from the hell called Put (by being born as a son). All the rivers and oceans brought gems and jewels and came there.…

verses.sanskrit: सर्वधर्मसमायुक्तो मेधावी बीजपुत्रकः । विख्यातो वसुधापृष्ठे दीर्घायुर्मानवो भवेत्
verses.transliteration: sarvadharmasamāyukto medhāvī bījaputrakaḥ / vikhyāto vasudhāpṛṣṭhe dīrghāyurmānavo bhavet
verses.translation: With the Havis of Indra the Havis of Brhaspati got mixed. The offering was made to Indra by the Devasand there¬ by Suta was born. 1 The Havya offering of the preceptor which was mingled with that meant for the disciple, was over-powered by the dis¬ ciple s Havis. On account of the (mingling) activity of the lower and the upper, a mixed caste came into being. A Suta (charioteer) is begot of a Brahmanas lady by a Ksatriya who belongs to an inferior caste. Hence Suta is pro¬ claimed to have rites of the latter (Ksattriya) one. It is the middle type of Dharma of a Suta, viz. that of Ksattriyas. (He has these duties:) looking after and mainte¬ nance of chariots, elephants, horses. Practice of medicine is (his) lowliest of duties. Both of them (Suta and Magadha) were called there by the Devas and Sages for eulogising Prthu. All the sages said to them: "May this king be eulogised. This is abefitting activity of yours. He is also a person deserving praise". Then Suta and Magadha told all the sages: "We shall propitiate the Devas and the sages with our activities. We do not know the performances, characteristics and reputation of this (Prthu) king. Wherefore, O Brahmanas, can we eulogise this brilliant king?" They were enjoined by the sages: cc Let him be eulo¬ gised by his future activities. He has control over his sense organs. He is always engaged in charitable rites. He is truthful, endowed with knowledge. He is munificent and is never defeated in battles.
verses.hindi: तथा शतसहस्र तु सप्तत्रिशाधिकानि तु। इत्येतहे प्रसंख्यातं पृथिव्यन्तस्य मण्डलम् ॥छड तारकासंनिवेशस्य दिवि यावद्धि सण्डलम् । पर्यासः संनिवेशस्य भूमेस्तावस् सण्डलम्
verses.wordMeaning: With the Havis of Indra the Havis of Brhaspati got mixed. The offering was made to Indra by the Devasand there¬ by Suta was born. 1 The Havya offering of the preceptor which was mingled with that meant for the disciple, was over-powered by the dis¬ ciple s Havis.…
verses.commentary: Sense: With the Havis of Indra the Havis of Brhaspati got mixed. The offering was made to Indra by the Devasand there¬ by Suta was born. 1 The Havya offering of the preceptor which was mingled with that meant for the disciple, was over-powered by the dis¬ ciple s Havis.…

verses.sanskrit: पुनः स्मरति तत्तीर्थं तत्र गत्वा नृपोत्तम । करोडेश्वरमभ्यर्च्य प्राप्नोति परमां गतिम्
verses.transliteration: punaḥ smarati tattīrthaṃ tatra gatvā nṛpottama / karoḍeśvaramabhyarcya prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim
verses.translation: Suta and Magadha eulogised him by composing songs about the past achievements of the powerful king Prthu. At the end of the eulogy, the delighted Prthu, the lord of the subjects, gave the land of Anupa to Suta and Magadha to Magadha. Ever since, all the kings are eulogised by Sutas Verses 136-146 explain how and why the mixed class called suta came into existence and the duties assigned to that caste. The relation between Magadha and the land called Magadha is understandable but not that between Suta and Anflpa (South Malwa). On seeing him (King Prthu), the subjects were extremely pleased. The great sages told (them): "Let this protector of men (King), the son of Vena, be the bestower of livelihood to you". Then the subjects hurried and flocked round (literally) the blessed son of Vena saying, "As per promise of the great sages you make arrangements for our livelihood. On being hustled by the subjects, the powerful (king Prthu), with the desire to perform what was beneficent to the subjects, took up his bow and arrows and rushed at Vasudha (the Earth). Being afraid of being hit, the Earth assumed the form of a cow and fled. Taking up his bow, Prthu ran in pursuit of the fleeing Earth. Frightened of the son of Vena, she (the Earth) ran to Brahmaloka and other worlds (but finally) saw in front of her the son of Vena holding the bow lifted up. He had his splendour brightened up by the blazing arrows and shafts. He was of never failing (power) and endow¬ ed with great Yogic power. He was invincible even to the Devas. He could not be thwarted by anyone.
verses.hindi: पर्यासपारिमाण्येन भुमेस्तुल्यं दिवं स्मृतम् । सप्तानामपि लोकप्नामेतन्सान प्रकीतितभ् ७६ पर्यासपारिसाण्येन सण्डलानुगतेन च । उपयुपरि लोकानां छत्रवत्परिसण्डलम् संस्थितिविहिता सर्वा येश्चु तिष्ठन्ति जन्तवः । एतदण्डकटाहस्य प्रमाण परिकीतितम् (७८ अण्डस्थान्तस्त्विमे लोका: सप्तद्वीपा च मेदिनो । भूलोंकिश्व भुवश्चेव तृतीयः स्वरिति स्मृतः ॥ महलोंको जनश्चेव तपः सत्यश्य सप्तमः १७६ एले सप्त कृता लोकाछत्राकारा व्यवस्थिताः । स्वकंरावरणेः सुक्ष्मेर्धायं माणाः पृथक्पृथक् ८०
verses.wordMeaning: Suta and Magadha eulogised him by composing songs about the past achievements of the powerful king Prthu. At the end of the eulogy, the delighted Prthu, the lord of the subjects, gave the land of Anupa to Suta and Magadha to Magadha. Ever since,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Suta and Magadha eulogised him by composing songs about the past achievements of the powerful king Prthu. At the end of the eulogy, the delighted Prthu, the lord of the subjects, gave the land of Anupa to Suta and Magadha to Magadha. Ever since,…

verses.sanskrit: इन्द्रचन्द्रयमैर् रुद्रैरादित्यैर्वसुभिस्तथा । विश्वेदेवैस्तथा सर्वैः स्थापितस्त्रिदशेश्वरः
verses.transliteration: indracandrayamair rudrairādityairvasubhistathā / viśvedevaistathā sarvaiḥ sthāpitastridaśeśvaraḥ
verses.translation: The goddess (Earth) who is always worthy of being worshipped by the three worlds, could not get succour (from elsewhere) and so yielded to the son of Vena with palms join¬ ed in reverence. She spoke to the son of Vena r "O king, you are not aware of the sin inherent in killing a lady. How are you going to sustain the subjects without me. O most excellent of all kings,-but for me the subjects will be ruined. O king, all the worlds rest in me. The whole universe is sustained by me. O protector of the Earth, if you wish to do what is beneficial to the subjects, it does not behove you to kill me. Pay heed to my words. All undertakings become fruitful if they are begun with proper means. O king, even after killing me, you will not be competent to protect and look after the subjects. O extremely refulgent one, I shall become the pro¬ ducer of food. Refrain from fury. They say that females are not to be killed even from among the hundreds of lower animal species. O protector of the Earth, in consideration of this, it does not behove you to forsake Dharma". On hearing these various statements the noble-minded king of righteous soul, restrained his anger and spoke thus to (the Earth):
verses.hindi: दशभागाधिकाभिश्वन ताभिः प्रकृतिभिबंहिः  धार्यंमाणा विशेषेश्चय समुत्पन्नेः परस्परम्
verses.wordMeaning: The goddess (Earth) who is always worthy of being worshipped by the three worlds, could not get succour (from elsewhere) and so yielded to the son of Vena with palms join¬ ed in reverence. She spoke to the son of Vena r "O king,…

verses.sanskrit: रेवाया उत्तरे कूले लोकानां हितकाम्यया । मानवो भक्तिसंयुक्तः प्रासादं कारयेत्तु यः
verses.transliteration: revāyā uttare kūle lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā / mānavo bhaktisaṃyuktaḥ prāsādaṃ kārayettu yaḥ
verses.translation: O auspicious lady, when many attain happiness, if one man is killed there is no great or small sin. O Earth (repository of wealth), if you do not act according to my instructions which are conducive to the welfare of the Universe, I will kill you for the cause of the subjects. If you turn your face (disobey) against my behest, I shall presently kill you with an (single) arrow. After proclaim- ing myself (as their Lord), I shall sustain the subjects. Hence, O excellent lady, foremost among the up¬ holders of virtue, paying heed to my words will enliven the subjects perpetually. There is no doubt about it that you are competent to do so. Be my daughter. This is the great and excellent step (in the circumstances). O furious-looking lady, 1 control you Thus admonished, the chaste lady, the Earth, spoke to O excellent one among the upholders of virtue, give me a crlf so that cangive, milk out of affection. Make me flat¬ surfaced and level everywhere so that I can spread everywhere the flowing milk." With the tip of his bow the son of Vena pushed away the heaps of rocks everywhere. The hills were raised up by him.
verses.hindi: मध्य में प्रत्येक और करोड़ योजन कहा गया है। फिर पृथ्वी का बाघ विस्तार एक करोड़ पचास हजार नवासी योजन है ।६८-७०। प्रथ्वी के सम्पूर्ण विस्तार को योजनों में सुनिये । चतुदिक इसका विस्तार तीन करोड़ एक लाख उनासी हजार योजन है। सातों द्वीपों और समुद्रों थाली प्रथ्वी का यही विस्तार है।. पृथ्वी के अन्त का मंडल इस विस्तार से तिग्ुना अधिक है। इस प्रकार गिना गया है कि समण्डल पृथ्वी का विस्तार ग्यारह करोड़ एक लाख संतीस योजन है। इस प्रकार पृथ्वी के अन्त तक के मंडल की नाप की गई है। आकाश में जहाँ तक तारागंण और उनका मंडल है, पृथ्वी के सन्निवेश का मंडल भी वहाँ तक कहा गया है। भूमि के विस्तार-परिमाण के ही अनुसार आकाश का भी परिमाण है। सातों लोकों का ऐसा ही मान कहा गया है ।७१-७६। पर्याप्त परिमाण के अनुसार मंडलानुक्रम से सातों लोक छत्र की तरह
verses.wordMeaning: O auspicious lady, when many attain happiness, if one man is killed there is no great or small sin. O Earth (repository of wealth), if you do not act according to my instructions which are conducive to the welfare of the Universe, I will kill you for the cause of the subjects.…
verses.commentary: Sense: O auspicious lady, when many attain happiness, if one man is killed there is no great or small sin. O Earth (repository of wealth), if you do not act according to my instructions which are conducive to the welfare of the Universe, I will kill you for the cause of the subjects.…

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नरश्रेष्ठ सद्गतिं समवाप्नुयात् । न्यायोपात्तधनेनैव दारुपाषाणकेष्टकैः
verses.transliteration: tasmiṃstīrthe naraśreṣṭha sadgatiṃ samavāpnuyāt / nyāyopāttadhanenaiva dārupāṣāṇakeṣṭakaiḥ
verses.translation: In the past Manvantaras the Earth was rugged and uneven. Naturally some parts were even and some uneven. In the course of the previous creations, there was no demarca¬ tion of cities and villages, as the Earth was uneven and rugged. In the Caksusa Manvantara there were no plants, no breeding of cows, no cultivation and no trade routes. All these occurred in the Vaivasvata Manvantara. Wherever there was evenness (plain ground) the subjects always occupied it. The diet cansisted of fruits and roots. Since the reign of the son of Vena all these things appeared in this world. When the medicinal herbs were destroyed, lord Prthu made Caksusa Manu the calf, and with great difficulty milked with his own hand, the Earth (in the form of a cow) 1 and pro¬ duced plants. Food grains and plants were milked by the son of Vena from the Earth-goddess after making Caksusa Manu the calf and the bare ground the vessel. The subjects always main¬ tained themselves with that food. The Earth (The holder of treasures)was eulogised by the sages and milked again. Their calf was Soma (the Moon) and the milker (milkman) was Brhaspati. The vessel was Gayatri and other (Vedic) metres. Their milk was penance and the eternal Brahman.
verses.hindi: ऊपर-ऊपर घेरे हुए हैं। इन्हीं लोकों में सभी जन्तु रहा करते हैं । अण्डकटाह का यही प्रमाण कहा गया है। इस अंडकटाह के मध्य में ही सब्तद्वीपा मेदिनौ है। सातों लोकों के नाम इस प्रकार हैं--भूलोंक, भवलककि, स्वलॉकि, महलोंक, तपोलोक और सत्यलोक ।७७-७९। ये सातों लोक छत्राकार रूप से अवस्थित हैं। ये सातों लोक अपने सूक्म आवरणों से आवृत होकर पृथक्-पृथक स्थित हैं। ये बहिः स्थित आवरण
verses.wordMeaning: In the past Manvantaras the Earth was rugged and uneven. Naturally some parts were even and some uneven. In the course of the previous creations, there was no demarca¬ tion of cities and villages, as the Earth was uneven and rugged.…
verses.commentary: Sense: In the past Manvantaras the Earth was rugged and uneven. Naturally some parts were even and some uneven. In the course of the previous creations, there was no demarca¬ tion of cities and villages, as the Earth was uneven and rugged.…

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यैः शूद्रैः स्त्रीभिश्च शक्तितः । ते ऽपि यान्ति नरा लोके शांकरे सुरपूजिते
verses.transliteration: brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyairvaiśyaiḥ śūdraiḥ strībhiśca śaktitaḥ / te 'pi yānti narā loke śāṃkare surapūjite
verses.translation: Again (the Earth was) eulogised by the groups of Devas led by Purandara after taking up a golden vessel and Ampta (Nectar) was milked by them. The Devas led by Indra sustained themselves with that alone. The Earth was eulogised by the Magas (Serpents) and milked. Poison was the milk, Vasuki the son of Kadru, was the milkman, on behalf of those highly powerful serpents. O excellent Brahmanas, the fierce, huge-bodied and The story of Pjthu and his milking of the Earth is a Puranic presen¬ tation of the Vedic conception of milking of the Viraj cow. The Virdj Sukta (AV. VIII.10) forms the basis of this Puranic legend. The Puranic legend asserts the right of sages (public leaders) to remove a wilful tyrant. After making themselves invisible, the Earth was milked again by the Yaksas and Punyajanas. They had made VaiSravana (Kubera) the calf. It was an unbaked vessel that they milked into. The milker was Jatunabha, the father of Manivara. He possessed great strength and excessive splendour. He had full self-control. Pie was the son of a Yaksa. The great sage said that they sustained themselves with that milk. The Earth was milked again by Raksasas and Pisacas. Their milkman was Kubera endowed with the knowl¬ edge of Brahman. The calf was the powerful Sumali. Blood was the milk yielded. It was a vessel of skull that the Raksasas milked into by being invisible. All the Raksasas sustain themselves with that milk.
verses.hindi: परस्पर दस-दस गुना अधिक हैं। ये परस्पर उत्पन्न हुए हैं; किन्तु एक से दूसरा विशेषता लिए हुए है और इन्हीं के ढ्वारा सातों लोकों का धारण हो रहा है ।८५०-५१। इस अंडे के चारों ओर घनीभूत समुद्र है। समनन्‍्तादनवातेन धार्यमाणं प्रतिष्ठितम । घनवातात्तथाइप्काशमाकाशं च महात्मना.. पदड भूतादिना बुतं सर्व भुतादिसंहता वृतः । ततो महाननन्‍्तेन प्रधानेनाव्ययात्मना
verses.wordMeaning: Again (the Earth was) eulogised by the groups of Devas led by Purandara after taking up a golden vessel and Ampta (Nectar) was milked by them. The Devas led by Indra sustained themselves with that alone. The Earth was eulogised by the Magas (Serpents) and milked.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Again (the Earth was) eulogised by the groups of Devas led by Purandara after taking up a golden vessel and Ampta (Nectar) was milked by them. The Devas led by Indra sustained themselves with that alone. The Earth was eulogised by the Magas (Serpents) and milked.…

verses.sanskrit: यः शृणोति सदा भक्त्या माहात्म्यं तीर्थजं नृप । तस्य पापं प्रणश्येत षण्मासाभ्यन्तरं च यत्
verses.transliteration: yaḥ śṛṇoti sadā bhaktyā māhātmyaṃ tīrthajaṃ nṛpa / tasya pāpaṃ praṇaśyeta ṣaṇmāsābhyantaraṃ ca yat
verses.translation: In the vessel of lotus (leaves) the Earth was milked again by Gandharvas and the groups ofApsaras-s. They made Citraratha the calf, and pure scents was the yield. Visvavasu who was the pure son of a sage and who was the very powerful king of Gandharvas and who was a noble soul resembling the sun was their milkman. The goddess Earth was eulogised and milked again by the mountains. The yield was the medicinal herbs in embodied form and various kinds of precious stones. Mt. Himavan was their calf. The great mountain Meru was the milkman. 1 The mountain itself was the vessel. With that the mountain was stabilised. The Earth-goddess was eulogised and milked again by the trees and creepers. They took the leafy cup of Palas'a as the vessel. The milk yielded was the ability to grow after being cut. The mountain in full bloom was Kamadhuk {the milk¬ man of what is desired). Plaksa tree was the calf. The Earth (was thus) the yielder of all desires, the benefactress of all liv¬ ing beings and very famous. Kalidasa echoes this in Kumara-sariibhaua 1.2.
verses.hindi: पुराणि लोकपालानां प्रवक्ष्यासि यथाक्रमम् । ज्योतिर्गणप्रचारस्य प्रमाणं परिवक्ष्यते. ७८६
verses.wordMeaning: In the vessel of lotus (leaves) the Earth was milked again by Gandharvas and the groups ofApsaras-s. They made Citraratha the calf, and pure scents was the yield.…
verses.commentary: Sense: In the vessel of lotus (leaves) the Earth was milked again by Gandharvas and the groups ofApsaras-s. They made Citraratha the calf, and pure scents was the yield.…

verses.sanskrit: ॥ इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे करोडीश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम द्विषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः॥ र्क्व् अध्याय ६३ श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: ततो गच्छेत् तु राजेन्द्र कुमारेश्वरम् उत्तमम् । प्रसिद्धं सर्वतीर्थानाम् अगस्त्येश्वरसन्निधौ
verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe karoḍīśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma dviṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ|| rkv adhyāya 63 śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: tato gacchet tu rājendra kumāreśvaram uttamam / prasiddhaṃ sarvatīrthānām agastyeśvarasannidhau
verses.translation: It is reported that the Earth extended to the oceans as its limit. It is called Vasudha, because it holds riches ( Vasil — wealth, Dharayate —holds). Formerly the earth was covered with the fat of Madhu and Kaitabha. Hence the Earth extending to the oceans became famous as Medini ( Medas —fat). Since the intelligent son of Vena, king Prthu, adopted her as his daughter, she is called Prthivi. 1 The division of this famous, beautiful Earth was former¬ ly made by King Prthu, The Earth consisting of a series of towns and mines (of various natural products) and populated by people of four castes was protected by that intelligent king. That excellent king, the son of Vena, had such prowess. Beingancient and born of Brahman, Prthu alone is worthy of being offered obeisance by Brahmanas of great dig¬ nity (and fortune) who were experts in the Vedas and their Ahgas (ancillary subjects). The primordial king Prthu, the valorous son of Vena should be bowed to by the excessively blessed kings who seek great fame.
verses.hindi: मानसोत्तरपृष्ठे तु लोकपालाभ्रतुदिशम् । स्थिता धर्मंव्यवस्थाये लोकसंरक्षणाय च .. लोकपालोपरिष्टात्तु सर्बतो दक्षिणायने । काष्ठागतस्य सुर्थस्य गतिर्या तां निबोधत
verses.wordMeaning: It is reported that the Earth extended to the oceans as its limit. It is called Vasudha, because it holds riches ( Vasil — wealth, Dharayate —holds). Formerly the earth was covered with the fat of Madhu and Kaitabha.…
verses.commentary: Sense: It is reported that the Earth extended to the oceans as its limit. It is called Vasudha, because it holds riches ( Vasil — wealth, Dharayate —holds). Formerly the earth was covered with the fat of Madhu and Kaitabha.…

verses.sanskrit: षण्मुखेन पुरा तात सर्वपातकनाशनम् । आराध्य परया भक्त्या सिद्धिः प्राप्ता नराधिप
verses.transliteration: ṣaṇmukhena purā tāta sarvapātakanāśanam / ārādhya parayā bhaktyā siddhiḥ prāptā narādhipa
verses.translation: Only Prthu, the first maker of men, should be bowed to by the warriors also seek victory in battle. The warrior who, after glorifying Pjrthu, proceeds to the battlefield, returns safely from the terrible battle and attains glorious fame. The saintly king Prthu, th~ excessively renowned one, should be bowed to by the Vaisyas, strictly adhering to the avocation and duties of Vaisyas, as it was he who gave them livelihood and sustenance. At the very outset the Earth was milked by the noble- shouled Brahma after making Vayu the calf. 1 The vjessel was the surface of the Earth and the yield, the seeds. Then in the early Svayambhuva Manvantara, the Earth was milked by Agnldhra 2 after making Svayambhuva Manu the calf. Formerly, when Svarocisa was Manu, the Earth was milked by the intelligent Gaitra, after making Svarocisa Manu the calf. The yield consisted of plants and foodgrains.
verses.hindi: इसी सघन जल के द्वारा सम्पूर्ण पृथ्वी का धारण किया गया है। इस घनीभूत समुद्र के बाद सघन तेज है। बाहैर से यह घनीभूत तेज नोचे ऊपर मंडलाकार होकर पृथ्वी को घारण करता है। इसके बाद चारों और घनीभूत वायु है, जिसके द्वारा भी पृृथ्वीमंडल का धारण किया गया है। घनौभूत वायु के बाद महा आकाश है । इस महा आकाश के द्वारा निखिल भूतादि आवृत हैं और भूतादि के द्वारा आकाश घिरा
verses.wordMeaning: Only Prthu, the first maker of men, should be bowed to by the warriors also seek victory in battle. The warrior who, after glorifying Pjrthu, proceeds to the battlefield, returns safely from the terrible battle and attains glorious fame. The saintly king Prthu,…

verses.sanskrit: देवसैन्याधिपो जातः सर्वशत्रुनिबर्हणः । उग्रतेजा महात्मासौ संजातस्तीर्थसेवनात्
verses.transliteration: devasainyādhipo jātaḥ sarvaśatrunibarhaṇaḥ / ugratejā mahātmāsau saṃjātastīrthasevanāt
verses.translation: In the Auttama Manvantara, the Earth was milked by the most excellent and intelligent Devabhuja, after making the Manu Uttama the calf. The yield consisted of all foodgrains. Again in the fifth Manvantara, viz. the Tamasa Man¬ vantara the Earth was milked by Balabandhu after making Tamasa Manu the calf. When the Manvantara of lord Carisnava Manu arrived, the Earth was milked by Purana after making Carisnava Manu the calf. When the Caksusa Manvantara arrived, the Earth was again milked by Purana, after making Caksusa Manu the calf. Verses 12-20 give the list of persons who "milked" the earth in each Manvantara. Each 'milking' shows in a way the advancement of human civilization, Bd. 2-37 reads Sarva-sasyani caiva hi ' all types of foodgrains were the milky yield". Here gri;ma probably stands for Agnidhra. But the milky yield is not mentioned in our text.
verses.hindi: हुआ है। एवं यह महा आकाझ प्रधान अव्ययात्मा अनन्त के द्वारा आवृत है ।८ २-८५५। अब हम यथाक्रम से लोकपालों के पुर का और ग्रह-नक्षत्रादि के गतिविषयक प्रमाण को कहते हैं। मेरु से प्रर और मानस के शिखर पर धनधान्यपूर्ण और सुवर्ण की तरह परिष्कृत पवित्र इन्द्रपुरी है ।६-८७। में से दक्षिण और मानस के शिखर पर ही संयमन नामक पुर में वेवस्वत यमराज निवास करते हैं। मेरु से पश्चिम और मानस के शिखर पर ही वरुणदेवता की रमणीय सुखा नामक पुरी हैं ।5८-५६। मेह से उत्तर और मानस के शिखर पर इन्द्रगगरी के समान सोम की विभावरी नामक पुरी है । मानस के उत्तरीय गंडशल पर चारों ओर लोकपालगण घममं की व्यवस्था को स्थिर रखने के लिए और लोंकों की रक्षा करने के लिए टिके हुए हैं 8०-६९ १। लोकपालों से ऊपर रहनेवाले सूयं जब दाक्षिणायन हो जाते हैं, तब उस दिक्षा में वर्तमान सूर्य

verses.transliteration: tadāprabhṛti tattīrthaṃ saṃjātaṃnarmadātaṭe / tatra tīrthe tu yo gatvā ekacitto jitendriyaḥ
verses.translation: When theCaksusa Manvantara elapsed and Vaivasvata Manvantara arrived, the Earth was again milked by the son of Vena, as narrated by me to you. Formerly in the previous Manvantaras the Earth was milked by the Devas and others, by human beings as well as by theBhutas (living beings or goblins) and others. Thus the Devas should be known in all the past and present Manvantaras. Now listen to the sons of Prthu. Two valorous sons, Antardhi and Palin were born to Prthu. SikhandinI bore to Antardhana (Antardhi) the son Havirdhana. Dhisana, the daughter of Agni,bore to Havirdhana six sons, viz. Praclnabarhis, Sukra, Gaya, Krsna, Vraja and Ajina. The holy lord Praclnabarhis was a great Prajapati.. Thanks to his strength, learning, penance and prowess, he was the sole Emperor of the Earth. The tips of his Kusa grasses pointed to the east by frequent use in Yajrias. Hence he is called Praclnabarhis. 1
verses.hindi: की जो मति है, उसे सुनिये । दक्षिण दिशा में सूर्य की गति धतुष से फेंके गये बाण की तरह हो जाती है। उस समय सूर्य-मंडल के साथ-साथ ज्योतिष्वक्र भी साथ-साथ चलने लगता है ।६३-६३ जब सूये

verses.sanskrit: कार्त्तिकस्य चतुर्दश्यामष्टम्यां च विशेषतः । स्नापयेद् गिरिजानाथं दधिदुग्धेन सर्पिषा
verses.transliteration: kārttikasya caturdaśyāmaṣṭamyāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ / snāpayed girijānāthaṃ dadhidugdhena sarpiṣā
verses.translation: That lord duly married Savarna, the daughter of the ocean, far beyond the extensive darkness. From the Prajapati the daughter of the ocean, Savarna, bore the ten sons of Pracl¬ nabarhis. All of them are named Pracetas. They were masters of the science of archery. Performing rtghteous actions (in close association) without being separated, they performed great pen¬ ance for ten thousand years lying in the waters, of the ocean. While the Pracetas were performing penance on the Earth the trees not being properly cared for covered the earth resulting in the decline and ruin of the subjects. When (the firmament) was obstructed in the Caksusa Manvantara, wind could not blow. The sky was covered with trees. The subjects could not (carry their activities) for ten thousand years. On realising it by means of their power of penance, all CfBd. 2.37.25—an etymology to explain the significance of the king's name.
verses.hindi: मध्यगश्चाम रावत्यां यदा भवति भास्करः। बेवस्वते संयमने उदयस्तत्र उच्यते दक्षिणापरदेश्यानां पूर्वाह्नः परिकीत्यंते । तेषामपररात्र च ये जना उत्तरापथे देशा उत्तरपूर्वा ये पुबंरात्रं तु तान्प्रति । एवमेवोत्तरेष्वकों भवनेषु विराजते

verses.sanskrit: गीतं तत्र प्रकर्तव्यं पिण्डदानं यथाविधि । ब्राह्मणैः श्रोत्रियैः पार्थ षट्कर्मनिरतैः शुभैः
verses.transliteration: gītaṃ tatra prakartavyaṃ piṇḍadānaṃ yathāvidhi / brāhmaṇaiḥ śrotriyaiḥ pārtha ṣaṭkarmanirataiḥ śubhaiḥ
verses.translation: Vayu uprooted those trees and dried them up. The fierce fire burned them. Thus the destruction of trees took place. Learning of the destruction of the trees (and when only) a few trees survived, king Soma (the Moon-god) approached these Pracetas and spoke to them: "O kings, O sons of Praclnabarhis, give up your anger after considering the benefits conferred (by flourishing trees) for the continuance of the worlds. The trees will grow on the Earth. May the fire and the wind calm down. This jewel of a girl of fair complexion is the daughter of the trees. Knowing this future (contingency), she has been nurtur¬ ed (and brought up) by me with my rays. She is named Marisa and is created by the trees themselves. May she, nurtured in the womb of the moon*, be your wife. By means of a moiety of your splendour as well as a moiety of my splendour, the learned Prajapati named Daksa will be born of her.
verses.hindi: अमरावती के बीचोबीच आ जाते हैं तब यमराज के संयमन पुर में सूयोदय होता है। जब सूर्य सुखा पुरी में आ जाते हैं, तब वहाँ आधी रात हो जाती है। वरुण देवता की इसी सुखा पुरी से सूथे का उदय देखा जाता है। सूर्य के विभावरी नगरी में जाने से आधीरात और इन्द्रपुरी में जाने से अस्त काल होता है। उस समय दक्षिण-पूर्वं दिशा में अपराक्तु और इस दक्षिण दिशा में अपर देशों में पूर्वाह्न हो जाता

verses.transliteration: yatkiṃciddīyate tatra akṣayaṃ pāṇḍunandana / sarvatīrthamayaṃ tīrtha nirmitaṃ śikhinā nṛpa
verses.translation: He, of fiery splendour, shall again develop the subjects andprotect theEarthalmost burnt by the fire of your brilliance." Then, at the instance of Soma (the Moon-god) those Pracetas curbed their fury and accepted righteously from the trees (their daughter) Marisa as their wife. They then impregnated Marisa mentally. Daksa the Prajapati was born of Marisa and the ten.Pracetas. He posses¬ sed great splendour and virility, thanks to the part of Soma. At first Daksa created progeny by mental process and subsequently by means of sexual intercourse. After creating the iinmboile beings, mobile beings, bipeds and quadrupeds mentally, Daksa created women (daughters) thereafter. He gave ten (of his daughters) to Dharma, thirteen to Kasyapa and twenty-seven engaged in the movement of time (i.e. the twenty-seven constellations) to the moon.. After giving these (daughters) to them he gave four other daughters to Aristanemi, two to Bahuputra, two to Angi- ras and one daughter to Kpsasva. Now know their progeny.
verses.hindi: है ।९४-९ ६४२१। जो जन उत्तरापथ में निवास करते हैं, उनके लिये वह रात्रि' का शेष काल और जो उत्तर- पूर्व देश में निवास करते हैं, उनके लिये वह रात्रि का पूर्व काल कहलाता है। जब सूर्य उत्तरीय भवन में विराजते हैं और जब वे वरण की सुखा नामक पुर में जाते हैं, तब मध्याक्न होता है एवं जब वे चन्द्र की विभावरी नगरी में जाते हैं, ब्रब. उदय होता है ।६९७-६६। उस समय अमरावती में आधी रात और यम के  एतदधंस्थाने5यं ग्रन्थ: ख. पुस्तके वर्तते-- विभावर्या सोनपुर्या भास्वरं सुर्यंसंशितम्

verses.sanskrit: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं कुमारेश्वरजं फलम् । कुमारदर्शनात्पुण्यं प्राप्यते पाण्डुनन्दन
verses.transliteration: etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ kumāreśvarajaṃ phalam / kumāradarśanātpuṇyaṃ prāpyate pāṇḍunandana
verses.translation: By this time, the sixth 'Man van tar a of Caksu$a Manu ceases giving place to the seventh Manvantara of the Prajapati Vaivasvata Manu. In them (the daughters of Dak$a) Devas, birds, cows, serpents, Daityas, Danavas, Gandharvas, Apsaras-s and other classes of beings were born. The creation of the earlier ones was due to thought, sight and touch. Thenceforth, the subjects in this world were born of sexual intercourse. 1 The auspicious birth of Devas, Danavas, Celestial Sages and the noble-souled Daksa has been narrated by you before. It was mentioned by you (before) that Daksa, the Pra¬ japati, was born of Prana. How did he who had great penance subsequently attain the status of the son of Pracetas? O Suta, it behoves you to clarify this doubt of ours. He was the son of the daughter of Soma. How did he become his (Soma's) father-in-law? O excellent ones, birth and dissolution (death) occur perpetually among living beings. The sages and those men who are endowed with learning are not deluded in this matter. O Brahmarias, Daksa and others are born in every Yuga. They undergo subsequent death too. A learned man is not confused in this matter.

verses.sanskrit: मृतः स्वर्गमवाप्नोति सत्यमीश्वरभाषितम्
verses.transliteration: mṛtaḥ svargamavāpnoti satyamīśvarabhāṣitam
verses.translation: O excellent Brahmanas, formerly there was neither seniority nor juniority among them. Penance alone was consi¬ dered weightier and prowess was the basis thereof. He who comprehends this creation of the mobile and the immobile beings in Caksusa Manvantara passes his life-span fully and is honoured in the heavenly region (after it). This is the main difference between the previous six Manvantaras and the present one. With this chapter closes the description of the Manvantara. This creation of Caksusa Manu has been succinctly nar¬ rated. Thus these six cycles of creation, in the form of Manvan- taras have elapsed. They have the Svayambhuva Manvantara as their first one and the Caksusa Manvantara as the last one. They have been briefly narrated in the proper sequence. O excellent Brahmanas, these creations have been narrated in accordance with my understanding. The details of these creations should be known through the creation in the Vaivasvata Manvantara. All the creations of Vivasvan are endless and non- different (from other Manvantaras) ( in the matter ofstates of health, duration of life, virtue, love and wealth. He who reads this without malice attains these attributes. Now I shall describe the creative activity of the current noble-souled Vaivasvata Manu succinctly and in detail (as the case may be). Listen and understand even as I recount.
verses.hindi: सरसेनापति: स्कन्दः पठचते5्ज्भा रको ग्रह:  नारायण बुध प्राहुदव श्ञानविदो बुधाः रुद्रो ववस्वतः साक्षाद्यमो लोकप्रभु: स्वयम् । महाग्रहों द्विजश्रेष्ठो मन्दगामी शनेहचरः: देवासुरगुरू दो तु भानुमन्तौ महाग्रही  प्रजापतिसुतावेतावुभो शुक्रब्ृहस्पती देवी महेन्द्रस्तत्नयो राधिपत्ये विनिभिती । आदित्यमुलमखिलं त्रैलोक्यं नात्र संशयः भवत्यस्य जगत्कृत्स्तं सदेवासुरमानुषम् । रुद्रे व्वोपेन्द्रचन्द्राणां विप्रेन्द्रास्त्रदिवोकसाम् दयतिद् तिमतः कृत्स्ता यत्तेज: सावेलौकिकम् । सर्वात्मा सबंलोकेशों मूलं परमहैवतम् ततः संजायते सर्व तत्र चैव प्रलीयते । भावाभावौ हि लोकानामादित्यान्निःसृतौ पुरा
