verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe kumāreśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma triṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 64 śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: tato gacchettu rājendra tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam / narāṇāṃ pāpanāśāya agastyeśvaramuttamam
verses.translation: In the seventh cycle called Vaivasvata Manvantara, the Devas and the great sages were born of Kasyapa, son ofMarici. 1 The eight groups of Devas are remembered as follows: (1) Adityas, (2)Vasus, (3) Rudras, (4)Sadhyas (5) Vis'vedevas (6) Maruts, (7) Bhrgus and (8) Angiras-s. (Among them) Adityas, Maruts and Rudras are to be known as the sons of KaSyapa. The three groups, viz. Sadhyas, Vasus and Visvedevas are the sons of Dharma. Lord Bhargava was born of Bhrgu and Angira was the son of Angiras. In this Vaivasvata Manvantara, those Devas are Hence the title of the chapter 'Marica creation*. The current auspicious creation should be known as that of the descendants of Marici. Their present brilliant Indra is Mahabala by name.
verses.hindi: राहपर्थ चामरावत्यापस्तवेति यमस्य च। सोमपुर्यां विभायां तु मध्याह्न॑ स्थादिवाकरः
verses.wordMeaning: In the seventh cycle called Vaivasvata Manvantara, the Devas and the great sages were born of Kasyapa, son ofMarici. 1 The eight groups of Devas are remembered as follows: (1) Adityas, (2)Vasus, (3) Rudras, (4)Sadhyas (5) Vis'vedevas (6) Maruts, (7) Bhrgus and (8) Angiras-s.…
verses.commentary: Sense: In the seventh cycle called Vaivasvata Manvantara, the Devas and the great sages were born of Kasyapa, son ofMarici. 1 The eight groups of Devas are remembered as follows: (1) Adityas, (2)Vasus, (3) Rudras, (4)Sadhyas (5) Vis'vedevas (6) Maruts, (7) Bhrgus and (8) Angiras-s.…

verses.sanskrit: तत्र स्नात्वा नरो राजन् मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्यया । कार्त्तिकस्य तु मासस्य कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दशी
verses.transliteration: tatra snātvā naro rājan mucyate brahmahatyayā / kārttikasya tu māsasya kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśī
verses.translation: All the Indras in the different Manvantaras whether of the past or future or those who exist now should be known as having equal characteristics. All of them are the lords of past, present and future objects, thousand-eyed and Purandara (destroyers of the cities of enemies). All of them are bountiful, crested (wearers of crowns with crests). They hold thunderbolt in the hand. All performed hundred sacrifices and all possessed hundreds of attributes. They establish themselves after excelling all the living beings in the three worlds, whether weak or mobile, for various reasons such as Dharma (Piety) etc. I shall explain everything as to how they are the lords of the past, present and future by means of splendour, penance, intellect, strength, learning and exploits; how they have become powerful; listen and understand even as I recount. Three worlds have been remembered by the Brahmanas asBhuta, Bhavya and Bhavisya A They are respectively remember¬ ed as follows: Bhurloka or the Earth, Bhuvarloka or the firma¬ ment and Bhavya or the heaven. I shall explain how they have been accomplished. This was uttered at the outset by Brahma who was desirous of sons and who was meditating. The word "Bhuh" was uttered in the beginning and this Bhurloka took shape. The root Bhu is remembered in the sense o {Sattd (existence) as also Loka Darina (visibility to the people). Since it existed and was visible it became Bhurloka, hence this first Loka is remembered as Bhuh, because it existed.
verses.hindi: नगर में सूर्यास्त होता है। जब चन्द्र की विभावरी पुरी में मध्याकह्न और इन्द्र की अमरावती में उदय होता है. उस समय संयमन पुर में आधी रात और वरुण की सुखा नगरी में अस्त होता है ।१००-१० १। सूर्य तदादित्यादुते येषां कालसंख्या न विद्यते । कालादुृते न नियमों न दीक्षा नाहिकक्रमः
verses.wordMeaning: All the Indras in the different Manvantaras whether of the past or future or those who exist now should be known as having equal characteristics. All of them are the lords of past, present and future objects, thousand-eyed and Purandara (destroyers of the cities of enemies).…
verses.commentary: Sense: All the Indras in the different Manvantaras whether of the past or future or those who exist now should be known as having equal characteristics. All of them are the lords of past, present and future objects, thousand-eyed and Purandara (destroyers of the cities of enemies).…

verses.sanskrit: घृतेन स्नापयेद् देवं समाधिस्थो जितेन्द्रियः । एकविंशतिकुलोपेतो च्यवेदैश्वरात् पदात्
verses.transliteration: ghṛtena snāpayed devaṃ samādhistho jitendriyaḥ / ekaviṃśatikulopeto cyavedaiśvarāt padāt
verses.translation: The word Bhuvarloka is derived from bhauana by those who know Nirukta (Etymology). Hence the firmament is called the second Loka i.e. Bhuvarloka. When Bhuvarloka had taken shape, the third word " Bhavya " was uttered by Brahma and then the Bhavya- loka took shape. The word Bhavya is used in the sense of what has not yet come about (i.e. the future). Hence this future world is remembered by the name Diva (Heaven). Another third word "Svah" was uttered (by Brahma). Then the Bhavyaloka (future world) took shape. The word Bhavya is used in the sense of future time. The Earth is remembered by the word Bhuh; the firma¬ ment is remembered as Bhuva/i; the heaven is remembered as Bhavya. This is the set of three worlds in a nutshell. By the utterances in combination with the three worlds the three Vyahrlis( i.e. the mantras Bhu/i, Bhuvah, Sva/i ) originated. The root JValh is remembered in the sense of 'protection' by those who know the (meanings of) roots.
verses.hindi: अभावो व्यवहाराणां देवानां दिवि चेह च । जगत्प्रतापनमृते भास्कर वारितस्करम्
verses.wordMeaning: The word Bhuvarloka is derived from bhauana by those who know Nirukta (Etymology). Hence the firmament is called the second Loka i.e. Bhuvarloka. When Bhuvarloka had taken shape, the third word " Bhavya " was uttered by Brahma and then the Bhavya- loka took shape.…
verses.commentary: Sense: The word Bhuvarloka is derived from bhauana by those who know Nirukta (Etymology). Hence the firmament is called the second Loka i.e. Bhuvarloka. When Bhuvarloka had taken shape, the third word " Bhavya " was uttered by Brahma and then the Bhavya- loka took shape.…

verses.sanskrit: धनं चोपानहौ छत्रं दद्याच्च घृतकम्बलम् । भोजनं चैव सर्वेषां सर्वं कोटिगुणं भवेत्
verses.transliteration: dhanaṃ copānahau chatraṃ dadyācca ghṛtakambalam / bhojanaṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ sarvaṃ koṭiguṇaṃ bhavet
verses.translation: Since they are the Lord Protectors of the Bhiila, Bhavya and Bhaval worlds they are the Mlhas (Protectors) of the three worlds. They are termed as Indras by the Brahmanas. The Devendras who are the chiefs in the Manvantaras as well as those Devas who are their (subordinates) become partakers of shares in the Tajfias. Yaksas, Gandharvas, Raksasas, Pisacas, Uragas and Danavas are all proclaimed as (the products of) the glory of the Devendras. The Devendras are the elders (preceptors), protectors, kings and parents. Those excellent Devas protect all these sub¬ jects righteously. Thus the characteristics of the Devendras have been briefly described. I shall now recount the seven sages who are stationed at present in the heaven. They are: (1) Vis'vamitra of great penance, the inte¬ lligent son of Gadhi who was born of the family of Kusika, (2) Jamadagni, the valorous son of Oru (Aurva) the scion of the family of Bhrgu, (3) Bharadvaja of great penance, the son of Bfhaspati, (4) Saradvan the learned and the virtuous son of Uta- Iksvaku, Nabhaga, Dhrsta, Saryati, the famous Narisyanta, Nabha, Uddista, Karusa, Prsadhra and Vasuman the tenth—these are the ten sons of Vaivasvata Manu glorified byme. The seventh Manvantara has been explained by me. O Brahmanas, the second Pada has been described by me in detail and in the proper order. What else shall I now explain?
verses.hindi: स एवं कालदचाग्निश्च द्वादशात्मा प्रजापति: । तपत्येष द्विजश्नेष्ठास्त्रलोक्य सचराचरम् तेबां श्रेष्ठा: पुनः सप्त रहमयो ग्रहयोनय: । सुषुम्नो हरिकेश्नश्च विदवकर्मा तथेव च विश्वश्रवाः पुनश्चान्यः संपद्ठ सुरतः परम । अर्वावसु: पुनश्चान्यः स्वराडन्य: प्रकीतित: सुषुम्ना सूय रश्मिस्तु क्षीणं शशिनमेघयन् । तियंगुध्व॑प्रचारोइसौ सुषुम्तः परिकीतितः हरिकेश. पुरस्त्वाद्या ऋक्षयोनिः प्रकीतिता । दक्षिणे विश्वकर्मा तु रश्मिवर्धयंते बुधम्
verses.wordMeaning: Since they are the Lord Protectors of the Bhiila, Bhavya and Bhaval worlds they are the Mlhas (Protectors) of the three worlds. They are termed as Indras by the Brahmanas.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Since they are the Lord Protectors of the Bhiila, Bhavya and Bhaval worlds they are the Mlhas (Protectors) of the three worlds. They are termed as Indras by the Brahmanas.…

verses.sanskrit: ॥ इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे अगस्त्येश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम चतुःषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ र्क्व् अध्याय ६५ श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: ततो गच्छेत्तु राजेन्द्र आनन्देश्वरमुत्तमम् । तत्तीर्थं कथयिष्यामि सर्वपापक्षयंकरम्
verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe agastyeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma catuḥṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 65 śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: tato gacchettu rājendra ānandeśvaramuttamam / tattīrthaṃ kathayiṣyāmi sarvapāpakṣayaṃkaram
verses.translation: On hearing the second section (in full) as narrated by the intelligent Suta, Samsapayana thereafter asked him about (the subject matter of) the third Pdda (Section). "The second Pdda has been narrated by you along with its sequel (Appendix); please recount the third Pdda in detail along with the (necessary) introduction'* Being requested thus, Suta began to speak with his inner soul highly delighted. OBrahmanas, I shall recount the third pada in detail along with (necessary) introduction. Even as I recount it, listen and understand it completely. O Brahmanas, listen in details and in proper order to the creative activity of the present Vaivasvata Manu of noble soul. The (Manu) period is already calculated as being of seventyone sets of four Yugas. After bowing to Vivasvan (the Sun-god) I shall narrate the Vaivasvata creation beginning with Manu and ending with the future events. It comprises Deva- ganas, Sages, Danavas, Pitrs, Gandharvas, Raksasas, Bhuta- ganas, human beings, animals, birds and immobile beings. The seven great sages who had passed away in the first Svayambhuva Manvantara and who were the creators and initi¬ ators then, are reborn in the Vaivasvata Manvantara after The seven sages were born again as seven mental sons of Brahma. They were adopted as sons by Svayambhu (the self-born god Brahma) himself. The creative activity was initiated again as before and in the proper order, by those noble souls who manifested them¬ selves and who created the series of subjects. I shall mention the progeny of those people of pure knowledge and holy rites in brief as well as in detail (according to the context) and in the proper order. This world consisting of mobile and immobile beings and embellished with planets and stars is filled with beings born of their families. On hearing these words a doubt arose in the minds of the sages. Overwhelmed by the doubt, the sages of pure holy rites honoured Suta and asked him for the sake of clarifica- tion of their doubts. O excellent one, how were the seven sages born as seven mental sons at the outset? How were they adopted as sons? Please explain this to us.
verses.hindi: एवं सूर्य प्रभावेण ग्रहनक्षत्रतारका: । वर्धन्ते विदिता: सर्वा विश्वं चेद पुनेंजग
verses.wordMeaning: On hearing the second section (in full) as narrated by the intelligent Suta, Samsapayana thereafter asked him about (the subject matter of) the third Pdda (Section). "The second Pdda has been narrated by you along with its sequel (Appendix);…
verses.commentary: Sense: On hearing the second section (in full) as narrated by the intelligent Suta, Samsapayana thereafter asked him about (the subject matter of) the third Pdda (Section). "The second Pdda has been narrated by you along with its sequel (Appendix);…

verses.sanskrit: युधिष्ठिर उवाच: आनन्दश्चैव संजातो रुद्रस्य द्विजसत्तम । कथ्यतां मे च तत्सर्वं संक्षेपात्सह बान्धवैः
verses.transliteration: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca: ānandaścaiva saṃjāto rudrasya dvijasattama / kathyatāṃ me ca tatsarvaṃ saṃkṣepātsaha bāndhavaiḥ
verses.translation: How the seven great sages who had been great Sidd- as in the Svayambhuva Manvantara, failed to attain the fruit of penance in the Vaivasvata Manvantara (I shall narrate.) Ovemhelmed with the curse of Bhava (Siva)they did not attain In the Svayambhuva Manvantara they had been curs¬ ed by Bhava. In order to make (the curse) truthful (i.e. fulfill¬ ed), they were born again. From the Jana Loka they went to heaven. We have heard that in the Yajiia of the great lord, Brahma assumed the form of Varuna. With a desire for progeny he had consigned the semen into the holy fire. It was then that the sages had their second birth. Bhrgu, Angiras, Marici, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Atri and Vasistha—these eight 1 were the sons of Brahma. In his grand elaborate Yajna all the Devas had come. All the Arigas (ancillaries) of the Yajna and Vasatkara had assu¬ med corporeal forms. The Saman mantras, thousands of Yajur mantras and the Rgveda embellished with Pada and Krama 2 (Pathas) were present there in embodied form. The Yajurveda enriched with (relevant) metres, brilli¬ ant with Oriikara as its mouth (face) was present here along with Suktas, Bralimanas and Mantras related to the Arthas (objects & purposes) of the Yajna. The Sama Veda so rich in (the variety of Vedic) me¬ tres and with all Mantra-Songs (which are) to be sung at the outset was present there along with Visvavasu and other Gand- harvas. The Braluna Veda (Atharva Veda) was (present there) accompanied by terriDie rites. (But) due to (the presence of the) There are two discrepancies here. Saptarsis means a set of seven sages but here eight sons of Brahma are enumerated. Apart from this discre¬ pancy in number the names of the Saptarsis of this Manvantara as given in vv 25-28 of the last chapter are different from this list even though v. 28 of that chapter asserts that "these seven sages exist in the present Manvan- tara n ( ete sap tar ay ah siddha vartante samprate'nlare). Krama is a special method of reciting vedic texts. It is so called as the recitation proceeds from the first member, either word or letter to the second, then the second is repeated and connected with the third and so on. (The following details about the recitation of the Vedas) Laksanas (the characteristic topics), Svaras (notes), Stobhas (chanted interjections in a Saman-song), Nirukta (etymologies), Svarabhaktis (insertion of vowel sound for ease in pronunciation), Atraya (resting places or annexation), Vasafkara (pronouncing e Vasat'), Nigraha (suppression) and Pragraha (vowels not subject to Sandhi rules) (all these were physically present).
verses.hindi: ताराणां तारका होता: शुक्लत्वाच्चेव तारका: । दिव्यानां पाथिवानां च नेशाना चेव सर्वेशः शुक्लत्वे चामृतत्वे च शीतत्वे च विभाव्यते । सूर्याचन्द्रमसोदिव्ये मण्डलं भास्करे खगे
verses.wordMeaning: How the seven great sages who had been great Sidd- as in the Svayambhuva Manvantara,…
verses.commentary: Sense: How the seven great sages who had been great Sidd- as in the Svayambhuva Manvantara,…

verses.sanskrit: श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: कथयामि नृपश्रेष्ठ आनन्देश्वरमुत्तमम् । दानवानां वधं कृत्वा देवदेवो महेश्वरः
verses.transliteration: śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: kathayāmi nṛpaśreṣṭha ānandeśvaramuttamam / dānavānāṃ vadhaṃ kṛtvā devadevo maheśvaraḥ
verses.translation: The brilliantly shining goddess Earth, the quarters, the intermediate quarters, the Lords of quarters, the celestial virgins, the wives of Devas, the mothers and Ayu—all these were present there in embodied form in front of the Lord (Brahma) who was performing the Yajna assuming the form of Varuna. On seeing the ladies, the semen virile of Svayambhu fell on the ground. There is no doubt about this that it took place on account of the dispensation of the inevitable in the case of Brahmarsis (Brahmanical sages). Pitamaha (god Brahma) then took it up by means of Sruks and Sruva (sacrificial spoons and ladles) and performed the Homa as if it were ghee, reciting the mantras duly. Thereafter, the Prajapati began the creation of living beings (or aggregate of elements). Due to the splendour that was beside, the fiery things were born; the Gunas Sattva and Rajas were not pervaded by the Guna Tamas. From the Saguna brilliance, Tamas stayed perpe¬ tually in the sky. All the living beings were born from the Tamas (darkness) and the Tejas (brilliance). When the sons born of Kantian were created, Brahma took up his Semen Virile in the ghee-pot and performed the Homa. When the Semen Virile was consigned to the holy fire, the great sages manifested themselves. They were embodied and very brilliant. All the seven (sages) had the attributes of new born infants. When.the Semen Virile was once poured into the fire, Mahadeva saw him coming out like that and said to Brahma: "I am desirous of a son and I am initiated. He is born to me, O lord. Hence may lord Bhrgu be my son." Mahadeva was permitted by god Brahma who said: "So be it". Mahadeva adopted Bhrgu as his son. All the descen¬ dants of Bhrgu are called Varunas. He became a holy lord (sage). A second (ladleful of) Semen Virile fell on the burning coals. Angiras was born of it with his limbs firmly united on fire (burning coals). Hence he is known as Angiras. On seeing his birth, the Fire-god spoke to Brahma: "It was I who held your Semen Virile. Hence may this second son be mine." The Fire-god was addressed by Brahma: "Let it be so". Hence, we have heard that all the descendants of Angiras are known as Agneyas.
verses.hindi: घनतेजोमय्य॑ शुक्ल॑ं मण्डल भास्करस्य तु । विशन्ति सर्वदेवास्तु स्थानान्येतानि सवंशः मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु छूुक्षसूर्यग्रहाक्रया:  तानि देवगृहाण्येव तदास्यास्ते भवस्ति च
verses.wordMeaning: The brilliantly shining goddess Earth, the quarters, the intermediate quarters, the Lords of quarters, the celestial virgins, the wives of Devas,…
verses.commentary: Sense: The brilliantly shining goddess Earth, the quarters, the intermediate quarters, the Lords of quarters, the celestial virgins, the wives of Devas,…

verses.sanskrit: पूजितो दैवतैः सर्वैः किन्नरैर्यक्षपन्नगैः । आनन्दसंयुतो देवो ननर्त वृषवाहनः
verses.transliteration: pūjito daivataiḥ sarvaiḥ kinnarairyakṣapannagaiḥ / ānandasaṃyuto devo nanarta vṛṣavāhanaḥ
verses.translation: When the Semen Virile was consigned to the holy fire for six more times by Brahma, the creator, the six Brahmas (sons of Brahma) were born. So it is heard. Marici was the first among them, born from the rays (of sacrificial fire). Since the (second) son was born in the Kratu (sacrifice), he is called Kratu. "I am the third" (Aham-Trtlya), saying thus the third son was born. So he is called Atri. The fourth son was born with sharp pointed hairs. Hence he is remembered as Pulastya. The son born with long hairs is remembered as Pulaha. He who was born out of the Vasu (fire?) was called Vasuman. He is called Vasistha by those who know the truth, by the expounders of Vedas. Thus these six great sages are the mental sons of Brahma. Gf. Brhad-devala V. 97-101 for the story of the births of Bhrgu, Angiras and Atri. Etymologies of these names also are borrowed therefrom though grammarians offer different derivations. They maintain the continunity of the worlds. These subjects are developed and nurtured by them. Hence Brahma s sons are mentioned as Prajapatis. Others called Pitrs were created by these great sages alone. The seven groups of sages are well known in the world, viz. Maricas,Bhargavas, Ahgirasas, Paulastyas, Paulahas, Vasisthas and Atreyas; these groups of Pitrs are well-known in the world. These three Ganas have been briefly mentioned before: They are Apurvas (Rare), Prakdsas (Brilliant) and Jyolifmaiitas (Illuminated ones). Their king is lord Yama and they have wiped off their sins by their (religious) observances. There are other Prajapatis also. Listen to them attentively. There are other Prajapatis many in number, viz. Kardama, Kasyapa, Sesa (?), Vikranta, Susruvas, Bahuputra, Kumara, Vivasvan, Sucilravas, Pracetas, Aristanemi, Bahula and many others. 1 Kusoccayas and Valakhilyas had become great sages. They had the speed of the mind. They could go anywhere. They became Emperors. The groups of sages called Vaikhanasas are honoured by Brahmanas. They were born of the sacred ashes. They are engaged in penance and learning.
verses.hindi: स शीघ्रमेति पर्येति भास्करोइलातचक्वत् । भ्रमन्व भ्रमसाणानि ऋक्षाणि गगने रविः पूर्वाह्ल॑ चापराह्ल तु हो हो देवालयों तु सः  तपत्येक॑ तु मध्याह्न तरेव तु स रश्मिभिः
verses.wordMeaning: When the Semen Virile was consigned to the holy fire for six more times by Brahma, the creator, the six Brahmas (sons of Brahma) were born. So it is heard. Marici was the first among them, born from the rays (of sacrificial fire).…
verses.commentary: Sense: When the Semen Virile was consigned to the holy fire for six more times by Brahma, the creator, the six Brahmas (sons of Brahma) were born. So it is heard. Marici was the first among them, born from the rays (of sacrificial fire).…

verses.sanskrit: भैरवं रूपमास्थाय गौर्या चार्द्धाङ्गसंस्थितः । भूतवेतालकङ्कालैर् भैरवैर् भैरवो वृतः
verses.transliteration: bhairavaṃ rūpamāsthāya gauryā cārddhāṅgasaṃsthitaḥ / bhūtavetālakaṅkālair bhairavair bhairavo vṛtaḥ
verses.translation: The handsome Asvinas were born of his ears. The pure ones born of the eyes are known as Ak$arajas. The elder Prajapatis were born of his vessels. The sages were born of the hair pores in the skin and the sweat dirt. From his tears and cry were born the terrible mouths Niryasas (?), the junctions of fortnights, years, days and nights and the terrible light of Pitrs. Raudra they say is the blood. Lohita is remembered as gold. That should be known as Maitra also. The smoke is remembered as animals. Different Puranas give different lists of Prajapatis. For example, the lists in Mbh., Mt. P. or Garuda differ from our text (and Bd. P) and inter se. The flames are Rudras and Adityas. Divine human beings were born of the burning coal and the flame. Brahma born of Brahman is the primordial being in the world. Requesting (for the hand of) a virgin, the sages told him who bestowed everything: "Brahma, the eldest among Suras, is delighted with Devas. These lords will be giving birth to all the subjects. All of them are Prajapatis. All of them are sages. These rites will uphold these worlds with his grace. They have developed couples increasing your splend¬ our. Among Devas there are learned ones in Vedas. All the saintly kings are also such. All of them are devoted to the Vedic Mantras. They have been born out of the attributes of Prajapatis. The infinite Brahman is the Truth and the greatest penance. O lord, all of us are your own children, the Brahman (Vedas), the Brahmanas and all the worlds including the mobile and the immobile beings. Beginning with Marlci and including all the sages, we Devas are thinking about and longing for children by your (blessings)".
verses.hindi: सर्वेषामुत्तरे मेरलॉकालोकस्तु दक्षिणे । विदूरभावादर्कस्य भूमेलेंखावुतस्य च ॥ .
verses.wordMeaning: The handsome Asvinas were born of his ears. The pure ones born of the eyes are known as Ak$arajas. The elder Prajapatis were born of his vessels. The sages were born of the hair pores in the skin and the sweat dirt.…

verses.sanskrit: ननर्त नर्मदातीरे दक्षिणे पाण्डुनन्दन । तुष्टैर्मरुद्गणैः सर्वैः स्थापितः कमलासनः
verses.transliteration: nanarta narmadātīre dakṣiṇe pāṇḍunandana / tuṣṭairmarudgaṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ sthāpitaḥ kamalāsanaḥ
verses.translation: (Siita said) O highly blessed ones, Devas along with sages identifying (themselves) with the abodes and the time are born in this family during the Yajna. In that very form, they may not establish these sub¬ jects. They may be stabilised from the beginning till the end of the Yugas. Then the preceptor of the world (Brahma), without any further thought, spoke—"O Devas, it was after deciding like this that the subjects had been created by me. There is no doubt about this. These sages have been born in your race". Among them I shall recount in detail and in proper sequence the race of Bhygu, the ancient noble soul and the first Prajapati. Bhrgu had two unequalled, excellent and auspicious wives of noble families. One was the daughter ofHiranyakasipu, famous by the name 'Divya' and the other was the fair-com- plexioned daughter of Puloman, named Pauloml. Divyabore to Bhrgu the planet Sukra (Venus) who was the preceptor of Dcvas and Asuras, who was the son of Kavi, and was known as Kavya, Sukra and Usanas. He was the most excellent among the knowers of Vedas. Sukra's wife named Ahgl was the mental daughter of the Soma-drinking Pitfs and very famous. She gave birth to four sons. He was endowed with Brahman's splendour and the most excellent among the knowers of Brahman. Sukia begot four sons of her, viz. Tvastr, Varutrin, Sanda and Amaika. They resembled the sun and in their prowess they were equal to Brahma. Ranjana, Prthurasmi and the scholarly Brhadgiras were the sons of Varutrin. They were devoted to Brahman and became the priests of Suras. They approached Manu with the motive of spoiling sacrificial rites. On seeing Dharma being violated, Indra spoke to Manu: "I would rather have the sacrifice performed through you than through these". On hearing these words of Indra, they fled from that place. When they absconded, Indra released (their) wife Cetana. Then he followed her. On seeing them come there again with the evil in¬ tention of killing Indra, he struck at them (while) they slept in the altar of the lord of Devas on the southern side. While they were being devoured by (dogs, jackals and wolves) their heads fell down simultaneously and became dates.
verses.hindi: ग्रहनक्षत्रताराणां दर्शनं भास्करस्य च्। उच्छूयस्य प्रमाणेन ज्ञेयसस्तमनो दयम् १०६ जब शीघ्र गति से भ्रमण करते हैं, तब जान पड़ता है कि नक्षत्रगण चक्राकार जलते हुए अओंगारे की तरह सूर्य के पीछे घूम रहे हैं। इस प्रकार सूय॑ दक्षिण दिशा होकर चारों द्वीषों में भ्रमण करते हैं ओर बारम्बार उदय-अस्तकाल में उदित और अस्त होते हैं ।१०२-१०३। सूर्थ अपनी किरणों से स्वर्गीय दोनों देवालयों में से एक पूर्वार्द को पूर्वाह्न में और पर्राद्ध को पराह्न में तपाते हैं एवं मध्याह्न में प्रत्येक को प्रतष्त करते हैं ।

verses.sanskrit: तदाप्रभृति तत्तीर्थम् आनन्देश्वरम् उच्यते । अष्टम्यां च चतुर्दश्यां पौर्णमास्यां नराधिप
verses.transliteration: tadāprabhṛti tattīrtham ānandeśvaram ucyate / aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ narādhipa
verses.translation: Thus, the sons of Varutrin were killed by Indra former¬ ly. Sukra begot (of his wife) Yajani the daughter Devayanl. The three-headed Visvarupa was the great son of Tvastr. Visvakarman is remembered as the younger twin- brother of Visvarupa. Twelve sons were born to Bhrgu (and were known as) Bhrgu (Gana) Devas 1. Lord Kavya begot of Devi those sons. Mt. P. gives a different list of these 12 Dcva Yajiiika Bhrgus in its lists of Gotras and Pravaras. They were—Bhuvana, Bhavana, Anya, Anyayata, Kratu, Sravas, Murdhan, Vyajaya, Vyasrusa, Prasava, Aja and the twelfth one Adhipati. These twelve sons of Bhrgu are remembered as twelve sacrificial Devas. PaulomI bore a lordly son having full self- control and engrossed in Brahman. Since he was sickly in the eighth month of conception, he was forcibly taken out of the womb by dire means and so his name became Cyavana. He became conscious due to Pracetas. Through the anger of Cyavana (revived by) Pracetas, Cyavana alias Pracetasa burned the man-eaters through anger 1 2. The son of Bhrgu (i.e. Cyavana) begot of Sukanya two sons honoured by saints, viz. Atmavana and Dadhica. The son Sarasvata was born to Sarasvatl and Dadhica. The blessed lady Ruci, daughter of Nahusa, was the wife of Atmavana. The sage Orva (Aurva in Bd. P. and Mbh.) of great renown was born of him after breaking through the thighs (of his mother)- Rclka was the son of Aurva. He was brilliant (in complexion) like a blazing fire. When the cams 3 (sacrificial offerings) pertaining to lludra and Vi?nu (charged with specific mantras ) by Bhrgu were interchanged, Jamadagni was born, as the Cara pertaining to Vais pa va fire was (mistakenly) eaten (by his mother). verses.hindi: सूर्य उदय से लेकर मध्याह्ल पर्यंन्त अपनी किरण को बढ़ाते हैं और मध्याह्ञ से अस्त पयंन्त धीरे-धीरे किरणों का हास करते हुये अस्त हो जाते हैं ।१०४-१०५॥ उदय और अस्त से हो पूर्व तथा पर्चिम दिल्ञाओं का ज्ञान होता है। सूर्थ जिस प्रकार आगे तपते हैं या प्रकाश का दान करते हैं, उसी प्रकार पीछे दोनों (पाइव) बगलों में भी जहाँ सूथं उदित हुए देखे जाते हैं वही उदयाचल कहलाता है और जहाँ वे अदृष्य हो जाते

verses.sanskrit: विधिवच्चार्चयेद् देवं सुगन्धेन विलेपयेत् । ब्राह्मणान्पूजयेत्तत्र यथाशक्त्या युधिष्ठिर
verses.transliteration: vidhivaccārcayed devaṃ sugandhena vilepayet / brāhmaṇānpūjayettatra yathāśaktyā yudhiṣṭhira
verses.translation: Listen to the narration of the family of Angiras, the intelligent son of Agni. It was in the family of Angiras, the intelligent son of Agni, that Bharadvajas along with Gautamas were born. The most important Devas belonging to the family of Angiras are Tvisimants (?) of great prowess. Atharvan, Angiras had three wives, viz. Surupa the daughter of Marica, Svarat the daughter ofKardama and Pathya the daughter of Manu. I shall mention their progeny. The heirs of Atharvan born of those wives were the uplifters of the family. They were born as a result of the great penance of that purified soul. Br-haspati was born of Surupa and Svarat gave birth to Gautama. Pathya gave birth of Avandhya, Vamadeva, Utathya and Usija. Dhisnu was thes on of Pathya. Samvarta was the mental son (of Atharvan). Vicitta, Ayasya and Sara- dvan were the sons of Utathya. Dxrghatama was the son of Asi. Brhaduttha was the son of Vamadeva. Dhisnu's son was Sudhanvan and his son was Rsabha. Rathakaras (Charioteers) are remembered as Devas. They are well-known as Rsis (Rbhus?). Bharadvaja of very great fame and well-known was born of Brhaspati. The progeny of Samvarta, (mental) son of Angiras, are considered as Devas. Listen to them. These Angiras Devas are regarded as junior to Bjrhaspati. Ten own sons of Angiras were born of Surupa. They were ten and their names are—Audarya, Ayu, Danu, Daksa, Darbha, Prana, Havisman, Havisnu, Kratu and Satya. The following ten and five (i.e. fifteen) are to be known as belonging to the Pakfa (i.e. Gotra ) of Angiras—Ayasya, Uta¬ thya, Vamadeva, Usija, Bharadvajas, Sankrtikas, Gargya, Kanva, Rathitara, Mudgalas, Vi§nuvrddhas, Haritas, Vayus, Bhaksas of Bharadvaja family, Arsabhas and Kimbhayas. Many others (external) sages (belonging to the families outside) are remembered among other sages. Contemplating on the waters (Apah) with a desire for progeny, Marlci desired the waters. The lord mentally concei¬ ved thus—"A son born of a praiseworthy woman, endowed with all good qualities and having good tastes is honoured". All the waters were called. Thelord dwelt in their company. The lord procreated an unequalled son named Aristanemi who became Prajapati and who was of well-con¬ trolled mind. Vadhauvesa 1 (?) begot the son Marica, having the splendour of the Sun. Contemplating on the speech of good men 2 he stay¬ ed under water for seven thousand years with a desire to beget sons. Hence (the son) became unequalled. Kasyapa was the knower of the sun (?) Hence he was on a par with Brahma. In every Manvantara, he is born through a part of Brahma.
verses.hindi: हैं, वही अस्ताचल कहलाता है ।१०६-१०७। सब लोकों से उत्तर मेरु है और दणिण में लोकालोक । बहुत दूर जाने के कारण यह स्थान भूमि की रेखा की तरह प्रतीयमान होता है। सूर्य की किरणें रात को क्षीण ही जाती हैं; अतः यह दिखाई नहीं पड़ता है १०८५। ग्रह, नक्षत्र, तारा और सूर्य के दर्शन तथा अस्त ऊँचे स्थानों से जाने जाते हैं। अग्नि और जल की छाया शुक्ल वर्ण की होती है तथा पृथ्वी की छाया कृष्ण वर्ण की। बहुत दूर रहने के कारण उगते हुए सूयय किरणों से हौन मालूम पड़ते हैं । क्षीणकिरण होने के कारण उस समय सूर्य में उतनी गर्मी भी नहीं रहती है और वे लोहित वर्ण हो जाते हैं ।१०६-११०। रेखा पर स्थित सुय्य जहाँ- जहाँ से देखे जाते हैं, वहाँ से वे हजार योजन ऊपर रहते हैं ।१११। सूर्य के अस्त हो जाने पर उनकी किरणों
verses.wordMeaning: Listen to the narration of the family of Angiras, the intelligent son of Agni. It was in the family of Angiras, the intelligent son of Agni, that Bharadvajas along with Gautamas were born.…

verses.transliteration: godānaṃ tatra kartavyaṃ vastradānaṃ śubhāvaham / vasantasya trayodaśyāṃ śrāddhaṃ tatraiva kārayet
verses.translation: The subjects 3 were angered by Daksa, it is said (?) for the sake of (his) daughters. Then he drank wine. The word 'JCaJya means wine. Hascekasas (?) 4 5 * should be known as Brahma's KaSya. KaSya is remembered by Brahmanas as wine. Because he drank Kaiya (wine) he is called Kasyapa. 8 He used harsh words. On being cursed by Daksa, he became infuriated and thereby became Kasyapa. On being requested by Kasyapa and urged by Brahma Paramesthin, Daksa gave his daughters to Kasyapa. Bd. P. reads nirata: so'psvatilapat 'who performed penance in waters'. Chaste goddess Vak (Bd. P.). Bd. P. (ibid. v. 120) reads Prabhuh for Prajah hereof. It means 'When the holy Lord got enraged at the over-bearing speech for his daughters'. HaScekasa is obscure. Bd. P. reads hasye kaSir hi vijiieyo 'The word KaSi should be understood in the sense of humour'. A funny derivation. The sage Kasyapa is so designated as he was a He who knows this holy creation of Rsis through Varuna becomes long-lived and meritorious. He becomes Puri¬ fied and attains excellent happiness. By listening to this and retaining this (in memory) he becomes free from all sins. Then all the sages spoke to Romaharsaria: "When the sixth Prajasarga (creation of the subjects) of Caksusa Manu had been dissolved, the creation of Vaivasvata Manu began to function (How did it take place?)." When the Vaivasvata Manvantara arrived, Daksa was commanded by the self-born lord himself—"Create the subjects". Daksa created mobile and the immobile living beings. Then Daksa proceeded to create the four types of Prajas (subjects), viz. Jarayujas (viviparous),Antfajas (oviparous), Udbhijjas (plants that pierce the ground and grow), and Svedajas (those born of sweat).
verses.hindi: प्रभा हि सोरी पादेन अस्तं गचछति भास्करे । अग्निमाविशते रात्रौ तस्मादूदूरात्प्रकाशते

verses.sanskrit: इङ्गुदैर् बदरैर् बिल्वैर् अक्षतैश्च जलेन वा । प्रेतानां कारयेच्छ्राद्धमानन्देश्वर उत्तमे
verses.transliteration: iṅgudair badarair bilvair akṣataiśca jalena vā / pretānāṃ kārayecchrāddhamānandeśvara uttame
verses.translation: He performed severe penance for ten thousand years. He became endowed with Yogic power and more parti¬ cularly with supernatural powers like Anima etc. As he possesses glorious power, he divided himself into human beings, serpents, Raksasas, Devas, Asuras and Gandharvas. All of them being endowed with divine bodies and wealth of beauty and splend¬ our, they were lords equal to himself. He was desirous of creat¬ ing other mental living beings of various kinds. (He created) sages, Devas, Gandharvas, human beings, serpents, Raksasa's, Yaksas, Bhutas,. Pisacas, birds, animals and deer. When these mentally created beings did not flourish and multiply, he was rebuked by the intelligent lord Mahadeva. He became then desirous of creating the different subjects by the process of sexual intercourse. He took to himself as wife the daughter of Vlrana, the Prajapati. She was Asikni who was endowed with great penance and who supported the worlds. The entire Universe consisting of the mobile and the immobile beings was sustained by her. In this matter they quoted two verses about Daksa, the son of Pracetas. "When Daksa married Asikni the great daughter of Vlrana, he created a million mobile wells On seeing those subjects desirous of flourishing the extremely powerful celestial sage, Brahma's son Narada, fond of arguments, spoke evil words to them resulting in himself be¬ ing cursed. The Brahmana (Narada) is sometimes called son of Kasyapa. Due to his mean action the Brahmana sage was afraid of Daksa's curse. Paramesthin was born as Kasyapa's son. Again due to the fear of curse of Daksa, he was born as his mental son. His second birth was as the mental son of Kasyapa. He was formerly born asNarada (son) of Paramesthin. Formerly Daksa's sons famous as Haryasvas were destroyed for the pur¬ pose of censure. They were undoubtedly annihilated. Lord Daksa became infuriated and attempted to destroy him (Narada). Keeping the Brahmarsis ahead, he (Daksa) was requested by Paramesthin (not to kill Narada). Then Daksa stipulated the conditions with Parame¬ sthin: "Let Narada be born of my daughter as your son". Then Daksa gave his beloved daughter to Parame¬ sthin. Narada was born thereof. The sage became calm and ceased to be afraid. On hearing this those Brahmanas became curious. They asked Suta, the seer of truth, the foremost among the eloquent ones: How were the sons of Prajapati, the subjects born of Pracetasa destroyed by the noblc-souled Narada?
verses.hindi: प्रकाश्यं च तथोष्णं च सुर्याग्नेयो च तेजसो । परस्परानृप्रवेशादाप्यायेते दिवानिशम् दिन सुययप्रकाशाख्यं तामसी रात्रिरुच्यते । तस्माहयवस्थिता रात्रि: सुयविक्ष्यमहः स्मृतम्॒

verses.sanskrit: आनन्दिता भवेयुस्ते यावदाभूतसम्प्लवम् । सन्ततेर्वै न विच्छेदः सप्तजन्मसु जायते । आनन्दो हि भवत्तेषां प्रतिजन्मनि भारत
verses.transliteration: ānanditā bhaveyuste yāvadābhūtasamplavam / santatervai na vicchedaḥ saptajanmasu jāyate / ānando hi bhavatteṣāṃ pratijanmani bhārata
verses.translation: On hearing these auspicious truthful words born of a desire to know, he (Suta) spoke these sweet words endowed with all good qualities: Haryasvas, the sons of Daksa, desirous of procreating subjects, the extremely powerful ones came there and Narada spoke to them: 1 "Alas, all of you are childish. You do not know the entire surface of the world. What is within, what is above and what is below, you do not know. How will you create the subjects? What is the extent of the Earth? What are the things to be created? Is it possible to create without knowing these? Small or great defects are sure to be seen therein". On hearing his words they went away to various quarters. On reaching the aerial zone, they were utterly non¬ plussed. Wandering (here and there) intermingled with the (blowing) winds, they have not returned till this day. Thus those great sages are wandering after reaching the aerial zone. When his sons were lost, Lord Daksa, the Pracetasa, begot again ofVirini a thousand sons. These sons (known as) Sabalasvas (having horses of diverse colours), desirous of multiplying subjects were told the same words by Narada. On hearing those words all those powerful young men spoke to one another—"The great sage has said well. Undoubtedly the track of our brothers should be followed. After knowing the magnitude of the Earth we shall easily create the subjects". They too went the same way to all the quarters. Even to this day they have not returned like the rivers (not returning) after falling into the oceans. Ever since then, if a younger brother goes in quest of a lost elder brother, he too gets lost. This is riot to be done by one who knows. When the Sabalasvas were lost, lord Daksa became infuriated and cursed Narada—"Be ruined, endure the According to Mbb Adi. 75.7-8, Narada instructed Haryasvas, the first batch of 1000 sons of Daksa, in Sankhya Philosophy. Thereby all be¬ came recluses and frustrated Dak;a's plan of populating the world. Here (w. 147-48) Narada advised them to know the magnitude of the earth, which they were going to populate. He who knows entirely this creation of Daksa precise¬ ly, becomes long-lived, famous, blessed and endowed with progeny.

verses.sanskrit: ॥ इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे आनन्देश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम पञ्चषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ र्क्व् अध्याय ६६ श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: ततो गच्छेत्तु राजेन्द्र मातृतीर्थमनुत्तमम् । सङ्गमस्य समीपस्थं नर्मदादक्षिणे तटे
verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe ānandeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 66 śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: tato gacchettu rājendra mātṛtīrthamanuttamam / saṅgamasya samīpasthaṃ narmadādakṣiṇe taṭe
verses.translation: Please narrate in detail the birth and origin of all I shall now recount the progeny of Dharma. (Listen and) understand. Daksa, the son of Pracetas, gave these ten daughters to Dharma as wives, viz. Arundhati, Vasu, Yarn!, Lariiba, Bhanu, Marutvatl, Sariikalpa, Muhurta, Sadhya and ViSva. Sadhya bore to Dharma twelve sons called Sadhyas. The highly fortunate Sadhyas were born according to their wish and were partakers of shares in Yajfias. Those who are conversant with Devas (Devata-lore) know them to be greater than other Devas. It is reported that the Devas (called) Jayas were creat¬ ed out of the mouth of Brahma through the desire for progeny. All of them are remembered as having Mantras as their bodies in the Manvantaras. These names of those Jayas are famous: Darsa, Paurnamasa, Brhad Rathantara, Citti, Vicitti, Akuti, Kuti, Vijnatr, Vijnata, Manas and Yajna. As a result of the curse of Brahma, they were born The blessed sons of Dharma, the twelve deathless ones (named) Sadhyas, had been formerly born in the Caksusa Manvantara. The highly powerful Devas who had passed away in the Svarocisa Manvantara assumed the name of Tusitas in the Caksusa Manvantara and spoke to one another. When the duration of Svarocisa Manvantara remained but little, the Tusita Devas conferred with one another—"We shall enter the blessed Sadhyas and be born in the Manvantara. That will be conducive to our welfare 5 '. After saying thus, all of them were born in the Cak¬ susa Manvantara as the twelve sons of Dharma, son of Svayam- bhu (god Brahma). Nara and Narayana too were born there again. Vipas- cit who was Indra and Satya who was Hari were in the Svaro¬ cisa Manvantara the Tusita gods. When Tu§itas became Sadhyas, these names are mentioned—Manas, Anumanta, Prana, Nara, the power¬ ful Yana, Citti, Haya, Naya, Harhsa, Narayana, Prabhava and Vibhu. They were born as the twelve Sadhyas. In the Svayariibhuva Manvantara at the outset, then in the Svarocisa Manvantara these were the names of the Tusitas. (Listen and) understand them. They were—Prana, Apana, Udana, Samana, Vyana, Caksus, Srotra, Prana(?), Sparsa, Buddhi and Manas.
verses.hindi: योजनाग्रान्मुहुतेस्य इसां संख्यां निबोधत । पूर्ण शतसहस्राणामे्कात्रिशत्तु सा स्मृता १२० प्चाशत्तु तथाअन्यानि सहस्राण्यधिकानि तु । मौहतिकी गतिहाँंषा सुर्यस्य तु विधोयते एतेन गतियोगेन यदा काष्ठां तु दक्षिणाम् । पर्यागच्छेत्तदा55वित्यो माघे काष्ठन्तमेव हि.

verses.sanskrit: मातरस्तत्र राजेन्द्र संजाता नर्मदातटे । उमार्धनारिर् देवेशो व्यालयज्ञोपवीतधृक्

verses.translation: Formerly only these • names of Tusitas were remem¬ bered: Prana, Apana, Udana, Samana and Vyana. The Vasus were the sons of Vasu. They are remember¬ ed as the younger brothers of Sadhyas. These are glorified as the eight Vasus Dhara, Dhruva, Soma, Apa, Anala, Anila, Prat- yusa and Prabhasa. Dravina and Hutahavyavaha were the sons of Dhara; Soma's sons were lord Varca and Budha who is known as a planet. These two were born of Rohini and are famous in the three worlds. Dhara, Ormi and Kalila—these three too were the sons of Candramas (Moon god). Apa's sons were Vaitandya, Sama and Santa. Skanda and Sanatkumara were born of the fourth part of Tejas (fire). Agni's son Kumara was born in the Sara grove (a kind of reed). Sakha, Visakha and Naigameya were his younger brothers. Anila's (Wind god) wife was Siva and her sons were Manojava and Avijnatagati. Anila had these two sons. They know that the son of Pratyusa was sage Devala by name. Devala had two sons Ksamavan and Manxsin. Brhaspati's sister was an excellent woman, celibate and having Yogic Siddhis. Unattached (to the worldly affairs or things) she roamed the entire Universe. She who became the wife of Prabhasa, the eighth among the Vasus, had a son Visvakarma who was the Prajapati of all Silpis (artisans and sculptors). He is the maker of all arts and crafts. He is the car¬ penter of the Devas. He makes and causes others to make orna¬ ments. He makes the aerial chariots of all Devas. The human craftsmen depend upon (and emulate) his mechanical arts. The ten renowned Visvedevas were born of Visva. They were—Kratu, Daksa, Sravas, Satya, Kala, Kama, Dhuni, Kuruvan, Prabhavan and Rocamana. [ They] are remembered as the ten sons of Dharma. They were the auspicious sons born of Visva.

verses.translation: The Marutvants were the sons of Marutvatl. The Bhanu groups were remembered as the sons ofBhanu. The The learned Samkalpa (conception) was born of Sam- kalpa. The Nagavlthls consisting of three patlis were born of Jam! (Yarn!). All the objects on the Earth were born of Arundhatl. Thus the learned and eternal creation of Dharma has been narrated. O men of holy rites, I shall mention the names of the Muhurta's and Tithis along with their presiding lords. 1 Even as I recount, listen and understand. (Incidentally I shall mention) the divisions of days and nights, the constellations in briefand all the Muhurtas and stars that appear during days and nights. More than six hundred Kalas are mentioned during days and nights. The manifestation of Rtus is based on the special movement of the Sun. Those who know Vedas calculate Tithis as the basis of festivals. For the purpose of charitable gifts on behalf of Pitrs, they utilise the different occasions (even if no apparent peculia¬ rity is seen). The divisions {Muhiirtas or Bhagas) in the day are Raudra, Sarva, Maitra, Pintjya, Vasava, Apya, Vaisvadeva, Brahma—these Muhurtas cover the period till mid-day. Praja- patya, Aindra, Indra, Nirrti, Varuna and Aryamna and Bhaga: these Muhurtas of the day are caused by the Sun. They are to be known in accordance with their magnitude by means of the gnomons. Aja, Ahir-Budhnya, Pusa, Yamadevata, Agneya, Prajapatya, Brahma, Saumya, Aditya, Barhaspatya, Vaisnava, Savitra, Tvas tra and Vayavya—these are the fifteen Muhurtas Only three positions have been assigned for all the planets. They must be known in order as southern, northern and middle ones. The constellations Purvaphalgunl, UttaraphalgunI and Magha are remembered as AryamI (Vithi), The constella¬ tions Hasta, Citra and Svatl are termed Govlthi). The constel¬ lations Jyestha, Visakha and Anuradha are remembered as Jaradgavi Vithi. These three Vlthis are mentioned to be in the middle path. The enumeration of Naksalras from Asvini shows that this portion of the Purana should be assigned to A JD. 300-400 as the Vedic list of Naksa- tras starts from Krttika. Vide H.D. V.l p -504 for a comparative table of the list ofNaksatras in Vedic Sariihitas, their deities, their modem names etc.

verses.translation: Vithis are the divisions of planetary sphere comprising of three aster- isms, c.g. Asvini, Bharaii, Krttika constitute Nagavithi. Verse 48 states, vithis are three in number in the northern path but actually only two Naga and Airavatl are mentioned. The line regarding Gajavlthl seems to be omitted. The constellations Mula, Purvasaqlha and Uttara- sadha are termed Ajavlthl. The constellations Sravana, Dhani- stha and Satabhisak are the GarglVithi. The constellations Purva Bhadrapada, U ttara Bhadrapada and Revati are glorified asVaisvanarl (Vithi). These three Vithls are remembered by learned men to be in the southern path. The twenty seven (constellations) daughters whom JDaksa gave to Soma (Moon god) are glorified in Astronomy as Naksatras by name (i.e. Stars). They all bore children illu¬ minated with unmeasured splendour. From the daughters (of Daksa) who remained, Kasyapa married fourteen 1 blessed ones. All of them are mothers of the worlds. They were Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kala, Arista, Surasa, Surabhi, Vinata, Tamra, Krodhavas'a, Ira, Kadru and Muni. O knowers ofDharma, listen and understand their progeny. The twelve Vaikuntha gods who were prominent in the Carisnava Manvantara that has passed, became Sadhyas, in the Caksusa Manvantara. When the present Vaivasvata Manvantara had arrived, they were propitiated by Aditi. They gathered together and spoke to one another. "We shall enter this blessed Aditi alone, in the present Vaivasvata Manvantara by means of a moiety of our Yagic splendour and become her sons. That will be conducive to our welfare. Those who are born of Aditi will attain the status of Adityas". Satakratu (Indra) and Visnu were born again as Nara and Narayana in the present Vaivasvata Manvantara. Death and birth are mentioned to happen even to those Devas. Just as the Sun rises and sets in this world, even so Since they are attached to the great Vedic tradition as well as worldly objects like sound and the eightfold super¬ human powers like Anima (minuteness) these Devas were born. The attachment to sensual objects is declared as the cause of birth. Due to the curse of Brahma, the Jayas were born in the Svayambhuva Manvantara as Jitas. In the Svaro- cisa Manvantara, they were born as Tusitas and in the Auttama Manvantara they were born as Satyas. Devas were born as Haris in the Tamasa Manvantara, Vaikunthas in theCaris- nava Manvantara, Sadhyas in the Caksusa Manvantara and Adityas in the present (i.e. Vaivasvata) Manvantara. The follwing are remembered as the twelve Adityas, the sons of Kasyapa: Dhata, Aryama, Mitra, Varuna, Ariisa, Bhaga, Indra, Vivasvan, Pusan, the tenth one Parjanya, Tvastr and Visnu the last but not the least (i.e. really the great).
verses.hindi: रात की व्यवस्था होती है ।११६-११८। इस प्रकार जब सूय॑ पुष्कर के बीच विचरण करते हैं। तब प्रृथ्वी के तीन अंश को वे एक मुह॒त॑ में ही पार कर जाते हैं. सूर्य एक मुह॒ते में जितने योजन जाते हैं, उसको सुनिये  सूर्य प्रति मुहुतं में एकतीस लाख पचास हजार योजन चला करते हैं ।११६-१२१। इस गति से जब सुयय दक्षिण दिद्या में जाते हैं, तब वे माघ महीने तक उस दिशा में रहते हैं। अब दक्षिण दिशा में

verses.transliteration: śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: tatra tīrthe tu yo bhaktyā navamyāṃ niyataḥ śuciḥ / upoṣya parayā bhaktyā pūjayenmātṛgocaram
verses.translation: Purified by penance and blessed by Mahadeva the chaste Surabhl bore to KaSyapa the eleven Rudras. They were Angaraka, Sarpa, Nirrti, Sadasaspati, Ajaikapat, Ahirbudhnya, Ordhvaketu, Jvara, Bhuvanesvara, Mrtyu and Kapala who was famous. With her great penance, Surabhl bore these elven Devas, the Rudras, the lords of the three worlds. Then she gave birth to two daughters, viz. RohinI hav¬ ing the lustre of Rudra and Gandharl the renowned. Four daughters, very famous in the worlds were born of RohinI, viz. Surupa, Harhsaklla, Bhadra and Kamadugha. Kamadugha and Surupa gave birth to two sons. Hamsaklla gave birth to Nrpa (king) and sages (?) and to Bhadra were born the famous and blessed Gandharvas, the sons of Vajin (horse). The horses Uccaissravas were born then; they roamed about in the firmament with the speed of mind. They were of different colours, white, red, tawny, deer-coloured, green and gray and (also of the lustre of) Rudra. These horses were of Gandharva wombs. They were the vehicles of the Devas. Verses 62-64 (in fact verses 56-65) stated that even gods like Brahma, Visnu and Siva have their births and deaths due to their attachment to sensual objects. Non-attachment is the way to liberation. Cf. w. 79-80 below. Aristanemi's wives had sixteen childern. The sons of the learned Bahuputra are remembered as Vidyuts. The excell¬ ent Rks honoured by Brahmarsis are born of Pratyangirasa. The sons of Krsasva, the celestial sage, are remembered as Devapraharanas. These are born again at the end of a thous¬ and Yugas. O Brahmanas, all the thirty-three groups of Devas are Chandajas (born from Vedic chandas or mantras). These Devas too are said to have annihilation and birth. Just as the sun rises and sets in this world, so also these groups of Devas are born in every Yuga. (How were) Sadhyas. Vasus, Visvedevas, Rudras and Adityas famous • by the nobility of their birth, greatness of the prowess or actions? We wish to know the difference among Prajapati, Visnu and the noble-souled Bhava as to who excels whom among them? Who originates from whom? Who is established in whom? Who is the eldest? Who is the middle one? who is the youngest among them? Who is the most important among them? Who is the greatest among them by means of actions, nobility of birth and prowess? Please mention all these to us as you know these precisely. In this context I shall describe the difference that is remembered among them. Listen to what I am going to say as to difference among Brahma, Visnu and Rudra. The bodies of the Self-born Lord that are said to be born from time to time are proclaimed as Rajasa, Tamasa and O excellent Brahmanas, it is not possible to state the difference among these bodies, since they are dependent upon the increase of (a particular) Guna and the two-fold bondage due to Anugraha (blessing or favouring) and Nigraha (control¬ ling). O Brahmanas, in accordance with my ability I shall recount Pravrtli (activity), Nivrtti (desistance from activity) and the increase of the Gunas of the bodies. (Listen to it) and understand.
verses.hindi: उनकी जो भति है, उसको सुनिये। इस दिशा में सूर्य दिन-रात में नौ करोड़ एक लाख पेंतालीस हजार मण्डल विषुवद्यापि? योजनेस्तन्निबोधत । तिम्रः कोटअस्तु विस्तीर्णा विषुवद्यापि? सा स्मृता

verses.sanskrit: तस्य स्युर्मातरः प्रीताः प्रीतो ऽयं वृषवाहनः । वन्ध्याया मृतवत्साया अपुत्राया युधिष्ठिर
verses.transliteration: tasya syurmātaraḥ prītāḥ prīto 'yaṃ vṛṣavāhanaḥ / vandhyāyā mṛtavatsāyā aputrāyā yudhiṣṭhira
verses.translation: One among them, the Rajasa body creates all the sub¬ jects; the Sattvika one staying in the ocean, blesses; and the Tamasa one swallows the subjects and overthrows them at the proper time. When god Brahmamanifests himself with the resurgence of Rajas guna, the Sattvika body which is called Purusa vanishes. With the excess of Tamas, when it assumes the form of Kala (the destroyer), the Rajasa form designated as Brahma disappears. When with the dominance of Sattva, the lord be¬ comes Purusa, the body named Kala ceases to exist. When Brahma manifests himself the difference.is mentioned. When the lord is Brahma, Purusa does not exist. Just as the crystal jewel assumes various colours due to its purity, and as a result of the contact with other objects, the colours and sizes being in accordance with those objects, so also the self-born assumes shapes and sizes due to the Verses 86-121: A philosophic synthesis of Brahma, Vi?$u and Siva— 'Three bodies of the single self-bom lord' (v. 99) for the three activities of creation, protection and destruction (v. 104)—The Vedas, Dharma-sastra, Sankhya and Yoga hold unanimously that Reality or the Supreme Lord is one. Synthesization of the Trinity of gods (Brahma, Visnu and Siva)as mani¬ festation of the Supreme Lord (Brahman) is a favourite subject of Purapas. Just as the cloud, though single, remains (or seems) different in colour and form so also the self-born Lord though single one assumes different forms due to Gunas and appears single, double or triple. The single entity has the three forms of Brahma (the creator), annihilator and Purusa. These three bodies arc remembered as those of the single self-bom Lord. The three bodies are Brahma, Paurusa and Antakarl. Herein what is (known as) His Rajasa body is verily the creator of subjects (i.e. the Universe). What is called the Tamasa form is the annihilator of the subjects. The Sattvika form called Paurusa is remembered as the bestower of bles¬ sings. From the Rajasa part of Brahma Marlci and Kasyapa were born. From the Tamasa form that causes dissolu¬ tion was born Bhava. The Sattvika or Paurusa form is called Visnu. These three bodies of the self-born are thus remem¬ bered in the three worlds. The supreme being, Kala, assumes states for different functions (such as) creating the subjects in the capacity of Brahma, supporting them in the status of Visnu and devouring in the guise of Rudra, the subjects who had been blessed by the Vaisnava form.
verses.hindi: तथा शतसहस्नाणामशीत्येकाधिका पुनः । श्रवण घोत्तरां काष्ठां चित्रभानुयंदा भवेत् ॥
verses.wordMeaning: One among them, the Rajasa body creates all the sub¬ jects; the Sattvika one staying in the ocean, blesses; and the Tamasa one swallows the subjects and overthrows them at the proper time. When god Brahmamanifests himself with the resurgence of Rajas guna,…
verses.commentary: Sense: One among them, the Rajasa body creates all the sub¬ jects; the Sattvika one staying in the ocean, blesses; and the Tamasa one swallows the subjects and overthrows them at the proper time. When god Brahmamanifests himself with the resurgence of Rajas guna,…

verses.sanskrit: स्नापनं चारभेत्तत्र मन्त्रशास्त्रविदुत्तमः । सहिरण्येन कुम्भेन पञ्चरत्नफलान्वितः
verses.transliteration: snāpanaṃ cārabhettatra mantraśāstraviduttamaḥ / sahiraṇyena kumbhena pañcaratnaphalānvitaḥ
verses.translation: The Self-born one, Kala, performs three activities through the three (bodies). It creates, supports and annihilates the subjects. Thus the three bodies of the self-born God which are called Prajapatya (belonging to Prajapati or god Brahma), Raudra (belonging to Rudra) and Vaisnava (belonging to Visnu) have been proclaimed. Only one body is remembered in the Vedas, Dharma Sastras and in the ancient (schools of) Sankhya and Yoga by the intelligent sages who could see (both) analytically and synthetically, were conversant with nobility of pedigree and prowess and could visualize the Reality. In the matter of unity and diversity people are of Some hold that Brahma is the cause (of the Universe); some say that it is Prajapati. Some say that Siva is the grea¬ test while others call Visnu supreme. Out of ignorance and with the mind vitiated by passion, attachment etc. they think like this. Considering the reality, time, place, cause and effects precisely, these deities are declared as working for diverse purposes. He who censures one among them censures them all. Pie who praises one, praises all of them. They call him Brahmavadin (propounder of Brahman) who undestands one Purusa. The attitude of non-censure must always be adopted towards the deities by one who knows (the Reality). It is im¬ possible to know Isvara established in all Ativarya (prosperity, power and glory). It is one supreme Soul. He becomes three and deludes the subjects. People seek difference among these three Beings, with diverse points of view, curiously testing their forms andsaying, "This is the greatest; this is not (so)", out of deluded mind. These deities permeate even Yatudhanas, Pisacas and human beings. The Self-born stays unified and separate deluding the subjects by means of the bodies solely consisting of the Gunas. He who worships one among them, worships all the three. These three deities remain non-different (factually). So where is separatness or unity? Where is their number? Whence do they come and go? Who is competent to know their unity or multiplicity? Since in view of their being united with the Gunas they create, sustain and devour the subjects in the three units of time, the supreme Being is said to be one.
verses.hindi: उत्तरायां च काष्ठायां प्रमाणं सण्डलस्य च्। योज॑नाग्रात्प्रसंख्याता कोटिरेका तु सा हिजेः अशीतिनियुतानीह योजनानां तथव च। अष्टपतचऑशतं चेव योजनान्यधिकानि तु १२६९
verses.wordMeaning: The Self-born one, Kala, performs three activities through the three (bodies). It creates, supports and annihilates the subjects. Thus the three bodies of the self-born God which are called Prajapatya (belonging to Prajapati or god Brahma),…
verses.commentary: Sense: The Self-born one, Kala, performs three activities through the three (bodies). It creates, supports and annihilates the subjects. Thus the three bodies of the self-born God which are called Prajapatya (belonging to Prajapati or god Brahma),…

verses.sanskrit: स्नापयेत् पुत्रकामायाः कांस्यपात्रेण देशिकः । पुत्रं सा लभते नारी वीर्यवन्तं गुणान्वितम्
verses.transliteration: snāpayet putrakāmāyāḥ kāṃsyapātreṇa deśikaḥ / putraṃ sā labhate nārī vīryavantaṃ guṇānvitam
verses.translation: Brahmanas call that one lord, Rudra, Brahma, Indra, guardians of the quarters, sages, Danus (Manus in Bd. P.) and Narayana, in diverse ways. The Prajapatya body (i.e. that of Brahma) and the Vaisnava body (i.e. that of Visnu) recur again and again in all the Manvantaras and Kalpas. In splendour, fame, intellect, learning and strength they are born equal to Him. Know them also. With the Rajasa part of Brahma, Marlci and Kasyapa were born. It is said that Rudra of the nature of Kala was born with theTamasa part. With the Sattvika part of Purusa Visnu was then born in the Yajna. The bodies born of parts of Brahma occur in all the three units of time. Becoming Kala, Rudra destroys the subjects again. When the end of the Kalpa approaches, the sun of seven rays becomes the Sariivartaka Sun (the sun at the time of world dissolution) and burns the three worlds. With changes in name and form, Visnu blesses i.e. sustains the subjects. In the different situations he is the cause of the origin of different things. With the Paurusa body of Bahma which had a predo¬ minance of Sattva guna, the god was born here in the first Svayambhuva Manvantara as the mental son of Akuti. 1 Thereafter, when the Svarocisa Manvantara arrived, he was born of Tusita along with the previous Tusita groups of Devas and passed away along with them. In the Auttama Manvantara also, he was known as Tusita. Born along with Vasavartis (i.e. Devas of that name), Hari was again known as Vasavartin. He was born of Satya, as-Satya, along with the excel¬ lent gods Satyas. When the Tamasa Manvantara arrived, Hari himself was bom of Harya along with the Haris. In the Carisnava Manvantara, Lord Hari was again born of Vaikuntha along with the Abhutarajasas. When the Caksusa Manvantara arrived that lord Vaikuntha was born as Narayana, Dharma and Sadhya along with the Sadhya group of gods. When the Vaivasvata Manvantara arrived, the lord Sadhya Narayana, was born of Aditi and Kasyapa, the son Verses 125-132 state different incarnations of Visnu in different Man¬ vantaras, and his achievement as Trivikrama. But the unity of Brahma, Vamana and the great Atman is emphasized. Thus the unity, separatness and the speciality of Brahma and Vamana, the great Atman have been glorified.
verses.hindi: काष्ठयोरन्तरं यच्च तद्॒क्ष्ये योजने: पुनः । एतच्छतसहस्नाणामेकत्रिशोत्तरं शतम् १३१ श्रयस्त्रिशाधिकाश्चान्ये त्रयस्त्रिशच्च योजने: । काष्ठयोरन्तरं हतद्योजनाग्रा्नतिष्ठितमू

verses.sanskrit: यो यं काममभिध्यायेत्ततः स लभते नृप । मातृतीर्थात्परं तीर्थं न भूतं न भविष्यति
verses.transliteration: yo yaṃ kāmamabhidhyāyettataḥ sa labhate nṛpa / mātṛtīrthātparaṃ tīrthaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati
verses.translation: Some men say that the lord alone is born partially. Others say that the deities are born of one anothers' part. Isvara, though one, becomes manifold, due to the power of his lordship. For the same reason after becoming mani¬ fold he becomes one again. From that (Lord) of good intentions and the diversity of brilliance are born the subjects consisting of mobile and the immobile beings in all the Manvantaras. When they are created once at the beginning of Sarga, they continue to live res¬ pectably (?) Whenever any Kalpa comes to a close Rudra annihi¬ lates the subjects. Isvaras are born by means of Yogic Maya deluding others. They are moving about due to their Aisvarya and the non-lsvaras (those devoid of Aisvarya) are deluded. Hence there is nothing proper or improper in things where faults spread. Those who spread scandal about living beings are wicked; those who are favourable to living beings are middling; those who slight and disregard living beings are competent. There are three Vedas for those who are eloquent. (A line is missing from the the Text.) Because it is heard firmly, because it is heard before, bacause it is a rumour and because it is worldly, for these four reasons one does not get at the precise truth. Formerly they meant and were used in another sense, and even after the lapse of time one does not accept the new sense out of spite. He who is a solid among solids, he who becomes the attribute therein, he who is the creator of activities and minds and he who is great due to pedigree, are glorified by those who know the tradition, for these four reasons. The incompetent and the infuriated know the deities only partially. They state these two verses in tins connection in regard to Yogesvara (Lord of Yogas). The Yogesvara makes replicas of himself and others in thousands by means of Yogic power. He moves about among them. He attains the (pleasures of) sensuous objects performing severe penance. Like the Sun withdrawing his brilliance and attributes (of heat etc.) he annihilates them all again.
verses.hindi: काष्ठयोलेंसयोश्चेंब अन्तरे दक्षिणोत्तरे  ते तु वक्ष्यामि संख्यांय योजनेस्तन्लिबोधत लेखयो: काष्ठयोश्चेव बाह्याभ्यन्तरयो: स्मृतम् । अभ्यन्तरं तु पर्यंति मण्डलान्युत्तरायण..

verses.sanskrit: ॥ इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे मातृतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम षट्षष्टितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ र्क्व् अध्याय ६७ श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: तस्यैवानन्तरं तात जलमध्ये व्यवस्थितम् । लुङ्केश्वरम् इति ख्यातं सुरासुरनमस्कृतम्
verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe mātṛtīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṭṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 67 śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: tasyaivānantaraṃ tāta jalamadhye vyavasthitam / luṅkeśvaram iti khyātaṃ surāsuranamaskṛtam
verses.translation: On hearing his words, the sages and ascetics of the Naimisa forest asked the most excellent one (i.e. Suta) in due course.
verses.hindi: योजन चला करते हैं। क्षीरोद समुद्र के उत्तर उदित होकर चलते हुये सूये जब दक्षिण दिल्ला से लौटकर विषुव रेखा पर स्थित होते हैं, उस काल में विषुब मण्डल के योजन-प्रमाण को धुनिये ।(२२-१२५२। इस विषुव का विस्तार तीन करोड़ एकासी लाख योजन है। छठ शाकद्वीप के उत्तर उदित होकर विचरण करते समय जब सूर्य श्रावण मास में उत्तर दिशा में चले जाते हैं, तब उत्तरीय दिशा के मण्डल-प्रमाण को
verses.wordMeaning: On hearing his words, the sages and ascetics of the Naimisa forest asked the most excellent one (i.e. Suta) in due course.
verses.commentary: Sense: On hearing his words, the sages and ascetics of the Naimisa forest asked the most excellent one (i.e. Suta) in due course.

verses.sanskrit: इदं तीर्थं महापुण्यं नानाश्चर्यं महीतले । अस्य तीर्थस्य माहात्म्यम् उत्पत्तिं शृणु भारत
verses.transliteration: idaṃ tīrthaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ nānāścaryaṃ mahītale / asya tīrthasya māhātmyam utpattiṃ śṛṇu bhārata
verses.translation: How were the Devas, the extremely powerful Adityas, the chief of whom were Indra and Visnu, born in the seven
verses.hindi: विद्वानों ने एक करोड़, अस्सी नियुत अठावन योजन बताया है। सूर्यके गमनमार्ग के दो नाम हैं नागवीथों और अजवीधी । उत्तरवाली नागवीबी है और दक्षिणवाली अजवीथी  मूल, पूर्वाषाढ और उत्तराषाढ़ नामक तीनों नक्षत्रों में जब सूर्य उदित होते हैं, तब उसका नाम अजबीथी होता है एवं अभिजित से लेकर तीन नक्षत्रों में जब उदय होता है, तब उसका नाम नागवीथी रहता है।१२६-१३०। इन दोनों दिशज्ञाओं में जो अन्तर है उसे हम योजनों में बताते हैं। यह दोनों दिशाओं का अन्तर एकतीस लाख तेंतीस सौ तैंतीस योजन का है, किस्तु इसकी संख्या एक योजन ऊपर से की गयी है । दक्षिण और उत्तर दिशाओं के रेखामध्यगत अम्तर की संख्या भी हम योजनों में बताते हैं, सुनिये ।!३१-१३३॥ इन दोगों रेखाओं में एक से दूसरे का अन्तर एकहृत्तर नियुत एक हजार पचहुत्तर योजन है। दोनों दिशाओं की बाहरी और
verses.wordMeaning: How were the Devas, the extremely powerful Adityas, the chief of whom were Indra and Visnu, born in the seven

verses.sanskrit: आसीत्पुरा महावीर्यो दानवो बलदर्पितः । कालपृष्ठ इति ख्यातः सुतो ब्रह्मसुतस्य च
verses.transliteration: āsītpurā mahāvīryo dānavo baladarpitaḥ / kālapṛṣṭha iti khyātaḥ suto brahmasutasya ca
verses.translation: On being urged and requested by the expounders of the Brahman (Vedas) the modest Suta, the most excellent among eloquent ones spoke in accordance with the query of the great sages.
verses.hindi: भीतरी रेखाओं का परिमाण एक सा ही कहा गया है सूं जब उत्तर की ओर रहते हैं, तब वे भीतरी
verses.wordMeaning: On being urged and requested by the expounders of the Brahman (Vedas) the modest Suta, the most excellent among eloquent ones spoke in accordance with the query of the great sages.
verses.commentary: Sense: On being urged and requested by the expounders of the Brahman (Vedas) the modest Suta, the most excellent among eloquent ones spoke in accordance with the query of the great sages.

verses.sanskrit: गङ्गातटं समाश्रित्य चचार विपुलं तपः । अधोमुखो ऽपि संस्थित्वापिबद्धूमम् अहर्निशम्
verses.transliteration: gaṅgātaṭaṃ samāśritya cacāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ / adhomukho 'pi saṃsthitvāpibaddhūmam aharniśam
verses.translation: All the Devas created from the mouth of Brahma with a desire for progeny in the Manvantaras had their bodies constituted of Mantras.
verses.hindi: चरते दक्षिण चापि तावदेव विभावसु:  प्रमाणं मण्डलस्याथ योजनाग्रान्निबोधत एकॉविशद्योजनानां सहल्लाणि समासत:ः । शते हूं पुनरप्यन्ये योजनानां प्रकोतिते
verses.wordMeaning: All the Devas created from the mouth of Brahma with a desire for progeny in the Manvantaras had their bodies constituted of Mantras.
verses.commentary: Sense: All the Devas created from the mouth of Brahma with a desire for progeny in the Manvantaras had their bodies constituted of Mantras.

verses.sanskrit: ततश्चानन्तरं देवस्तिष्ठते ह्युमया सह । दृष्ट्वा तं पार्वती सा तु तपस्युग्रे व्यवस्थितम्
verses.transliteration: tataścānantaraṃ devastiṣṭhate hyumayā saha / dṛṣṭvā taṃ pārvatī sā tu tapasyugre vyavasthitam
verses.translation: But they did not act in accordance with the instruc¬ tion of Paramesthin (Brahma). They found out defects even in those who abide by the mental, verbal and physical activities of a truthful nature; they saw the fruits of actions excessively reduced; they hated progeny and procreation. They were alei t but free from the sense of my-ness (possession); they aspired for permanence; they were detached (from worldly objects); they saw defects (in worldly activities); they abandon¬ ed wealth, love and virtue; they adhered to knowledge pertaining to the supreme being and remained with their splendour withdrawn.
verses.hindi: विष्कम्भो मण्डलस्थेव तिर्यंक्स तु विधीयते । प्रत्यहुं चरते तानि सूर्यो वे सण्डलक्रमम्
verses.wordMeaning: But they did not act in accordance with the instruc¬ tion of Paramesthin (Brahma). They found out defects even in those who abide by the mental, verbal and physical activities of a truthful nature; they saw the fruits of actions excessively reduced;…
verses.commentary: Sense: But they did not act in accordance with the instruc¬ tion of Paramesthin (Brahma). They found out defects even in those who abide by the mental, verbal and physical activities of a truthful nature; they saw the fruits of actions excessively reduced;…

verses.sanskrit: पश्य पश्य महादेव धूमाशी तिष्ठते नरः । प्रसीद तं कुरुष्वाद्य देहि शीघ्रं वरं विभो
verses.transliteration: paśya paśya mahādeva dhūmāśī tiṣṭhate naraḥ / prasīda taṃ kuruṣvādya dehi śīghraṃ varaṃ vibho
verses.translation: On realising the trend of their thought, Brahma became angry. Brahma spoke to those gods in despair.
verses.hindi: कुलालचक्पयेन्तो यथा शीघ्र निवतंते । दक्षिणे प्रक्ृसे सुयेस्तथा शीघ्र निवतंते तस्मात्प्रकृष्टां भूमि च कालेनाल्‍पेन गच्छति । सूर्यो द्वादशभिः शीघ्र मुह॒र्तेदेक्षिणोत्तरे
verses.wordMeaning: On realising the trend of their thought, Brahma became angry. Brahma spoke to those gods in despair.
verses.commentary: Sense: On realising the trend of their thought, Brahma became angry. Brahma spoke to those gods in despair.

verses.sanskrit: ईश्वर उवाच: यदुक्तं वचनं देवि न तन्मे रोचते प्रिये । स्वकार्यं च सदा चिन्त्यं परकार्यं विसर्जयेत्
verses.transliteration: īśvara uvāca: yaduktaṃ vacanaṃ devi na tanme rocate priye / svakāryaṃ ca sadā cintyaṃ parakāryaṃ visarjayet
verses.translation: "You have been created by me for the sake of further procieation and not otherwise. X have already told you to pro¬ create and be victorious.
verses.hindi: त्रयोदशार्धमर्घेन ऋक्षाणां चरते रविः ॥ तस्माद्दीघेंण कालेन भुमिमल्‍पां निगच्छति (३१४४५ अष्टादशमुहततेंस्तु उत्तरापणपश्चिमम् । अहरभेंवति तच्चापि चरते मन्दविक्वम:ः
verses.wordMeaning: "You have been created by me for the sake of further procieation and not otherwise. X have already told you to pro¬ create and be victorious.
verses.commentary: Sense: "You have been created by me for the sake of further procieation and not otherwise. X have already told you to pro¬ create and be victorious.

verses.sanskrit: मूर्खस्त्रीबालशत्रूणां यश्छन्देनानुवर्तते । व्यसने पतते घोरे सत्यमेतदुदीरितम्
verses.transliteration: mūrkhastrībālaśatrūṇāṃ yaśchandenānuvartate / vyasane patate ghore satyametadudīritam
verses.translation: You have disregarded my words andh ave adhered to detachment. You hate your own birth. Hence you do not
verses.hindi: मण्डल में परिभ्रमण करते हैं ओर जब दक्षिण में रहते हैं तब बाहरी मण्डल की परिक्रमा करते हैं। इसी क्रम से वे सदा एक सौ अस्सी मण्डलों के भीतर-बाहर घूमा करते हैं । दक्षिण दिश्या में भी सूर्य इसी प्रकार चला करते हैं। यहाँ के मण्डल का परिमाण भी संलेप से योजनों में सुनिये ।(३४-१३७।. इस मण्डल का प्रमाण इक्कीस ' हजार दो सो इककीस योजन कहा गया है । मण्डल का विष्कम्भ या विस्तार बक्र है। सूर्य प्रति दिन मण्डलक्रम से अथात् एक के बाद दूसरे पर विचरण किया करते हैं।१३५-१४०। कुम्हार का चकक्‍का ज॑से शीघत्ष घूम आता है, उसी प्रकार सूर्य भी दक्षिण दिल्ला में जाकर ज्ञीघत्र लौट आते हैं। सूब॑ थोड़े हो काल में आर्थात् बारह घड़ियों में ही दक्षिण दिशा की उत्तमोत्तम भूमि में विचर आते हैं। दिन में सूय॑ साढ़े तेरह नक्षत्रों का परिभ्रमण कर लेते हैं और रात में बे अठारह मुह॒तों में फिर उतने ही
verses.wordMeaning: You have disregarded my words andh ave adhered to detachment. You hate your own birth. Hence you do not
verses.commentary: Sense: You have disregarded my words andh ave adhered to detachment. You hate your own birth. Hence you do not

verses.sanskrit: देव्युवाच: भार्ययाभ्यर्थितो भर्ता कारणं बहु भाषते । लघुत्वं याति सा नारी एवं शास्त्रेषु पठ्यते
verses.transliteration: devyuvāca: bhāryayābhyarthito bhartā kāraṇaṃ bahu bhāṣate / laghutvaṃ yāti sā nārī evaṃ śāstreṣu paṭhyate
verses.translation: When they bowed to him and implored, Brahma said to them again: "Who deserves (i.e. is capable) to be indepen¬ dent' in this world without being permitted by me.
verses.hindi: नक्षत्रों का परिभ्रमण करते हूँ कुम्हार के चक्‍के के बीच का हिस्सा जिस प्रकार धीरे-धीरे घृमता है, उसी प्रकार उत्तरायण होने पर सूर्य का भी पराक्रम मन्‍्द हो जाता है. और वे धीरे-धीरे चलने लगते हैं । इस समय सूर्य अधिक देर में थोड़ी सी ही दूरी तय कर पाते हैं ।!४१-१४६। उत्तरायण काल में पश्चिम दिद्या में मन्द पराक्रम वाले सूय॑ अठारह मुहतों में चोदह नक्षत्रों का परिशक्रमण दिन में करते हैं। फिर रात में
verses.wordMeaning: When they bowed to him and implored, Brahma said to them again: "Who deserves (i.e. is capable) to be indepen¬ dent' in this world without being permitted by me.
verses.commentary: Sense: When they bowed to him and implored, Brahma said to them again: "Who deserves (i.e. is capable) to be indepen¬ dent' in this world without being permitted by me.

verses.sanskrit: प्राणत्यागं करिष्यामि यदि मां त्वं न मन्यसे । पार्वत्या प्रेरितो देवो गतो ऽसौ दानवं प्रति
verses.transliteration: prāṇatyāgaṃ kariṣyāmi yadi māṃ tvaṃ na manyase / pārvatyā prerito devo gato 'sau dānavaṃ prati
verses.translation: Everything is pervaded by me. As against my will how will living beings attain anything auspicious or inauspicious.
verses.hindi: त्रिशन्मुहतनिवा55हरहोरात्र श्रुवो श्रमन् । उभयो: काष्ठयोमंध्ये क्रमते सण्डलानि सः १४६ उभयोः काष्ठयोमंध्ये भ्रमतो मण्डलानि तु । दिवा नकत॑ च सूर्यस्य सन्‍दा शीक्रा च वे गतिः
verses.wordMeaning: Everything is pervaded by me. As against my will how will living beings attain anything auspicious or inauspicious.
verses.commentary: Sense: Everything is pervaded by me. As against my will how will living beings attain anything auspicious or inauspicious.

verses.sanskrit: ईश्वर उवाच: किमर्थं पिबसे धूमं किमर्थं तप्यसे तपः । किं दुःखं किं नु सन्तापो वद कार्यमभीप्सितम्
verses.transliteration: īśvara uvāca: kimarthaṃ pibase dhūmaṃ kimarthaṃ tapyase tapaḥ / kiṃ duḥkhaṃ kiṃ nu santāpo vada kāryamabhīpsitam
verses.translation: Whatever exists in the lvorld or is endowed with Sattva (existence) or Asattva (non-existence) has been pei- vaded by me with intellect and soul. Who in the world dare to deceive me?
verses.hindi: दक्षिणे प्रकरमे चेव दिवा शीघ्र' विधोयते । गतिः सूर्यस्य नकतं वे मनन्‍्दा चापि तथा स्मुता.
verses.wordMeaning: Whatever exists in the lvorld or is endowed with Sattva (existence) or Asattva (non-existence) has been pei- vaded by me with intellect and soul. Who in the world dare to deceive me?
verses.commentary: Sense: Whatever exists in the lvorld or is endowed with Sattva (existence) or Asattva (non-existence) has been pei- vaded by me with intellect and soul. Who in the world dare to deceive me?

verses.sanskrit: युवा त्वं दृश्यसे ऽद्यापि वर्षविंशतिर् एव च । तदाचक्ष्व हि मे सर्वं तपसः कारणं महत्
verses.transliteration: yuvā tvaṃ dṛśyase 'dyāpi varṣaviṃśatir eva ca / tadācakṣva hi me sarvaṃ tapasaḥ kāraṇaṃ mahat
verses.translation: Whatever has been conjectured, decided or considered by the living beings is entirely known to me.
verses.hindi: एवं गतिविशेषेण विभजनराज्यहानि तु। तथा विचरते भार्ग समेन विषमेण चर. लोकालोके स्थिता ये ते लोकपालाश्रतुदिशम् । अगस्त्यश्ररते तेषासुपरिष्टाज्जवेन तु ॥। भजन्नसावहोरात्रमेव॑ गतिविशेषणेः
verses.wordMeaning: Whatever has been conjectured, decided or considered by the living beings is entirely known to me.
verses.commentary: Sense: Whatever has been conjectured, decided or considered by the living beings is entirely known to me.

verses.sanskrit: दानव उवाच: अचला दीयतां भक्तिर्मम स्थैर्यं तवोपरि । अपरं वर्षसाहस्रं निर्विघ्नं मे गतं विभो
verses.transliteration: dānava uvāca: acalā dīyatāṃ bhaktirmama sthairyaṃ tavopari / aparaṃ varṣasāhasraṃ nirvighnaṃ me gataṃ vibho
verses.translation: The entire Universe consisting of the mobile and the
verses.hindi: दक्षिणे नागवीथ्यायां लोकालोकस्य चोत्तरभ् । लोकसंतारकों हांष वेश्वानरपथादबहिः:
verses.wordMeaning: The entire Universe consisting of the mobile and the
verses.commentary: Sense: The entire Universe consisting of the mobile and the

verses.sanskrit: दिवसानां सहस्रे द्वे पूर्णे त्वत्तपसा मम
verses.transliteration: divasānāṃ sahasre dve pūrṇe tvattapasā mama
verses.translation: Since I have transformed myself for the sake of creation and not for any other purpose, who will be free
verses.hindi: पृष्ठे यावत्प्रभा सौरी पुरस्तात्संप्रकाशते । पाश्वयो: प्ृष्ठतस्तावललोकालोकस्य सर्वतः भी वे उतने ही नक्षत्रों का परिभ्रमण अठारह मुहरतों में ही करते हैं। फिर चक्र की गति धीमी पड़ जाने से जसे उसके बीच का मृत्पिण्ड घूमता रहता है उसी प्रकार दोनों दिशाओं के मध्य में अवस्थित ध्रूव भी उस समय घूमा करता है। ध्रूव तीस मुह॒तों में एक अहोरात्र का परिम्रमण कर दोनों दिशाओं के मध्य में स्थित मण्डलों की परिक्रमा करता है । कुम्हार के चक्‍के का नाभि-देश ज॑से जहाँ का तहाँ पड़ा रहता है,
verses.wordMeaning: Since I have transformed myself for the sake of creation and not for any other purpose, who will be free
verses.commentary: Sense: Since I have transformed myself for the sake of creation and not for any other purpose, who will be free

verses.sanskrit: ईश्वर उवाच: याचयाभीप्सितं कार्यं तुष्टो ऽहं तव सुव्रत । देवस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा चिन्तयामास दानवः
verses.transliteration: īśvara uvāca: yācayābhīpsitaṃ kāryaṃ tuṣṭo 'haṃ tava suvrata / devasya vacanaṃ śrutvā cintayāmāsa dānavaḥ
verses.translation: After saying this to the group ofjaya Devas who ac¬ cepted his punishment and who were dejected, Prajapati spoke again to them (in consolation).
