verses.hindi: पुष्करा नाम ते मेघा बृहन्तस्तोयमत्सराः । पुष्करावतंकास्तेन कारणेनेह शब्द्रिता:... ३६ नानारूपधराश्चेव महाघोरतराश्च ते । कल्पान्तवुष्ठेः स्रष्टारः संवर्ताग्नेनियासका:
verses.wordMeaning: May my sons have seven abodes in heaven. Let my seven sons roam about these wind-regions (Vataskandhas) ( at i- ways of wind). May they be renowned as the seven Maruts, the
verses.commentary: Sense: May my sons have seven abodes in heaven. Let my seven sons roam about these wind-regions (Vataskandhas) ( at i- ways of wind). May they be renowned as the seven Maruts, the

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणी क्षत्रिणी वैशी शूद्री यावत् तथैव च । द्वितीयो न भवेद् भर्ता एकाकी चेह जन्मनि
verses.transliteration: brāhmaṇī kṣatriṇī vaiśī śūdrī yāvat tathaiva ca / dvitīyo na bhaved bhartā ekākī ceha janmani
verses.translation: May the first Skandha (region) be on the Earth, the second in the Sun, the third in the Moon, audthe fourth should be known in the groups of luminaries.
verses.hindi: वर्षन्त्येते युगान्तेषु तृतीयास्ते प्रकोतिताः । अनेकरूपसंस्थानाः पुरयन्तो महीतलम् ॥॥ बाय॑ पर वहन्तः स्युराशिताः कल्पसाधकाः ॥४ १
verses.wordMeaning: May the first Skandha (region) be on the Earth, the second in the Sun, the third in the Moon, audthe fourth should be known in the groups of luminaries.
verses.commentary: Sense: May the first Skandha (region) be on the Earth, the second in the Sun, the third in the Moon, audthe fourth should be known in the groups of luminaries.

verses.sanskrit: दानव उवाच: यत्त्वया गदितं वाक्यं तन्मया धारितं हृदि । प्रत्ययं मे कुरुष्वाद्य यत्ते मनसि रोचते
verses.transliteration: dānava uvāca: yattvayā gaditaṃ vākyaṃ tanmayā dhāritaṃ hṛdi / pratyayaṃ me kuruṣvādya yatte manasi rocate
verses.translation: May the fifth Skandha be among the planets, the sixth in the sphere of the Seven Sages and the seventh m Dhruva. That is the last region of the wind.
verses.hindi: तान्येवाण्डकपालस्य सर्वे सेघाः प्रकीतिता
verses.wordMeaning: May the fifth Skandha be among the planets, the sixth in the sphere of the Seven Sages and the seventh m Dhruva. That is the last region of the wind.
verses.commentary: Sense: May the fifth Skandha be among the planets, the sixth in the sphere of the Seven Sages and the seventh m Dhruva. That is the last region of the wind.

verses.sanskrit: कन्योवाच: जानीष्व गोपकन्यां मां क्रीडामि सखिभिः सह । अस्मत्कुलेषु यद्दिव्यं तत्कुरुष्व यथाविधि
verses.transliteration: kanyovāca: jānīṣva gopakanyāṃ māṃ krīḍāmi sakhibhiḥ saha / asmatkuleṣu yaddivyaṃ tatkuruṣva yathāvidhi
verses.translation: May my sons roam about among them on different
verses.hindi: गजानां पव॑तानां च मेघानां भोगिभिः सह । कुलमेक॑ पृथरभुतं योनिरेका जल॑ स्पृ तम् ३४४ श्रेष्ठ: परिवहो नाम तेषां वायुरपाश्रय: । योइसो बिभति भगवान्गड्रामसाकाशगोचराम् ॥ दिव्याम्ृतजलां पुण्यां त्रिधा स्वर्गंपथे स्थिताम्
verses.wordMeaning: May my sons roam about among them on different
verses.commentary: Sense: May my sons roam about among them on different

verses.sanskrit: न तद्दिव्यं कुले ऽस्माकं विषं कोशं न तत्तुला । गोपान्वयेषु सर्वेषु हस्तः शिरसि दीयते
verses.transliteration: na taddivyaṃ kule 'smākaṃ viṣaṃ kośaṃ na tattulā / gopānvayeṣu sarveṣu hastaḥ śirasi dīyate
verses.translation: The second Valaskandha extends from the clouds upto the Sun. It is called Pravaha. Let the second set (of my sons) walk in the second Vataskandha.
verses.hindi: तस्याविष्यन्दर्ज तोय॑ं दिग्गजाः पृथुभिः करें: । शीकर संप्रमुच्चति नोहार इति स स्पृतः
verses.wordMeaning: The second Valaskandha extends from the clouds upto the Sun. It is called Pravaha. Let the second set (of my sons) walk in the second Vataskandha.
verses.commentary: Sense: The second Valaskandha extends from the clouds upto the Sun. It is called Pravaha. Let the second set (of my sons) walk in the second Vataskandha.

verses.sanskrit: कामान्धेनैव राजेन्द्र निक्षिप्तो मस्तके करः । तत्क्षणाद् भस्मसाद्भूतो दग्धस् तृणचयो यथा
verses.transliteration: kāmāndhenaiva rājendra nikṣipto mastake karaḥ / tatkṣaṇād bhasmasādbhūto dagdhas tṛṇacayo yathā
verses.translation: Above the solar region and extending upto the Moon is the Vataskandha remembered as Udvaha. May the third set (of my sons) walk through the Valaskandha.
verses.hindi: बाले पर्व॑तों का पक्ष काट दिया था ॥३६-३८। वे ही विशाल पक्ष जलपूर्ण होकर मेघाकार हो गये । उच्त मेघों का नाम हुआ पुष्कर । इसी कारण वे पुष्करावतंक नाम से प्रसिद्ध हैं। ये मेघ नाना रूप को धारण करने वाले, महाभयद्धुर, कल्पान्त में वृष्टि करने वाले और संवर्तक अग्नि के नियामक हैं ३६-४०। ये तृतीय श्रेणी के मेघ कल्पान्त में वृष्टि करते हैं और विविध रूप धारण कर महीमण्डल को पूर्ण कर देते हैं एवं परावह वायु का आअय लेकर कलपों को बदल दिया करते हैं। चार मुंहवाले' स्वयम्भू ब्रह्म, जिस प्राकृत अण्डकपाल से उत्पन्न हुये हैं, उसी अण्डपाल से सभी मेघ हुये हैं ॥४१-४२। सभी मेघों को धुम आप्याधित यानी तृप्त करते हैं। उन सभी मेघों में पजंन्‍्य श्रेष्ठ हैं और दिग्गज चतुष्टय । गज, पर्वत, सेघ और साँपों का कुल प्रथक होने पर भी एक ही है; क्योंकि इन सब का उत्पत्ति-स्थान जल ही कहा गया है ।४२-४४। हैमन्त काल में सम्पूर्ण सस्यों की बृद्धि
verses.wordMeaning: Above the solar region and extending upto the Moon is the Vataskandha remembered as Udvaha. May the third set (of my sons) walk through the Valaskandha.
verses.commentary: Sense: Above the solar region and extending upto the Moon is the Vataskandha remembered as Udvaha. May the third set (of my sons) walk through the Valaskandha.

verses.sanskrit: केशवोपरि देवैस्तु पुष्पवृष्टिः शुभा कृता । हृष्टाः सर्वे ऽगमन्देवाः स्वस्थानं विगतज्वराः
verses.transliteration: keśavopari devaistu puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ śubhā kṛtā / hṛṣṭāḥ sarve 'gamandevāḥ svasthānaṃ vigatajvarāḥ
verses.translation: Above the lunar region and extending upto the stars is the fourth Vataskandha which is called Suvaha. O lord, may the fourth set of my sons walk therein.
verses.hindi: करने के लिये शीत सम्भव दिग्गज और पर्जन्य तुषार वृष्टि किया करते हं। श्रेष्ठ परिवह वायु इन सबका आश्रय-स्थान है। यही भगवान् परिवह वायु स्वगंपथ में तीन धाराओं में बहने वाली, दिव्य, पवित्र और अमृत की तरह जल वाली आकाश-गड़ा को धारण करने वाले हैं। आकाश-गड्भा के जल को दिग्गजगण अपनी मोटी सूंड्ों से फुहारे की तरह उछालते हैं। बही जलकण नौहार कहलाता है ।४१५-४७। सुमेरु के दक्षिण और
verses.wordMeaning: Above the lunar region and extending upto the stars is the fourth Vataskandha which is called Suvaha. O lord, may the fourth set of my sons walk therein.
verses.commentary: Sense: Above the lunar region and extending upto the stars is the fourth Vataskandha which is called Suvaha. O lord, may the fourth set of my sons walk therein.

verses.sanskrit: क्षीरोदं केशवो गच्छत्कालपृष्ठे निपातिते । य इदं शृणुयाद्भक्त्या चरितं दानवस्य च
verses.transliteration: kṣīrodaṃ keśavo gacchatkālapṛṣṭhe nipātite / ya idaṃ śṛṇuyādbhaktyā caritaṃ dānavasya ca
verses.translation: This psuedo-scientific classification of higher space into seven strata
verses.hindi: हिमालय के उत्तर हेमकूट नामक एक परत है। इसके निकट पुण्ड़ू नामक एक प्रसिद्ध नगर है।४८। वहाँ तुषार- तस्मिन्निपतितं वर्ष यत्तुषारसमुझूब । ततस्तदावहो वायुहिसशलात्समुद्दहन् ॥।
verses.wordMeaning: This psuedo-scientific classification of higher space into seven strata
verses.commentary: Sense: This psuedo-scientific classification of higher space into seven strata

verses.sanskrit: स जयी जायते नित्यं शङ्करस्य वचो यथा । एतस्मात् कारणाद् राजंल् लिङ्गेश्वरमिति श्रुतम्
verses.transliteration: sa jayī jāyate nityaṃ śaṅkarasya vaco yathā / etasmāt kāraṇād rājaṃl liṅgeśvaramiti śrutam
verses.translation: Above the planets and extending up to the Seven Sages (Great Bear) is the sixth Skandha which is called Parahala (Anu-
verses.hindi: मेघावा(उचा55)प्यायनं चेव स्वमेतत्प्रकीतितम् । सूर्य एवं तु वष्टीनां ख्रष्ठा समुपदिश्यते
verses.wordMeaning: Above the planets and extending up to the Seven Sages (Great Bear) is the sixth Skandha which is called Parahala (Anu-
verses.commentary: Sense: Above the planets and extending up to the Seven Sages (Great Bear) is the sixth Skandha which is called Parahala (Anu-

verses.sanskrit: लीनं च पातकं यस्मात् स्नानमात्रेण नश्यति । त्वगस्थि शोणितं मांसं मेदःस्नायुस्तथैव च
verses.transliteration: līnaṃ ca pātakaṃ yasmāt snānamātreṇa naśyati / tvagasthi śoṇitaṃ māṃsaṃ medaḥsnāyustathaiva ca
verses.translation: Above the Seven Sages and extending up to Dhruva (Pole Star) is the seventh Vataskandha which is called Parivaha- Maymy sons stay therein.
verses.hindi: श्रुवेषा55वेष्टितां सुर्येस्ताभ्यां वृष्टिः प्रवरतते । ध्रुवेणा5४वेष्टितों वायुव् ५िट संहरते पुनः ५२ हिरण्मयेन भगवान्परवंणा तु महौजसा। नष्टवर्त्माइन्धकारेण षट्प्रकारेकनेमिना॥ द चक्रेण भास्वता सूर्यः स्यन्दनेन प्रसपेति
verses.wordMeaning: Above the Seven Sages and extending up to Dhruva (Pole Star) is the seventh Vataskandha which is called Parivaha- Maymy sons stay therein.
verses.commentary: Sense: Above the Seven Sages and extending up to Dhruva (Pole Star) is the seventh Vataskandha which is called Parivaha- Maymy sons stay therein.

verses.sanskrit: मज्जाशुक्रगतं पापं नश्यते जन्मकोटिजम् । लुङ्केश्वरे महाराज तोयं पिबति भक्तितः
verses.transliteration: majjāśukragataṃ pāpaṃ naśyate janmakoṭijam / luṅkeśvare mahārāja toyaṃ pibati bhaktitaḥ
verses.translation: May my sons move about all these on different occa¬ sions. There let these be known by the name Maruts."
verses.hindi: स् तस्य ब्रह्मणा सृष्टो रथो हार्थवशेन तु । असज्भः काचचनो दिव्यो युक्तः परमगहँयः .. ३५७
verses.wordMeaning: May my sons move about all these on different occa¬ sions. There let these be known by the name Maruts."
verses.commentary: Sense: May my sons move about all these on different occa¬ sions. There let these be known by the name Maruts."

verses.sanskrit: त्रिभिः प्रसृतिमात्राभिः पापं याति सहस्रधा । विशेषेण चतुर्दश्यामुभौ पक्षौ तु चाष्टमी
verses.transliteration: tribhiḥ prasṛtimātrābhiḥ pāpaṃ yāti sahasradhā / viśeṣeṇa caturdaśyāmubhau pakṣau tu cāṣṭamī
verses.translation: Then the mother and the son named them Maruts through the actions performed by them. They separately named the seven Maruts of each set.
verses.hindi: तेनासो सपंति व्योस्नि भास्वता तु दिवाकरः ४८ की ही वृष्टि हुआ करती है। तब फिर आवह नामक वायु उस तुषार को अपने सामथ्यं से बटोर कर उस महाशल से महागिरि हिमालय पर बरसा देते हैं। यह वृष्टि हिमालय तक ही समाप्त हो जाती है। इसके बाद अन्य देशों में वैसी वष्टि नहीं होती; किन्तु जो कुछ भी होती है, उसी से सस्य-वृद्धि होती है ४९-५०। मेघ और उनका वद्धि-वृत्तान्त इस प्रकार कहा गया; किन्तु वास्तव में वृष्टि करने वाले सूर्य ही बताये गये हैँ । सूर्य
verses.wordMeaning: Then the mother and the son named them Maruts through the actions performed by them. They separately named the seven Maruts of each set.
verses.commentary: Sense: Then the mother and the son named them Maruts through the actions performed by them. They separately named the seven Maruts of each set.

verses.sanskrit: उपोष्य यो नरो भक्त्या पित्ःणां पाण्डुनन्दन । उद्धृतास्तेन ते सर्वे नारकीयाः पितामहाः
verses.transliteration: upoṣya yo naro bhaktyā pitḥṇāṃ pāṇḍunandana / uddhṛtāstena te sarve nārakīyāḥ pitāmahāḥ
verses.translation: The following constitute the other sets: Krta, Satva, Dhruva, Dharta, Vidharta, Vidharaya, Dhvanta, Dhuni, Ugra, Bhlma, Abhiyu, Saksipa. This is known as Ahvayagana*, Idpk, Anyadrk, Yadrk, Pratikrt, Samiti, Samrambha, Idrk, Purusa, Anyadrk sa, Cetasa, Samita, Asamitadrksa, Pratidrksa and others.
verses.hindi: के द्वारा वृष्टि होती है ओर वायु के द्वारा बृष्टि रोकी जाती है; इसलिये प्रूव से अवेष्टित सूर्य और वायु ही वृष्टि करने वाले और थृष्टि को रोकने वाले हैँ ।११-५२। वायु सूर्य ग्रह से निकल कर सम्पूर्ण नक्षत्र मण्डल का परिभ्रमण कर दिन के अन्त में पुनः प्रूव द्वारा परिवेष्टित सूर्य में ही प्रवेश कर जाता है। अब सूर्य के रथ का संनिवेश सुनिये । इस रथ में एक चकका, पाँच अरायें और तीन नाभियाँ हैँ । अन्धकार से आच्छन्न पथ
verses.wordMeaning: The following constitute the other sets: Krta, Satva, Dhruva, Dharta, Vidharta, Vidharaya, Dhvanta, Dhuni, Ugra, Bhlma, Abhiyu, Saksipa. This is known as Ahvayagana*, Idpk, Anyadrk, Yadrk, Pratikrt, Samiti, Samrambha, Idrk, Purusa, Anyadrk sa, Cetasa, Samita, Asamitadrksa,…
verses.commentary: Sense: The following constitute the other sets: Krta, Satva, Dhruva, Dharta, Vidharta, Vidharaya, Dhvanta, Dhuni, Ugra, Bhlma, Abhiyu, Saksipa. This is known as Ahvayagana*, Idpk, Anyadrk, Yadrk, Pratikrt, Samiti, Samrambha, Idrk, Purusa, Anyadrk sa, Cetasa, Samita, Asamitadrksa,…

verses.sanskrit: काकिणीं चैव यो दद्याद् ब्राह्मणे वेदपारगे । तेन दानफलं सर्वं कुरुक्षेत्रादिकं च यत्
verses.transliteration: kākiṇīṃ caiva yo dadyād brāhmaṇe vedapārage / tena dānaphalaṃ sarvaṃ kurukṣetrādikaṃ ca yat
verses.translation: These forty-nine are the different Maruts with their own separate names. They have been enumerated by Diti and Indra.
verses.hindi: पर इस हिरण्मय अत्यन्त भास्वर, महावेगशाली, षड्विध नाभिवाले और तेजोमय रथ के चक्र से अन्धकार को नष्ट करते हुये भगवान् सूर्य गमन करते हें ।१३-५५॥ इस रथ का विस्तार दस हजार योजन है। इस रथ के मध्य से ईषादण्ड का प्रमाण दुगुना है। प्रयोजन वश या सूय के लिये ब्रह्मा ने इस रथ का निर्माण किया है। यह रथ असज्भ, सुवर्णमय, दिव्य और परम वेगगामी अइवों से युक्त है। छन्दः स्वरूप अबवों से युक्त यह रथ जहाँ शुक्र हैं, वहाँ ठहरा है एवं लक्षण में वरुण के रथ के समान है। इसी चमकोले रथ के द्वारा सूय॑
verses.wordMeaning: These forty-nine are the different Maruts with their own separate names. They have been enumerated by Diti and Indra.
verses.commentary: Sense: These forty-nine are the different Maruts with their own separate names. They have been enumerated by Diti and Indra.

verses.sanskrit: प्राप्तं तु नान्यथा राजञ्छङ्करो वदते त्विदम् । स्पर्शलिङ्गमिदं राजञ्छङ्करेण तु निर्मितम्
verses.transliteration: prāptaṃ tu nānyathā rājañchaṅkaro vadate tvidam / sparśaliṅgamidaṃ rājañchaṅkareṇa tu nirmitam
verses.translation: On hearing their names, Diti said to Indra, "O son, may my sons roam about in the Vdtaskandha. May my sons walk in the company of Devas. Welfare unto you.
verses.hindi: ३८२ : वायुपुराणम्
verses.wordMeaning: On hearing their names, Diti said to Indra, "O son, may my sons roam about in the Vdtaskandha. May my sons walk in the company of Devas. Welfare unto you.
verses.commentary: Sense: On hearing their names, Diti said to Indra, "O son, may my sons roam about in the Vdtaskandha. May my sons walk in the company of Devas. Welfare unto you.

verses.sanskrit: स्पर्शमात्रे मनुष्याणां रुद्रवासो ऽभिजायते । तेन दानफलं सर्वं कुरुक्षेत्रादिकं च यत्
verses.transliteration: sparśamātre manuṣyāṇāṃ rudravāso 'bhijāyate / tena dānaphalaṃ sarvaṃ kurukṣetrādikaṃ ca yat
verses.translation: On hearing her words, the thousand-eyed Purandara joined his palms in reverence and said: "Mother, be it so.
verses.hindi: तस्य काष्ठाः स्मृता घाणा ईषादण्डः क्षणास्तु वे । नि्ेषाध्चानुकर्षो5सप ईषा चास्य लवाः स्मृता: ॥ रात्रिवंरूथों धर्मोउस्य ध्वज ऊध्वः समुच्छितः । युगाक्षकोटी ते तस्य अर्थंकामाबुभो स्पूती..
verses.wordMeaning: On hearing her words, the thousand-eyed Purandara joined his palms in reverence and said: "Mother, be it so.
verses.commentary: Sense: On hearing her words, the thousand-eyed Purandara joined his palms in reverence and said: "Mother, be it so.

verses.sanskrit: एतस्मात् कारणाद् राजंल् लोकपालाश्च रक्षकाः । दुर्गा च रक्षणे सृष्टा चतुर्हस्तधरा शुभा
verses.transliteration: etasmāt kāraṇād rājaṃl lokapālāśca rakṣakāḥ / durgā ca rakṣaṇe sṛṣṭā caturhastadharā śubhā
verses.translation: Undoubtedly all this will happen as mentioned by you. These sons of noble souls (shall) become Devas and will be ho¬ noured by Devas. Similarly, your sons will become partakers of the fruits of Yajiias along with Devas."
verses.hindi: सप्ताध्वरूपाच्छन्दांसि वहन्ते वामतो धुरम् । गायत्री चेंब त्रिष्दुण्च अनुष्दुबूजगती तथा ३६४
verses.wordMeaning: Undoubtedly all this will happen as mentioned by you. These sons of noble souls (shall) become Devas and will be ho¬ noured by Devas. Similarly, your sons will become partakers of the fruits of Yajiias along with Devas."
verses.commentary: Sense: Undoubtedly all this will happen as mentioned by you. These sons of noble souls (shall) become Devas and will be ho¬ noured by Devas. Similarly, your sons will become partakers of the fruits of Yajiias along with Devas."

verses.sanskrit: धनदो लोकपालेशो रक्षकश्चेश्वरस्य च । रक्षति च सदा कालं ग्रहव्यापाररूपतः
verses.transliteration: dhanado lokapāleśo rakṣakaśceśvarasya ca / rakṣati ca sadā kālaṃ grahavyāpārarūpataḥ
verses.translation: Hence all those Maruts should be known as Devas (shining ones), younger brothers of Indra and Amaras (deathless ones). All of them, the sons of Diti were ascetics and gods. After knowing this decisively, the mother and the son of ascetic nature went to heaven delightedly. Sakra too went to heaven.
verses.hindi: सहचक़ों अमत्यक्ष: सहाक्षों भ्रसति श्रुवः। अक्षः सहैब चक्रेण अ्रमते5सो श्रुवेरितः तेनासौ तरणिदेंवस्तरसा सर्पते दिवि। युगाक्षकोटिसंबद्धो रश्मी द्वो स्थन्दनस्य हि ६८
verses.wordMeaning: Hence all those Maruts should be known as Devas (shining ones), younger brothers of Indra and Amaras (deathless ones). All of them, the sons of Diti were ascetics and gods. After knowing this decisively, the mother and the son of ascetic nature went to heaven delightedly.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Hence all those Maruts should be known as Devas (shining ones), younger brothers of Indra and Amaras (deathless ones). All of them, the sons of Diti were ascetics and gods. After knowing this decisively, the mother and the son of ascetic nature went to heaven delightedly.…

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रभ्रातृसमारूपैः स्वामिसम्बन्धरूपिभिः । लङ्केश्वरं च राजेन्द्र देवैर्नाद्यापि मुच्यते
verses.transliteration: putrabhrātṛsamārūpaiḥ svāmisambandharūpibhiḥ / laṅkeśvaraṃ ca rājendra devairnādyāpi mucyate
verses.translation: He who reads or listens to the auspicious origin of Maruts shall become long-lived. He never meets with (he fear of drought.
verses.hindi: युगाक्षकोटी ते तस्य दक्षिणे स्थन्दनस्य तु । भुवेण संगृहीते वे द्विचक्रश्वेतरज्जुवत्
verses.wordMeaning: He who reads or listens to the auspicious origin of Maruts shall become long-lived. He never meets with (he fear of drought.
verses.commentary: Sense: He who reads or listens to the auspicious origin of Maruts shall become long-lived. He never meets with (he fear of drought.

verses.sanskrit: ॥ इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे लुङ्केश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम सप्तषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ र्क्व् अध्याय ६८ श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: धनदस्य तु तत्तीर्थं ततो गच्छेद् युधिष्ठिर । नर्मदादक्षिणे कूले सर्वपापक्षयंकरम्
verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe luṅkeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma saptaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 68 śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: dhanadasya tu tattīrthaṃ tato gacched yudhiṣṭhira / narmadādakṣiṇe kūle sarvapāpakṣayaṃkaram
verses.translation: Henceforth, I shall recount the sons of Danu. Listen to and understand them. The sons of Danu, the great Asuras, have been famous in their race, There were hundred demons of very fierce valour of whom Vipracitti was the chief. All of them had performed good penances and had been endowed with boons.
verses.hindi: अ्रमन्‍्तमनुगच्छेतां ध्रुव रश्मी तु तावुभो । युगाक्षकोटी ते तस्य बातों स्पन्दनस्य तु ७१ आकाद-मार्ग में गमन करते हैं ।५६-५८। सूर्य-रथ के जितने अवयव हैं, वे संवत्सर के अज्जों द्वारा यथाक्रम कल्पित हुये हैं। बूयं-रथ का नाभि-स्थान दिन है। यही एक चक्र भी कहलाता है। पाँचों ऋतुएँ उसकी अरायें हैं और छः ऋतुएं नेमि कही गई हैँ ।५६-६०। रथ का मध्य स्थान वर्ष, दोनों जुये अयन, बन्धुर मुहते, युगकील कला, घोणा काष्ठा. ईषादण्ड क्षण, अनुकर्ष निमेष, ईषा लव, वरूथ रात्रि, समुन्नत ध्वज धर्म युग और
verses.wordMeaning: Henceforth, I shall recount the sons of Danu. Listen to and understand them. The sons of Danu, the great Asuras, have been famous in their race, There were hundred demons of very fierce valour of whom Vipracitti was the chief.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Henceforth, I shall recount the sons of Danu. Listen to and understand them. The sons of Danu, the great Asuras, have been famous in their race, There were hundred demons of very fierce valour of whom Vipracitti was the chief.…

verses.sanskrit: सर्वतीर्थफलं तत्र प्राप्यते नात्र संशयः । चैत्रमासत्रयोदश्यां शुक्लपक्षे जितेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration: sarvatīrthaphalaṃ tatra prāpyate nātra saṃśayaḥ / caitramāsatrayodaśyāṃ śuklapakṣe jitendriyaḥ
verses.translation: They were truthful, valorous, ruthless and expert in Maya (illusive power). These Danavas were very powerful, unfavourable to Brahmanas and disinclined to perform Yajiias. I shall enumerate them all in accordance with their importance. (Listen to) and understand. The chief of the sons of Danu were: Dvimurdha, Sankuvarna, Saiiku, Niramaya, Sarikukarna, Mahavisva, Gavesthi, Dundubhi, Ajamukha, prosperous Sila, Vamanasa, Marlci, Raksaka, Mahagargya, Angiravrta, Viksobhya, Suketu, Suvlrya, Suhrda, Indrajit, Visvajit, Suravimardana, Ekacakra, Subahu, the powerful Taraka, Vaisvanara, Puloman, Pravlna, Mahasiras, Svarbhanu, Vrsaparvan, the great Asura Munqlaka, Dhrtarastra, Surya, Candra, Indra, Tapina, Suksma, Nicandra, Ornanabha, Mahagiri. Asiloman, Sukesa, Sada, Balaka, Adas'a, Gaganamurdhan, Kumbhanabha, Mahodara, Pramodaha, Kupatha, the valorous Hayagriva, the Asura Virupaksa, the great Asura Supatha, Aja, Hiranmaya, Satamayu, Sambara, Sarabha and Salabha. Surya (the Sun) and Candramas (the Moon) were the lords of Asuras formerly but now they are the lords of Suras. Thus the important scions of the family of Danu have been enumerated. Their sons and grandsons are unending and innumerable.
verses.hindi: अक्षकोटि अर्थ तथा काम एवं गायत्री, त्रिष्टुप्, अनुष्टुपू, पंक्ति, बृहती, जगती, उष्णिक् आदि सातों छन्द सप्ताध्व हैं। रथ के अक्ष में चक्र मिला हुआ है ओर चक्र ध्र.व से मिला हुआ है, इसलिये अक्ष के साथ ही चके घूमता है और चक्र के साथ-ही-साथ भव घूमा करता है ध्रव की प्ररेणां से चक्र के साथ अक्ष भी घूमा करता है ।६१-६६। प्रयोजनवश सूर्य के रथ का इस प्रकार संघटन किया गया है। उस रथ का संघटन इस प्रकार
verses.wordMeaning: They were truthful, valorous, ruthless and expert in Maya (illusive power). These Danavas were very powerful, unfavourable to Brahmanas and disinclined to perform Yajiias. I shall enumerate them all in accordance with their importance. (Listen to) and understand.…
verses.commentary: Sense: They were truthful, valorous, ruthless and expert in Maya (illusive power). These Danavas were very powerful, unfavourable to Brahmanas and disinclined to perform Yajiias. I shall enumerate them all in accordance with their importance. (Listen to) and understand.…

verses.sanskrit: उपोष्य परया भक्त्या रात्रौ कुर्वीत जागरम् । पञ्चामृतेन राजेन्द्र स्नापयेद् धनदं बुधः
verses.transliteration: upoṣya parayā bhaktyā rātrau kurvīta jāgaram / pañcāmṛtena rājendra snāpayed dhanadaṃ budhaḥ
verses.translation: Those who are the sons (descendants) of Did and Danu are (commonly known) as Asuras. Those mentioned just now are the sons and descendants of Danu. Svarbhanu is remembered as the son of Did (i.e. a Daitya) and Anubhanuwas the son of Danu. Ekaksa, Rsabha, Ari§ta, Prabandha, Naraka, In- drabadhana, KesI, Meru, Samba, Dhenuka, Gavesthi, Gavaksa and powerful Talaketu—these were the sons of Danu but followed human rites and activities. So I remember.
verses.hindi: किया गया है कि, उसमें अतिशय प्रभा आ गई है। उसी रथ के द्वारा सूये भगवान् वेग पूर्वक आकाश में गमन करते हैं ६७-६६। रथ के युग ओर अक्षकोटि में इस प्रकार की दो किरण जुड़ी हुई हैँ, जो ध्रूव द्वारा परिचालित होने पर आकाश तल में रथ को मण्डलाकार बना देती हैं। उस रथ के दक्षिण भाग में जो युगाक्षकोटि है, वह प्रू,व द्वारा संगृहीत या संलग्न होने पर उस तरह दीखती हैं, जेसे श्वेत तन्तुओं के दो चक्र हों। रथ की युगाक्षकोटि में लगी हुई बे दोनों किरणें वायुमय है, जो घूमते हुये श्रूव का अनुसरण करती

verses.sanskrit: दीपं घृतेन दातव्यं गीतं वाद्यं च कारयेत् । प्रभाते पूजयेद् विप्रान् आत्मनः श्रेय इच्छति
verses.transliteration: dīpaṃ ghṛtena dātavyaṃ gītaṃ vādyaṃ ca kārayet / prabhāte pūjayed viprān ātmanaḥ śreya icchati
verses.translation: The following sons of Vipracitd born of Simhika became terrible, valorous in the clashes between Daityas and Danavas. They are well known as Saimhikeyas. They are fourteen great Asuras, viz. Satagala, Balavan, Nyasa, Samba, Anuloma, Suci, Vatapi, Sitamsuka, Hara, Kalpa, Kalanabha, Bhauma and Naraka and the eldest of all of them Rahu who oppresses the Moon and the Sun. Thus these are the sons of Simhika invincible even to Devas. All of them were of terrible lineage, ruthless and haters of Brahmanas. There are ten thousand other Asuras constituting the Saimhikeya group.
verses.hindi: अशौतिमण्डलशतं काष्ठयोरुभयोश्ररन् । भ्रुवेण मुच्यमाना भ्थां रश्मिभ्यां पुनरेव तु

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिग्रहसमर्थांश्च विद्यासिद्धान्तवादिनः । श्रौतस्मार्तक्रियायुक्तान् परदारपराङ्मुखान्
verses.transliteration: pratigrahasamarthāṃśca vidyāsiddhāntavādinaḥ / śrautasmārtakriyāyuktān paradāraparāṅmukhān
verses.translation: They were killed by the powerful son of Jamadagni of Upadanavl was the daughter of Maya, Sarmistha was the daughter of Vrsaparvan. Puloma and Kalika were the daughters of Vaisvanara.
verses.hindi: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्तेइतुष जपादे ज्योतिष्प्रचारों नामैकपञ्चाशो5्ध्यायः स रथो5घिष्ठितो देवेरादित्येऋ पिभिस्तथा । गन्धर्वेरप्सरोभिश्न ग्रामणीसर्प राक्षस: १
verses.wordMeaning: They were killed by the powerful son of Jamadagni of Upadanavl was the daughter of Maya, Sarmistha was the daughter of Vrsaparvan. Puloma and Kalika were the daughters of Vaisvanara.
verses.commentary: Sense: They were killed by the powerful son of Jamadagni of Upadanavl was the daughter of Maya, Sarmistha was the daughter of Vrsaparvan. Puloma and Kalika were the daughters of Vaisvanara.

verses.sanskrit: पूजयेद्गोहिरण्येन वस्त्रोपानहभोजनैः । छत्रशय्याप्रदानेन सर्वपापक्षयो भवेत्
verses.transliteration: pūjayedgohiraṇyena vastropānahabhojanaiḥ / chatraśayyāpradānena sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet
verses.translation: Nahusa was the son of Prabha and Jayanta was the son of Sacx. Sarmistha gave birth to Puru and Upadanavl to Dusyanta. The Paulomas and Kalakeyas were Danavas of great strength. They could not be killed by Devas, but were slain by Savyasaci (Arjuna).
verses.hindi: हैँ ७०-७१ खूंट से बंधा हुआ धागा जैसे चारों दिशाओं में धूमता है, उसी प्रकार रब्मियाँ घूमती हैँ; किर उत्तरायण होने पर किरणें कुछ घट जाती हैँ और दक्षिणायन होने पर बढ़ जाती हैं। इस तरह मण्डलाक घूमते हुये रथ की किरणों को ध्रूव जब खींचता है, तब सूर्य भी खिंच जाते हैं। ध्रव जब उन दोनों किरणों को खींचता है, तब सुर्य॑ भीतरी मण्डल में घूमते हैं ।७२-७४। उस समय सूर्य दोनों दिशाओं के एक सौ
verses.wordMeaning: Nahusa was the son of Prabha and Jayanta was the son of Sacx. Sarmistha gave birth to Puru and Upadanavl to Dusyanta. The Paulomas and Kalakeyas were Danavas of great strength. They could not be killed by Devas, but were slain by Savyasaci (Arjuna).
verses.commentary: Sense: Nahusa was the son of Prabha and Jayanta was the son of Sacx. Sarmistha gave birth to Puru and Upadanavl to Dusyanta. The Paulomas and Kalakeyas were Danavas of great strength. They could not be killed by Devas, but were slain by Savyasaci (Arjuna).

verses.sanskrit: त्रिजन्मजनितं पापं वरदस्य प्रभावतः । स्वर्गदं दुर्विनीतानां विनीतानां च मोक्षदम्
verses.transliteration: trijanmajanitaṃ pāpaṃ varadasya prabhāvataḥ / svargadaṃ durvinītānāṃ vinītānāṃ ca mokṣadam
verses.translation: All the sons born of Maya were heroic and valorous, viz. Mayavl, Dundubhi, Vfsa, Mahisa, Balika and Vajrakarna. A daughter Mandodari was also born to him. Thus the creation of Daityas and Danavas has been enumerated. Five sons of great strength are remembered as born of Danayusa, viz. Aruru, Bali, Jarhbha, Virak§a and Visa.
verses.hindi: अस्सी मण्डलों का चक्‍कर लगाते हैं। फिर जब प्रूव दोनों रश्मियों को जोड़ देता है, तब सूथे बाहरी मण्डल में घूमने लगते हैं । उस समय वे बेग से मण्डलों को आबुत करते हुये घुमते हैं ।७४-७६॥। सूतजी बोले--उस रथ पर देव, आदित्य, गन्धवं, अप्सरा, ग्रामणी (शिल्पी),
verses.wordMeaning: All the sons born of Maya were heroic and valorous, viz. Mayavl, Dundubhi, Vfsa, Mahisa, Balika and Vajrakarna. A daughter Mandodari was also born to him. Thus the creation of Daityas and Danavas has been enumerated.…
verses.commentary: Sense: All the sons born of Maya were heroic and valorous, viz. Mayavl, Dundubhi, Vfsa, Mahisa, Balika and Vajrakarna. A daughter Mandodari was also born to him. Thus the creation of Daityas and Danavas has been enumerated.…

verses.sanskrit: अन्नदं च दरिद्राणां भवेज्जन्मनिजन्मनि । कुलीनत्वं दुःखहानिः स्वभावाजायते नरे
verses.transliteration: annadaṃ ca daridrāṇāṃ bhavejjanmanijanmani / kulīnatvaṃ duḥkhahāniḥ svabhāvājāyate nare
verses.translation: Aruru's son was a cruel great Asura named Dhundhu. It is reported that he was killed by Kuvalasva at the instance of Uttanka. The two sons of Bali were very valorous and unequal¬ led in splendour. They were Kumbhila and Cakravarma. (The latter) was Kama in his previous* birth.
verses.hindi: उरगो वासुकिश्चेव संकीर्णारश्र तावभौ । तुम्बुरानारदश्चेब गन्धवो' गायतां बरो ४३ क़तुस्थल्यप्सराश्चेब तथा वे पुजिजिकस्थला। ग्रामणी रथकृच्छुश्न तथोजंश्चेव तावुभौ
verses.wordMeaning: Aruru's son was a cruel great Asura named Dhundhu. It is reported that he was killed by Kuvalasva at the instance of Uttanka. The two sons of Bali were very valorous and unequal¬ led in splendour. They were Kumbhila and Cakravarma. (The latter) was Kama in his previous* birth.
verses.commentary: Sense: Aruru's son was a cruel great Asura named Dhundhu. It is reported that he was killed by Kuvalasva at the instance of Uttanka. The two sons of Bali were very valorous and unequal¬ led in splendour. They were Kumbhila and Cakravarma. (The latter) was Kama in his previous* birth.

verses.sanskrit: व्याधिध्वंसो भवेत् तेषां नर्मदोदकसेवनात् । धनदस्य तु यस्तीर्थे विद्यादानं प्रयच्छति
verses.transliteration: vyādhidhvaṃso bhavet teṣāṃ narmadodakasevanāt / dhanadasya tu yastīrthe vidyādānaṃ prayacchati
verses.translation: Viraksa had two sons Kalaka and Varavisa. Varavisa had four sons of cruel activities, viz. Sraddhaha, Yajnahk, Brahmaha and PaSuha. The sons of Danayusa have been enumerated. Now understand the sons of V r tra who were born of the terrible breath of Vrtra while engaged in battle with Indra.
verses.hindi: रक्षो हेतिः प्रहेतिश्न यातुधानावुदाहुती । मधुमाधवयोरेष गणो वसति भास्करे ... वासन्तौ ग्रेष्मिको मासौ मिन्रश्च वरुणभ्य हु। ऋषिरत्रियंशिष्ठश्च तक्षकों रम्भ एवं च ६ मेनका सहजन्या च गन्धवों च हहा हहूः । रथस्वनश्च ग्रामण्यौ रथचित्रश्च तावुभो
verses.wordMeaning: Viraksa had two sons Kalaka and Varavisa. Varavisa had four sons of cruel activities, viz. Sraddhaha, Yajnahk, Brahmaha and PaSuha. The sons of Danayusa have been enumerated.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Viraksa had two sons Kalaka and Varavisa. Varavisa had four sons of cruel activities, viz. Sraddhaha, Yajnahk, Brahmaha and PaSuha. The sons of Danayusa have been enumerated.…

verses.sanskrit: स याति भास्करे लोके सर्वव्याधिविवर्जिते । देवद्रोणीं च तत्रैव स्वशक्त्या पाण्डुनन्दन
verses.transliteration: sa yāti bhāskare loke sarvavyādhivivarjite / devadroṇīṃ ca tatraiva svaśaktyā pāṇḍunandana
verses.translation: They were Raksasas of great strength and were the rulers mentally famous. They were a hundred thousand in number and are remembered as the followers of Mahendra. AH were knowers of the Veda, gentle, righteous, subtie- formed. All were immanent in the subjects. All were very righteous.
verses.hindi: ततः सूर्य पुनस्त्वन्या निवसन्‍्तीह देवता: । इन्द्रश्चेव विवस्वांश्च अज्धिरा भृगुरेव च
verses.wordMeaning: They were Raksasas of great strength and were the rulers mentally famous. They were a hundred thousand in number and are remembered as the followers of Mahendra. AH were knowers of the Veda, gentle, righteous, subtie- formed. All were immanent in the subjects.…
verses.commentary: Sense: They were Raksasas of great strength and were the rulers mentally famous. They were a hundred thousand in number and are remembered as the followers of Mahendra. AH were knowers of the Veda, gentle, righteous, subtie- formed. All were immanent in the subjects.…

verses.sanskrit: ये प्रकुर्वन्ति भूयिष्ठां रेवाया दक्षिणे तटे । ते यान्ति शांकरे लोके सर्वदुःखविवर्जिते
verses.transliteration: ye prakurvanti bhūyiṣṭhāṃ revāyā dakṣiṇe taṭe / te yānti śāṃkare loke sarvaduḥkhavivarjite
verses.translation: Thus the creation of Daityas and Danavas has been narrated. Pravahi bore sons in the Yajna. They were excellent in singnig. Sattvan, Sattvatmaka, Kalapa, Viryavan, Krtavirya, Brahmacarin, the seventh one Supandu, Pana, Taranya and the tenth one Sucandra: These ten are to be known as Devas and Gandharvas. They have been enumerated.
verses.hindi: एलापर्णस्तथा सर्प: शद्भूपालश्च तावुभौ । विश्वावसूभ्रसेनो च प्रातश्चेवारणश्च ह् . नभोनभस्ययोरेष गणो वसति भास्करे  द
verses.wordMeaning: Thus the creation of Daityas and Danavas has been narrated. Pravahi bore sons in the Yajna. They were excellent in singnig. Sattvan, Sattvatmaka, Kalapa, Viryavan, Krtavirya, Brahmacarin, the seventh one Supandu, Pana,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Thus the creation of Daityas and Danavas has been narrated. Pravahi bore sons in the Yajna. They were excellent in singnig. Sattvan, Sattvatmaka, Kalapa, Viryavan, Krtavirya, Brahmacarin, the seventh one Supandu, Pana,…

verses.sanskrit: ॥ इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे धनदतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामाष्टषष्टितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ र्क्व् अध्याय ६९ श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: ततो गच्छेत्तु राजेन्द्र मङ्गलेश्वरमुत्तमम् । स्थापितं भूमिपुत्रेण लोकानां हितकाम्यया
verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe dhanadatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmāṣṭaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 69 śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: tato gacchettu rājendra maṅgaleśvaramuttamam / sthāpitaṃ bhūmiputreṇa lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā
verses.translation: The holy Gandharvas and Apsaras-s are glorified as the children of Muni, viz. Gitrasena, Ugrasena, Grnayu, Anagha, Dhptarastra, Puloman, Suryavarcas, Yugapat, Trnapat, Kali, Diti, Citraratha, the thirteenth Bhramisiras, the fourteenth Parjanya, the fifteenth Kali and the sixteenth Narada—these divine Gandharvas are glorified as descendants of Muni. There are their thirtyfour 2 younger sisters, the aus¬ picious Apsaras-s, viz. Antara, Daravatya, Priyamukhya, Surot- tama, Misrakesi SacI, Parninx, Alambusa, Marica, MarxcT, Putrika, Vidyud, Varna, Tilottama, Adrika, Laksana, Devi, Rarhbha, Manorama, Suvara, Subahu, Purnita, Supratisthita, Pundarika, Sugandha, Sudanta,Surasa, Hemasara, Suti, Suvrtta, Kamala, Subhuja, Hamsapada—these are the worldly 3 Apsaras-s. This chapter enumerates the prominent members of clans of Gandharvas, Apsaras-s, birds, serpents, Yaksas, Raksasas, Pisacas, Y&tudha- nas and other species possessing supernatural powers. Even after splitting Vidyudvarna into Vidyutand Varna the number of these Apsaras-s is 32 and not 34 stated here. Bd. 3.7-5 states twentyfour as the number of Apsaras-s. It is not understood why the sons of Muni are called 'Deoa- Gandharvas * (Divine Gandharvas) while their sisters, the Apsaras-s are called The daughters of Gandharvas had been (will be) narra¬ ted by me. Now listen to my enumeration of their names. Suyasa was the first among them. GandharvI comes next. Then are Vidyavatl, Carumukhx and SumukhI of ex¬ cellent face. The sons of Suyas'a were very powerful and valorous. Yaksas were the sons of Pracetas. Listen to their names. Kambala, Harikesa, Kapila, Kancana and Megha- mall are said to constitute the group of Yaksas. Suyasa's four daughters are remembered as Apsaras-s. Listen to and understand their names, as I recount them. Loheyi was the eldest; Bharata was the next. Then were Krsangl and Visala who were unequalled in beauty. From them other four groups of Yaksas were procreated by the valorous and noble-souled Visala. Loheya, Bharateya, the renowned Krsangeya and ViSaleya were the groups of Yaksas famous in the Purana. O excellent ones among the knowers of Loka and Aloka, (the worlds) have been occupied by these terrible Asuras of great strength and prowess. The Gandharvas called Valeyas were procreated by the noble-souled Vikranta. They were the leaders of great Gandharvas. They possessed great prowess, and were richly endowed with valour and liberal-mindedness. I shall mention duly and in proper order the names of those highly mighty and valorous Gandharvas. They were: Citrangada, Citravarma of great prowess, the highly fortunate Citraketu and the valorous Somadatta. There were three daughters also. Their names are being men¬ tioned.
verses.hindi: शरदुतो पुनः शुश्रा वसन्ति मुनिदेवताः । पर्जन्यश्चाथ पूषा च भरद्वाजः सगौतमः १२ विश्वावसुश्च गन्धर्वास्तथव सुरभिश्च यः(या) । विश्वाची वा घृताची च उमे ते शुभलक्षण.
verses.wordMeaning: The holy Gandharvas and Apsaras-s are glorified as the children of Muni, viz. Gitrasena, Ugrasena, Grnayu, Anagha, Dhptarastra, Puloman, Suryavarcas, Yugapat, Trnapat, Kali, Diti, Citraratha, the thirteenth Bhramisiras, the fourteenth Parjanya,…
verses.commentary: Sense: The holy Gandharvas and Apsaras-s are glorified as the children of Muni, viz. Gitrasena, Ugrasena, Grnayu, Anagha, Dhptarastra, Puloman, Suryavarcas, Yugapat, Trnapat, Kali, Diti, Citraratha, the thirteenth Bhramisiras, the fourteenth Parjanya,…

verses.sanskrit: तोषितः परया भक्त्या शङ्करः शशिशेखरः । चतुर्दश्यां गुरुर्देवः प्रत्यक्षो मङ्गलेश्वरः
verses.transliteration: toṣitaḥ parayā bhaktyā śaṅkaraḥ śaśiśekharaḥ / caturdaśyāṃ gururdevaḥ pratyakṣo maṅgaleśvaraḥ
verses.translation: The first was Agnika. Kambala was the next. Then was Vasumati. All these had unequalled splendour. Three other important groups of the chief Gandh- arvas were begotten of them by Kumara. They were valorous and invincible in war. They were Agneyas, Kambaleyas and sons of Vasumati. This world consisting of the mobile and the immobile is pervaded by these various groups. They possessed learning and were procreated by the noble-souled Vikranta. They were blessed and were richly endowed with beauty, learning and wealth. Listen to the enumeration of the names of those noble- souled Gandharvas of distinctive prowess. They were: Hiranyaroman, Kapila, Suloman, Mag- adha, Candraketu, Ganga and the highly powerful Goda. These were the first among the groups who were ascetics, valorous and pure on account of deep learning. They were Siva and Sumanas. The groups Saiveya, the valorous and Saumanasa as well were begotten of them by the noble-souled Visravas. They practised learning. This world is pervaded by these three groups of Vidyadharas. From these, many hundreds of groups of firmament- walkers were born in the world due to the activities of the Vidyadharas. Samudra, Sena, Kalinda, Mahanetra, Mahabala, Suvarnaghosa, Sugrlva, the valorous Mahaghosa and others are the leading ones of the noble-souled Kinnaras with the faces of horses. They are being glorified as extensive (in number) by scholars. O Sarhsapayana, human-faced Kinnaras too were similarly procreated by the noble-souled Vikranta. Harisena, Susena, the valorous Varisena, Rudra- datta, Indradatta,Candradruma,Mahadruma, Bindu andBindu- sara were the Kinnaras of the lunar race. Thus these excellent and auspicious Kinnaras have become famous in the world. O excellent Brahmanas, in this world there are hundreds of clans of these noble-souled Kinnaras, very efficient in dance and music. They are Yaksas calmed by Yaksas (?) The beauti¬ ful daughter of Loheya, named Suravinda was brilliant and honoured by the Siddhas. (Defective Verse) The groups of Bhutas (goblins) had been procreated by the terrible Upayakctana. Listen to their names (?). The groups of Bhutas (goblins) should be known as those who haunt from within and without etc. ( avesakas, nivesakas). They are declared as being visible in the world. Those that are the excellent ones among Bhutas that move about in the sky are to be known as the leaders of these Bhutas in the world. Undoubtedly they move about in the sky up to the tops of trees.
verses.hindi: नाग ऐरावतश्चेव विश्रुतश्च धनंजयः । सेन (ना )जिच्च सुषेणश्च सेनानी्ँग्रामणीश्च तो निवास करते हैं। ये सब क्रम से दो-दो महीना सूर्य के रथ पर रहते हैं। धाता-अयमा आदित्य, पुलस्त्य-पुलह प्रजापति वासुकि-संकीर्णार सपं, तुम्बुरु-नारद गायक श्रेष्ठ गन्धर्व, ऋतु-स्थली पुवज्जिकस्थला अप्सरायें, रथ कृच्छु-उर्ज ग्रामणी यानी शिल्पी, हेति-प्रहेति यातुधान राक्षस चैत्र-वेशाख में सूय के गण होकर उनके साथ रहते हैं ।१-५। फिर ज्येष्ठ आषाढ़ में यानी वसन्‍्त के बाद ग्रीष्म ऋतु में मित्र-वरुण आदित्य, अन्रि-वसिष्ठ
verses.wordMeaning: The first was Agnika. Kambala was the next. Then was Vasumati. All these had unequalled splendour. Three other important groups of the chief Gandh- arvas were begotten of them by Kumara. They were valorous and invincible in war. They were Agneyas,…

verses.sanskrit: ब्रूहि पुत्र वरं शुभ्रं तं ते दास्यामि मङ्गल
verses.transliteration: brūhi putra varaṃ śubhraṃ taṃ te dāsyāmi maṅgala
verses.translation: Almost all Devas and Gandharvas have been nar¬ rated by me. Those famous persons should be known as engaged in worshipping Devas. Along with Gandharvas, Devas who are clever musicians and experts in dance and music stay in all the worlds. They worship Narayana who is lotus-eyed, free from Rajas Guna and the foremost of gods, god Brahma who is self-born and four-faced, great god Sankara who is Isana and the lord of the Universe. (They worship) Rudras and Adityas led by Indra, along with Vasus. The blessed Varistha who is honoured by gods, gave birth to eight sons. Hariisa was the eldest and the youngest was another. The middle ones were Haha and Huhu. The fourth was Dhisana. Then Vasiruci (was born). Tumburu was the sixth among them. Then Visvavasu. These Apsaras-s(celestial artiste) are considered as divine and of auspicious characteristics. Manovati and Sukesa were the two daughters of Tumburu. Urvasi who was faultless (exquisitely beautiful) in every Men aka was the daughter of Mena, delightedly engros¬ sed in meditating upon Brahman. All of them are expounders of Brahman (Vedas) and great Yoginis. The groups of the holy Apsaras-s are fourteen. Among these fourteen gagas Ahutas (is the first) and Sobhayantls is the (fourteenth) x. (Ahutas) are the mental daughters of Brahma and Sobhayantls are Manu's daughters. Vegavantis are the daughters of Arista and Agnisambhavas are the daughters of fjrja. 1 2 3 Ayusmantls are shining groups born of the rays of the sun. The groups born of water i.e. produced from Amrta (water, nectar) are remembered by the name Amrtas. The Vayu-born groups are named Mudas, those born of the Earth are Bhavas, the groups Rues are born of Vidyut (lightning) and the daughters of Mrtyu are Bhairavas. The group Sobhayantls have the attributes of Kama (Cupid). Thus the fourteen groups have been narrated. They have been created with exquisitely superb beauty by the groups of Suras including Indra and Upendra (Visnu). The divine lady Tilottama is of auspicious features and extremely blessed. Thecelestial damselPrabhavatl richly endowed Our text has given only the names of the first and the fourteenth group. Probably some lines missing in our text are found in Bd. 3.7.18-20a as follows: The text needs emendation: 'The Urjas are born of the Fire-god* as Orjas arc a garia of Apsaras-s (vide Bd. 3.7..21). Some lines appear to be missing. This translation is of the printed text of Va. P. The missing lines are probably the same as Bd. 3.7.21b and They mention the classes of divine damsels,viz. Yuvatis, Kurus, Sruks and Barhis who are respectively born from the Sun-god, the Moon-god, Yajna (Sacrifice) and Kusavati.
verses.hindi: ऋषि, तक्षक-रम्भसप, मेनका-सहजन्या अप्सरा, हाहा-ह॒ह गनन्‍्धवें, रथस्वन, रथचित्र ग्रामणी तथा पौरुषेय- बध नामक यातुधान राक्षस सूर्य के साथ करते हैं। सावन-भादों में उनके साथ दूसरे-दुसरे देवता निवास करते हैं ।६-८१। जैसे, इन्द्र विवस्वान् आदित्य, अंगिरा, भूगु मुनि, एलापर्ण, शंखपाल सप, विष्वावसू उद्मसेन गन्धवे, प्रात:-अरुण प्रम्लोचा-निम्लोचा अप्सरा और व्याप्र रवेत राक्षस । आश्विन-कार्तिक (शरद ऋतु) में आगे

verses.sanskrit: मङ्गल उवाच: प्रसादं कुरु मे शम्भो प्रतिजन्मनि शङ्कर । त्वदङ्गस्वेदसम्भूतो ग्रहमध्ये वसाम्यहम्
verses.transliteration: maṅgala uvāca: prasādaṃ kuru me śambho pratijanmani śaṅkara / tvadaṅgasvedasambhūto grahamadhye vasāmyaham
verses.translation: The celestial woman of great lustre, Vedavatl by name, was born from the bottom (surface) of the altar of the intelligent four-faced lord (Brahma). Similarly the daughter of Yama, the bright-eyed celes¬ tial woman Hema had the lustre of excellent gold and possessed beauty and youth..- Thus there are many thousands of shining groups of Apsaras-s. They are the wives and mothers of Devas and Sages. All the Apsaras-s are equally fragrant with the comple¬ xion of Gampa (Mickelia Champacca ). During the. course of their intercourse with their lovers, they are inebriated without imbib¬ ing wine. By their contact, their pleasure increases. Vinata had two sons Aruna and Garuda who had thirty- six sisters. They are remembered as their younger sisters. Gayatrl and other chandas (Vedic Metres), birds bom of Garuda and also the Havyavaha groups present in the quar¬ ters (pertain to Vinata?) Kadrii 1 gave birth to a thousand serpents both mobile and immobile. They are hydra-headed noble souls, capable of traversing in the sky, since they are great in number. They have many names (but) learn the chief of them. The most important of those serpents are Sesa, Vasuki, Taksaka, Karnlra, Jambha, Anjana, Vamana, Airavata, Mahapadma,{Kambala, Asvatara,Ailapatra, Sankha, Karkotaka, Dhananjaya, Mahakarna, Mahanila, Dhrtarastra, Balahaka, Kumara, Puspadanta, Sumukha, Durmukha, Silimukha, Dadhi- mukha, Kallya, Salipindaka, Bindupada, Pundarlka, the serpent Apurana, Kapila, Ambarisa, Dhrtapada, Kacchapa, Prahlada, Padmacitra, Gandharva, Manasvika, Nahusa, Khararoman and Mani and many others like them. The sons of Kadru have been enumerated by me. Understand those of Khasa. Khasa gave birth to two sons who were well-known as Verses 65-67 enumerate the names of most important of Kadru's children, viz. serpents. At first, Khasa gave birth to a very terrible son of the following description: He was excessively red in colour and devoid of ears. He had four arms, four feet, two heads and two¬ fold gait. He had hair all over the body. He had a huge body with a raised-up nose (like a snout) and a big belly. The head was big, the ears large and the hair like Munja grass in accor¬ dance with his desire. The lips were like those of an elephant. The shanks were long. His fangs were like those of a horse. The chin was huge; the tongue red and the eyes had matted hair(?) The mouth was huge and the nose long. He was a Guhyaka (ke¬ eper of secrets (?) ). The ears were variegated (?) in colour. He was extremely delighted and had a great face. Khasa gave birth to such an extremely terrible son. Khasa gave birth to his younger brother, a second son. He had three heads, three feet and three hands. His eyes were black. Thehair stood upright. The moustache was green in colour. His body was as firm as a rock. He had a huge body (short in stature). His arms were mighty and of great strength. His mouth was slit up to the ears. The eyebrows were suspended and the nose was stout. The lips were big. He had eight fangs and two tongues. He was pike-eared. His eyes were red and tawny-colou¬ red. His complexion was tawny. He had matted hair. He had huge ears and broad chest. He was devoid of hips and the belly was slender. She gave birth to the younger brother who had claws and whose neck was red. Immediately after the birth, they increased in size. Their bodies became mature and capable of sensual enjoyment. With their bodies thus grown up in size, they embellished their mother. The elder one of the two who was ruthless, seized his mother. He said: "Mother, I am distressed with hunger. Come here as my prey." The younger brother, however, forbade the elder one. He said frequently, "Save this Khasa, our mother". Seizing him with both the arms, he released his mother. Then the sage told his wife, "Tell us at the outset, how
verses.hindi: कहे हुए देव-मुनिगण सूर्य के साथ निवास करते हैं ।९-११३ । पज॑न्य-पूषा आदिध्य, भरद्वाज, गौतम मुनि, विश्वावसु-सुरभि गन्धेवं, विश्वाची-धृताची अप्सरा, ऐरावत-धंनंजय सपं, सेनाजित्-सुषेण सेनानी आमणी और आप वात नामक राक्षस  फिर हेमनत ऋतु के अगहन-पूष मास में सूद से साथ अंश-भग आदित्य, हैमन्तिकौ तु दो मसो वसन्ति तु दिवाकरे। अंशो भगश्च द्वावेती फश्यपश्च ऋतुश्च ह् भुजज़श्च महापद्मः सर्प: कर्कोटकस्तथा । चित्रसेनश्च गन्धवं ऊर्णायुश्चेव तावुभो उर्वशी विप्रचित्तिश्व तथवाप्सरसो शुभे । ताक्ष्यंश्वारिष्टनेमिश्च सेनानीग्रमिणीश्च तो विद्युत्स्फ्जंश्च॒ तावुग्रो यातृुधानावुदाहुतो । सहे चेव सहस्ये च बसन्‍्त्येते दिवाकरे

verses.transliteration: tvatprasādena īśāna pūjyo 'haṃ sarvadaivataiḥ / kṛtārtho hyadya saṃjātastava darśanabhāṣaṇāt
verses.translation: A son adopts the traits of his maternal uncle and a daughter those of the paternal ancestors. A son adopts the same Water certainly assumes the colour of that (bed of) earth on which it flows. Children become diffcrnt due to the defects as well as the good qualities in the conduct of their mothers or through their faculty of discrimination. Among (my wives), Aditi is interested in righteousness with her pious conduct and (inherent) strength 1. She is endowed with piety, good conduct, enlightenment and strength. Arista is interested in music. Danu is remembered as fond of magic and illusiveness. The good lady Vinata loves aerial movement. Surabhi is embellished with the conduct of performance of penance. Kadru is of a furious temperament. She is of unple* asant conduct due to anger. The conduct of Danayusa is characterised both by enmity and blessing. O blessed gentle lady, you are considered as of furious temperament by me. The forms of the whole Universe are naturally Rajasika, Sattvika and Tamasika. Your sons have taken after their uncle in their character and activities". After saying thus to the incomparable Khasa, he called the sons and made them fearless 2 by means of gentle words. Kasyapa describes the characteristics of his wives like Dili's fondness for fragrance etc. But the line is missing in the text. Hence the apparent duplication of adjectives. cakre somam abhltayah is obscure. Bd. 3.7.58 reads cakrc tabhyam tu nSmani 'accorded names unto them'. Then KhaSa told him what had been done by them to her. As the mother narrated their activities severally, the sage who saw the truth gave them names according to the meaning of the roots. The root V yaks means "to eat and to seize". Since he said ' Yaksaye' (I will eat), he will be a Yaksa. The root V raks means "to protect". Since he said "Save my mother Khas'a", your (second) son will be known by the name "Raksasa". Then, on seeing them like that and searching (further) he was surprised*. The Prajapati assigned to them blood and fat as their diet. On seeing them hungry, the father granted them this boon: "Only at night can your hands feel the touch of anything. You will move about and take your food during the night. By day, you will be enjoying sleep. You will be powerful during the night and will be sleeping during the day time.
verses.hindi: ततः शेशिरयोश्चापि मासयोनिवसन्ति वे । त्वष्ठा विष्णु्जमदग्निविश्वामित्रस्तथेव च काद्रवेयो तथा नागौ कम्बलाश्वतरावुभों । गन्धर्वों धृतराष्ट्रश्व सूर्यवर्चास्तथेव च तिलोत्तमाप्सराश्चेव देवी रम्भा सनोरमा  ऋतजित्सत्यजिच्चव ग्रामण्यो लोकविश्वुतौं ब्रह्मोपेतस्तथा दक्षों मज्ञोपेतश्च स स्मृतः । एते देवा वसनत्यकें दो सासो तु क़मेण तु

verses.translation: Protect your mother. Let righteousness be practised." After saying thus to his sons, Kasyapa vanished there itself. When their father had gone, those two heroes, natu.ally terrible, began to behave (and do) what was exactly opposed (to their father's directions), eating anything they pleased and harassing living beings. They had great strength and energy. They were invincible and huge-bodied. They possessed the illusive mdya power. Sometimes they would be visible and immediately they would vanish. They assumed forms as they pleased. They were terrible and hideous naturally. Both of them became powerful by means of their diet in accordance with the forms (they assumed). They used to roam about at night everywhere and for their food they were desirous of seizing Devas, Asuras, Sages, Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Pisacas, human beings, serpents, birds and animals. They were given the boons by Indra of not killing (not being killed?). Their diet consisted of blood, flesh and fat. They were man-eaters of great strength. They were accompanied by their two daughters with a desire to do what pleased them. The two daughters could assume any form they pleased. Though they were splendid (in appearance), their behaviour was like that of (their father). They were wandering for the sake of food m the There they saw the highly powerful Raksasa who could assume any form as he pleased. As they met one another accidentally, they wanted to seize the other and save themselves. The father told the daughters, "Seize this young fellow alive- this fellow who is throbbing at every step and bring him here quickly". Then the two daughters approached him and seized him. Caught by both the hands, he was brought to the presence The two Pisacas asked that Raksasa who was caught His antecedents were known. After knowing him as the foremost of Raksasas, Aja and Khanda, the two Pisacas who were delighted at his activity, gave him those two girls, their daughters. (Defective Verse) By means of the Paisaca form of matrimonial 1 alliance the Raksasa married the bright-toothed 2 (girls). Aja and Khanda then recounted their wealth. Khantfa said, "This is my daughter named Brahma- dhana. She is devoid of hair. She has Brahmanas (along with their wealth) as her staple diet."- "This is my daughter beautiful in every limb. Her name is Jantudhana. All the animals are her diet ahd wealth". (So said Aja.) Thus both of them narrated the wealth (of their dau¬ ghters). Out of the eight forms of marriage, Paisaca is the lowest form where¬ in money is received by the father for the girl. 'sudalya buddha-vahanah' in the text is obscure. Bd. 3.7.83 reads rudanlyavudvavaha safi 'He married them while they were crying'. She gave birth to a boy Brahmadhana and a girl Dha- Heti, Praheti, Ugra, Pauruseya, Vadha, Visphurji, Vata, Apa, Vyaghra and Sarpa—these were Raksasas, the ten sons of Yatudhana. They were the followers of the Sun and they whirl along with him. Lanku was the son of Heti. Lanku had two sons, Mal- yavan and Sumali. Now listen to the sons of Praheti. Praheti's son was the glorious and well-known Puloman.
verses.hindi: स्थानाभिमानिनों होते गणा द्वादश सप्तकाः । सर्यमाप्याययन्त्येते लेजसा तेज उत्तमम् एलेषामेव देवानां यथावीयं यथातपः । यथोयोगं यथासत्त्वं यथाधर्म यथाबलम्

verses.sanskrit: मङ्गलो ऽपि महात्मा वै स्थापयित्वा महेश्वरम् । आत्मयोगबलेनैव शूलिनापूजयत्ततः
verses.transliteration: maṅgalo 'pi mahātmā vai sthāpayitvā maheśvaram / ātmayogabalenaiva śūlināpūjayattataḥ
verses.translation: Vadha's son was Nikumbha who was ruthless Brahma- raksasa. Vata's son was Viraga and Apa's son was Jambuka. Vyaghra's son was Nirananda who caused obstacles to all living beings. Thus all the cruel Raksasas have been enu¬ merated. Yatudhanas have been mentioned. Now under¬ stand the sons of Brahmadhana. They were Yajiia, Pita, Dhuni, Ksema, Brahma, Papa, Yajnaha, Svakotaka, Kali and Sarpa. They were the ten sons of Brahmadhana. The following are their sisters, terrible Brahmaraksasxs. They were—Raktakarna, Mahajihva, Ak§aya and Upaharinl. Brahmaraksasas were born of their families on the earth. Generally they are found on the Slesmataka (Cardya Myxia) trees. They live there. Thus Raksasas have been enumerated. Understand Yaksas. Yaksa loved the Apsaras Kratusthali other¬ wise known as Pancasthula (stout in five limbs). Brooding over her and desirous of securing her, he wandered in the parks of Nandana, Vaibhraja, Surabhi and Caitraratha. In the park of Nandana, he saw her seated along with Apsaras-s. He did not know of any means of acquiring her despite his pondering, because he was defiled (ugly) in form and defiled and corrupt in his activities. He thought, "All living beings are afraid and disgus¬ ted with me who am noxious and hurtful. So how shall I secure this lady of beautiful limbs?'*. He thought of a plan and hastened to put it into ac¬ tion. The Guhyaka (Yaksa) assumed the honoured form of a Gandharva. Then he seized Kratusthali from the midst of (other) Apsaras-s. Knowing him to be beautiful in form, she followed him with emotional attachment. Even as he was being observed by the group of Apsaras-s, he was embraced by her. When he achieved his cause (i.e. desired object), a son of full-fledged sense-organs and height was born to him imme¬ diately. New-born though he was, he (as if) blazed in his glory. He spoke to his father—"I am a king. I am Nabhi" The father replied, "Since you are born, there is no fear" When the son emulated his mother in beauty and father in valour, Yaksa was overjoyed and due to that exultation regained his original form. Big Yaksas and Raksasas regain their own form while dying, when asleep, angry or frightened and when extremely delighted. Then that Guhyaka smilingly spoke to the Apsaras— "O lady of beautiful hips and excellent complexion, come to my house along with your son." On seeing him who regained his form suddenly after saying this, all the Apsaras-s were furious, perplexed and frightened and they fled.

verses.transliteration: sarvaduḥkhaharaṃ liṅgaṃ nāmnā vai maṅgaleśvaram / tatra tīrthe tu vai rājanbrāhmaṇānprīṇayetsudhīḥ
verses.translation: Kratusthali followed the Apsaras-s who were fleeing. But the son consoled her with his words. He took her to the middle ofGandharvas and Apsaras-s and returned. On seeing the birth of Yaksa, the group of Apsaras-s spoke to Kratusthali—"You are the mother of Yaksas". The Yaksa Rajatanabha was the grandfather of Guhyakas. He married Bhadra, the excellent daughter of the (They were) Siddhartha, Suryateja, Sumanta, Nandana, Kanyaka, Yavika, Manidatta, Vasu, Sarvanubhuta, Sankha, Pmgak§a, Bhiru, Mandarasobhi, Padma, Candrapra- bha, Maghapurna, Subhadra, Pradyota, Mahaujas, Dyutiman Ketuman, Mitra, Mauli and Sudarsana. Thus there are twenty- four auspicious Punyajanas born to Manibhadra. All of them were characteristically meritorious. Their sons and grandsons were the auspicious Yaksas and Punyajanas. Devajanani (Devajani) bore to Manivara the fol¬ lowing sons—Purnabhadra, Heraaratha, Maniman, Nandivard- hana, Kustumburu, PiSahgabha, Sthulakarna, Mahajaya, Sveta, ipula, Puspavan, Bhayavaha, Padmavarna, Sunetra, Yaksa, Bala, Baka, Kumuda, Ksemaka.Vardhamana, Dama, Padmana- bha, Varanga, Suvira, Vijaya, K r ti, Purnamasa, Hiranyaksa, Surupa, and others. These sons of Manivara are remembered as Yaksas and Guhyakas. Some are handsome and some are ugly. They are garlanded and very pleasing to see. They had hundreds and thousands of sons and grandsons. There were other sons of Khasa who be came Raksasas who could assume forms as they pleased. Listen to and under¬ stand the important ones among them as they are being enumerated. They were—Lalavi, Kuthana, Bhlma, Sumali, Madhu, Visphurjita, Vidyujjihva, Matanga, Dhumrita, Cand- rarka, Sukara, Budhna, Kapiloman, Prahasaka, Krida, Paras'u- nabha, Cakraksa, Nisacara, Trisiras, Satadamstra, the Raksasa Tundakesa, the Yaksa Akampana, Durmukha and Silimukha. These excellent Raksasas were valorous. In the form of groups, they move about in all the worlds. They have the ability to move on equal footing with the Devas. She (Khasa) had seven otherdaughters. Listen to them (their enumeration) in order, their progeny and the groups formed by them. Alarhba, Utkaca, Krena, Nirrta, Kapila, Siva and the blessed KesinI are the seven sisters remembered. The following auspicious groups of Raksasas were born of them. They are the devourers of people, meat-eaters, killers and invincible in war. The group called Alambeya was cruel. Similarly the group Utkaceya was also cruel. The groups of excellent Raksa¬ sas were the Karsneyas and Saiveyas. The group of Raksasas called Nairrta comprised the progeny created by leading Ganesvara who was the follower of Siva. These Yaksas and Raksasas were procreated by the powerful (Ganesvaras). They were valorous and endowed with heroism. These Devaraksasas, the Nairftas had the renowned Virupaka as their leader. Many hundreds of these proud and noble-souled groups mostly follow Sankara, the lord of the Universe. TheKapileyas,.IieDaityaraksa.-as of great prowess, of huge body and of great strength and exploit were procreated by the noble-souled king of Daityas, Kumbha. The Yaksa Kam- pana begot of KesinI, very powerful Yaksas and Raksasas. Kesini's daughter Nila bore to Alambeya Surasika many Raksa¬ sas of petty mentality. They are called Nailas. They were invin¬ cible and were terrible in their exploits.
verses.hindi: कश्यय-ऋतु मुनि, महापद्य-कर्कोटक सपं, चित्रसेन-ऊर्गायु गन्धवं, उर्वशी-विप्रचित्ति अप्सरा, ताक्ष्यं, अरिष्टनेमि सेनानी; ग्रामणी, विद्युत्-स्फूर्ज राक्षस रहते हैं !२-१६९। फिर शिशिर ऋतु के माघ-फाग्रुत महीने में ये सब देव दो मास सूर्य के साथ निवास करते हैं त्वष्टा-विष्ण भादित्य, जमदस्नि-विश्वामित्र ऋषि, काद्रवेय- कम्बलाश्वतर सप, धृतरपष्ट्र-सूयंवर्चागन्धवं, देवी तिलोत्मा और मनोहारिणी रम्भा अप्सरा, विश्वविख्यात ऋतजित््-सध्यजित् ग्रामणी एवं ब्रह्मोपेत राक्षस ।२०-२३। सात श्रेणी के ये बारह देवता अर्थात् चोरासी देवता स्थानाभिमानी कहलाते हैं। ये अपने तेज से उत्तम तेज वाले सूर्य को समृद्ध करते हैं । मुनिगण अभिमत बचनों द्वारा सूयं की स्तुति करते हैं, गन्धववं और अप्सराएँ नृत्य-गीतों से उपासना करती हैं, ग्रामणी यज्ञ भूतादि भयद्भुरता का संग्रह करते हैं, सपंगण सु को ढोते हैं, राक्षस उनकी रक्षा करते हैं और बालखिल्य ऋषिगण उदय

verses.sanskrit: सपत्नीकान् नृपश्रेष्ठ चतुर्थ्यङ्गारके व्रते । पत्नीभर्तारसंयुक्तं विद्वांसं श्रोत्रियं द्विजम्
verses.transliteration: sapatnīkān nṛpaśreṣṭha caturthyaṅgārake vrate / patnībhartārasaṃyuktaṃ vidvāṃsaṃ śrotriyaṃ dvijam
verses.translation: Endowed with divine and worldly power, they move about on the entire earth. Since they are innumerable, the details of this creation cannot be recounted. The same Nila had a daughter, the demoness Vikaca, naturally devoid of hair and possessing mediocre strength and exploit. The same (Vikaca) bore terrible Asuras by the contact of the ugly Nairrta. Listen to them in order. They are Harakas, Bhisakas, Kramakas, Vainakas, Pisacas, Vahakas and Prasakas. All of them are hideous with their terrible fangs. They have huge ears and bellies. These are Bhumi-raksasas (Earthly Demons). They possess manly exploit though slow-witted. They assume multifarious forms and move about here and there unseen by others. Those whose strength and energy There are many terrible Bhutas having the same traits as their mother Putana. They harass children in the human world like the evil planets, causing dejectedness. There are hundreds of the groups of these evil (Raksasas) like the deceitful types of Skandagrahas and Bhutas named Pu tanas, lakhs and lakhs of them roaming about in There are Yaksas called Punyajanas and others called Guhyakas. There are still others called Devajanas. All these are included in the group of Guhyakas. There are Raksa¬ sas called Agastyas, Paulastyas and Visvamitras. The great king Kubera, the ruler of Alaka, is the king of all these Yaksas and Raksasas including Paulastyas and Agastyas. Yaksas drink blood, and swallow flesh and fat of men by merely looking at them. Raksasas do so by entering the body and Pisacas by crushing and harassing. All Guhyakas are inferior to Gandharvas by three- fourths. All Raksasas should be known as equal to Yaksas in prowess. Pisacas are three times less powerful in their AUvarya (prosperity and glory) than Yaksas. Thus in wealth, beauty, longevity, strength, righ¬ teousness, affluence, mastery, intellect, penance, learning and exploits, the four Devayonis, beginning with Gandharvas and ending with Pisacas are (consecutively) three-fourths inferior to Devas and Asuras. Welfare unto you. Henceforth, hear about the proge¬ ny of the family of Krodha. Krodha gave birth to twelve daughters. They became the wives of Pulaha. Understand them by name. They were—Mrgi, Mrgamanda, Haribhadra, Iravatl, Bhuta, Kapisa, Damstra, Nisa, Tirya, Sveta, Svara and Surasa. They are well-known. The sons of Mpgi were the different types of deer, viz. Karinas, Nyankus, Rurus and Prsalas as well as such other animals Verses 192-197 describe the gradation (in descending order) of the divine and semi-divine beings as follows: (Defective Verse) Only this elephant has the strength of being a vehicle, since it is born of water, has a single root six teeth and the lustre of gold. It is of the Bhadra variety of elephants.
verses.hindi: होते ही सूर्य की परिचर्या करने लगते हैं और उन्हें अस्ताचल पहुंचा देते हैं ।२४-२६। इन देवों का जैसा वीय॑े तप, योग, सत्य, और बल है, उसी के अनुसार सूर्य उनके तेज द्वारा तप्त होते हैं। ये सब दो दो महीने सूर्य

verses.sanskrit: व्रतान्ते चैव गौर्धुर्यैः शिवमुद्दिश्य दीयते । प्रीयतां मे महादेवः सपत्नीको वृषध्वजः
verses.transliteration: vratānte caiva gaurdhuryaiḥ śivamuddiśya dīyate / prīyatāṃ me mahādevaḥ sapatnīko vṛṣadhvajaḥ
verses.translation: Airavata had four sons, viz. Anjana, Supratlka, Va- mana and Padma. His mate was Abhramu. Sveta gave birth to four swift-footed sons who became the elephants of the quarters. They belonged to the varieties such as Bhadra, Mrga, Manda and Samklrna. Anjana, though belonging to the Sanklrna variety is the vehicle of Yama. Supratlka who belongs to the Bhadra variety and is green in colour is the vehicle of the Lord of Waters (Varuna). Padma which belongs to the Manda variety and is of white colour is the vehicle of Ailavila (Kubera). (Vamana) which was dark-coloured and belonged to the Mrga variety was the vehicle of the Fire-god (Agni). 2 (Defective) He has eight sons, viz. Padmottara The text is very corrupt and is translated tentatively in the light of Bd. P. vv. 332-33a. In his race elephants possessing lofty stature, white nails and hair, yellowish colour'are born. I shall recount Mata- ngaja and other (types) of elephants in due order. The elephant Pundarlka was grey-coloured and Rathanara had a flowery colour. Their sons were Supratistha and Pramardana. (Defective Verse) Other types of elephants—spear- shaped, stout, with raised heads, having white (?) hair and nails, strong and energetic. They are called Akulika elephants. Puspadanta, Brhatsaman, Saddanta, Dantapuspavan and Tamra varna were his sons and companion tuskers. * 1 In his family are born elephants beautiful in appeara¬ nce having protruding lips, dark-coloured, fierce and able to endure diverse kinds of ordeal (?) Vamadeva was as dark as collyrium. From Saman was bom Vamana. His wife was Angada and the two sons were Nilavan and Laksana. These elephants were fierce. Their necks and heads were beautiful. Their chests were broad and they were swift¬ footed. If they are bound by men, the elephants born become deformed. There is no other elephant equal to Supratlka in beauty. He had three sons, viz. Praharl, Sampatl and Prthu. The animals with long palate and lips and with symmetrical portions of head and belly, of gentle birth (?) bom in his family, become Matangajas. Anjana was bom to Anjana and Anjana vatl to Saman. The mother of both of them is reputed to be the daughter (s) of Ayurajas.
verses.hindi: ३४६ ...वायुपुराणमृ ऋषयो देवगन्धर्वाः पन्मगाप्सरसां गणा:। ग्रामण्यश्च तथा यक्षा यातुधानाश्च भुय्शः २६ एते तपन्ति वर्षन्ति भान्ति वान्ति सुजन्ति च। भूतानासशुभं कर्म व्यपोहन्तीह कीतिताः .

verses.transliteration: vastrayugmaṃ pradātavyaṃ lohitaṃ pāṇḍunandana / dhūrvahau raktavarṇau ca śubhraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tathaiva ca
verses.translation: In his family were bom elephants with (distinctly divided) symmetrical heads, resembling the smooth clouds. Pidapatdnanah in some editions is obscure and should be emended as Piidyaiananah 'with large and stout (big) faces (heads)as in Bd. P. V. 338. From Candramas and Saman were born Pingala and Kumudadyuti. Pihgala's sons were Mahapadma and Ormi- malin. Know that the elephants born of his family have equal and unrivalled tusks. They are fierce. Their strength is enormous. Their belly is large. They are fond of elephant fights. In the course of wars between Devas and Asuras, Suras used them for the purpose of victory. When they achieved their object, those elephants were let off by them and they went to different directions as mentioned before. Devas gave unto Lomapada, the king of Anga and author of a Sutra work, elephants born in these families and well-trained. (The various names of elephants are to be etymo¬ logically derived as follows:) The curvedness of their tongues and their muteness are due to Agni's curse. The fact that they are unaware of their strength and that the scrotum is concealed—these two are due to the curses of Svayambhu and Suras. Elephants of diverse inherent strengths are born of girls of Deva, Danava, Gandharva, Pisaca, Uraga (Ser¬ pent) and Raksasa tribes through their union with the ele¬ phants of the quarters ( Dih-nagas ). The story of the origin, development and derivation (Defective Verse) The forest in the east bound by the rivers Kausiki and Ganga and the sea belongs to Anjana and the family of elephants of which he is the founder (or of one tusk?). The forest of Supratlka is situated north of Vin- dhya, south of Ganga and in between the land of Karusa and the source of Ganga. The fifth forest west of Utkala and extending upto the land of Vedi is remembered as the forest of Vamana who is the sole Atman (?) The forest to the west of Lauhitya extending west¬ wards upto the sea, is said to be the forest of Yama. It is near a mountain. Bhuti gave birth to Bhutas (goblins) who are the followers of lord Rudra. They were stout, lean, longish, dwar¬ fish, short-statured and normal. The ears of some were hang¬ ing down. The lips of some were suspended. Some had tongues, breasts and bellies hanging down. Some had single form, some double form. The hips of some hung down. Some had stout calves of the leg. They stayed on the banks of rivers, lakes or seas. They were of all colours, black, white, blue, grey, red and pink. Some were smoke-coloured and some had variegated colours. Some were terrible like Raksasas and Kadrus (?). Some had dishevelled hair like the Munja grass. Some had hair standing up. Some wore serpents as the sacred thread. Some had eyes removed; some had hideous eyes. Some had small eyes. Somehad only a single eye. Some had many heads. Some had no head. Somehad a single head. Some had the head cut off. They were fierce and hideous. Some had no hair. Some had plenty of it. Some were blind. Some had matted hair. Some were yellow. Some were dwarfish. They resorted to the banks of rivers, lakes an oceans. Some had a single ear, some had large ears. Some were spike-eared, some had no ear. Some had fangs. Some had claws. Some had no teeth. Some had two tongues. Some had a All of them directed their minds towards lord Bhava (Siva) as the greatest god. They had no wives or sons. All of them were celibate with sublimated sexuality.

verses.transliteration: chatraṃ śayyāṃ śubhāṃ caiva raktamālyānulepanam / dātavyaṃ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭha viśuddhenāntarātmanā
verses.translation: These Bhutas, the great Almayogins, numbered a hund¬ red thousand. Thus all these noble-souled sons of Bhuti have been recounted. Kapisa, Kusmandl bore to Kusmanda twins of Pis¬ acas who were tawny-coloured. Because they were brownish, they were called Pisacas. 2 All of them were flesh-eaters. There are sixteen other twins. Their descendants are living now. I shall mention by names the man-eaters belonging to their family. They are Chagala and Chagall, Vakra and Vakra- mukhi, Sue! and Suclmukha, Kumbhapatra and Kumbhl, Bd. 3.7.367 reads sumanaska 'of very good minds*. The Purana distinguishes between Bhutas and Pisacas. Bhutas are noble-souled sons of Bhuti, celibate yogins and devotees of God Siva. Pisacas arc the progeny of Kusmandl. The superstitions about Pisacas current at the time of this text are recorded in vv. 251-282. These are the sixteen families born of Kusman- das: Ajamukhas, Vakramukhas, Purins, Skandins, Vipa- das, Angarikas, Kumbhapatras, Prakundakas, Upacarolukha- likas, Anarkas, Kukhandikas, Panipatras, Naitundas, Ornasas, Nipunas, and Sucimukhocchesanadas. Those who are born as Sukalpas 1 (?) should be known as Pisacas. There are infinite number of sons and grandsons of hideous nature and ignoble activities. Hence, understand the characteristics of Pisacas. Pisacas have hair on all their limbs. Their eyes are round. They have claws and fangs. Their limbs are crooked. They are man-eaters and their faces are turned down. The Pisacas called Kusmandikas are devoid of hair on their heads or bodies. Skins and hides constitute their garments. They always eat gingelly seeds and flesh. Some Pis'acas have curved limbs, and feet. They walk in a zigzag manner. They should be known as Vakrapisacas. They are of crooked gait. They can assume any form as they please. Some Pisacas have protruding bellies. Their noses are like snouts. Their bodies are short. Their heads and arms are small. These are called Nitunflakas. Gingelly seeds form Some Pisacas have dwarfish forms 3. They are garrulous. They go about galloping. They are Anarkamarka Some Pisacas keep their hands lifted up (always). Bd.P. V. 390 reads Vanardhtayah -having the form of monkeys'.
