verses.sanskrit: चतुर्थ्यां तु तथाष्टम्यां पक्षयोः शुक्लकृष्णयोः । श्राद्धं तत्रैव कर्तव्यं वित्तशाठ्येन वर्जितः
verses.transliteration: caturthyāṃ tu tathāṣṭamyāṃ pakṣayoḥ śuklakṛṣṇayoḥ / śrāddhaṃ tatraiva kartavyaṃ vittaśāṭhyena varjitaḥ
verses.translation: The Pisacas called Upaviras are very considerate about their veins*. Their bodies are dry. They have plenty of moustache. They wear bark garments. Cremation ground is their abode. The Udukhala (Ulukhala) types of Pisacas have stable motionless eyes and long tongues with which they lick their lips. Their heads are as large as those of elephants and camels. They move about severally or jointly. Those Pisacas are called Kumbhapatras, who take cooked food without seeing it (invisibly?). They are small and yellow-complcxioned with hairy bodies. They move about visibly and invisibly. The Pisacas called Nipunas enter and infest those persons who go alone. Their mouths extend upto their ears. The eye-brows are long and the noses are thick. (A line is missing from the text.) The Pisacas called Baladas (devourers of children) are short-statured and they attack people with their hands and feet. Their eyes are turned towards the earth. They resort to lying-in-chambers. Those Pisacas called Pisitadas (flesh eaters) drink blood from the battlefield. Their hands and feet are turned back¬ wards. They are short and are as swift as wind. The Pisacas called Skandins are naked and have no fixed abodes. They are globular in shape with long hair. There are other types of Pisacas eating leavings of food. Thus the sixteen types of Pisacas have been narrated. On seeing these types of Pisacas deficient in intellect and in a dejected condition among his progeny, Brahma sym¬ pathetically granted them the boons of vanishing and assuming forms as they pleased. He permitted them to move about at the time of the two junctions (viz. dawn and dusk). (I shall mention) their abodes and way of maintaining themselves. Houses in Unrighteous persons, those who violate the dis¬ cipline of castes and stages of life and artisans and masons constitute the livelihood of these Pisacas as ordained by Suras. These Pisacas will be the presiding deities where holy rites are performed by means of money earned by unjustifiable means such as breach of trust and theft of nectar-like articles. The oblations to Pisacas consist of honey (wine), flesh, cooked rice mixed with curds, powdered gingelly seeds, toddies and similar (intoxicating) beverages, incense, turmeric, Krsaras (i.e. balls of gingelly seeds in treacle), oil, rice mixed with jaggery, black cloths and flowers. At the junctions of Parvans, these things must be offered to Pisacas. Brahma, the lord, ordained thus. He made the trident-bearing Girisa the lord of all Bhutas and Pisacas. Panthers, pythons and beasts of prey are also her sons. Mina, Mata, Vrtta, Pari vrtta and Anuvrtta are to be known (as her daughters). Listen to (the enumeration of) her children: Sharks and crocodiles with a thousand teeth, the types of fish known as Pathina, Timi and Rohita and other groups are called Maina (born of Mina) groups. They are extensive. The four types of Grdhas (crocodiles) —Anujyestha- kas, Niskas, Sisumaras etc. were born of Mata.
verses.hindi: के निकट निवास करते हैं । ऋषि, देव, गन्धव, सर्प अप्सरा, ग्रामणी, यज्ञ और राक्षसगण ही तपते हैं, चमकते है. वायू की तरह बहते हैं और जीवों के शुभाशुभ कर्म का उत्पादन करके उसका विनाश भी करते हैं (२७-३०। कभी ये मानवों के शुभ कार्य का अपहरण करते हैं और कभी पापियों के पापका नाश करते हैं। वायु के समान वेगवाले ये देवषण दिव्य विमान पर चढ़कर सूर्य के साथ प्रतिदिन गमन करते हैं। प्रलयकाल पयेनत ये सभी
verses.wordMeaning: The Pisacas called Upaviras are very considerate about their veins*. Their bodies are dry. They have plenty of moustache. They wear bark garments. Cremation ground is their abode.…
verses.commentary: Sense: The Pisacas called Upaviras are very considerate about their veins*. Their bodies are dry. They have plenty of moustache. They wear bark garments. Cremation ground is their abode.…

verses.sanskrit: प्रेता भवन्ति सुप्रीता युगमेकं महीपते । सपुत्रो जायते मर्त्यः प्रतिजन्म नृपोत्तम
verses.transliteration: pretā bhavanti suprītā yugamekaṃ mahīpate / saputro jāyate martyaḥ pratijanma nṛpottama
verses.translation: Vrtta gave birth to different types of tortoises and other aquatic animals as well as varieties of conches. Anuvrtta gave birth to different types of toads and Parivrtta gave birth to different varieties of oyster- shells, cowrie-shells and conchs. She produced the varieties of Kalakuta poison and leeches as well. Thus the race of Rsa consisting of five branches has been enumerated. O Brahmanas, these insects are born of the bodies of Svastipika 2 (?). The producers are human beings. The insects known as Usanas are born of dirt and sweat of men. So also the other insects and groups of ants moving about in rows. There are varieties of insects born of conchs, pebbles which work like nails. 3 These and many others are the earthly groups of sweat-born creatures. Similarly, these creatures are born out of water heated by the sun as well as of the rain water. Many of these insects are born of the bodies of other animals. The following tiny creatures are born both of water and of sweat: Small shrimps (minaka), ants, (mosquito¬ like) biting or stinging creatures (darhia), Tittira-pulrikas (tiny partridge-like creatures?). The Alakas (hair) are bluish or variegated in colour (nila-citrah) and very massive. The line is corrupt. The corresponding line in Bd. P. V. 421 reads 2 lirydhetukam apydhur bahulam uamia-vistaraml 'They say that there is an extensive line of living beings procreated by Tirya'. This obscure word is a misprint for ' Svtda-Klinna 'born of bodies mois- stened by sweat' (vid Bd. P. V. 422). Kilakdcarakdni 'which work lik nails' in the text is rather obscure. Bd. P. V. 423 b reads kilakavaranani 'Pebbles smaller than pins'. Some creatures are born of ghee, black gram and green gram. Some are born of the fruits of Jamb u (Rose apple) Bilva, mango and arecanut. Creatures are born of the dry hollows of trees and also of green gram, jack fruits and rice grains when kept (for a long time). Creatures are born of other things also when kept for a long time. Germs and worms are born of horses and other (animals) and even from poison etc. When cowdung is kept for a number of days, O Brahmanas, creatures are produced from them. White ants and other creatures are born of (putrefying) wood.
verses.hindi: जीवों की रक्षा करते है और प्रजाजन को वृष्टि तथा ताप द्वारा प्रसन्न करते हैं।३१-३३॥ इन स्थानाभिमानी देवों का यह स्थान भूत, भविष्य और वर्तमान सभी मन्वतरों में एक सा रहता है। ये देव सप्तक चौदहों मन्वन्तर के समय में सूर्य के चारों तरफ इसी प्रकार निवास करते हैँ। भगवान् भुवन-भास्कर ऋतुकाल के अनुसार किरणों को बदल-बदल कर देवता, पितर और मनुष्यों को तृप्त किया करते हैं।३४ ३६। वे ग्रीष्म ऋतु में घाम. जाड़े में ठंढक और बरसात में पानी बरसा कर दिन-रात का विभाग किया करते हैं । सूर्य देव अपनी सृषुम्न किरण द्वारा चन्द्रमा को बढ़ाते हैं और देवों को अमृत पिलाकर सनन्‍्तुष्ट करते हैं । दिवसक्रम से जब चन्द्रमा शुक्लपक्ष में पूर्ण हो जाते. हैं, तब क्ृष्णपक्ष में देवगण उन्हें अर्थात् उनके अमृत को पी जाते हैं । पिये जाने पर दो कलामात्र होष सोम क्ृष्णपक्ष के बीतने पर जिस किरण का क्षरण करते हैं, उस अमृतरूपी
verses.wordMeaning: Vrtta gave birth to different types of tortoises and other aquatic animals as well as varieties of conches. Anuvrtta gave birth to different types of toads and Parivrtta gave birth to different varieties of oyster- shells, cowrie-shells and conchs.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Vrtta gave birth to different types of tortoises and other aquatic animals as well as varieties of conches. Anuvrtta gave birth to different types of toads and Parivrtta gave birth to different varieties of oyster- shells, cowrie-shells and conchs.…

verses.sanskrit: तस्य तीर्थस्य भावेन सर्वाङ्गरुचिरो नृप । मङ्गलं भवते वंशो नाशुभं विद्यते क्वचित्
verses.transliteration: tasya tīrthasya bhāvena sarvāṅgaruciro nṛpa / maṅgalaṃ bhavate vaṃśo nāśubhaṃ vidyate kvacit
verses.translation: Various kinds of blue flies are born of trees in due course. The creatures Putrikas (white ants?) are born of drying and withering things. Everywhere serpents are born seasonally from Satikas (?). Scorpions and sweat-born creatures are produced from dry cow-dung. Different types of leeches are born of eggs such as Caivtrikas and Gajas and many other subtle creatures too. Different types of flies etc. are born of eggs. These are laid generally on the leavings of food, water and sloughs. Different types of mosquitoes and black bees are also born of eggs. The creatures known as nits {Putrikas and Putra- bhasakas) are produced from grass. The insects Manicchedas and Vyalas are said to be produced from foetus with no enveloping membrane ( potajas ). Varieties of Salaveri (?) are born of dry cow-dung. Thus innumerable groups of sweat-born creatures have been enumerated by me in brief. It is to be remembered that these are born as a result of their actions in a previous birth. There are other beings of Nairfta nature (i.e. born of Nirpti). They are remembered as Upasargajas (born of paroxysm due to possession by devils). Some beings are born of womb {Tonijas) and some are Autpaltikas (born spontaneously). Generally all Devas are to be known as Autpaltikas. Some The children of Sarama are the sons Tulalagha and TheKadrukas (?) are Sydma (dark-coloured), Sabala (ofvariegated colour), Arjuna (white), Harita (green-coloured), Krsna (black), Dhumraruna (smoke-coloured and pink-coloured— Aruna), Tulalagha (?). Surasa gave birth to a hundred (serpents) with nectar in their heads (Siro'm T tam). The king ofSarpas (serpents) is Taksaka and that of the snakes is Vasuki. Thus this group Now understand the bosom creation of Pulaha from Tamra. Many well-known daughters were born of Tamra. Sampati procreated one son and one daughter. Crows, vultures and ASvakarnins (a variety of vultures?) were the sons of Jatayu. The wives of Garutman (Garuda) were Bhasi, Kraunci, Sukl, Dhrtarastri and Bhadra. Their sons are being enumerated. Suki bore six well known sons to Garutman, viz. the sweet-faced Tris'ira, Bala, Pr?tha of great strength,* Trisahkhanetra, Susukha of good form and Surasa the power¬ ful. The sons and grandsons of these ruthless descendants of Garuda, the noble-souled serpent-eaters, numbering fourteen thousand. By procreation of sons and grandsons their family became extensive. I shall mention in due order the lands where they spread themselves—the whole of Salmall Dvipa, the mountain Devakuta, the leading mountains Maniman, Sahasra-sikhara, Parnamala, Sukesa, Satasniga, Kauraja, Pancasikhara and Hemakuta—all these mountains were occupied by the noble- souled descendants of Garuda. They were brightened with ruby stones and (while flying) they produced gusts of violent winds.
verses.hindi: किरण को पितर लोग स्वधा समझकर पीते हैँ और देवगण उसे कव्य समझकर पीते हैं ।३७-३८। फिर सूर्य

verses.sanskrit: भक्त्या यः कीर्तयेन् नित्यं तस्य पापं व्यपोहति
verses.transliteration: bhaktyā yaḥ kīrtayen nityaṃ tasya pāpaṃ vyapohati
verses.translation: Garutfa's children have been enumerated. Listen to the progeny of Ira. Ira gave birth to three daughters with eyes They were Lata, Valll and Vlrudha. They are the mothers of all types of plants, trees and creepers. Lata gave birth to Vanaspalis i.e. the non-flowering plants growing on the banks of rivers etc. She herself gave birth to Vfksas or trees with flowers and fruits. Valli gave birth to hedges, grasses and bamboo etc. of the-same species. Vlrudha gave birth to Virudhas i.e. creepers spreading all round. The description of the race is concluded Thus the mobile and the immobile progeny of Kas- yapa have been enumerated. The whole Universe is filled with their sons and grandsons. Thus a portion of the entire creation has been enumerat¬ ed. The Prajasarga of Marica (KaSyapa) has been succinctly narrated. O Brahmanas, it cannot be explained (in details) even in hundreds of years. Aditi was of righteous, pious temperament. Diti is -re¬ membered as strong-minded. Surabhi was inclined towards the performance of penance. Danu was of a deceitful nature. Kadru was of ruthless mind. KrauncI was disposed towards learning. Ira had the receptive capacity. Danayu was interested in taking food. Vinata was capable of bearing burdens. Tamra was habituated to use nooses and strings. These are the natures and temperaments of the mothers of the worlds. The bosom-born progeny of Kasyapa were born with Since these were born of the daughters of Daksa who were human beings, hence human beings are the most excellent in all the Manvantaras. Human beings are the aspirants of Dharma (Virtue) Artha(Wealth), Kama (Love) and Moksa (Salvation). There- fore, Suras and Asuras are born as Adhah-srotas (downward flow). They are born again and again among human beings for the purpose of achieving their object. Thus the origin of the race of ascetics has been recounted. The meritorious story of Suras, Asuras, Gan¬ dharvas, Apsaras-s, Yaksas, Raksasas, Pisacas, Suparnas, ser¬ pents, birds, pythons, peacocks, all medicinal herbs, worms, germs, insects, insignificant creatures born in water, animals and glorious Brahmanas, is conducive to longevity and wealth. It is pleasing and beneficial. It is meritorious. It must be heard always and retained by one who is devoid of malice and jealousy. He who regularly reads this story of the race (of ascetics) of noble souls in the assembly of Brahmanas and physi¬ cians will attain children, abundant wealth and prosperity and the glorious goal after death.
verses.hindi: विसगंकाले विसुजंश्व ताः पुनविर्भात शश्वत्सविता चराचरम् ४ १ अहोरात्राद्रथेनाइसों एकचक्रेण तु भ्रमन् । सप्तद्वीसमुद्राश्य सप्तभिः सप्तभिहंये:

verses.sanskrit: ॥ इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे मङ्गलेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकोनसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ र्क्व् अध्याय ७० श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: रेवाया उत्तरे कूले तीर्थं परमशोभनम् । रविणा निर्मितं पार्थ सर्वपापक्षयंकरम्
verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe maṅgaleśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 70 śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: revāyā uttare kūle tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam / raviṇā nirmitaṃ pārtha sarvapāpakṣayaṃkaram
verses.translation: Thus when the entire mobile and immobile crea¬ tions had been created and established by the noblc-souled Kasyapa, he the chief Prajapati, crowned (the chiefs of them) He made Prahlada, the delighter of Diti, the king of Daityas: Narayana the king of Sadhyas; and the Bull- bannered lord (Siva) the king of Rudras. He directed Vipracitti to be the king of Danavas. He ordered Varuna to be the king of waters. He made Vaisravana (Kubera) the lord of Yaksas, Raksasas and the wealth of (worldly) kings. He coronated Yama, the son of Vivasvan (the Sun), in He made Himavan the ruler of mountains; ocean, of the rivers; and Citraratha the ruler of Gandharvas. He crowned Uccaissravas as the king of horses, tiger as the king of deer and cows, and bulls the lords of quadrupeds. He made Garufla the most excellent among flying be¬ ings, the lord of all birds. He made Maruta the lord of scents and unembodied beings. He made Vayu, the most excellent among strong be¬ ings, the lord of sound, sky and strength. He made Sesa, the lord of allfanged (reptiles), and Vasuki the lord of serpents. He made Taksaka, the lord of vipers, serpents and reptiles. He crowned Parjanya, one of the Adityas, as the lord of oceans, rivers, clouds and rains. He crowned Kamadeva the king of all groups of Apsaras-s. Verses 1-20 enumerate the heads of different categories of creation. Here one is reminded of the Vibhutiyoga (BG.X). The Prajapati crowned Sudhaman, the famous son of Rajas, as the king in the eastern quarter. In the western quarter, he crowned the noble-souled Ketuman, the unerring son of Rajas, the king. He made Vaivasvata Manu the lord of human beings. The entire earth consisting of seven continents along with the towns therein, is being ruled righteously by them in their res¬ pective areas. They had been crowned formerly by Brahma in the Svayambhuva Manvantara. Only those who become Manu are consecrated as kings. In the Manvantaras that have passed, these kings (had ruled and) passed away. When the Manvantaras occur again, others will be crowned again. All the kings, past and future, are proclaimed as Lords of Manvantaras. Prthu was crowned by these excellent men at the time of Rajasuya. The valorous king was made so in accordance with the injunctions of the Vedas. The lord of Prajas, Kasyapa, procreated these sons, for the purpose of the continuity of the progeny. Thereafter, desirous of his own lineage, he performed a severe penance. He contemplated—"May sons, the founders of the lineage, be born to me".
verses.hindi: बाह्ममभ्यन्तरं चंब मण्डल दिवसक्रमात् । कल्पादो संप्रयुक्तास्ते वहन्त्याभुतसंप्लबात्॥ द आवत्ता बालखिल्यस्ते भ्रमन्ते राज्यहाणि तु

verses.sanskrit: स्वांशेन भास्करस्तत्र तिष्ठते चोत्तरे तटे । सर्वव्याधिहरः पुंसां नर्मदायां व्यवस्थितः
verses.transliteration: svāṃśena bhāskarastatra tiṣṭhate cottare taṭe / sarvavyādhiharaḥ puṃsāṃ narmadāyāṃ vyavasthitaḥ
verses.translation: As Kasyapa, the noble soul, contemplated, two power¬ ful sons born of Brahma's part were born to him. They were Vatsara and Asita. Both of them were pro¬ pounders of Brahman. Nidhruva and Raibhya of great fame were born of Vatsara. The Raibhyas should be known as the (descendants) of Raibhya. Understand (those) of Nidhruva. Gyavana begot Sumcdhas of Sukanya. Nidhruva's wife 1 was the mother of Kundapayins. Brahniistha (Devala in Bd.P.) was born of Ekaparna and Asita. On hearing (i.e. paying heed to) the words of Sandilya, Devala became excessively famous. Nidhruvas, Sandilyas and Raibhyas all these three formed the Kas- yapa Gotra later 2. Vara (Vajri i.e. Indra in Bd. P.) and other Devas are the progeny of Devala. These subjects function in Dvapara Yuga that remains (i.e. occurs) after eleven cycles of the sets of four Yugas have passed. Carisyanta (Nairisyanta in Bd. P.) was the son of Manasa and his son was Dama. Manasa who was well-known as Tfnabindu, was his heir and successor. In the beginning of the third Treta Yuga, he became the king. His daughter Idavida was unrivalled in her beauty. The saintly king gave her to Pulastya. The sage Visravas was born of Idavida. He had four wives who made the family of Pulastya flourish. Brhaspati, the preceptor of the Devas, had a famous daughter named Devavarnini. He (Visravas) married that girl. He (Visravas) married Puspotkata and Vaka, the daughters of Malyavan as well as Kaikasi, the daughter of Malin. Listen to their progeny. Devavarnini gave birth to his eldest son Vaisravana who had divine fate and saintly learning, (but) had the form of a Raksasa and the strength of an Asura. He had three feet, a huge body, stout head, a large chin 3, eight fangs, green moustache, pike-like ears and red com¬ plexion. His arms were short and long (i.e. one short, one long). He was yellowish in colour (?) and very terrible to look at. He had the knowledge of the illusory world. He was enlight¬ ened with knowledge. Sumcdhas as per Bd. P. iMn in the text is a tautology. It should be maM-hanum as in On seeing such a son assuming a cosmic form, the father himself said—"This is Kubera (ugly-bodied one) ". 1 The word 'Ku' is used to indicate contempt. The body is mentioned by the word Bera. Hence he is called Kubera be¬ cause his body was deformed. Since he was the child of Visravas and he appeared like Visravas, he will be known in the world by the name Vaisravana.
verses.hindi: की किरणों से हौ जल उत्पन्न होता है  वृष्टि से ओषधि और अन्न उत्पन्न होते हैं. जिनमें मानव अपनी क्षधा शान्त करते हैं । देवों को अमृत से अर्द्ध मास तक तृप्ति होती है और पितरों को भी स्व्रधा से आधे मास तक । किन्तु मनुष्यों को अन्न के द्वारा सदा तृप्ति मिलती है. क्‍योंकि सूर्य किरणों से अन्न को पुष्ट किया करते हैं। सूर्य हरिद्वण के अश्वों पर चढ़ कर किरणों द्वारा जल का शोषण करते हैं। फिर वर्षाकाल में जल बरसाकर सूयंदेव चराचर का पोषण करते हैं ।३६-४१। सूय हरिद्वर्ण के घोड़े पर चढ़कर हजारों किरणों से जल का शोषण करते हैं फिर हरिद्वर्ण के धोड़े पर घूमते हुये वे जल बरसा देते हैं। इस प्रकार प्रलयकाल तक सूर्य देव एक चकक्‍के के रथ पर सवार होकर मंगलकारक बलिष्ठ अश्वों द्वारा वेग से आकाश में भ्रमण करते हैं। सूर्थ एक चक्र रथ द्वारा समुद्रान्त सातों द्वीपोंवाली पृथ्वी का भ्रमण दिन-रात किया करते हैं ।४२-४४। उनके
verses.wordMeaning: As Kasyapa, the noble soul, contemplated, two power¬ ful sons born of Brahma's part were born to him. They were Vatsara and Asita. Both of them were pro¬ pounders of Brahman. Nidhruva and Raibhya of great fame were born of Vatsara.…

verses.sanskrit: षष्ठ्यांषष्ठ्यां नृपश्रेष्ठ ह्यष्टम्यां च चतुर्दशीम् । स्नानं यः कारयेन्मर्त्यः श्राद्धं प्रेतेषु भक्तितः । तस्य पापक्षयः पार्थ सूर्यलोके महीयते
verses.transliteration: ṣaṣṭhyāṃṣaṣṭhyāṃ nṛpaśreṣṭha hyaṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśīm / snānaṃ yaḥ kārayenmartyaḥ śrāddhaṃ preteṣu bhaktitaḥ / tasya pāpakṣayaḥ pārtha sūryaloke mahīyate
verses.translation: Kubera begot of Rddhi the famous (son) Nalakubara. Kaikasi gave birth to four children Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Vibhlsana (the three sons and) a daughter Surpanakha. His span of life as reckoned by Brahmanas, experts in calculation, extended to five crores and sixtyone lakhs of years. For sixty lakhs of years 3, this Ravana made Devas and Sages terribly sleepless (by means of his atrocities). In the twenty-fourth Tretayuga, when his merit of penance declin¬ ed, he met Rama, the son of Dasaratha, (in battle) and was slain along with his followers. Etymology of'Kubera*, the god of wealth. The Purana-writer entertained fantastic ideas about Ravana. Jaina Raraayanas give a sober and a more realistic picture of Ravana, e.g. Ravana was one-headed but due to the reflection of his face in the nine precious stones of his necklace, he was (poetically) called 'ten-headed*. Ravana's harrasment is not thus delimited elsewhere. It should be a part of his span of life. Bd. 3.8.53 correctly reads Satfim caiva sahasrayi 'sixty thousand years' as a part of Ravana's total life. For, a set of the four Yugas=4320000 years, thirteen such sets=56160000 years. Ravaria is credited with this span. Mahodara, Prahasta, Mahapariisu and Khara were the sons of Puspotkata and Kumbhlnasl was her daughter. Trisiras, Dusana, the Raksasa Vidyujjihva and the daughter Asalika are remembered as the children of Vaka. These are the ten Raksasa descendants of Pulastya. They were cruel in their activities. All of their followers were terrible and unassailable even by Devas. All of them had secured boons. All of them were endowed with sons and grandsons. Thus, there are seven classes of Raksasas (including the above three and the following four groups): Panlastyas, Nairrtas, Agastyas and Kausikas. I shall describe the natural features of all these* (Raksasas) 1: They had round eyes. They were yellowish in colour. They had huge bodies and bellies. They had eight fangs; pikelike ears and hairs standing upright. They had their mouths extending (as if) upto the ears. Some had hair like the Munja grass. Some had smoke-coloured upright hair. Some had stout heads shedding white lustre. Some were short-statured. Some had long arms. Some had copper-coloured faces. Some had long (dangling down) tongues and lips. Some had long eyebrows and stout noses. Some were blue-bodied with red necks and majestic eyes. They were terrific. They were excessively terrible-voiced and hideous. They went in groups. They were stout with promi- Superstitions about Raksasas The deer, all the fanged beasts of prey, Bhutas, Pisacas, serpents, bees, elephants, monkeys, Kinnaras, Yamakimpurusas 1 (?) and all those mentioned by me as born of Krodhavasa—all these were Pulaha's sons. In that Vaivasvata Manvantara, Kratu is remembered as childless. He had neither a son nor a grandson. He remained with fully controlled splendour (semen) (i.e. He was celibate). I shall now recount the lineage of Atri 2, the third Praja- pati. He had ten chaste and beautiful wives. Bhadrasva begot of Ghftacl the Apsaras, ten daugh¬ ters. They were:Bhadra, Sudra, Madra, Salada, Malada, Vela, Khala, these seven and Gocapala, Manarasa and Ratnakuta. The founder of the lineage of Atri was famous by the name of Prabhakara (the originator of lustre). He was their husband. He begot of Bhadra, the famous son Soma (the Moon). When the Sun, struck by Rahu, was falling down to¬ wards the earth from the sky, the whole world was enveloped in darkness and it was he (the sage Atri) who spread light every¬ where whereby be got the name Prabhakara. While the Sun was falling the words 'welfare unto you' were addressed to him. At these words of the Brahmana sage Atri (the Sun) did not fall on the earth from heaven.
verses.hindi: बेगवाले, ब्रह्मवगादी, समर्थ, हरित्पिज्ग्ल वर्ण के और रथ में एक ही बार जोते गये हैं। वे घोड़े एक वष में एक सौ अस्सीमंडल का परिभ्रण किया करते हैं ।४५-४६। कल्प के आदि में धोड़े एक बार जोते गये हैं और कल्पान्त तक वे रथ को खींचते रहते हैं। इस तरह वे दिवसक्रम से बाह्य और आशभ्यन्तर मण्डलों का परिभ्रण

verses.sanskrit: ततः स्वर्गाच्च्युतः सो ऽपि जायते विमले कुले । धनाढ्यो व्याधिनिर्मुक्तो जीवेज्जन्मनिजन्मनि
verses.transliteration: tataḥ svargāccyutaḥ so 'pi jāyate vimale kule / dhanāḍhyo vyādhinirmukto jīvejjanmanijanmani
verses.translation: Atri who was the performer of great penance founded excellent Gotras. Among Yajnas (the one called) Atrighana (?) is initiated by Suras. The race of Atri is described in vv. 67-78. He begot of them ten sons, all equal to him. They had no names. All the ten were purified by great penance. They were the sages famous by the name 'Svastyatrcyas. They were mas¬ ters of Vedas. Among them, two were very famous, powerful and expounders of Brahman the eldest was Dattalreya and Durvasas was his younger brother. The youngest daughter was Abala who expounded Brahman. In this connection, the for¬ mer (ancient) Pauranikas cite this verse. Those who arc conversant with Puranas say that Atri's son Dattatreya is embodied Visnu. The noble-souled one is free from sins and tranquil in mind. Four persons born in his spiritual lineage were famous on the earth. They were- Syamas, Mudgalas, Balarakas and Gavisthiras. These are remembered as the groups of very power- fill men. From Kasyapa Narada, Parvata and Arundhati were born. O excellent ones, (listen to and) understand (thesons)of Arundhati. Narada gave Arundhati (in marriage) to Vasistha. 1 Due to the curse of Daksa, the brilliant Narada (was compel¬ led to be) celibate. Formerly when there was a great battle between Devas and Asuras, called Tarakamava, the whole world was op¬ pressed by drought and Sakra was aggrieved along with Suras. The intelligent Vasistha sustained all the subjects by means of his penance. Making use of the medicinal herbs, fruits and roots (the sage) sympathetically enlivened them. (Defective Verse) O Brahmanas, Vasistha begot Sakti of Arundhati. Ad r syanti (wife of Sakti) bore Parara to Sakti on the seashore (?) Kali bore K r?nadvaipayana, the holy lord, to Parasara. FromDvaipayana, Suka, endowed with good qualities, was born, The following six children were born of Plvar! to Suka: five sons, viz. Bhurisravas, Prabhu, Sambhu, Krsna and Gaura and a daughter Kirtimati by name. She was firm'in her holy rites and a Yogic mother. She was the wife of Sattvaguha and the mother of Brahmadatta. 1 here were eight groups (spiritual lineage) of Parasaras of noble souls. They were Svetas, Kfsnas, Gauras, Syamas, Dhumras, Samfilikas, Darakas, the imbibers of hot ' (drinks?/ (Osmapas) and Nilas. Henceforth, understand the progeny of Indrapratima. Kusiti, who was bom of Kapinjall-GhrtacI to Vasistha is called Indrapratima. Vasu was his son born of Pflhu's daughter. Upamanyu was his son whose (descendants) were these Upamanyus. Kundins who were famous as descendants of Mitra- Varuna have one spiritual lineage. Others are well-known as Vasisthas. These are the eleven Gotras of Vasisthas. Thus these eight renowned mental sons of Brahma have been recounted. They were blessed brothers and their spiritual lineages have been established. They sustain these three worlds consisting of groups of Dcvas and sages. Their sons and grandsons are hundreds and thousands. By them the entire Earth is pervaded as with the rays of the Sun.
verses.hindi: ३८ वायुपुर्राणम् प्रधितेवंचोभिरपये: स्तुयमानो महर्षिभिः । सेव्यते गीतनुत्येश्व गन्धर्वेरप्सरोगंणेः ॥

verses.sanskrit: ॥ इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे रवितीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम सप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ र्क्व् अध्याय ७१ श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: कामेश्वरं ततश्चान्यच्छृणु पाण्डवसत्तम । सिद्धो यत्र गणाध्यक्षो गौरीपुत्रो महाबलः
verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe ravitīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma saptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 71 śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: kāmeśvaraṃ tataścānyacchṛṇu pāṇḍavasattama / siddho yatra gaṇādhyakṣo gaurīputro mahābalaḥ
verses.translation: After hearing this narrative of Su ta, the knower of Atman, the Brahmanas, subsequently asked him as follows: Sraddha is a form of ancestor worship. It is based on the belief in after-death survival of the deceased ancestors and their residence in a parti¬ cular region called Pitr-loka. It is an important topic and forms an integral part of Hindu Dharmasastra. This belief is pre-Vcdic as it dates back to the Indo-Iranian period {vide S.B.E. IV, ). Ancestor-worship was regarded essential for the continuation of one's race and prosperity to How was BhavanI who was formerly Satl, born for the second time? She was DaksayanI at first. How did she become (Who are the Pitrs) whose grandson was Mainaka and whose grand-daughters wei'e Uma, Ekaparna, Ekapatala and Gaiiga, the most excellent one among rivers as well as the eldest of them all? Even before this, all this has been already desired to be pointed out (by you). Please listen to all my requests. Are there many Pitrs P * 1 And then where do they stay? Welfare unto you. I wish to hear the great procedure of Sraddha. Whose sons are they (Pitrs) remembered to be? How are they the Pitrs? How were the Pitrs born and whose sons were they? Of what nature are they? Are there other Pitrs who are deities (i.e. worthy of wor¬ ship) unto the Devas in heaven? Thus I wish to hear the excellent creation of Pitrs and how the Sraddha performed by us (as per prescribed injunctions) propitiates Pitrs. What is regarded (in the Smrtis) as the reason of their being not visible? What types of Pitrs stay in heaven and what types in hell? What Sraddhas are to be offered (to Pitrs)? How do these Sraddhas reach Pitrs—the Sraddhas that are offered uttering the names of father, father's father and great¬ grandfather against the three ricc-balls (Pintfas)? How are they (Pitrs), if stationed in hell, competent to grant benefits? Who are these called by the name' Pitrs? Whom shall we worship again? We have heard that even Devas in heaven worship Pitrs. O extremely learned one, we wish to hear this in de¬ tail. It behoves you to explain the significance of this clearly. On hearing the words of the sages, Suta, the seer of reality, said in accordance with the questions and the desire in the minds of the sages. I shall describe to you (in detail) what I have heard (regaxding Sraddha), in accordance with my intellectual ability. In every Manvantara, Pitrs are born as the sons of Devas.' In the past and the future Manvantaras, they are respectively the eldest and the youngest. I shall precisely recount the Pitrs who have gone in the past Manvantaras along with Devas and who exist at present, They were cursed by Brahma—"O deluded ones! You will all become devoid of sense." They did not know anything. Then the whole world became deluded. All of them bowed to god Brahma and implored him. In order to bless the worlds, the lord spoke to them again. "Perform expiatory rites for the transgression which has been committed. Ask your sons and therefrom you will attain knowledge." Desirous of knowing (the procedure of) expiatory rites, Devas controlled themselves duly and asked their own sons mutually. Those sons who were conversant with real Dharma and possessed self-control, explained to them the various modes of expiatory rites—verbal, mental and physical. The heaven-dwellers who regained their senses became delighted and spoke to their sons—"You are our fathers (Pitrs), since we are enlightened by you. What boon should be granted— virtue, knowledge or love?". Then Brahma spoke to them—"You are the speakers of truth. Hence what is spoken by you shall be so and not otherwise. This is what is uttered by you—your own sons have been mentioned by you as your Pitrs (fathers;. They will be your Pitrs. Let this boon be given to them." On account of the words of Brahma, Paramesthin, the sons (Pitrs) attained the status of fathers (of Devas) and Devas, the real fathers, the status of sons. Hence it is declared (in Dharma-Sastra) that the sons (of Devas) are Pitrs and the status of Pitr-hood is proclai¬ med about them. "If anyone will perform any holy rite without worship¬ ping Pitrs in a Sraddha, Raksasas and Danavas will obtain the fruit (good results) thereof. The Pitrs propitiated and developed by means of Sraddhas (develop) the imperishable Soma. Propitiated and developed by you all, they will always increase. Soma (the Moon-god) strengthened and developed by means of Sraddhas, will develop the people and the entire world, along with mountains and forests surrounded ( = inhabi¬ ted) by mobile and immobile beings. Those men, who, desirous of nourishment, perform Sraddhas are always granted development and progeny by Pitrs. Those (Pitrs) to whom they (the performers of Sraddha) offer three balls of rice ( Pinzas ) mentioning their names and Gotraupto great-grandfather, they (Pitrs) who are present (everywhere), strengthen and develop their progeny by that offering of Sraddha." There is no doubt in this that Pitrs grant you perfect knowledge. After hearing these words of Suta possessing self- knowledge, the sages asked him again subsequently: How many are the groups of these Pitrs? At what time did those groups (come into existence)—Pitrs who were the excellent ancestors of Devas and who developed and strengthened Soma? I shall recount to you the most excellent creation of Pitrs. This is the same question which had been formerly put to his father Brhaspati by Sarhyu. As Brhaspati, the great expertin all fields of knowledge, was seated, his son Sarhyu endowed with humility, put this question. "Who are these Pitrs? What are their names? How were they born? How did they attain Pitr-hood? What is the reason for which Pitrs are worshipped at the outset in every Yajna? All the holy rites of noble souls begin with the performance of Sraddhas. To whom all these Sraddhas are to be offered? What is the great benefit when they are offered? In which of the holy centres and sacred rivers does the Sraddha performance yield ever-lasting benefit? What are those holy centres in Which excellent Brahmanas (ought to) perform Sraddha to obtain all (desired) benefits? What is the (proper) time for Sraddha? What is the procedure to be followed? O holy sire, I wish that what has been enquired by me be explained in detail in the proper sequence." Verses 20-34 explain the paradox why Pitrs who were the sons of Devas became the fathers of their own fathers? Manu III. 201, however, differs and states that Pitrs sprang from Sages and from Pitrs were born Devas (gods) and human beings. On being asked thus clearly and specifically, the highly intelligent Brhaspati, the most excellent of those who understand (the implications of) questions, answered all the questions in the proper order. O dear one! I shall explain the solemn excellent question which you ask me with due propriety and proper humility. At that time, there was neither the heaven nor the firmament, neither the earth nor the stars nor the quarters, neither the sun, nor the moon, nor the day, nor the night. O dear, the whole Universe was in complete darkness. Brahma alone performed an austere penance difficult for others to perform. Samyu again spoke to his father who was the most excellent among the knowers of Brahman, who always performed holy ablutions in the form of rites and who was the most ex¬ cellent of all knowers of perfect knowledge. "What sort of a penance did Prajapati, the lord of all living beings perform?" Of all types of penance, Yukti i.e. Yoga penance is the most excellent. Meditating on it, the lord then created all the worlds by means of that Yoga. The past and future (items of) knowledge, the entire worlds and Vedas were created after practising Yoga by Brahma, by means of his Yogic vision.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र तीर्थे तु यो भक्त्या भक्तियुक्तो जितेन्द्रियः । पञ्चामृतेन संस्नाप्य धूपनैवेद्यपूजनैः
verses.transliteration: tatra tīrthe tu yo bhaktyā bhaktiyukto jitendriyaḥ / pañcāmṛtena saṃsnāpya dhūpanaivedyapūjanaiḥ
verses.translation: The worlds, the heaven are named * Santanikas * where the shining deities of the Devas well-known as 'Vairajas* stay. Even at the outset then, the lord Brahma, endowed with Yoga and penance, had created Devas after practising the eternal Yoga. They are well known as Adidevas (the primordial Devas). They have great splendour and energy. They are the bestowers of all desires. They are worthy of being worshipped by Devas, Danavas and human beings. There are seven groups of those Devas. They are worshipped by aJl the three worlds. Three of them are Arnurtis (devoid of forms) and four of them have splendid forms. The three sets which have conceptual forms (Bkava murlis) are stationed above. The four Suksmamurlis (having subtle forms) are stationed beneath them. Thereafter, the (common) Devas are stationed and then the earth. This is the situation of the series of worlds. They (the groups of Devas) are stationed in this world The clouds take their origin from them, rain-showers are due to them and, thanks to rain-showers, the worlds (and people) are created again. Since they develop and strengthen the moon and the food-grains and make them flourish by means of Yogic power They are as speedy as mind. Svadhd constitutes their diet. They have every requisite they desire. They are devoid of greed, delusion and fear. They are certainly devoid of sorrow. After giving up Yoga, they have attained the worlds beautiful and pleasant to look at. They become divine, merit¬ orious and sinless noble souls. At the end of a thousand Yugas, they become expoun¬ ders of Brahman. Regaining the Yogic power once again., they attain salvation in a bodiless state. They forsake both the manifestand unmanifest (bodies) by means of their great Yogic power and perish (vanish) like a meteor or like the fading flash of lightning in the sky. By abandoning all the bodies (and other adjuncts) by means of their great Yogic power, they attain the state of namelessness like rivers merging into the ocean. Engaged everyday in holy rites and the worship of preceptors, Pitrs develop their Yogic power and satisfyall (make them flourish). Propitiated in Sraddha, Pitrs nourish Soma (the Moon) making use of their Yogic power whereby the three worlds sustain their lives. Hcncc Sraddhas must always be offered to Yogins 1 with (special efforts). Indeed, the mainstay of Pilfs is Yoga and from (thanks to) Yoga the Moon functions. One may feed thousands of Brahmanas or as many as do come, but listen that one knower of Yogas, if delighted, deserves all (propitiating a Yogin is as fruitful as feeding thousands of Brahmanas). What is taken in by a thousand invited (ordinary Brahmanas), or by a hundred Sndtakas (Brahmanas initiated into householder's life) or by one master of Yoga saves one from great fear. One Yogin excels a thousand householders, a hundred Vdnaprasthas (Forest-hermits) and a thousand Brahmacarins (celibate students). Prajapati has ordained: "(One may be) an atheist, an evil-doer, a person of mixed caste or a thief, (but) he cannot have redemption 2 ( Tdranam ) from anything else, except (by offering) a charitable gift unto those who have Yogic power. His ancestors are delighted like the husbandmen by a good timely rain, even if his son or grandson feeds a (Yogic) meditator. If meditating mendicants are not available, one should feed two Brahmacarins. When they too are not available, one should feed a householder not much engrossed in worldly affairs." It is the injunction of Brahma that a meditating Yogin is greater than one. who (performs penance) for a hundred years standing on one leg and taking in nothing but air. The Siddhas roam over the Earth in the guise of Brahmanas. Hence one should approach the in-coming guest with palms joined in reverence. He should honour him with the vessel containing materials of worship. He shall offer him place of residence and food. The masters of Yoga assume diverse forms Karanam in the text is irrelevant and obscure. Hence Tarariam, the reading in Bd. P. ibid V. 71 is accepted. In heaven, there are seven excellent groups of highly intelligent Pitrs. Four of them have forms and three are formless (Amurta) A Understand as I shall recount their creative activity in the world. (I shall describe) those who are proclaimed (in Smrtis) as their daughters and daughters' sons. There are three excellent groups of those who assume Dharmic bodies and forms. I shall briefly recount their names and creative activity. The disembodied groups of Pitrs, the sons of Prajapati, abide in the shining worlds named Virajas. O Brahmanas, they belong to Virajas. Hence they are famous as excellent Vairajas. I have thus mentioned the first group of Vairajas. 'Sanctifying the worlds'—Bd. P. V. 76. This chapter is textually similar to Bd. 3,10. Reference are given to verses in that chapter. For similar seven divisions of Pitrs vide Pd. P. V.9.2-3, Bd. P. V-l, Their fair-complexioned mental daughter Mena is the wife of the great mountain Himavan. From her the son Mainaka was born. The mountain Mainaka, the holder of all medicinal herbs, the mine of all gems, the holy leader of mountains, was born of her. Kraunca was his son. The king of mountains procreated three daughters of Mena, viz. Aparna, Ekaparna and the third Ekapatala. Two of them had support (They had their permanent abodes). But Aparna performed penance without an abode. Ekaparna had a Nyagrodha tree as her abode and Ekapatala had Pa tala (trumpet flower) tree as her abode. For a hundred thousand years, they performed such a penance as was difficult to be performed even by Devas and Danavas. A single leaf was the diet of Ekaparna and a single Patala flower (trumpet flower) was the diet of Ekapatala. Both of them took their food once, (when) a thousand years had been completed. One of the daughters (viz. Aparna) remained without taking food. Their mother spoke to her thus. Out of affection, the distressed mother forbade her with the words "U" <c Ma " (O daughter! do not). Since she was addressed thus by her mother, the blessed gentle lady per¬ forming the difficult task (penance) became famous as "Umd". The auspicious lady got the name derived from her action. 1 The world of (supported by?) these three ladies will survive for ever. It will be proud of (drptam) their penance, while the earth lasts. All the three, endowed with Yogic power, sustained their bodies by means of their penance. All those blessed gentle ladies possessed permanent youth. All of them were expounders of Brahman. All of them were celibate. Uma was the greatest (eldest), the most excellent (girl) of the fairest complexion. Ekaparna was the wife of Asita. She was chaste and firm m her holy vows. She was given to that intelligent master of Yoga by Himavan. She gave birth to the mental son Devala who was engrossed in meditation on Brahman. Ekapatala, the third of these daughters, wooed Jaigi- savya, the son of Satasilaka, as her husband. Rudrani was the best among them. She excelled others by her good attributes. Between Uma and Sankara the mutual love (was ideal). On realising that they were in close embrace, the slayer <5f Vrtra (i.e. Indra) became apprehensive. (Fire-god) was sent near them by Indra who was afraid of the birth of a child from them engaged in sexual intercourse. (He said to Agni) "O Fire-god, create an impediment in their sexual intercourse. You are present everywhere. So there cannot be any blame (on you in your going there)". When he was told thus, Fire-god acted accordingly. Forsaking (i.e. aside from) the body of Uma, the semen virile was discharged on the ground (by Siva). O Samsapayana, then Fire-god was cursed by the infuriated goddess. With words choked with anger, she spoke to Fire-god thus: "O Fire, since you have caused an impediment in sexual intercourse even before I had been satisfied, therefore you have committed an action which you should nothave committed, you evil-minded one!
verses.hindi: इत्येते नासभिः से दश चन्द्रमसो हयाः । एते चन्द्रससं देवं वहन्ति दिवसक्षयात् ४४ देवेः परिवृतः सोमः पितृभिश्चेव गच्छति । सोमस्य शुक्लपक्षादों भास्करे पुरतः स्थिते ॥ देवे: पीत॑ क्षये सोममाप्याययति नित्यदा । पीत॑ पञ्चदशाहूं तु रश्मिनेकेन भास्करः

verses.sanskrit: प्रसाद्य जगतामीशं सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते । अष्टम्यां मार्गशीर्षस्य तत्र स्नात्वा युधिष्ठिर
verses.transliteration: prasādya jagatāmīśaṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate / aṣṭamyāṃ mārgaśīrṣasya tatra snātvā yudhiṣṭhira
verses.translation: Since the lustrous semen virile of Rudra has not been retained (in my womb), you should hold the foetus yourself by way of punishment (for this act)". The reading danla-kanvoiana is obscure. Bd. 3.10.18 reads dattakaSco- Sanas etc. is clear and is supported by Puraijas. Hence its acceptance here. Smrti works are attributed to them, though the antiquity of those works is doubtful. Approaching (the river) Ganga, he said—"O excellent river, may this be heard. Excessive distress is caused to me by the retention of the foetus. O river, for my relief and welfare, please carry this foetus. Due to my gracious favour, your trouble will be less". Saying "So be it", the highly delighted great river held the foetus (although) with a mind burning (as there was burn¬ ing sensation within her). Distressed by the great pain though she was, she retain¬ ed the foetus for a long time. The foetus was dropped into an auspicious crevasse of Himavan by her. There is an auspicious forest named Saravana where diverse trees were in bloom. It was there that she depo¬ sited the foetus that was blazing like fire. It was there that the son of Rudra, Agni and Ganga was born. He had rosy lustre. He was valorous and brilliant like hundreds of suns. When that blessed son (Kumara) of Jahnavl (Ganga) was born, the sky was covered (crowded) with aerial cars, as if by birds. Celestial drums produced sweet sound in the sky. Siddhas and Caranas moving about in the sky discharged sho¬ wers of flowers. The chief Gandharvas, Yaksas, Vidyadharas and all the Siddhas and Kinnaras sang (laudatory songs) everywhere. Thousands of great serpents and excellent birds approached with reverence the son of Sankara born through Agni. Daityas, Danavas and Raksasas were struck (down) by him by means of his prowess. Even at the very outset, the son of Agni was observed by the wives of the Seven Sages (excepting Arundhati) who had come there for their ablutions. The lordly on of Rudra, resembling the rising sun, was surrounded by those ladies who were very affectionate (towards him), as though they were his.real mothers. Desirous of seeing all those ladies simultaneously, out of affection for them, the extremely lustrous son of Jahnavi created six faces and he was very glorious. 1 He was glorious and he resembled the midday sun He had eyes like the petals of lotus. When he was born, the lustre of all the worlds was bedimmed. The groups of Danavas who could not brook Devas, had a purge ( Skandita ) when that great (deity) was born and (hence) that valorous (deity) became known as 'Skanda.' 2 Because the ancient (deity), the slayer of Asuras, had been nourished (breast-fed and) nurtured by the Krttikas, he became famous as Karttikeya. While that enemy of Daityas was yawning, his (we¬ apon) Sakti (spear) called Aparajita (unvanquished) came out of his mouth, blazing with flames of fire. For the purpose of Skanda's play, two birds named Prabhadrakas, a peacock and a cock, were created out of Garutfa by Visnu, the powerful god. A banner was given by Vayu (Wind-god). A great Vina (lute) of loud sound was presented by Sarasvati. A goat was given by the self-born (deity) (i.e. Brahma) and a ram was given by Sambhu. O Brahmanas, when the (mountain) Kraunca was felled down in his sport out of Maya (his illusive power), when the rising leader of Asuras, Taraka was also struck down, the lordly son of Agni, the valorous enemy of Daityas was crowned as commander-in-chief (of their army) by the blessed Devas including Indra and Upendra. Mbh. AnuS&sana chs. 85 & 86 give a different version of Skanda'i birth and the cause of his six faces. According to Mbh. Anu 86.14, the child came to be known as Skanda due to the casting off of the semen of £iva by Agni and Ganga (skannatvdt skanda tam prdptah) (While) Slipping from heaven and falling down, she saw the aerial chariots as small as a mote and in them she saw the fallen Pitrs. They were very subtle and unforsakcn 2 (?) (a-parityak- tan). They were like sparks of fire imposed on sparks of fire. Falling down topsy-turvy, she appealed to them, "Save, ye She was consoled by them—"Do not be afraid 55. When thus urged, she became steady. Then she propitiated those Pitrs with pitiable words. Those Pitre spoke to the girl who fell down from her glory due to her transgression: "O lady of sparkling smiles, you are fallen from your prosperity due to your own fault. (Hence) you fall. Deities (god) attain (experience) the fruits of their actions by means of the same bodies with which they perform those actions. In the case of Devas, the actions fructify immediately. In the case of human beings, they fructify after death. Hence you will attain the status of the child of Amavasu after death and will attain the fruit 55. On being told thus (by her Pitrs), she again propitiated Pitrs. After meditating (for a while), they took pity on her and became pacified and pleased. The missing lines are traceable to Bd. 3.10. w. 53-b to 58. They are translated here to supply the lacuna: 53b-54. "It is heard that the Pitrs named Barbisads are somapas (imbibers of Soma). The mental daughter of the Pitrs was the river named Acchoda. Those Pitrs had never before been seen by her. She was born as their mental daughter. Hence she did not know her Pitrs. Transgressing those real Pitrs, she chose Amavasu as her father. He was traversing the sky accompanied by the Apsaras named Adrika. He was seated man aerial chariot. in the firmament. But due to her trans¬ gression (of her real father), she was unable to move about in the sky. After seeking another father (viz. Amavasu) she slipped from her Yogic power and fell down." On foreseeing what is surely destined to happen, Devas, the Soma-imbibing Pitrs spoke to the girl, "You will become the daughter of the noble-souled king Amavasu who is born on the earth as a human being and thereafter attain these worlds of your own. In the twenty-eighth Dvapara Yuga you will be born of the womb of a fish; you will be the daughter of this very same king Amavasu and (the celestial damsel) Adrika. You will give birth to the successor of the sage Para- Sara. That Brahmanical sage will divide the single Veda into four parts. You alone will give birth to two sons who will heighten the glory of Mahabhisa (?) Santanu—the sons Vicitravlrya, the knower of Dharma, and Citrangada, the king endowed with the attributes of brilliance and strength. After giving birth to these sons, you will regain your own worlds. Due to your transgression towards the Pitrs, you will attain that despicable birth. You will become the daughter of the very same king and Adrika. After becoming (his) daughter, you will regain these worlds." In the confluence of Ganga and Yamuna, she was born of the fish Adrika, She was born as the daughter of Amavasu in Adrika the fish. 1 Indeed, she was the daughter of that king (being bom of) the semen virile of the king. There the Pitrs are the Agnisvattas of shining lustre. With a desire for (attaining) excellent fruits, groups of Danavas, Yaksas, Raksasas, Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Bhutas, ser¬ pents and Pisacas worship them. Thus, these sons of Pulaha, the Prajapati, have been recounted. These groups are said to be three. They are auspicious and assumers of Dharma-form. In the missing lines in the text supplemented from Bd. P. (w. 55- 58) and w. 51-66, the Purana writers have used the curse-motif to explain the unusual matrimonial life of Satyavati. Their mental daughter is (will be) famous by the name of Pivarl. She was (will be) reputed to be a YoginI, a Yogic wife and a Yogic mother. In the (future) twenty-eighth Dvaparayuga (a sage) of great penance named Suka will be born in the family of Parasara.
verses.hindi: बालखिल्य ऋषियों द्वारा आवुत होकर दिन-रांत किया करते हैं। अग्रगामी मह॒षि अभिमत बचनों द्वारा उनकी स्तुति करते हैं और गन्धवे-अप्सराएँ नृत्य-गीत से उनकी सेवा करती हैं। इस प्रकार आकाहगामो दिन नामक सूर्य अश्वों के साथ भ्रमण करते हैं ।४७-४५। चन्द्रमा भी नक्षत्रों की गलियों से चला करते हैं । इनकी किरणों का भी सूर्य की तरह वृद्धि और नाश हुआ करता है । चन्द्रमा के रथ में तीन चकके हैं ओर

verses.transliteration: yo yena yajate tatra sa taṃ kāmamavāpnuyāt
verses.translation: O excellent Brahmanas, he will be a glorious and great Yogin. Yoga (will spread) from him. He will be born of Vyasa, from the AranI (a piece of wood used for the production of fire by attrition) like the smokeless fire. In the (mental) daughter of the Pitrs, he will beget these well-known Yogic preceptors, viz. Krsna, Gaura, Prabhu, Sambhu and Bhurisruta. He will beget a daughter Klrtimati who will be a YoginI and a Yogic mother. She will become the queen of Anuha and the mother of Brahmadatta. After begetting these children and attaining great Yogic power, he will become a great Yogin and ascetic. He will attain that goal from which there is no return. Like the rays of the sun, he will attain the status of no rebirth. The great sage will become omnipresent and liberated. These three are the disembodied Pitrs who assume Dharmic forms. There are four others. (Listen and) understand. O excellent Brahmanas! The Pitrs whom I shall describe assume forms of great lustre. They are Kavyas*, sons of Agni, Kavi (the wise one?) born of Svadha. These are the Pitrs shining i n the worlds of Devas with their lustre amidst the luminaries. They are richly endowed with all desirable objects and the -Brahmanas revere them. Their mental daughter was famous in heaven by There were thirty-one Pit r s who heightened the glory of Bhrgus. Their worlds were known as Maricigarbhcs (having rays within) which envelop the heavens. Those sons of Angiras, nourished along with Sadhyas, are remembered as the Pitrs Upahutas. They shine in heaven. Looking up to them, the Pitr Groups of Ksatriyas, those who are desirous of benefits, revere them. Their mental daughter is well known by the name of Yaioda. She was the wife of Visvamahan and the daughter-in- law of Visvasarmin. 2 The gentle lady was the mother of the saintly king Khatvanga of noble soul, in whose Yajna Gatha (a laudatory verse) was sung formerly by great sages. After seeing the birth of fire (in the Yajna) of the noble-souled Sanqlilya, the deathless Devas conquering heaven with purity of mind observe the Yajamana (under whose auspices the Yajna is performed) Dilipa, the noble soul of truthful rites. Ajyapaswere the Pitrs of Kardama, the Prajapati, who was born of Pulaha. They were born of him again. Moving about in the sky, they are stationed in these worlds that go about as they please. Groups of Vaisyas who are desirous of benefits, revere these in Sraddha. Their mental daughter is famous by the name of Viraja. The chaste lady was the wife of Nahusa and the mother of Yayati. This is the translation of *Datlasend Kumareria.* The absurdity of the text is obvious. 3d. P. ibid V. 87 reads Dattd Sanatkumareria 'She was given by Sanatkumara*. The reading in Bd. P. deserves adoption here as the next line reads "She became the beloved...of Sukra". The combined verses can be constructed as follows: Sukalas are the Pitrs of Vasistha, the Prajapati. They are the sons of Hiranyagarbha. There are the worlds named Manasas where these are stationed. Their mental daughter is Narmada, the most excellent of rivers. Flowing in the southern region, she sanctifies living beings. She was tiie wife of Purukutsa and the mother of Trasadasyu. Manu became the lord of Manvantara by adopting these (Pitrs). In the beginning of Manvantara, he initiates all types of Sraddhas. O excellent Brahmanas, (I have recounted), all the Pitrs in their proper order. Hence Sraddha is to be* offered with faith in accordance with one's Dharma. A Sraddha offered in silver vessels or those of silver alloy, after proferring Svadha, propitiates Pitrs. By the propitiation of Soma, Agni and Vaivasvata (Manu) and by the performance of Homo, in the sacrificial fire during the northern transit (of the sun), one shall attain the fruit of an Asvamcdha (a Horse Sacrifice). Pitrs delight him who propitiates Pitrs with devo¬ tion. There is no doubt in this that Pitrs bestow nourish¬ ment or progeny. The rites of pitrs are always far superior to the rites of deities. It is ordained that the propitiation of Pitrs must be given priority over that of deities. The subtle movement (or goal) of Yoga or the satiation of Pitrs is not visible through the physical eye. Thus Pitrs, their worlds, their grandsons, their Yajamanas and those who been recounted. (Out of the seven classes of Pitrs) four hav< and three are formless. Devas honour them ar oraddhas to them devoutly and assiduously. 1 All the Devas including Indra concentrate their minds on them. They join their palms in reverence and de¬ votedly worship them. Visvedevas, Sikatas, Prsnijas, Srrigins Krsnas, Svetas and Ajas worship them duly. Desirous of benefits, the subjects Vatarasanas, DivakJrtyas, Lekhas Maruts, Brahma and other heaven-dwellers, Atri, Bhr«n/ Angiras and all other sages, Yaksas, Nagas, Suparnas, Kinnaras and Raksasas always worshipped Pitrs. These noble-souled (Pitrs), if duly honoured and worshipped in Sraddha, grant all desires hundred-fold and thousand-fold. These grandfathers (Pitrs) bestow Yogic Power (and prosperity) and liberation (from Samsara) after one has aban¬ doned the three worlds of normal existence involving old age and death. Pitamahas, the deities of subtle bodies, grant the means of salvation, AiSvarya (prosperity), complete detachment and infiniteness. Practised Yoga is AiSvarya', and Ativarya is the excellent wealth. Without Yoga and Aisvarya liberation (from Sarhsara) is impossible (to be achieved). Vairajas Barhisads Agnisvattas Kavyas (sons of Agni and Svadha) Upahutas (sons of Angiras) Ajyapas (sons of Pulaha) Sukala (sons of Vasisfha It (Moksa) is as impossible as the movement of a wingless bird in the sky. il4bA/a-Dharma is the greatest of all Dharmas and eternal. Pitamahas (manes) grant thousands of aerial chariots attended by groups of Apsaras-s and richly equipped with all desirable things. Intellect, nourishment, power of memory, brain, kingdom and health can be attained only through the grace of the noble-souled Pitrs. Pitamahas grant crores of gems, pearls, lapis lazuli, garments and thousands of horses and elephants. Pitamahas always bestow on men chariots fitted with swans and peacocks, studded with pearls and lapis lazuli and decorated with tinkling bells and provided with perpetual flowers and fruits.
verses.hindi: दोनों तरफ घोड़ जुने हुये हैं। इसका यह यह रथ अरृव और सारथि के साथ जल के भीतर से उत्पन्न हुआ है । इस रथ में एक सौ अरायें, तीन, तीन चक्‍्के और उज्ज्वल वर्ण के उत्तम घोड़े जुते हुये हैं ।४६-५४०। ये दिव्य अहव गिनती में दस हैं। ये मन की तरह वेगवान्, केश, असज्भ ओर कल्पादि में एक बार जोते गये हैं, जो युगान्त पर्यन्त रथ का वहन करते हैं । रथ में जुते हुए उज्ज्वल वर्ण के वे अष्व के समान कान्तिवाले चन्द्र के रथ को आकाश में खींचते रहते हैं ।५१०-५२। चन्द्रमा के दसों घोड़ों के नाम हैं--ययु, त्रिमना, वष, राजीवल, वाम, तुरण्य, हंस, व्योमी और मृग । ये घोड़े चन्द्रदेव को कल्पांत पर्यन्त वहन करते हैं  देवों और पितरों द्वारा सेव्यमान होकर चन्द्रमा इसी प्रकार गमन करते हैं ।१३-१५५॥ शुक्ल पक्ष में सूर्य चन्द्रमा के आगे रहते हैं और देवों द्वारा पिये गये चन्द्र को दिवस क्रम से नित्य प्रति परिपुष्ट कर तृप्त करते हैं। इस प्रकार

verses.sanskrit: ॥ इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे कामेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकसप्ततितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ र्क्व् अध्याय ७२ श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: ततो गच्छेत्तु राजेन्द्र मणिनागेश्वरं शुभम् । उत्तरे नर्मदाकूले सर्वपापक्षयंकरम् । स्थापितं मणिनागेन लोकानां हितकाम्यया
verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe kāmeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 72 śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: tato gacchettu rājendra maṇināgeśvaraṃ śubham / uttare narmadākūle sarvapāpakṣayaṃkaram / sthāpitaṃ maṇināgena lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā

verses.transliteration: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca: āśīviṣeṇa sarpeṇa īśvarastoṣitaḥ katham / kṣudrāḥ sarvasya lokasya bhayadā viṣaśālinaḥ
verses.translation: "Olord, lord of past and future, lord of the worlds, lord of the Universe, O Brahma of good rites, what shall I do for you?"
verses.hindi: पिबन्त्यस्बुमयं देवा मधु सौम्यं सुधासयम् संभृतं चार्धभासेन असृतं सर्यतेजसा । भक्षार्थमम्ृतं सोम्यं पोर्णमास्यामुपासते
verses.wordMeaning: "Olord, lord of past and future, lord of the worlds, lord of the Universe, O Brahma of good rites, what shall I do for you?"
verses.commentary: Sense: "Olord, lord of past and future, lord of the worlds, lord of the Universe, O Brahma of good rites, what shall I do for you?"

verses.sanskrit: कथ्यतां तात मे सर्वं पातकस्योपशान्तिदम् । मम सन्तापजं दुःखं दुर्योधनसमुद्भवम्
verses.transliteration: kathyatāṃ tāta me sarvaṃ pātakasyopaśāntidam / mama santāpajaṃ duḥkhaṃ duryodhanasamudbhavam
verses.translation: Purarias try to synthesize Vaisnavism and Saivism by identifying Siva with Vi|nu.
verses.hindi: एकराद्र सुरेः सर्वे: पितुभिश्य महषिभिः  सोमस्य छृष्णपक्षादों भास्कराभिसुखस्यथ च ॥
verses.wordMeaning: Purarias try to synthesize Vaisnavism and Saivism by identifying Siva with Vi|nu.
verses.commentary: Sense: Purarias try to synthesize Vaisnavism and Saivism by identifying Siva with Vi|nu.

verses.sanskrit: कर्णभीष्मोद्भवं रौद्रं दुःखं पाञ्चालिसम्भवम् । तव वक्त्राम्बुजौघेन प्लावितं निर्वृतिं गतः
verses.transliteration: karṇabhīṣmodbhavaṃ raudraṃ duḥkhaṃ pāñcālisambhavam / tava vaktrāmbujaughena plāvitaṃ nirvṛtiṃ gataḥ
verses.translation: On hearing my words, the lotus-eyed Brahma replied: «q Is vara, O lord of the past, present and future, may this be listened.
verses.hindi: (+त्रयभ्र त्रिशतं चेव श्रयस्रिशसयेव च । श्रयरलिशत्सहस्राश्व देवा: सोम पिबन्ति व पितरश्रोपतिष्ठन्ति अमाबास्थां निशाकरम्ू. ६४५
verses.wordMeaning: On hearing my words, the lotus-eyed Brahma replied: «q Is vara, O lord of the past, present and future, may this be listened.
verses.commentary: Sense: On hearing my words, the lotus-eyed Brahma replied: «q Is vara, O lord of the past, present and future, may this be listened.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वा तव मुखोद्गीतां कथां वै पापनाशिनीम् । अयुक्तमिदमस्माकं द्विज क्लेशो न शाम्यति
verses.transliteration: śrutvā tava mukhodgītāṃ kathāṃ vai pāpanāśinīm / ayuktamidamasmākaṃ dvija kleśo na śāmyati
verses.translation: O lotus-eyed lord, when the ocean was being churned by Devas and Asuras, the terrible poison, resembling a cloud, shining like a blue cloud, having the lustre of the Samvarta fire, refulgent like the sun at the end of the Yugas, appeared in front like the Black Death.
verses.hindi: करते हैं। तब सुषुम्त किरण द्वारा परिपूर्ण चन्द्रमा की कला उज्ज्वलतर हो जाती है। अतः क्ृष्णपक्ष में चन्द्र का हास होता है और शुक्ल पक्ष में वे परिपूर्ण होते हैं । इस प्रकार सूर्य के सामथ्यें से चन्द्रमा का शरीर घटता-बढ़ता है । शुक्लपक्ष में दिन क्रम से चन्द्रदेव परिपुष्ट हो जाते हैं और वे पूणिमा को उज्ज्वल परिपूर्ण मण्डल से प्रकाशित होने लगते हैं ।(६-५६। फिर क्रृष्णपक्ष की द्वितीया से लेकर चतुदंशी पर्यक्त देवगण जल
verses.wordMeaning: O lotus-eyed lord, when the ocean was being churned by Devas and Asuras, the terrible poison, resembling a cloud, shining like a blue cloud, having the lustre of the Samvarta fire, refulgent like the sun at the end of the Yugas, appeared in front like the Black Death.
verses.commentary: Sense: O lotus-eyed lord, when the ocean was being churned by Devas and Asuras, the terrible poison, resembling a cloud, shining like a blue cloud, having the lustre of the Samvarta fire, refulgent like the sun at the end of the Yugas, appeared in front like the Black Death.

verses.sanskrit: अथवा प्राप्स्यते तात विद्यादानस्य यत्फलम् । तत्फलं प्राप्यते नित्यं कथाश्रवणतो हरेः
verses.transliteration: athavā prāpsyate tāta vidyādānasya yatphalam / tatphalaṃ prāpyate nityaṃ kathāśravaṇato hareḥ
verses.translation: It has the brilliance of the sun capable of destroying the three worlds. It sparkles all round. The poison having the lustre of deadly fire has risen in front.
verses.hindi: के सार स्वरूप और रसमय चन्द्र के जल प्रधान और सुधामय सुन्दर मधु का पान करते हैं  वह अमृत सूर्य के तेज से आधे मास में संचित होकर पूर्णमासी में देवों के भोजन के लिये कल्पित होता है। कृष्णपक्ष के आदि में एक रात देवता, पितर और मह॒षिगण भास्कराभिमुखवर्ती चन्द्र का पान करते हैं। पीने पर उनकी कला फिर धीरे-धीरे क्षीण होने लगती हैं।६०-६२। तेंतीस हजार तैतीस सौ तीन देवता चन्द्र के मधु का पान करते हैं। इसके द्वारा पी जाने पर चन्द्रमा की क्ृष्णपक्ष की कला फिर बढ़ने लगती है। इसीलिये कृष्णपक्ष में इनकी कला क्षीण होती है और शुक्ल पक्ष में बढ़ने लगती है। इसी प्रकार देवगण प्रतिदिनक्रम से आधे मास तक चन्द्रमा को पीकर अमावास्या को प्रस्थान करते हैं। पुनः अमावास्था आते ही पितर लोग चन्द्रमा के निकट आ जाते हैं ।६३-६५। चम्द्रमा की पन्द्रहवीं कला का जो अवशेष रह जाता है, उसे पितर
verses.wordMeaning: It has the brilliance of the sun capable of destroying the three worlds. It sparkles all round. The poison having the lustre of deadly fire has risen in front.
verses.commentary: Sense: It has the brilliance of the sun capable of destroying the three worlds. It sparkles all round. The poison having the lustre of deadly fire has risen in front.

verses.sanskrit: श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: यथायथा त्वं नृप भाषसे च तथातथा मे सुखमेति भारती । शैथिल्यता वा जरयान्वितस्य त्वत्सौहृदं नश्यति नैव तात । शृणुष्व तस्मात्सह बान्धवैश्च कथामिमां पापहरां प्रशस्ताम्
verses.transliteration: śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: yathāyathā tvaṃ nṛpa bhāṣase ca tathātathā me sukhameti bhāratī / śaithilyatā vā jarayānvitasya tvatsauhṛdaṃ naśyati naiva tāta / śṛṇuṣva tasmātsaha bāndhavaiśca kathāmimāṃ pāpaharāṃ praśastām
verses.translation: On seeing it we are much frightened and agitated. O Mahadeva, desiring the welfare of the worlds, you will please drink it. O Sir, you are the enjoyer of the most splendid, you are the excellent lord.
verses.hindi: धनुश्चिह्नान्तगंतग्रन्थः क, ग. पुस्तकेयोर्नास्ति ।-+: एतदरधस्थान इदमर्ध बतेते -- क्षीयन्ति तस्माच्छक्ला
verses.wordMeaning: On seeing it we are much frightened and agitated. O Mahadeva, desiring the welfare of the worlds, you will please drink it. O Sir, you are the enjoyer of the most splendid, you are the excellent lord.
verses.commentary: Sense: On seeing it we are much frightened and agitated. O Mahadeva, desiring the welfare of the worlds, you will please drink it. O Sir, you are the enjoyer of the most splendid, you are the excellent lord.

verses.sanskrit: कथयामि यथावृत्तमितिहासं पुरातनम्
verses.transliteration: kathayāmi yathāvṛttamitihāsaṃ purātanam
verses.translation: O Mahadeva, excepting you, there is no one to en¬ dure the poison. No other person is sung about (= glorified) as capable of it, in the three worlds".
verses.hindi: ततः पतच्दशे भागे किचिच्छिष्टे कलात्मके । अपराह्हल पितृगणेजंघन्यः पर्युपास्यते पिबन्ति द्विकल काले शिष्टा तस्य तु या कला। निःसृतं तदसावास्यां गेभस्तिभ्यः स्वधामृतम् ॥
verses.wordMeaning: O Mahadeva, excepting you, there is no one to en¬ dure the poison. No other person is sung about (= glorified) as capable of it, in the three worlds".
verses.commentary: Sense: O Mahadeva, excepting you, there is no one to en¬ dure the poison. No other person is sung about (= glorified) as capable of it, in the three worlds".

verses.sanskrit: कथितं पूर्वतो वृत्तैः पारम्पर्येण भारत
verses.transliteration: kathitaṃ pūrvato vṛttaiḥ pāramparyeṇa bhārata
verses.translation: On hearing these words of Brahma, O splendid¬ faced lady, I concurred and said "So be it". Then I began to drink the poison that resembled death. As I drank the terrible poison frightening even the gods, O lady of excellent comple¬ xion, my throat immediately turned black.
verses.hindi: एवं सुयंनिमित्तषां क्षयवृद्धिनिशाकरे । ताराग्रहाणां वक्ष्यासि स्वर्भानोश्व रथं पुनः
verses.wordMeaning: On hearing these words of Brahma, O splendid¬ faced lady, I concurred and said "So be it". Then I began to drink the poison that resembled death. As I drank the terrible poison frightening even the gods, O lady of excellent comple¬ xion, my throat immediately turned black.
verses.commentary: Sense: On hearing these words of Brahma, O splendid¬ faced lady, I concurred and said "So be it". Then I began to drink the poison that resembled death. As I drank the terrible poison frightening even the gods, O lady of excellent comple¬ xion, my throat immediately turned black.

verses.sanskrit: द्वे भार्ये कश्यपस्यास्तां सर्वलोकेष्वनुत्तमे । गरुत्मन्तं च विनतासूत कद्रूर् अहीनथ
verses.transliteration: dve bhārye kaśyapasyāstāṃ sarvalokeṣvanuttame / garutmantaṃ ca vinatāsūta kadrūr ahīnatha
verses.translation: On seeing the poison that had the lustre of the petal of blue lotus and that had appeared like the king of Serpents, Taksaka, clinging to my throat and putting out its tongues, Brahma, the grandfather of the worlds, possessor of excessive splendour, spoke: "O Mahadeva, of good rites, really you shine due to this throat".
verses.hindi: तोयतेजोमयः शुश्रः सोमपुत्रस्य वे रथः । युक्तो हयेः पिशडगैस्तु अष्टाभि्वातरंहसे:ः सवरूथः सानुकर्ष: सुतो दिव्यों रथे महान् । सोपासडःगपताकस्तु सध्यजो मेघसंनिभः १७४
verses.wordMeaning: On seeing the poison that had the lustre of the petal of blue lotus and that had appeared like the king of Serpents, Taksaka, clinging to my throat and putting out its tongues, Brahma, the grandfather of the worlds, possessor of excessive splendour, spoke: "O Mahadeva,…
verses.commentary: Sense: On seeing the poison that had the lustre of the petal of blue lotus and that had appeared like the king of Serpents, Taksaka, clinging to my throat and putting out its tongues, Brahma, the grandfather of the worlds, possessor of excessive splendour, spoke: "O Mahadeva,…

verses.sanskrit: संतोषेण च ते तात तिष्ठतः काश्यपे गृहे । कद्रूश्च विनता नाम हृष्टे च वनिते सदा
verses.transliteration: saṃtoṣeṇa ca te tāta tiṣṭhataḥ kāśyape gṛhe / kadrūśca vinatā nāma hṛṣṭe ca vanite sadā
verses.translation: O daughter of the king of mountains, on seeing the Kalakuta, that poison of fierce potency, being retained by me in the throat, Devas and Daityas were wonder-struck.
verses.hindi: लोग मध्याह्न काल में पीते हैं। उस अवशिष्ट कला से जो स्वधा रूपी अमृत क्षरित होता है, उसको द्विकलात्मक कालमात्र में पान कर पितर लोग एक महोने तक तृप्त रहते हैं ।६६५। सोम्प, बहिषद्, अग्निष्वात्त और कब्य पितर ही हैं । विद्वानों ने जिसे पंचाब्द संवत्सर कहा है, वही कव्य है। ऋतु सोम्य, मास बहिषद और ऋतु अग्निष्वात्त हैं ब्राह्मणो ! पितृसर्ग यानी पितरों की व्यापार-वार्ता इसी प्रकार की है। अमावास्या में पितरों
verses.wordMeaning: O daughter of the king of mountains, on seeing the Kalakuta, that poison of fierce potency, being retained by me in the throat, Devas and Daityas were wonder-struck.
verses.commentary: Sense: O daughter of the king of mountains, on seeing the Kalakuta, that poison of fierce potency, being retained by me in the throat, Devas and Daityas were wonder-struck.

verses.sanskrit: ताभ्यां सार्द्धं क्रीडते च कश्यपो ऽपि प्रजापतिः । ततस्त्वेकदिने प्राप्ते आश्रमस्था शुभानना
verses.transliteration: tābhyāṃ sārddhaṃ krīḍate ca kaśyapo 'pi prajāpatiḥ / tatastvekadine prāpte āśramasthā śubhānanā
verses.translation: Then, O fair lady with the gait of inebriated elephant,
verses.hindi: द्वारा षीत चन्द्र की पन्द्रहवीं कला के परिपुण भाग का जब तक क्षय होता है, तब तक उनका अन्तिम भाग पूर्ण हो जाता है। अर्थात् सोलहवीं कला का नाश नहीं है  पक्षादि में चन्द्रमा का वृद्धि क्षय इसी प्रकार होता रहता है  चन्द्रमा की जो यह क्षय-वुद्धि होती है, उसका भुख्य कारण सूर्य ही है ।६७-७०३। अब हम तारकादि ग्रहों और राहु के रथ के सम्बन्ध में कहते हैं। बुध का रथ शुश्रवर्ण और जलीय तेज से युक्त अर्थात् उसमें जल का तेज वर्तमान है। वायु की तरह बेगवान् पिशंग वर्ण के आठ घोड़े उसमें जुते हुये हैं। वह रथ मैध की तरह है, जिस पर ध्वजा-पताका फहरा रही हैं, तरकस रखे हुये हैं। उस दिव्य रथ के नीचे काठ लगा हुआ है और ऊपर से फौलादी चादर कढ़ी हुई है । उस रथ का सारथी भी दिव्य है। शुक्र का रथ तेज में सूर्य की तरह और शोभा सम्पन्न है। इसमें पृथ्वी से उत्पन्न नाना वर्ण के मोदे-मोटे वायु की तरह वेगशाली दस घोड़े
verses.wordMeaning: Then, O fair lady with the gait of inebriated elephant,
verses.commentary: Sense: Then, O fair lady with the gait of inebriated elephant,

verses.sanskrit: उच्चैःश्रवं हयं दृष्ट्वा मनोवेगसमन्वितम् । पश्य पश्य हि तन्वङ्गी हयं सर्वत्र पाण्डुरम्
verses.transliteration: uccaiḥśravaṃ hayaṃ dṛṣṭvā manovegasamanvitam / paśya paśya hi tanvaṅgī hayaṃ sarvatra pāṇḍuram
verses.translation: "Wonderful is your strength, prowess and valour. Oh, wonderful is the strength of your Yoga. O lord of Devas', wondeiful is your lordship, O lord, whose dishevelled hair is flooded with Ganga water.
verses.hindi: जुते हुये हैं। ये घोड़ों में श्रेष्ठ महाभाग अइ्ब श्वेत, पिशज्भ, सारंग, नील, लोहित, पीत, कृष्ण, हरित, पृषत
verses.wordMeaning: "Wonderful is your strength, prowess and valour. Oh, wonderful is the strength of your Yoga. O lord of Devas', wondeiful is your lordship, O lord, whose dishevelled hair is flooded with Ganga water.
verses.commentary: Sense: "Wonderful is your strength, prowess and valour. Oh, wonderful is the strength of your Yoga. O lord of Devas', wondeiful is your lordship, O lord, whose dishevelled hair is flooded with Ganga water.

verses.sanskrit: धावमानमविश्रान्तं जवेन मनसोपमम् । तं दृष्ट्वा सहसा चाश्वमीर्ष्याभावेन चाब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration: dhāvamānamaviśrāntaṃ javena manasopamam / taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasā cāśvamīrṣyābhāvena cābravīt
verses.translation: You alone are Visnu, the., four-faced Brahma and Yama, the god of death; you alone are the bestower of boons; you alone are the sun, the moon, the earth and the water.
verses.hindi: अष्टाश्वः काउचनः श्रीमान्सो मस्यापि रथो5भवत् । असइगेलों हितेरश्वे: सर्वंगेरग्निसंभवे: ॥ तवस्त्वाडिगरसो विद्वान्देवाचार्यो ब्रहस्पति: । शोण रश्व:ः काञचनेन स्यन्दनेन प्रसपंति ७८
verses.wordMeaning: You alone are Visnu, the., four-faced Brahma and Yama, the god of death; you alone are the bestower of boons; you alone are the sun, the moon, the earth and the water.
verses.commentary: Sense: You alone are Visnu, the., four-faced Brahma and Yama, the god of death; you alone are the bestower of boons; you alone are the sun, the moon, the earth and the water.

verses.sanskrit: कद्रूर् उवाच: ब्रूहि भद्रे सहस्रांशोर् अश्वः किंवर्णको भवेत् । अहं ब्रवीमि कृष्णो ऽयं त्वं किं वदसि तद्वद
verses.transliteration: kadrūr uvāca: brūhi bhadre sahasrāṃśor aśvaḥ kiṃvarṇako bhavet / ahaṃ bravīmi kṛṣṇo 'yaṃ tvaṃ kiṃ vadasi tadvada
verses.translation: You alone are sacrifice, the rites and observances; you alone are the past and future. You alone are the origin and end; you alone are both gross and subtle Purusa.
verses.hindi: तत: श्नेश्ररोध्प्यश्वः शवलेव्योमिसंभवे: । कार्ष्णायसं समारह्म स्पन्दनं याति वे शनेः
verses.wordMeaning: You alone are sacrifice, the rites and observances; you alone are the past and future. You alone are the origin and end; you alone are both gross and subtle Purusa.
verses.commentary: Sense: You alone are sacrifice, the rites and observances; you alone are the past and future. You alone are the origin and end; you alone are both gross and subtle Purusa.

verses.sanskrit: विनतोवाच: पश्यसे ननु नेत्रैश्च कृष्णं श्वेतं न पश्यसि । असत्यभाषणाद्भद्रे यमलोकं गमिष्यसि
verses.transliteration: vinatovāca: paśyase nanu netraiśca kṛṣṇaṃ śvetaṃ na paśyasi / asatyabhāṣaṇādbhadre yamalokaṃ gamiṣyasi
verses.translation: You alone are the subtlest of the subtle; you alone are the fire and the wind; you alone are the creator, protector and annihilator of the world, both mobile and immobile.*'
verses.hindi: स्वर्भानोस्तु तथवाश्वा: कृष्णा ह्ाष्टो मनोजवाः  रथं तमोमयं तस्य सक्षद्यक्ता वहन्त्युत अथ केतुरथस्याश्वरा अष्टाष्टो बातरंहुस:। पलालध्मसंकाशा: शबला रासभारुणाः णरे एते वाह! ग्रहाणां वे मया प्रोक्ता रथः सह । सबवे श्रुवनिबद्धास्ते प्रबद्धा वातरश्मिभिः...
verses.wordMeaning: You alone are the subtlest of the subtle; you alone are the fire and the wind; you alone are the creator, protector and annihilator of the world, both mobile and immobile.*'
verses.commentary: Sense: You alone are the subtlest of the subtle; you alone are the fire and the wind; you alone are the creator, protector and annihilator of the world, both mobile and immobile.*'

verses.sanskrit: सत्यानृते तु वचने पणस्तव ममैव तु । सहस्रं चैव वर्षाणां दास्यहं तव मन्दिरे
verses.transliteration: satyānṛte tu vacane paṇastava mamaiva tu / sahasraṃ caiva varṣāṇāṃ dāsyahaṃ tava mandire
verses.translation: After saying these words and bowing their heads, the leading Devas, the noble souls, went to Meru in their aerial chariots.
verses.hindi: और पृश्टिन रंग के हैं मंगल का रथ सोने का है, जिसमें आठ घोड़े जुते हुये हैँ। यह रथ अत्यन्त शोभा सम्पन्न है। इनके लोहित वर्ण के बेजोड़ घोड़े अग्नि से उत्पन्न हुये हैं और सबवंत्र गमन करने वाले हैं ।७१-७६। मंगल इन्हीं पर आरोहण कर सीधी और टेढ़ी गति से राशिचक्र का भ्रमण करते हैं। अंगिरातनय देवाचारय विद्वानू बृहस्पति सोने के रथ पर घूमा करते हैं। इनके दिव्य घोड़े लाल रंग के हैं और रथ सर्वत्र गमन करने वाला है,
verses.wordMeaning: After saying these words and bowing their heads, the leading Devas, the noble souls, went to Meru in their aerial chariots.
verses.commentary: Sense: After saying these words and bowing their heads, the leading Devas, the noble souls, went to Meru in their aerial chariots.

verses.sanskrit: असत्या यदि मे वाणी कृष्ण उच्चैःश्रवा यदि । तदाहं त्वद्गृहे दासी भवामि सर्पमातृके
verses.transliteration: asatyā yadi me vāṇī kṛṣṇa uccaiḥśravā yadi / tadāhaṃ tvadgṛhe dāsī bhavāmi sarpamātṛke
verses.translation: Thus the greatest of secrets, the holiest of holy things, the story of what is famous as Nilakantha has been narrated to you.
verses.hindi: जिसमें वायु की तरह वेगशाली आठ घोड़े जुते हुये हैं। ये एक राशि पर एक वर्ष निवास करते हैं शर्नरचर का रथ काले लोहे का बना है। इनके चितकबरे घोड़े आकाश से उत्पन्न हुये हैं। वे अपने रथ पर चढ़कर धीरे-धीरे चला करते हैं। राहु के तमोमय क्रंष्णवर्ण के रथ में मन की तरह वेगशाली काले रंग के आठ घोड़े एक ही बार जोत दिये गये हैं। ये रथ को सदा खींचा करते हैं। राहु पव॑ के दिन सूर्यमंडल से निकल कर चन्द्र मण्डल में प्रवेश करते हैं और फिर पर में ही चन्द्रमण्डल से निकलकर सूयेमण्डल में प्रवेश
verses.wordMeaning: Thus the greatest of secrets, the holiest of holy things, the story of what is famous as Nilakantha has been narrated to you.
