verses.sanskrit: ईश्वर उवाच: वरं वृणीष्व हव्याश यस्ते मनसि वर्तते
verses.transliteration: īśvara uvāca: varaṃ vṛṇīṣva havyāśa yaste manasi vartate
verses.translation: He became still more powerful by staying under the control of Uttanka. Dhundhu was found out by his sons who were digging. He had been lying hidden beneath the sand on the western side. He seemed to be furiously covering the worlds by means of the fire coming out of his mouth. O excellent one among the imbibers of Soma, by means of his Yogic power, he exuded water like the great ocean at the time of Moon-rise. It was a vast sheet of water with currents and waves. His sons excepting three were burnt by the Raksasa. Then the king of great strength destroyed all the attendants and kinsmen of Dhundhu. The king who was a Yogin, drank up his behemence in the form of water-flood (let loose by him) by means of his Yogic power and extinguished the fire by means of water. Then he overpowered the huge-bodied aquatic DrdhaSva was the eldest ofhis three sons who survived. BhadraSva and Kapilaiva were the younger ones.. DrdhaSva was known as Dhaundhumari (son of Dhundhumara). Haryasva was his son. His son was Nikumbha who was always engaged in Ksatra Dharma (military Pro- fession). Samhatasva was the son of Nikumbha. He is reputed as an expert in warfare. Krsasva and Aksayasva were the sons of Samhatasva. His wife was Haimavati who was like the river DfSadvati to the minds of the good. She was famous in the three worlds. Her son was Prasenajit. Yuvanasva was his son. He was very brilliant and famous in the three worlds as highly virtuous. The chaste lady Gauri was his wife. She was cursed by her husband and turned into the river Bahuda. 1 Her son Gaurika became an emperor. Mandhata, the son of Yuvanasva, became a king con¬ quering the three worlds. In this connection, Brahmanas well versed in Puranas, cite these two verses. "The entire region from the place where the Sun rises up to (the place) where he sets, the whole of it, is called the territory of Mandhata, son of Yuvanasva". People who know the (details of) different races also quote this verse. "Those who know Puranas call the son of Yuvanasva, noble-souled, a performer of sacrifices and (a king) of unmeasured splendour. Mandhata is the embodied form of Visnu."
verses.hindi: आनर्य कहते हैं। सप्तर्षि गण पूर्व कल्पों में उत्पन्न होने. वाले लोगों को ऋक्, यजु, साभ आदि श्रुतियों एवं वेदाज़ों का उपदेश कर श्रीत धरम का ज्ञान लाभ कराते हैं ऐसा सना जाता है। बीते हुए मन्वन्तरों में . उत्पन्न होने वाले लोगों के आचारों का स्मरण कर वे वतेमान मन्वन्तर के लोगों को उपदेश करते हैं अत वर्णाश्रम के विभागों से संयक्त उस धर्म को स्मात॑ घर्मं कहते हैं ।३०-३२॥ इस प्रक्रार लोक मेंये दो श्रोत्त

verses.sanskrit: वह्निर् उवाच: नमस्ते सर्वलोकेश उग्रमूर्ते नमो ऽस्तु ते । रेतसा तव संदग्धः कुष्ठी जातो महेश्वर । कृपां कुरु महादेव मम रोगं विनाशय
verses.transliteration: vahnir uvāca: namaste sarvalokeśa ugramūrte namo 'stu te / retasā tava saṃdagdhaḥ kuṣṭhī jāto maheśvara / kṛpāṃ kuru mahādeva mama rogaṃ vināśaya
verses.translation: His wife CaitrarathI was Sasabindu's daughter. She was known by the name ofBindumati also. She was a chaste lady and had no equal in beauty all over the earth. She was the eldest sister often thousand brothers. She was devotedly attached to her husband. Mandhata begot three sons of her. They were Purukutsa, Ambarisa and Mucukunda. Ambarlsa's successor was another Yuvanasva. Harita was Yuvanasva's son. Descendants of Harita are remembered by the name Suris. They were the (adopted) sons of Ahgiras (spiritual lineage). They were Brahmanas endowed with martial qualities. Purukutsa's successor was Trasaddasyu of great fame. He was born of Narmada. His son was Sambhuta. Sambhuta's son was the valorous Anaranya. He was killed by Ravana formerly while he was conquering the three Trasadasva was the son of Anaranya. His son was Haryasva. From Haryasva Drsadvatl gave birth to king Vasumata. His son was the virtuous king Tridhanva by name. The scholarly king Trayyaruna was the son of Tridhanvan. He had a powerful son named Satyavrata. Vidarbha's wife was abducted by him after killing (i.e. defeat¬ ing) the heaven-dwellers, when all the sacred mantras of marriage ceremony had been chanted and the ceremonies con¬ cluded. Visnuvfddha was his son whence his descendants are remembered as Visnuvrddhas. They were also the (adopted) sons of Ahgiras endowed with martial qualities. That (sin) was committed by him out of lust, or (pride) due to his strength, or to the powerful force exerted by the inevitable destiny, though he was intelligent. His father Trayyaruna banished him as he was sinful. Being infuriated with him, he repeated many times, "Be He spoke to his father again and again, Visvamitra of great penance left his wife in that land and performed a severe penance in the marshy land near the His wife tied her own bosom-born middle son (with; a rope) round his neck and offered him for sale in exchange for a hundred cows for maintaining (the remaining ones).
verses.hindi: एवं स्मार्त धर्म शिष्टाचार नाम से प्रसिद्ध हैं। शेष छाब्द से शिष्ट शब्द की निष्पत्ति होती है और उन्हीं शिष्ट लोगों के आचारों को शिष्टाच।र कहा जाता हैं । प्रत्येक मन्वन्तरों की समाप्ति के असवर पर जिन धामिक प्रवृत्ति वाले मनु एवं सप्त्धि प्रभति महानुभावों की सत्ता लोक में सन्‍्तानोत्पत्ति के बीजारोपण एवं धर्म की +धनश्चिद्धान्तरप्रन्थों ग. पुस्तके नास्ति ।

verses.sanskrit: ईश्वर उवाच: हव्यवाह भवारोगो मत्प्रसादाच्च सत्वरम् । अत्र तीर्थे कृतस्नानः स्वरूपं प्रतिपत्स्यसे
verses.transliteration: īśvara uvāca: havyavāha bhavārogo matprasādācca satvaram / atra tīrthe kṛtasnānaḥ svarūpaṃ pratipatsyase
verses.translation: On seeing the son of the sage tied round the neck, the excellent man of good rites, the virtuous-souled Satyavrata of great intellect, got him released by being sold. He nurtured him in order to propitiate Visvamitra and gain his sympathy. The boy came to be known as Galava because he had been tied round the neck {Gala ). That descendant of Kusika, a great sage of severe penance had been redeemed by that powerful (King). On account of his (?) sacred vow, devotion, mercy and solemn declaration, the king who adhered to the rules of discipline, sustained Visvamitra's wife also. After killing deer, boars, buffaloes and other forest animals, he cooked that flesh near the hermitage of ViSvamitra. At the behest of the father, he adopted a secret vow (UpdrhSu Vrata) and for that purpose took initiation ex¬ tending to twelve years. As the king (Satyavrata's father) had gone to the forest, the sage Vasistha, in the capacity of the king s priest, protected Ayodhya, the kingdom and the harem. Out of childishness, or due to the force of the inevit¬ able destiny, Satyavrata nursed a great grudge against Vasistha. While he was crying on being exiled by his father and banished from the kingdom, the sage Vasistha had not restrain- The Mantras chanted during the celebration of a marriage are concluded at the seventhstep (of the Saptafiadi rite) but Satyavrata abducted her (the bride ofVidarbha) at the seventh step. Vasistha the knower of Dharmas does not wish to repeat the hantras. So Vasistha was inwardly angry with Satyavrata* (?) It was because of being fully mindful of his position as preceptor that Vasistha did so then. Nor did Satyavrata understand the secret vow of (the sage). (Defective verses) When the father of lofty mind passed away, Indra did not shower for twelve years. Thereby all the people on the earth became weak. All these years the son was having Dikfa (i.e. performing holy rites in accordance with his fathers' injunction). Vasistha thought that the people would be saved if he was crowned again. So he restrained Satyavrata from keeping out of the kingdom further. The powerful (younger king) performed the holy rites for twelve years. When there was no meat avail¬ able, the son of the king saw the cow of the noble-souled Vasi¬ stha, Kamadugha (i.e. the yielder of desired objects). Out of spite, due to delusion and exhaustion and because he was hungry, the foremost among powerful persons who had adopted the practice ofDasyus (robbers and Candalas), killed the cow. He himself ate the meat and fed the sons of Visvamitra also. On hearing it Vasistha abandoned him then. The holy lord Vasistha spoke also thus to the son of the king (i.e. Satyavrata): "O base one among men, had it not been for the fact that you have already three Sahkus (sins), O cruel one, I would have let this iron Sahku (rod) fall on you. Your transgression (commission of sins) is of three forms: One because of the dissatisfaction of your father, the other due to the slaughter of the preceptor's cow and (finally) due to the partaking of unsanctified (flesh)

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा च महादेवस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत । अनन्तरं हव्यवाहः सस्नौ रेवाजले त्वरन्
verses.transliteration: ityuktvā ca mahādevastatraivāntaradhīyata / anantaraṃ havyavāhaḥ sasnau revājale tvaran
verses.translation: To Vasistha who was watching, it was very surprising. By the favour of Visvamitra, Tnsanku shines in heaven with great brilliance in the company of Devas. It is the result of the blessing of that intelligent one. A beautiful woman bedecked by the moon in the season Hemanta proceeds slowly. She is embellished by the three Bhavas and adorned by the heavenly body—a planet (called) TriSanku. Satyarata hailing from the Kekaya family was his wife. She gave birth to a son, HariScandra, the sinless. That king Hariscmdra was well known as Traisankava (son of Trisanku). He was renowned as an emperor and a performer of Rajasuya sacrifice. Hari&jandra's son was Rohita, the powerful. Harita, wasRohita's son. Cancu is called Harita (son of Harita). Vijaya and Sudeva were the sons of Cancu. Since he was the conqueror of all Ksatriyas, he is remembered as Vijaya. Ruruka was his son. He was a king, a great expert in matters pertaining to religion and wealth. Hrtaka (or Dhrtaka) was the son of Ruruka and Bahu was born of him. The king (viz. Bahu) who was addicted to vice was Even in that righteous Satyayuga that king was not very virtuous. Sagara was born as the son of Bahu. He was bom with a body containing poison in the hermitage of Bhrgu. He was saved by Turva (Aurva). After obtaining the missile pertaining to Fire-god from Bhargava, the king Sagara went over the whole of the earth and killed Talajanghas along with Haihayas. The unerring king repudiated the Dharma (code of Plow was the king Sagara (Sa-gara) born with poison (inside)? Why did the infuriated unerring.king repudi¬ ate the traditional holy rites of those powerful Ksatriyas such as the Sakas and others? These five clans, viz. Yavanas, Paradas, Kambojas, Pahlavas, (and Sakas) attacked him. His kingdom was plundered and taken by these powerful leading Ksatriyas. King Bahu whose realm was seized, renounced the world. Accompanied by his wife the righteous- souled king entered the forest and performed penance.
verses.hindi: मत्वादयश्र ये शिष्टा ये मया प्रागुदीरिताः । ते: शिष्टेश्ररितो धर्म: सम्यगेव युगे युगे.. . त्रयी बार्ता दण्डनीतिरिज्या वर्णाश्रमस्तथा । शिष्टराचयंते यस्मान्मेंनुना व पुनः पुनः ॥

verses.sanskrit: तदैव रोगनिर्मुक्तो ऽभवद्दिव्यस्वरूपवान् । स्थापयामास देवेशं स वह्निः पिङ्गलेश्वरम्
verses.transliteration: tadaiva roganirmukto 'bhavaddivyasvarūpavān / sthāpayāmāsa deveśaṃ sa vahniḥ piṅgaleśvaram
verses.translation: After some time the king once went to fetch water. Due to advancing years and weakness he died midway. His wife Yadavl who was pregnant then, followed him. Poison had been administered to her by her co-wife with a desire to kill the foetus. She prepared the funeral pyre of her husband, got him placed and lit it and was (about) to enter into the fire, In his urVa.fiministercd) poison. Thus she gave (child) alongh the: | t P Being harassed and victimised by the heroic and noble-souled Sagara, all of them desirous of protection sought Remembering his own vow and on hearing the words of his preceptor, Sagara put an end to their traditional rites of worship and made them change their dress and apparel. 1 He got half of the heads of Sakas shaved and released them. He got the heads of Yavanas and Kambojas comp¬ Paradas were compelled to keep their hair dis¬ hevelled and Pahlavas were made to grow their beards. They were debarred from Vedic study and the use of Va$afkara by that noble-souled king. Sakas, Yavanas, Kambojas, Pahlavas, Paradas, Kelisparsas, Mahisikas, Darvas, Colas and Khasas—all these were clans of Ksatriyas. Their traditional religious rites were prohibited by the noble-souled Sagara at the instance of Vasi$tha. Conducting his conquests righteously, the king con¬ quered the earth and took initiation for the performance of a horse-sacrifice. He let loose the horse. As it was being taken round, it was stolen near the shore of the south-eastern sea and made to enter beneath the earth. The king made all his sons to dig the whole area. Then ultimately, in the great ocean, they met with the primordial Being, Lord Visnu, Lord Hari, K r sna, the Lord of subjects, Lord Hamsa, Lord Narayana, in the form of Kapila. They came within the range of the vision of that brilliant being. Then all those sons (ofSagara) were burnt and four of them survived. They were Barhiketu, Suketu, Dharmarata and the heroic Pancavana. All these continued the lineage of the lord (Sagara).
verses.hindi: प्रत्यद्भानि च वक्ष्यामि धर्मस्येह तु लक्षणम् द द द रे६ दृष्द्वा प्रमुतमर्थ यः पृष्टो वे न निगृहति । यथा भुतप्रवादस्तु इत्येतत्सत्यलक्षणस् है ब्रह्मचर्थ जपो मौन निराहारत्वमेव च। इत्येतत्तपसो मल सुधोरं तददुरासदम् ४ १ पशुनां द्रव्यहृविषामक्सामयजुषां तथा । ऋत्विजां दंक्षिणानां च संयोगो यज्ञ उच्यते

verses.sanskrit: नाम्ना संपूजयामास तुष्टाव स्तुतिभिर्मुदा । ततो जगाम देशं स्वं देवानां हव्यवाहनः
verses.transliteration: nāmnā saṃpūjayāmāsa tuṣṭāva stutibhirmudā / tato jagāma deśaṃ svaṃ devānāṃ havyavāhanaḥ
verses.translation: Lord Hari, Narayana granted him boons such as the everlasting nature of his race, the benefit of a hundred horse-sacrifices, the all-pervading Samudra (ocean) as the son and perpetual residence in heaven. Taking the horse with him, the ocean, the lord of rivers, came there and bowed to him. On account of that action he earned the title of "Sagara" (born ofSagara). After regaining the horse from the ocean the king performed horse-sacrifices again and again making up the total of one hundred. We have heard (it reported) that there were sixty thousand sons. Those sixty thousand sons were burnt. Those noble-souled sixty thousand sons entered (merged in) the divine brilliance of Narayana. By what means did the sixty thousand sons of Sagara become powerful and valorous? Please narrate. Sagara had two wives. By means of penance they had burnt all their sins. The elder of them named Ke$Ini was the daughter of Vidarbha. Sumati, the sister of Suparna, accepted the boon of sixty thousand sons from the noble-souled sage, in accordance After some time the elder wife gave birth to the Sumati, the famous lady, gave birth to a gourd-like foetus. From the gourd-like foetus all the sixty thousand sons came out. The king caused (pieces of) the foetus to be depo¬ sited in (sixty thousand) jars of ghee and engaged as many nurses to look after them individually. Then, In the course of nine months, they grew well and came out of them (jars) hale and hearty; those blessed sons heightened the pleasure of Sagara. After a long time those sixty thousand sons (of Sagara) attained youth. Of those who (later) (closely) followed the horse (of Asvamedha) the eldest son of Sagara was a tiger among men. The powerful one was famous as Asamanja, otherwise known as Barhiketu. Since he was engaged in activities against the interest of the citizens, he was banished by his father at the very outset. The son of Asamanja was the powerful Amsuman. His son was a virtuous soul. He was well-known by the name of Dilipa. From Dillpa was born Bhagiratha, a hero of great splendour.
verses.hindi: मर्यादा व्यवस्था स्थापना के लिए शेष रह जाती है, उन्हें ही वास्तव में शिष्ट कट्दा जाता है। मनु प्रभूति : जिन शिष्ट महानुभावों का वर्णन मैं अभी-अभी थोड़ी देर पहिले कर चुका हूं, उन्हीं लोगों द्वारा प्रत्येक युगों में भली तरह आचरण किया गया धर्म भौत तथा स्मात॑ के नाम से प्रसिद्ध है।३३-३५। त्रयीवार्ता दण्डनीति, यज्ञाराधन, वर्णाश्रम व्यवस्था--इन सब का यतः मनु और पृबंकालीन शिष्ट ऋषिगण आचरण करते हैं, और बहुत दिनों से उनकी परम्परा अक्षुण्ण चली आती है, अतः वही शाश्वत ( सर्वदा वतंमान रहने वाला ) शिष्टाचार है। दान, सत्य, तपस्या, लोभनिवत्ति, विद्याध्ययन, यज्ञाराधन. सन्तानोत्पत्ति और दया--ये आठ शिष्टों के आचरण शिष्ठाचार के लक्षण हैं। यतः सभी मन्वन्तरों में मनु, सप्तर्षि तथा शिष्ट लोग इन धर्मों का पालन करते है अतः इन्हें दशिष्टाचार कहते हैं। इन धर्मों को श्रवण (सुनने) द्वारा ज्ञात होने के कारण
verses.wordMeaning: Lord Hari, Narayana granted him boons such as the everlasting nature of his race, the benefit of a hundred horse-sacrifices, the all-pervading Samudra (ocean) as the son and perpetual residence in heaven. Taking the horse with him, the ocean, the lord of rivers,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Lord Hari, Narayana granted him boons such as the everlasting nature of his race, the benefit of a hundred horse-sacrifices, the all-pervading Samudra (ocean) as the son and perpetual residence in heaven. Taking the horse with him, the ocean, the lord of rivers,…

verses.sanskrit: हव्यवाहेन भूपैवं स्थापितः पिङ्गलेश्वरः । जितक्रोधो हि यस्तत्र उपवासं समाचरेत्
verses.transliteration: havyavāhena bhūpaivaṃ sthāpitaḥ piṅgaleśvaraḥ / jitakrodho hi yastatra upavāsaṃ samācaret
verses.translation: Ganga, the most excellent of rivers, rendered beauti¬ ful with aerial chariots, was (brought here in this world) by him. She was given the status of a daughter by the (king), the "Bhaglratha brought down Ganga by means of his active endeavour. Hence Ganga is called Bhaglrathl by those who are the foremost ones among those conversant with genealogies (of kings)." Bhaglratha s son was Sruta by name. His successor was Nabhaga. He was always engaged in religious activities. Ambarisa was his son. Sindhudvlpa succeeded him. It is well-known that the knowers of the Purana of genealogies sing thus: "Protected by the arms of Ambarisa, son of Nabhaga, the earth became completely free from three types of Tapa (distress)". Ayutayu, the powerful, was the son of Sindhudvlpa. Rtuparna of great fame was the successor of Ayutayu. He was the knower of the divine Aksahrdaya Mantra (the Mantra with which people become sure winners at the game of dice). He was a powerful king and a friend to Nala. One of them was the son of Virasena and the other a leading member of the Iksvaku race. Rtuparna's son was Sarvakama who was lord of the people. King Sudasa was his son. He was Hamsamukha (one with the face of a swan) 2. Sudasa's son was the king Saudasa. He was well-known by the names of Kalmasapada and Mitrasaha. Vasistha, of great brilliance, begot of Kalma- sapada's wife the son Asmaka, for the purpose of making the line of Iksvaku flourish (and perpetuate). Urakama was the son of Asmaka and his son was Mulaka. As regards King Mulaka, they cite the following (verse). The text: Ijanena samudrddvai is obscure and gives an awkward meaning, especially of samudrat. Bd. P. v.167: ihanM sureSSd vai etc. 'was brought The heroic Rama, the knower of Dharmas, well-known After killing Lavana, the son of Madhu, Satrughna entered his Madhuvana and founded die city of Mathura there.
verses.hindi: श्रोत और स्मरण द्वारा ज्ञात होने के कारण स्मातें जानना चाहिए। इनमें यज्ञाराधन वेदाध्ययन प्रभृति घर कार्यों को श्रौत और ब्राह्मणादि चारों वर्ण एवं गृहस्थाश्रम प्रभृति चारों आश्रमों के अनुकूल किये जाने वाले धर्म कार्यों को स्मातें जानना चाहिए । अब मैं धर्म के प्रत्येक अंगों के लक्षण एवं उनकी व्याख्या कर॑ रहा हूं ३६-३६। जो व्यक्ति घटित घटना को देखकर पूछे जाने पर कुछ भी नहीं छिपाता और वास्तविक

verses.sanskrit: अतिरान्त्रफलं तस्य अन्ते रुद्रत्वमाप्नुयात् । गुणान्विताय विप्राय कपिलां तत्र भारत
verses.transliteration: atirāntraphalaṃ tasya ante rudratvamāpnuyāt / guṇānvitāya viprāya kapilāṃ tatra bhārata
verses.translation: Angada and Candraketu were the sons of Laksmana. Their territories at the border of mountain Himalaya were very prosperous and flourishing. Angadiya, the capital city of Angada, was in the land Karapatha. 1 Candravakfra, the city of the mighty Candraketu, was very auspicious. Tak?a and Puskara were the heroic sons of Bharata. Modem Karabagh or Baghan on the west bank of the Indus, at the foot of salt range called Niti hill in the Bannu district (cf. RaghuvamJa. XV-90). The beautiful city of Tak§a, viz. Takasila 1 is renowned in all the quarters. Puskaravati, 2 the city of the heroic Puskara, is also well-known. The people who know the Puranas sing this Gatha (laudatory verse): "All the principles are fettered to (con¬ centrated in) intelligent Rama due to his greatness." Rama was a dark-complexioned, youthful, red-eyed, bright-faced hero with arms extending upto the knees. With a smiling face and leonine shoulders, that mighty-armed (one) uttered only measured words. Rama reigned for ten thousand years. The sound of the chanting of Rk, Saman and Yajur Mantras and the twanging of his bow string were always heard. Proceeding in search of Slta, that renowned leader of men killed the (demon) of the family of Pulastya, who had committed sins before. Rama, son of Dasaratha, was brilliant with his own splendour. He possessed Sattvic qualities. He was richly endowed with good attributes. He surpassed even the Sun and the blazing fire in brilliance. Thus the mighty-armed scion of the family of Iksvaku killed Ravana along with all of his followers and then went back to Heaven. Srirama's son was called Kusa, He had another son Lava of great prowess. Understand (the names of) their realms. According to VR. VII. 101.10-15 it was founded by Bharata. Probably the same as 'Poukelaotes* mentioned by Greeks as being sacked by Alexander the great. De ( ) identifies it with Charsaddah eighteen miles north of Peshawar, on the Landi near its junction with the Kabul river. Modem Nasik or Paficavafi in Maharashtra.
verses.hindi: बात को ज्यों का त्यों प्रकट कर देता है, उसके इस व्यवहार को सत्य कहा गया है। ब्रह्मचर्य, जप, मौन, और निराहार--ये अति कठिन तथा दुर्लभ तपस्या के मूल हैं। पशु, द्रव्य हवनीय पदार्थ ऋक, साम, और यजुववेद के मंत्र, पुरोहित और दक्षिणा---इन सबके संयोग का नाम यज्ञ कहा जाता है। हित एवं अहित करने वाले सभी प्रकार के जीवों में अपने समान दृष्टि रखना दया का लक्षण कहा गया है ।४००४३। :: ४७८ वायुपुराणम् ।
verses.wordMeaning: Angada and Candraketu were the sons of Laksmana. Their territories at the border of mountain Himalaya were very prosperous and flourishing. Angadiya, the capital city of Angada, was in the land Karapatha. 1 Candravakfra, the city of the mighty Candraketu, was very auspicious.…

verses.sanskrit: अलंकृत्य सवत्सां च शक्त्यालङ्कारभूषिताम् । यः प्रयच्छति राजेन्द्र स गच्छेत्परमां गतिम्
verses.transliteration: alaṃkṛtya savatsāṃ ca śaktyālaṅkārabhūṣitām / yaḥ prayacchati rājendra sa gacchetparamāṃ gatim
verses.translation: Ahlnagu's successor was Pariyatra of great fame. His son was Dala and from him was born the king Bala. Bala's son was a pious-souled (king) Auhka 2 by name. His son was Vajranabha whose son was Sarikhana. Sankhana's son Dhyusitasva was a renowned scholar. King Visvasaha was the son of Dhyusitasva. Hiranyanabha belonged to Kosala. His son was Vasistha. He was remembered as the disciple of the grandson of Jaimini in all auspicious rites. He had studied five hundred Vedic Samhitas. 3 The Yoga philosophy was learned from him by the intelligent Yajfiavalkya. Pusya, his son, was a great scholar. His son was Dhruvasandhi. Sudarana was his son and Agnivarna was born of Sudarsana. Agnivarna's son was Slghra and Manu (Maru in Bd. P.) is remembered as the son of Slghraka. Manu adopted Dc(p. Ill) identifies it with Ujjain but our text locates it on the ridges of the Vindhya mountain. 'Uluka* as per Bd. P.v. 205. Pargiter, in the list of kings of Ayodhya, calls him'Uktha* ( A1HT\ ). Bd.P. v. 207 states that Pausyaiiji was his teacher in Sama Veda. Pau?yanji, a disciple of Sukarman, taught 500 branches of the Sama Veda. Manu'ssonwas Prasusruta. His son was Susandhi. Susandhi's son was A-marsa, otherwise known by the name Sahasvan. Sahasvan's son was the king known by the name ViSrutavan. Visrutavan's son was the king Brhadbala. These are the mostly remembered kings, the successors of Iksvaku. The most important members of the race have been enumerated here. One who reads well this creation of Vivasvan, the son of Aditi, becomes endowed with progeny. He attains identity with Vaivasvata Manu, lord Sraddha-Deva who bestows prosperity on the subjects. He becomes free from sins and Rajasic qualities. He becomes long-lived and does not swerve from the righteous path.
verses.hindi: आक्रुष्टो5भिहतो वा5पि ना5क्रोशेद्यो न हन्ति वा। ताइ-मनःकर्म भिः क्षान्तिस्तितिक्षेषा क्षमा स्मृता ॥
verses.wordMeaning: Ahlnagu's successor was Pariyatra of great fame. His son was Dala and from him was born the king Bala. Bala's son was a pious-souled (king) Auhka 2 by name. His son was Vajranabha whose son was Sarikhana. Sankhana's son Dhyusitasva was a renowned scholar.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Ahlnagu's successor was Pariyatra of great fame. His son was Dala and from him was born the king Bala. Bala's son was a pious-souled (king) Auhka 2 by name. His son was Vajranabha whose son was Sarikhana. Sankhana's son Dhyusitasva was a renowned scholar.…

verses.sanskrit: ॥ इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे पिङ्गलेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नाम षडशीतितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ र्क्व् अध्याय ८७ श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: ततो गच्छेन्महीपाल तीर्थं परमशोभनम् । स्थापितं मुनिसङ्घैर् यद्ब्रह्मवंशसमुद्भवैः
verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe piṅgaleśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaḍaśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 87 śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: tato gacchenmahīpāla tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam / sthāpitaṃ munisaṅghair yadbrahmavaṃśasamudbhavaiḥ
verses.translation: On being thus addressed, the infuriated Vaisarhpayana spoke to Yajnavalkya: "Return so me whatever you have learnt from me 55.
verses.hindi: स्वामिना5रक्ष्यमाणानामुत्सृष्टानां च सत्सु च। परस्वानामनादानमलोभ इह कीत्यंते दशात्मके यो विषये कारण चाष्टलक्षणे । न क्ुध्येत्तु प्रतिहतः स जितात्मा विभाष्यते ४८
verses.wordMeaning: On being thus addressed, the infuriated Vaisarhpayana spoke to Yajnavalkya: "Return so me whatever you have learnt from me 55.
verses.commentary: Sense: On being thus addressed, the infuriated Vaisarhpayana spoke to Yajnavalkya: "Return so me whatever you have learnt from me 55.

verses.sanskrit: ऋणमोचनमित्याख्यं रेवातटसमाश्रितम् । षण्मासं मनुजो भक्त्या तर्पयन् पितृदेवताः
verses.transliteration: ṛṇamocanamityākhyaṃ revātaṭasamāśritam / ṣaṇmāsaṃ manujo bhaktyā tarpayan pitṛdevatāḥ
verses.translation: On being commanded thus, that sage Yajnavalkya, the most excellent among the knowers of Brahman, vomited the embodied forms of Yajur-Mantras smeared with blood and gave them back to his preceptor.
verses.hindi: कारण्यात्सवंभूते भ्यः सुविभागस्तु बन्धुषु
verses.wordMeaning: On being commanded thus, that sage Yajnavalkya, the most excellent among the knowers of Brahman, vomited the embodied forms of Yajur-Mantras smeared with blood and gave them back to his preceptor.
verses.commentary: Sense: On being commanded thus, that sage Yajnavalkya, the most excellent among the knowers of Brahman, vomited the embodied forms of Yajur-Mantras smeared with blood and gave them back to his preceptor.

verses.sanskrit: देवैः पितृमनुष्यैश्च ऋणमात्मकृतं च यत् । मुच्यते तत्क्षणान् मर्त्यः स्नातो वै नर्मदाजले
verses.transliteration: devaiḥ pitṛmanuṣyaiśca ṛṇamātmakṛtaṃ ca yat / mucyate tatkṣaṇān martyaḥ snāto vai narmadājale
verses.translation: O Brahmanas, then he meditated and worshipped the Sun-god. What was vomited rose up in the sky and stood near the Solar Brahman.
verses.hindi: श्रुतिस्मृतिभ्यां विहितो धर्मों वर्णाश्रभात्मकः । शिष्टाचाराविरुद्धश्व धमः सत्साधुसद्भतः ५१ संस्थासः कर्मणो न्यासः कृतानासकृतेः सह । कुशलाकुशलानां च प्रह्म्ं त्याग उच्चते..
verses.wordMeaning: O Brahmanas, then he meditated and worshipped the Sun-god. What was vomited rose up in the sky and stood near the Solar Brahman.
verses.commentary: Sense: O Brahmanas, then he meditated and worshipped the Sun-god. What was vomited rose up in the sky and stood near the Solar Brahman.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्यक्षं दुरितं तत्र दृश्यते फलरूपतः । तत्र तीर्थे तु यो राजन्नेकचित्तो जितेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration: pratyakṣaṃ duritaṃ tatra dṛśyate phalarūpataḥ / tatra tīrthe tu yo rājannekacitto jitendriyaḥ
verses.translation: The delighted Sun handed over the Yajur-Mantras which had gone up to the solar disc. The Sun-god gave them to the intelligent Brahmarati (in Bd. P.) Yajnavalkya who had assumed the form of a horse.
verses.hindi: जो दूसरों हरा गाली फटकार पाने पर अथवा मार पीट खा जाने पर भी अपकर्त्ता को गाली फटकार नहीं देता अथवा उसे नहीं मारता तथा मनसा, वाचा, कर्मणा उन सब अपंकारों को सहन कर लेता है, उसके इस व्यवहार का नाम क्षमा कहा गया है। स्वामी द्वारान रखाई जाने वाली एवं छोड़ी गई या. पड़ी हुईं परकीय वस्तु को ग्रहण न करना निर्लोभता के लक्षण कहे गये हैं। मैथुन (स्त्री पुरुष संयोग)
verses.wordMeaning: The delighted Sun handed over the Yajur-Mantras which had gone up to the solar disc. The Sun-god gave them to the intelligent Brahmarati (in Bd. P.) Yajnavalkya who had assumed the form of a horse.
verses.commentary: Sense: The delighted Sun handed over the Yajur-Mantras which had gone up to the solar disc. The Sun-god gave them to the intelligent Brahmarati (in Bd. P.) Yajnavalkya who had assumed the form of a horse.

verses.sanskrit: स्नात्वा दानं च वै दद्याद् अर्चयेद् गिरिजापतिम् । ऋणत्रयविनिर्मुक्तो नाके दीप्यति देववत्
verses.transliteration: snātvā dānaṃ ca vai dadyād arcayed girijāpatim / ṛṇatrayavinirmukto nāke dīpyati devavat
verses.translation: Thenceforth, the Brahmanas who began the study of the Yajus handed over to Yajnavalkya in the form of a horse ( Vajin ) became known as Vajins.
verses.hindi: का व्यवहार न करना, मन से भी उसकी चिन्तना एवं कल्पना ने करना तथा भोग विलास विषयक अन्य वस्तुओं से सच्ची निवृत्ति प्राप्त कर लेना ब्रह्मचयं कहा गया है । और उसका पूर्ण रूपेण पालन करना दम है ।४४-४६। अपने लिए अथवा पराये के लिए जिसकी इन्द्रियाँ मिथ्या विषयों में अभिनिविष्ट नहीं होती उसके इस व्यवहार का नाम शम है। जो व्यक्ति दसों प्रकार के ऐन्द्रियक विषयों एवं आठ प्रकार के लक्षणों में फसकर या प्रतिहत होकर भी क्रोध नहीं प्रकट करता वह॒जितास्मा कहा जाता है। जो जो अपने को अति प्रिय लगने वाली वस्तु-हो, तथा जिसकी प्राप्ति ध्याय मार्ग से हुई हो, उसे गुणवानों को समर्वित करना दान का लक्षण है ।४७-४६। दान तीन प्रकार के होते हैं, कनिष्ठ, ज्येष्ठ और मध्यम । उनमें निःश्रेयस् (मोक्ष) की प्राप्ति के लिये किया गया दान ज्येष्ठ और स्वार्थ सिद्धि के लिए किया गया दान कनिष्ठ कहलाता
verses.wordMeaning: Thenceforth, the Brahmanas who began the study of the Yajus handed over to Yajnavalkya in the form of a horse ( Vajin ) became known as Vajins.
verses.commentary: Sense: Thenceforth, the Brahmanas who began the study of the Yajus handed over to Yajnavalkya in the form of a horse ( Vajin ) became known as Vajins.

verses.translation: From Udavasu was born the extremely pious-souled Nandivardhana. From Nandivardhana was born the heroic and pious Suketu. From Suketu was born the pious-souled Devarata of great strength. It is heard that the pious-souled Brhaduccha was Devarata's son. Brhaduccha's son was the valorous Mahavlrya. Dhrti- man was the son of Mahavlrya and his son was Sudhrti. The pious-souled Dhrstaketu, the oppressor of enemies, was the son of Sudhrti. Dhrstaketu's son was well known by the name of Haryasva.

verses.translation: Also called Janakapur, capital of Videha in the district of Darbhanga (Bihar). It was famous for its Brahmanical University (upto 14th cent. A.D ). Now a new Sanskrit University has been founded there some years Pratimbaka in Bd.P.v, 11. Pargiter records 'Pratindhaka* as his name From Maharoma was born, the famous Svarnaroma. Svarnaroma's son was the king Hrasvaroma. It is heard that the son of Hrasvaroma was the scholar Slradhvaja. While this king was ploughing, Sita, of great fame, was born. She became the chaste queen of Rama. She was devoted to her husband and a virtuous wife.

verses.translation: How was Sita of great fame born while (the field) was being ploughed. Why did the king plough the field wherein she was born? While the Agniksetra (the field where sacrifice was to be performed) was being ploughed in accordance with the injunction in the course of the horse-sacrifice of the noble soul she was born out of it. From Slradhvaja was born the Maithila (king of Mithila) named Bhanuman. His brother was Kusadhvaja, the lord and king of Kasl.

verses.hindi: अव्यक्त एवं अविशेष से अचेतन में जो चेतनात्मक विकार प्रादुभूत होते हैं, उनके चेतनत्व, अचेतनत्व एवं अनध्यत्व के सम्यक् ज्ञान को ही वास्तविक ज्ञान कहते हैं । धर्म के प्रत्येक अंगों का.यही लक्षण पूर्वकाल में स्वायम्भूव मन्वश्तर में वर्तमान, धर्म के तत्वों को जानने वाले ऋषियों ने बतलाया हैं ।५४-५५॥ अब इसके उपराब्त आप लोगों को मैं मन्वन्तर की विधि बतला रहा हूँ, और यह भी बतला रहा हैँ कि उसमें चारों वर्णों के अपने-अपने तथा परस्पर एक दूसरे के साथ कंसे व्यवहार होते रहे हैं। प्रत्येक मन्वन्तर में समस्त श्रतियों का विभिन्न ढंग से विधान होता है। शतरुद्रिय को छोड़कर ऋक्, यजु, साम, देवता, स्तोत्र, विधि, हवन--ये सभी पहिले ही की तरह प्रव्तित होते हैं। द्रव्यस्तोत्र, गुणस्तोत्र, कर्मस्‍्तोत्र और आधभिजनिक स्तोत्र-ये चार प्रकार के स्तोत्र कहे गये हैं ।५६-५८। प्रत्येक मन्वन्तरों में जिस प्रकार के

verses.sanskrit: ॥ इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे कपिलेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामाष्टाशीतितमो ऽध्यायः ॥ र्क्व् अध्याय ८९ श्रीमार्कण्डेय उवाच: ततो गच्छेत्तु राजेन्द्र पूतिकेश्वरमुत्तमम् । नर्मदादक्षिणे कूले सर्वपापक्षयंकरम्
verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe kapileśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmāṣṭāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 89 śrīmārkaṇḍeya uvāca: tato gacchettu rājendra pūtikeśvaramuttamam / narmadādakṣiṇe kūle sarvapāpakṣayaṃkaram
verses.translation: The highly intelligent Brahmana had sublimated his sexual urge. He stood without even winking his eyes. His body attained the status of Soma. The sage of sanctified soul in the state of Soma rose up (to the sky). The Soma juice exuded from his eyes illuminating all the quarters. On being ordered by Vidhi (Brahma), the ten Devis (i.e. the quarters) gathered together there and received it in their womb collectively, but could not do so (for long). When those goddesses (ladies) were unable to hold the foetus in their wombs, the foetus endowed with lustre, illu¬ minated the worlds like the Moon (now) blessing everyone; it emerged from the quarters (womb of the ladies) and fell on the ground (assuming the form of) the Moon along with them (the goddesses). On seeing Soma falling, Brahma, the grandfather of the worlds, placed him in a chariot, with a desire for the welfare of the worlds. O Brahmanas, indeed he (the Moon) was a Deva(god) himself, a seeker of righteousness and truthful to the. promise. We have heard that (the chariot) was (fitted with) yoked to a thousand white horses. When that great soul, the son of Atri, had fallen, There itself, the sons of Angiras and Bhj*gu eulogised by means, of Rks, Yajur mantras and many Atharva Ahgirasa mantras.
verses.hindi: मंत्रों की उत्पत्ति हुईं। अब इसके बाद मैं अतीत एवं भविष्यत्कालीन ऋषियों के ऋषित्व का लक्षण बतला रहा हूँ ।५९-६२। वे ऋषिगण पाँच प्रकार के कहे गये हैं। उन ऋषियों के भा धर्म की उत्पत्ति के ४८० ' वायुपुराणम्

verses.sanskrit: स्थापितं जाम्बुवन्तेन लोकानां तु हितार्थिना । राजा प्रसेनजिन्नाम तस्यां वक्षस्थलान् मणौ
verses.transliteration: sthāpitaṃ jāmbuvantena lokānāṃ tu hitārthinā / rājā prasenajinnāma tasyāṃ vakṣasthalān maṇau
verses.translation: The brilliance of the shining Moon who was being eulo¬ gised, developed further and it purified all the three worlds. In that prominent chariot, he circumambulated the earth extending upto the ocean twenty-one times. His splendour that reached the earth became medicinal herbs. They sparkle by means of his brilliance. O excellent Brahamans! He sustains subjects of four types and the universe with them (herbs). Lord Soma is indeed the nourisher of the universe. Having acquired splendour through the penance (of Atri), the eulogy (of Devas and sages) and his own religious activities, the blessed one (Soma) performed penance for ten times ten Padma years, (one Padma<= a thousand billion). Soma who is famous by his own Karmans will be the pervader of those (ten) gold-complexioned goddesses (viz. quarters) who sustain the whole world. Thereafter, Brahma the foremost among the knowers of Brahman, entrusted him with the kingdom of seeds, herbs, Brahmanas and waters. Being naturally the foremost among those who shine brilliantly and, thereafter, being crowned over a big kingdom, (Soma) of great splendour became the king of kings and puri¬ fied the worlds and developed them.
verses.hindi: अतीतानागतानां तु पत्चचा ऋषिरुच्यते । अतस्त्वुषीणां वक्ष्यामि ह्यार्षस्प स समुख्ध व् ६३ गुणसाम्ये वर्तमाने सर्वंसंप्रलये तदा । अतिचारे तु देवानामतिदेशे तयोयेथा

verses.transliteration: samutkṣipte tu tenaiva sapūtirabhavadvraṇaḥ / tatra tīrthe tapastaptvā nirvraṇaḥ samajāyata
verses.translation: Daksa, the son of Pracetas, gave twenty-seven Daksa- yanls (daughters of Daksa) of great holy rites to Indu (the Moon). They (people) know them as Naksatras (constellations). Having attained that great kingdom, Soma the lord of possessors of Sonia (i.e. Brahmanas) performed the Rajasuya sacrifice, wherein the Daksina amounted to hundred thousands. In that sacrifice, Hiranyagarbha was the Udgatr (the presiding priest who recites mantras); Brahma occupied the seat of Brahma and lord Narayana Hari was the Sadasya (member of the witnessing assembly). He was surrounded by Sanatkumara and other leading original Brahmarsis. O Brah¬ manas, we have heard that Soma gave the three worlds as Nine Devls, viz. Smi,_Kuhu,v P Though implored by Devas and celestial sages, he O Brahraanas, Usanas, one of the Ahgiras (?) took h is side. Indeed, he had been the highly brilliant disciple of Bphas- Thanks to that affection, lord Rudra took The great miraculous weapon was discharged by that noble soul aiming at the chief Brahmana sage and Devas whereby their fame was destroyed. There ensued a great battle directly (between Devas andAsuras). It was called Tarakamaya 1 2 (concerningTara?)• It caused great destruction of Devas, Danavas and all the worlds.

verses.translation: Only three Devas survived. They are remembered by the name Tusitas. They sought shelter in Brahma, the primor¬ dial lord, the grandfather of the worlds. Then Pitamaha (Brahma) himself prevented Usanas and Rudra, the eldest (deity) Sankara, (from fighting) and handed over Tara to Ahgiras (Brhaspati). Sini and Kuhu are deities presiding over (i) the day preceding the new moon day on which the moon rises with scarcely visible crescent and (ii) the new moon day when the moon is invisible, respectively. Out of the twelve wars between Devas and Asuras this was the fifth one. On seeing that Tara, the lady with a moon-like face, was pregnant, the Brahmana Brhaspati said: "Don't you cast off the foetus? In (your) body belonging to me another foetus shall by no means be held in the womb." Still she did not cast off the child • Dasyu-hantama * (the slayer of robbers). Like the fire that blazes after catching the I§ika grass, the son surpassed the beautiful bodies of Devas at the very instant he was born. Their suspicion having been aroused, Suras spoke to Tara: "Tell us the truth, whose son is he, Soma's or Brhas- pati's r

verses.sanskrit: सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति सम्पूज्य परमेश्वरम् । कृष्णाष्टम्यां चतुर्दश्यां सर्वकालं नराधिप । ये ऽर्चयन्ति सदा देवं ते न यान्ति यमालयम्
verses.transliteration: sarvānkāmānavāpnoti sampūjya parameśvaram / kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ sarvakālaṃ narādhipa / ye 'rcayanti sadā devaṃ te na yānti yamālayam
verses.translation: When she, out of bashfulness, did not tell Devas, 'yes' or 'no*, the boy Dasyuhantaraa was about to curse her. Preventing him, Brahma said to Tara, "(We have) suspicion that it is Candra's (Moon's), O Tara; therefore, speak the truth. Whose son is this?" With palms joined in reverence, she said this to lord Brahma, the granter of boons, that the noble-souled boy Das- yuhantama was Soma's. Thereafter, sniffing at the head of his son, Lord Soma, the Prajapati, named his intelligent son as Budha. (Defective verse) While rising up to go towards the east*, Budha begot a son of the princess (Ila). Pururavas, his son of great brilliance, was born of Ila. In UrvasI, six sons of great prowess were born (to Pururavas). Then, being violently attacked by pulmonary con¬ sumption Soma became exhausted and helpless. Overwhelmed by consumption, the Moon's disc became pale and weak. He, therefore, sought refuge in his own father Atri. Atri, of great fame, quelled his sin (disease). He was cured of the pulmonary consumption and so he shone with bri¬ lliance all round. O excellent Brahmanas, thus the origin of Soma has been recounted by me. Listen to and understand his race that is being recounted to you, O excellent Brahmanas.

verses.translation: He was an expounder of Brahman (Vedas), destro¬ yer of foes and invincible in battle. He regularly performed Agnihotra and granted gifts of lands to sacrificial priests. He was truthful in speech and intelligently engaged in holy rites. Handsome in features, he indulged in sexual inter¬ course in great privacy. He was an extraordinarily dutiful son, and in beauty of form was unequalled in all the worlds.

verses.translation: The present chapter which corresponds to Bd. 3.66, opens with the episode of Pururavas, the founder of the Lunar race and Urvasi, the celestial nymph. This episode gives the background of the famous "Dialogue" sukta in the RV. This romantic story inspired Kalidasa to write his immortal play Vikramorvattya. UrvasI was a Gandharva lady. Forsaking Devas, how did she attain the king, a mere human being? O (sage)' of extensive learning, please explain it to us.

verses.translation: She was overwhelmed by the curse of Brahma and therefore had to approach a human being. The beautiful lady (became the wife of) Aila Pururavas under certain stipulated conditions. In order to redeem herself from the evil effects of the curse, she stipulated that she should not see him naked except at the time of sexual intercourse or when swayed with passionate love.

verses.translation: Urvasi, as her name indicates, seems to have hailed from the ancient central Asian town Ur. It appears that fashionable ladies from Ur had a fascination for rams in the fourth millennium B.G. In his excavation at Ur, Sir Leonard Wooley discovered in a queen's tomb of 3300 B.G. a pair of rams, "beautifully and intricately made. Their bodies were covered with fleece of shell....their heads and legs were of gold" (quoted on in A. J. Karandikar's introduction to his Marathi book Background of the Mahabharata —Mahabhdratdci PdrSvabhdmi 9 Poona, 1980. This fascination for rams may be the cause of the inclusion and importance attached to this term in the marriage-contract between Pururavas and UrvaSi. verses.sanskrit: तालमेघभयात् पार्थ रविरुद्राः सवासवाः । यमः स्कन्दो जलेशो ऽग्निर्वायुर्देवो धनेश्वरः
verses.transliteration: tālameghabhayāt pārtha ravirudrāḥ savāsavāḥ / yamaḥ skando jaleśo 'gnirvāyurdevo dhaneśvaraḥ
verses.translation: Then the Gandharvas took away the second ram as well. When the second ram was taken away, the queen spoke "O Lord, O king, my sons are taken away as though they are the sons of a helpless woman". Thus taunted the king got up and rushed out (though he was) naked.
verses.hindi: रहता है। वह महान् तमोराशि के पार व्यवस्थित रहकर उसकी अपेक्षा अपनी विलक्षण ज्योति के कारण इस रूप में प्रकट होता है। सर्वज्ञानाधार महान् की स्थिति वहीं अन्धकार के अवसान स्थल पर है--ऐसी श्रुति है ।६९-७३। महान् के विवर्तित होने पर ज्ञान, वेराग्य, ऐश्वर्य और धर्मं--ये चार प्रकार की बुद्धि उत्पन्न हुई । उसकी यह बुद्धि स्वाभाविक तथा सर्वाधिक प्रभाव शालिनी होती है। शरीरयुक्त महत्त्व के बिवतं से ही सिद्धि प्राप्त होती कहौ जाती है जो अव्यक्त नाम से प्रसिद्ध उस पुरी में शयन करता है । तथा उस पुरी का स्वामी है, एवं जिसको उस क्षेत्र का सम्यक् ज्ञान है, उसे पुरुष कहते हैं। क्षेत्र के सम्यक ज्ञान होने के कारण ही उसे क्षेत्रज्ञ कहा जाता है। मनन करने के कारण वह भगवान् एवं अधण्ड बुद्धि के साथ संयुक्त रहने के कारण बोधात्मक कहा जाता है। वह अचेतन प्रकृति के स्वाभाविक गुण एवं परिमाणव्ञ
verses.wordMeaning: Then the Gandharvas took away the second ram as well. When the second ram was taken away, the queen spoke "O Lord, O king, my sons are taken away as though they are the sons of a helpless woman". Thus taunted the king got up and rushed out (though he was) naked.
verses.commentary: Sense: Then the Gandharvas took away the second ram as well. When the second ram was taken away, the queen spoke "O Lord, O king, my sons are taken away as though they are the sons of a helpless woman". Thus taunted the king got up and rushed out (though he was) naked.

verses.sanskrit: सवाक्पतिमहेशाश्च नष्टचित्ताः पितामहम् । गता देवा ब्रह्मलोकं तत्र दृष्ट्वा पितामहम्
verses.transliteration: savākpatimaheśāśca naṣṭacittāḥ pitāmaham / gatā devā brahmalokaṃ tatra dṛṣṭvā pitāmaham
verses.translation: The king rushed out seeking the sheep taken away by the Gandharvas, whereupon a great Maya (i lusion) was produced by them. The great palace became illuminated sud denly and she saw the naked king. On seeing the king naked, the Apsara lady (Urvasi) who could assume any form she wished, vanished (from there). On realising that she had vanished, the Gandharvas abandoned the rams there and disappeared themselves.
verses.hindi: व्यक्ताव्यक्त सभी पदार्थों में संसिद्धि (लोक-सिद्धि) के लिये परिगत (व्याप्त) रहता है ।७४-७७। क्षेत्रज्ञ द्वारा अधिष्टित क्षेत्र शक्ति इस प्रकार स्वयं निष्क्रिय रहकर क्षेत्रज्ञ द्वारा भोग्यविषय रूप में परिज्ञात होती है ।७८। ऋष् धातु गमन, मोक्ष, प्राप्ति, ज्ञान, श्रुति, सत्य एवं तपस्था--इन अ्थों में प्रयुक्त होता है, जो इन अर्थों से समन्बवित होकर पर ब्रह्म में निरत रहता है वह ऋषि कहा जाहा है ।७९। जो ऋषि
verses.wordMeaning: The king rushed out seeking the sheep taken away by the Gandharvas, whereupon a great Maya (i lusion) was produced by them. The great palace became illuminated sud denly and she saw the naked king. On seeing the king naked,…
verses.commentary: Sense: The king rushed out seeking the sheep taken away by the Gandharvas, whereupon a great Maya (i lusion) was produced by them. The great palace became illuminated sud denly and she saw the naked king. On seeing the king naked,…

verses.sanskrit: तुष्टुवुर्विविधैः स्तोत्रैर् वागीशप्रमुखाः सुराः । गुणत्रयविभागाय पश्चाद् भेदम् उपेयुषे
verses.transliteration: tuṣṭuvurvividhaiḥ stotrair vāgīśapramukhāḥ surāḥ / guṇatrayavibhāgāya paścād bhedam upeyuṣe
verses.translation: On seeing the abandoned rams, the king, the lord, took them with him and returned. Unable to see her there, the king became extremely dejected and lamented. Seeking her here and there, the king roamed over
verses.hindi: सासारिक विषयों से निवृत्ति प्राप्त करते समय उस अव्यक्त परम तत्व में निवेश करता है वह परम (महा) ऋषि कहा गया है। गमन अथ में प्रयुक्त होने वाले ऋष् धातु से ऋषि शब्द की निष्पत्ति होती है, सृष्टि के के आदि काल में यतः स्वयमेव समुत्पन्न हुए थे अतः इनकों भी ऋषि कहते हैं। परम ऐद्वर्य सम्पन्न ब्रह्मा ४८२ ...वायुपुराणम्
verses.wordMeaning: On seeing the abandoned rams, the king, the lord, took them with him and returned. Unable to see her there, the king became extremely dejected and lamented. Seeking her here and there, the king roamed over
verses.commentary: Sense: On seeing the abandoned rams, the king, the lord, took them with him and returned. Unable to see her there, the king became extremely dejected and lamented. Seeking her here and there, the king roamed over

verses.sanskrit: दृष्ट्वा देवान् निरुत्साहान् विवर्णान् अवनीपते । प्रसादाभिमुखो देवः प्रत्युवाच दिवौकसः
verses.transliteration: dṛṣṭvā devān nirutsāhān vivarṇān avanīpate / prasādābhimukho devaḥ pratyuvāca divaukasaḥ
verses.translation: The lady of splendid evebrows saw the king not very far. Urvasi then spoke to her friends: "Here is that excellent man with whom I lived." She pointed out che king to them. Then those ladies, the Apsaras (with five braids of hair) appeared in front (of him). On seeing her (Urvasi) the king was delighted. He began to lament in diverse ways, "o cruel lady, come (unto me). Stay willingly, stand by your words."
verses.hindi: ईश्वराणां शुभास्तेषां मानसा औरसाभ्र ते । अहंकार तपश्चेव त्यक्त्वा च ऋषितां गताः
verses.wordMeaning: The lady of splendid evebrows saw the king not very far. Urvasi then spoke to her friends: "Here is that excellent man with whom I lived." She pointed out che king to them. Then those ladies, the Apsaras (with five braids of hair) appeared in front (of him).…

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मोवाच: स्वागतं सुरसङ्घस्य कान्तिर्नष्टा पुरातनी । हिमक्लिष्टप्रभावेण ज्योतींषीव मुखानि वः
verses.transliteration: brahmovāca: svāgataṃ surasaṅghasya kāntirnaṣṭā purātanī / himakliṣṭaprabhāveṇa jyotīṃṣīva mukhāni vaḥ
verses.translation: These and similar subtle words they exchanged. Urvasi then spoke to Aila: "O lord, I have been rendered pregnant by you. Undoubtedly your son will be born within a year." The king stayed for a night with her. The king went back to his city with great delight. When a year elapsed, the king of great fame came to Urvasi again.
verses.hindi: तस्मात्त ऋषयस्ते वे भृतादौ तत्त्वदर्शना:। ऋषिपुत्रा ऋषीकास्तु मैथुनादगर्भसंभवाः ८४ ऋषीणां च सुतास्ते तु विज्ञेया ऋषिपुत्रका:। ऋषन्ति वे श्रुत॑ तस्माहिशेषां चेव तत्त्वतः ॥।
verses.wordMeaning: These and similar subtle words they exchanged. Urvasi then spoke to Aila: "O lord, I have been rendered pregnant by you. Undoubtedly your son will be born within a year." The king stayed for a night with her. The king went back to his city with great delight.…

verses.sanskrit: प्रशमादर्चिषाम् एतद् अनुद्गीर्णं सुरायुधम् । वृत्रस्य हन्तुः कुलिशं कुण्ठितश्रीव लक्ष्यते
verses.transliteration: praśamādarciṣām etad anudgīrṇaṃ surāyudham / vṛtrasya hantuḥ kuliśaṃ kuṇṭhitaśrīva lakṣyate
verses.translation: After staying with her for a night, the lofty-minded king became overwhelmed by passionate love. In a pitiable tone he spoke: "Be mine for ever". Urvasi then said to Aila: "The Gandharvas will grant you (that) boon. O great king, choose that boon and tell them this yourself:
verses.hindi: अव्यक्तात्मा महात्मा चाहंकारात्मा तथेब च्। भृतात्मा चेन्द्रियात्मा च तेषां तजुज्ञानमुच्यते ॥॥ इत्येता ऋषिजातीस्तु नामभिः पन्च वे शूणु ८७
verses.wordMeaning: After staying with her for a night, the lofty-minded king became overwhelmed by passionate love. In a pitiable tone he spoke: "Be mine for ever". Urvasi then said to Aila: "The Gandharvas will grant you (that) boon. O great king, choose that boon and tell them this yourself:

verses.sanskrit: किं चायमरिदुर्वारः पाणौ पाशः प्रचेतसः । मन्त्रेण हतवीर्यस्य फणिनो दैन्यम् आश्रितः
verses.transliteration: kiṃ cāyamaridurvāraḥ pāṇau pāśaḥ pracetasaḥ / mantreṇa hatavīryasya phaṇino dainyam āśritaḥ
verses.translation: T choose the boon of Salokya (having the same world) with the noble-souled Gandharvas' ". The king accepted the suggestion saying "So be it", and requested the Gandharvas for the boon. The Gandharvas replied, "So be it". After filling the Sthali (mud-pot) with fire, the Gandharvas spoke to him: "O king, performing the sacrifice with this, you will attain that world." 1
verses.hindi: ब्रह्मणो मानसा हयत उद्भूताः स्वयमीश्वराः के मानस पुत्र ऋषिगण आदि काल में स्वयमेव उत्पन्न हुये थे। जो किसी मान (परिमाण) द्वारा नापा नहीं जा सकता अर्थात् जिसके परिमाण की कोई सीमा नहीं है, वही महान् कहा जाता है। जो बुद्धि के पारदर्शी (परम बुद्धिमान) तथा धैयंशाली विद्वान गण, सभी ओर से सभी गुणों में महान् का अवलम्बन करते हैं अथवा उस (महान) के सानब्निध्य को प्राप्त करते हैं, वे महषि कहे जाते हैं ।४०-८२। उन परम

verses.sanskrit: कुबेरस्य मनःशल्यं शंसतीव पराभवम् । अपविद्धगतो वायुर्भग्नशाख इव द्रुमः
verses.transliteration: kuberasya manaḥśalyaṃ śaṃsatīva parābhavam / apaviddhagato vāyurbhagnaśākha iva drumaḥ
verses.translation: He took the fire and went back to his city along with the prince. He placed the fire in the Arani and went to his abode along with his son. As w. 40-45 show, this Puraria attributes to Pururavas, the institution (or encouragement) of the performance of Yajha out of the fire created from Arafii ( of Asvattha wood) by attrition. Bd. 3.66.19 gives the credit of introducing three fires (Daksinagni etc.) to Pururavas.
verses.hindi: ऐप्वयेंशाली महर्षियों के औरस तथा मानस पुत्रों ने भी अहद्धुार एवं अज्ञान का परित्याग कर ऋषित्व को प्राप्ति की ।5३। इस प्रकार सभी चराचर जीवों में तत्व के दर्शन करने वाले ऋषि कहलाये और उन ऋषियों के मैथन द्वारा गर्भ से उत्पन्त होने वाले पुत्र गण ऋषीक कहलाये । जो सत्य के परम पुजारी एवं महातेजस्वी ऋषिगण पंचतन्मात्राओं एवं सत्य पर निर्भर रहने बाले हैं वे सप्तर्षि कहलाते हैं। ऋषियों के
verses.wordMeaning: He took the fire and went back to his city along with the prince. He placed the fire in the Arani and went to his abode along with his son. As w. 40-45 show, this Puraria attributes to Pururavas,…

verses.sanskrit: यमो ऽपि विलिखन्भूमिं दण्डेनास्तमितत्विषा । कुरुते ऽस्मिन्न् अमोघो ऽपि निर्वाणालातलाघवम्
verses.transliteration: yamo 'pi vilikhanbhūmiṃ daṇḍenāstamitatviṣā / kurute 'sminn amogho 'pi nirvāṇālātalāghavam
verses.translation: S rim an, the successor of Bhima, was a king with go en lustre (otherwise known as Kancanaprabha). The scholarly and powerful Suhotra was the son of Kancana (i.e. Kancana- prabha). Jahnu was the son of Suhotra, born of Kesika s
verses.hindi: पुत्र गण, जो कि ऋषीकों के नाम से विख्यात हैं, शास्त्रों के तत्त्व पर विशेष अधिकार रखते हैं, अतः श्रुत ज्ञान (शास्त्रीय ज्ञान के सम्यक् विश्लेषण करने के कारण वे श्रूतषि नाम से विख्यात हैं ।०४-०६। अव्यक्तात्मा महात्मा, अहड्भारात्मा, भूतात्मा तथा इन्द्रियात्मा--ये ऋषिगण पाँच प्रकार के ज्ञान का अनुशीलन करते कहे जाते हैं । ऋषियों की यह जाति पाँच प्रकार की है, जिनको नाम सहित बतला रहा हू । सुनिये। भग्ु, मरीचि, अन्रि, अज्ञिरा, पुलह, क्रतु,. मनु, दक्ष कशिष्ठ और पुलस्त्य-ये दस ऋषि गण अति ऐश्वयंशाली एवं ब्रह्मा के मानस पुत्र कहे गये है, जो सृष्टि के आदिकाल में स्वयमेव आविर्भूत हुए थे ।

verses.sanskrit: अमी च कथमादित्याः प्रतापक्षतिशीतलाः । चित्रन्यस्ता इव गताः प्रकामालोकनीयताम्
verses.transliteration: amī ca kathamādityāḥ pratāpakṣatiśītalāḥ / citranyastā iva gatāḥ prakāmālokanīyatām
verses.translation: Amavasu was the founder of Kanyakubja kingdom—Pargiter, AITH, It was a result of the curse of Yuvanasva that Ganga was produced by him. Kaverl, the most excellent of all rivers, became the praise-worthy wife of Jahnu. Jahnu begot a beloved righteous son named Suhotra, of Kaverl. Suhotra's son was Ajaka.
verses.hindi: अधनुश्रिन्वान्तगंतग्रन्थो घ. पुस्तके नास्ति ।
verses.wordMeaning: Amavasu was the founder of Kanyakubja kingdom—Pargiter, AITH, It was a result of the curse of Yuvanasva that Ganga was produced by him. Kaverl, the most excellent of all rivers, became the praise-worthy wife of Jahnu. Jahnu begot a beloved righteous son named Suhotra,…

verses.sanskrit: तद्ब्रूत वत्साः किमितः प्रार्थयध्वं समागताः । किमागमनकृत्यं वो ब्रूत निःसंशयं सुराः
verses.transliteration: tadbrūta vatsāḥ kimitaḥ prārthayadhvaṃ samāgatāḥ / kimāgamanakṛtyaṃ vo brūta niḥsaṃśayaṃ surāḥ
verses.translation: Ajaka's successor was Balakasva of great fame. Gaya, Slla and Kusa are remembered as sons born to him. Kusa had four sons brilliant due to their Vedic know¬ ledge. They were Kusasva, Kusanabha, Amurtarayasas and Vasu.
verses.hindi: एकोनषश्ितमोडअध्याय; द ४८३ काव्यों बृहस्पतिश्चेब कश्यपश्चोशनास्तथा । उतथ्यो वामदेवश्च अयोज्यश्रोशिजस्तथा १६० कदंमो विश्ववाः शक्तिबालखिल्यस्तथा धराः । इत्येत ऋषय:ः प्रोक्ता ज्ञाततो ऋषितां गताः:.
verses.wordMeaning: Ajaka's successor was Balakasva of great fame. Gaya, Slla and Kusa are remembered as sons born to him. Kusa had four sons brilliant due to their Vedic know¬ ledge. They were Kusasva, Kusanabha, Amurtarayasas and Vasu.
verses.commentary: Sense: Ajaka's successor was Balakasva of great fame. Gaya, Slla and Kusa are remembered as sons born to him. Kusa had four sons brilliant due to their Vedic know¬ ledge. They were Kusasva, Kusanabha, Amurtarayasas and Vasu.

verses.sanskrit: मयि सृष्टिर् हि लोकानां रक्षा युष्मास्ववस्थिता । ततो मन्दानिलोद्भूतकमलाकरशोभिना
verses.transliteration: mayi sṛṣṭir hi lokānāṃ rakṣā yuṣmāsvavasthitā / tato mandānilodbhūtakamalākaraśobhinā
verses.translation: The excellent king Kusastamba desirous of a son, performed a penance. When a thousand years were completed he saw Satakratu (Indra). On seeing him who performed severe penance, the thousand-eyed Purandara decided to become his son, as he was competent to do so. The enemy of Paka (i.e. Indra) became his son and took the name Gadhi. He was called Kausika also, being a member of the family of Kusa.
verses.hindi: ऋषिपुत्रानषीकांस्तु गर्भात्पन्नान्षिबोधत । वत्सरो नप्नहुश्चेव भारद्ाजस्तथव॒ च ६२ बृहदुत्थः शरद्वांश्व॒ अगस्त्यश्रौशिजस्तथा । ऋषिदी्घंतमाश्चेव बृहदुक्थ शरद्वतः ३६३ वाजश्रवाः सुवित्तश्न सुवाग्वेषप रायण: । दधीचः शद्भूमांश्चेब राजा वेश्रवणस्तथा ॥।
verses.wordMeaning: The excellent king Kusastamba desirous of a son, performed a penance. When a thousand years were completed he saw Satakratu (Indra). On seeing him who performed severe penance, the thousand-eyed Purandara decided to become his son, as he was competent to do so.…
verses.commentary: Sense: The excellent king Kusastamba desirous of a son, performed a penance. When a thousand years were completed he saw Satakratu (Indra). On seeing him who performed severe penance, the thousand-eyed Purandara decided to become his son, as he was competent to do so.…

verses.sanskrit: गुरुं नेत्रसहस्रेण प्रेरयामास वृत्रहा । स द्विनेत्रं हरेश्चक्षुः सहस्रनयनाधिकम्
verses.transliteration: guruṃ netrasahasreṇa prerayāmāsa vṛtrahā / sa dvinetraṃ hareścakṣuḥ sahasranayanādhikam
verses.translation: Kusastamba's wife was Paurukutsa and Gadhi was born of her. Lord Gadhi gave his eldest daughter, the splendid and blessed Satyavati, to Rcika who was a descendant of Bhrgu (Kavya?). Her husband, himself a descendant of Bhrgu and the delighter of the Bhrgu family, prepared Cam (consecrated cooked rice) for the sake (of the birth) of a son to himself as well as to Gadhi. The courageous sageRcIka, the descendant of Bhrgu, called (his wife Satyavati and said): "O splendid lady, this Caru should be taken by you and this by your mother. A brilliant leader of Ksatriyas will be born to her. He cannot be conquered by Ksatriyas in battle. He will be the destroyer of prominent Ksatriyas. This Caru will give you, O splendid lady, an excellent Brahmana as a son. He will be courageous and quiescent, possessing penance as his wealth (i.e. he will become a great sage)."
verses.hindi: इत्येत ऋषिका: प्रोक्तास्ते सत्यादृषितां गताः ईश्वरा ऋषिकाश्चेव ये चान्ये वे तथा स्मृता  एते मन्त्रकृतः सर्वे कृत्स्नशस्तान्चिबोधत
verses.wordMeaning: Kusastamba's wife was Paurukutsa and Gadhi was born of her. Lord Gadhi gave his eldest daughter, the splendid and blessed Satyavati, to Rcika who was a descendant of Bhrgu (Kavya?). Her husband, himself a descendant of Bhrgu and the delighter of the Bhrgu family,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Kusastamba's wife was Paurukutsa and Gadhi was born of her. Lord Gadhi gave his eldest daughter, the splendid and blessed Satyavati, to Rcika who was a descendant of Bhrgu (Kavya?). Her husband, himself a descendant of Bhrgu and the delighter of the Bhrgu family,…

verses.sanskrit: वाचस्पतिरुवाचेदं प्राञ्जलिर् जलजासनम् । युष्मद्वंशोद्भवस्तात तालमेघो महाबलः
verses.transliteration: vācaspatiruvācedaṃ prāñjalir jalajāsanam / yuṣmadvaṃśodbhavastāta tālamegho mahābalaḥ
verses.translation: After saying entered the forest, Then Satyavatl Conceived in her womb a foetus that
verses.hindi: भृगुः काव्य: प्रचेतास्तु दधोचों ह्यात्मवानपि । ओर्वोदथ जम॒दस्निश्च विदः सारस्वतस्तथा
verses.wordMeaning: After saying entered the forest, Then Satyavatl Conceived in her womb a foetus that
verses.commentary: Sense: After saying entered the forest, Then Satyavatl Conceived in her womb a foetus that

verses.sanskrit: उपतापयते देवान्धूमकेतुरिवोच्छ्रितः । तेन देवगणाः सर्वे दुःखिता दानवेन च
verses.transliteration: upatāpayate devāndhūmaketurivocchritaḥ / tena devagaṇāḥ sarve duḥkhitā dānavena ca
verses.translation: On seeing it and pondering over it by means of Yogic power, Rcika, the excellent Brahmana, spoke to his fair- complexioned wife: Your mother will give birth to such a saintly son. The entire Brahman (Vedic knowledge) has been instilled into it by me.

verses.sanskrit: तालमेघो दैत्यपतिः सर्वान्नो बाधते बली । तस्मात्त्वां शरणं प्राप्ताः शरणं नो विधे भव
verses.transliteration: tālamegho daityapatiḥ sarvānno bādhate balī / tasmāttvāṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptāḥ śaraṇaṃ no vidhe bhava
verses.translation: Thus warned by her husband, the blessed lady Satya¬ vatl propitiated her husband: "May my son never be like this. Let another be a base Brahmana". Thus requested, the sage said: "O gentle lady, this has never been thought of nor desired by me or by you. The son may be one of terrible activities due to the fault of his father or mother".
verses.hindi: यह महान स्वयमेव उन समस्त ऋषियों के रूप में परिणत होकर आविर्भूत होता है अतः उन्हें मह॒षि कहते हैं, इन परमैश्वर्य सम्पन्न ऋषियों के पुत्र अन्य ऋषियों के बारे में बतला रहा हूं, सुनिये
verses.wordMeaning: Thus warned by her husband, the blessed lady Satya¬ vatl propitiated her husband: "May my son never be like this. Let another be a base Brahmana". Thus requested, the sage said: "O gentle lady, this has never been thought of nor desired by me or by you.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Thus warned by her husband, the blessed lady Satya¬ vatl propitiated her husband: "May my son never be like this. Let another be a base Brahmana". Thus requested, the sage said: "O gentle lady, this has never been thought of nor desired by me or by you.…

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रसन्नो भगवान् वेधास्तान् अब्रवीद् वचः
verses.transliteration: tataḥ prasanno bhagavān vedhāstān abravīd vacaḥ
verses.translation: Thus addressed, Satyavatl spoke again these words: "O sage, if you wish, you can create many worlds. What then a mere son? This explains why Parasuraraa, though ]a Brahmana, was of a militant nature and Visvamitra, though K?atriya by birth, attained Brahm ana-hood.
verses.hindi: काव्य, बृहस्पति, कश्यप, उद्यना, उतथ्य, वामदेव अयोज्य, ओऔशिज, कदम, विश्रवा, शक्ति, बालखिल्य, धरा ये समस्त ऋषिगण अपने ज्ञान बल से ऋष्त्व को प्राप्त हुये कह्टे जाते हैं। ऋषि के पुत्र ऋषीकों को गर्भ से उत्पन्न हुआ समझिये । ब्त्सर, नग्रहु, भारद्वाज, बृहदुत्थ, शस्द्वानू, अगस्त्य, औशिज, दीघंतमा, बृहदुक्थ, शरद्गवत्, वाजश्रवा, सुवित्त. सुबाक; वेष परायण ? दधीचि, शद्भमान्, राजा वेश्रवण---ये समस्त ऋषी- कगण अपने सत्य के बल पर ऋषित्व को प्राप्त हुए कहे जाते हैं। इन समस्त ऋषिपृनत्र ऋषीकों के अतिरिक्त अन्य जो ऐश्वयंबान् ऋषिगण कहे गये हैं, वे भी मंत्रों के निर्माण करने वाले हैं, उन सब को मैं बतला रहा हूँ, सुनिये ।६०-१५॥ भगु, काव्य, प्रचेता, दधीच. आत्मवानू, औव॑ जमदग्ति, बिद, सारस्वत, अद्विषेण, अरूप, वीतह॒व्य, वृमेघस वन्य, प्रथ, दिवोदास, पश्वास्य, गुत्समान् और नभ--ये उन्‍नीस मंत्रवादी ऋषि
verses.wordMeaning: Thus addressed, Satyavatl spoke again these words: "O sage, if you wish, you can create many worlds. What then a mere son? This explains why Parasuraraa, though ]a Brahmana, was of a militant nature and Visvamitra, though K?atriya by birth, attained Brahm ana-hood.
verses.commentary: Sense: Thus addressed, Satyavatl spoke again these words: "O sage, if you wish, you can create many worlds. What then a mere son? This explains why Parasuraraa, though ]a Brahmana, was of a militant nature and Visvamitra, though K?atriya by birth, attained Brahm ana-hood.

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मोवाच: तालमेघेन वो मध्ये बली तेन समः सुराः । विना माधवदेवेन साध्यो मे नैव दानवः
verses.transliteration: brahmovāca: tālameghena vo madhye balī tena samaḥ surāḥ / vinā mādhavadevena sādhyo me naiva dānavaḥ
verses.translation: O holy lord, O master, it behoves you to grant me a son who will be quiescent and straightforward. O Lord, say 'Let such a son be born'. O excellent Brahmana, nothing other than this can be done to me". Thereafter, by means of the power of his penance, he made her delighted.
verses.hindi: कहे गये हैं ।६६-६७। अंगिरा, वेधस्, भारद्वाज, बाष्कलि, अमृत, गाग्यें, शेनी, संहृति, पुरुकुत्स, मांधाता,
verses.wordMeaning: O holy lord, O master, it behoves you to grant me a son who will be quiescent and straightforward. O Lord, say 'Let such a son be born'. O excellent Brahmana, nothing other than this can be done to me". Thereafter, by means of the power of his penance, he made her delighted.
verses.commentary: Sense: O holy lord, O master, it behoves you to grant me a son who will be quiescent and straightforward. O Lord, say 'Let such a son be born'. O excellent Brahmana, nothing other than this can be done to me". Thereafter, by means of the power of his penance, he made her delighted.

verses.sanskrit: ततः सुरगणाः सर्वे विरिञ्चिप्रमुखा नृप । क्षीरोदं प्रस्थिताः सर्वे दुःखितास्तेन वैरिणा
verses.transliteration: tataḥ suragaṇāḥ sarve viriñcipramukhā nṛpa / kṣīrodaṃ prasthitāḥ sarve duḥkhitāstena vairiṇā
verses.translation: "O fair-complexioned lady, it makes no difference as far as I am concerned whether it is the son or the grand¬ son. O gentle lady, everything shall be in accordance with the words spoken by you." Therefore Satyavatl gave birth to a son, the scion of the family of Bhrgu. He was Jamadagni, the quiescent and self-controlled. He was interested in penance.
verses.hindi: कृष्व, मुद्गल, उतथ्य, भरद्वाज, वाजश्रवा, आयाप्य, सुवित्तिक, वामदेव औगज, वृह॒दुक्थ, दीघेतपा, उतथ्यश्च भरद्वाजस्तथा वाजअबा अपि । आयाप्यश्च सुवित्तिश्च वामदेवस्तथव तर १०१ ओऔगजो बृहदुकूथश्च ऋषिदीरघंतपस्तथा । कक्षीवांश्च त्रयस्त्रिशत्स्मुता अड्िरसो वरा: ॥
verses.wordMeaning: "O fair-complexioned lady, it makes no difference as far as I am concerned whether it is the son or the grand¬ son. O gentle lady, everything shall be in accordance with the words spoken by you." Therefore Satyavatl gave birth to a son, the scion of the family of Bhrgu.…
verses.commentary: Sense: "O fair-complexioned lady, it makes no difference as far as I am concerned whether it is the son or the grand¬ son. O gentle lady, everything shall be in accordance with the words spoken by you." Therefore Satyavatl gave birth to a son, the scion of the family of Bhrgu.…

verses.sanskrit: त्वरिताः प्रस्थिता देवाः केशवं द्रष्टुकाम्यया । क्षीरोदं सागरं गत्वास्तुवंस्ते जलशायिनम्
verses.transliteration: tvaritāḥ prasthitā devāḥ keśavaṃ draṣṭukāmyayā / kṣīrodaṃ sāgaraṃ gatvāstuvaṃste jalaśāyinam
verses.translation: Formerly when there was an interchange of Raudra and Vaisnava Cams in the Yajna of Bhrgu, he ate ( Jamanat) the Vaisnava nre and so he came to be known as 'Jamadagni'. Having obtained Visvamitra as his successor, Gadhi the delighter of KuSikas (members of the family of Kusika) attained the status equal to that of Brahmana sages. He was selected to be such by Brahma.
verses.hindi: एते मन्त्रकृत: सर्वे काश्यपांस्तु निबोधत १०२ कस्यपश्चव वत्सारो विभ्रमो रेभ्य एव च । असितो देवलश्चेव षडते ब्रह्मवादिनः
verses.wordMeaning: Formerly when there was an interchange of Raudra and Vaisnava Cams in the Yajna of Bhrgu, he ate ( Jamanat) the Vaisnava nre and so he came to be known as 'Jamadagni'. Having obtained Visvamitra as his successor,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Formerly when there was an interchange of Raudra and Vaisnava Cams in the Yajna of Bhrgu, he ate ( Jamanat) the Vaisnava nre and so he came to be known as 'Jamadagni'. Having obtained Visvamitra as his successor,…

verses.sanskrit: देवा ऊचुः । जगदादिरनादिस्त्वं जगदन्तो ऽप्यनन्तकः । जगन्मूर्तिरमूर्तिस्त्वं जय गीर्वाणपूजित
verses.transliteration: devā ūcuḥ / jagadādiranādistvaṃ jagadanto 'pyanantakaḥ / jaganmūrtiramūrtistvaṃ jaya gīrvāṇapūjita
verses.translation: In this manner, the lofty-minded Jamadagni, the fore¬ most among those who know Brahman, was born of Satya vatl, thanks to the semen virile of Aurva Rcika. The middle son was Sunahsepha and the youngest was Sunahpuccha. The pious-souled Visvamitra is remembered by the name Visvaratha also. By the favour of Bhrgu, he was born of Kau£ika, as the perpetuator of the race of Kausika.
verses.hindi: अन्रिरचिसनश्चव श्याभावांश्वाथ निष्ठुर:  बल्गुतको मुनिर्धामांस्तथा पूर्वातिथिश्च यः ॥ इत्येते चात्रयः प्रोक्ता मन्त्रकारा महर्षयः
verses.wordMeaning: In this manner, the lofty-minded Jamadagni, the fore¬ most among those who know Brahman, was born of Satya vatl, thanks to the semen virile of Aurva Rcika. The middle son was Sunahsepha and the youngest was Sunahpuccha.…
verses.commentary: Sense: In this manner, the lofty-minded Jamadagni, the fore¬ most among those who know Brahman, was born of Satya vatl, thanks to the semen virile of Aurva Rcika. The middle son was Sunahsepha and the youngest was Sunahpuccha.…

verses.sanskrit: जय क्षीरोदशयन जय लक्ष्म्या सदा वृत । जय दानवनाशाय जय देवकिनन्दन
verses.transliteration: jaya kṣīrodaśayana jaya lakṣmyā sadā vṛta / jaya dānavanāśāya jaya devakinandana
verses.translation: Some other families of the Brahmarsi Kausika, the holy descendant of Pururavas are: Sosrumas and Saindhava- Astaka, born of Drsadvat!, was also Visvamitra's son. Astaka's sons (and descendants) constituting the Jahnu family have already been recounted by me.
verses.hindi: षष्ठस्तु मैत्रावरुण: कुण्डिन: सप्तमस्तथा ।  एते सप्तर्षयो विप्रा ब्रह्मक्षेत्रनिवासिनः १०६ ब्रह्मक्षेत्र महातीर्थ ब्रह्मणा निर्मितं पुरा। + कुरुक्षेत्र पुण्यतमे पितामहनिषेविते १०७ देवानां च ऋषीणां च मुनीनां तत्र सद्भमः  ब्रह्मणा च कृत प्रश्न क्‍्व दुष्टा वायुदेवता १०८
verses.wordMeaning: Some other families of the Brahmarsi Kausika, the holy descendant of Pururavas are: Sosrumas and Saindhava- Astaka, born of Drsadvat!, was also Visvamitra's son. Astaka's sons (and descendants) constituting the Jahnu family have already been recounted by me.
verses.commentary: Sense: Some other families of the Brahmarsi Kausika, the holy descendant of Pururavas are: Sosrumas and Saindhava- Astaka, born of Drsadvat!, was also Visvamitra's son. Astaka's sons (and descendants) constituting the Jahnu family have already been recounted by me.

verses.sanskrit: जय शङ्खगदापाणे जय चक्रधर प्रभो । इति देवस्तुतिं श्रुत्वा प्रबुद्धो जलशाय्यथ
verses.transliteration: jaya śaṅkhagadāpāṇe jaya cakradhara prabho / iti devastutiṃ śrutvā prabuddho jalaśāyyatha
verses.translation: What are the characteristics of Dharma, penance and learning whereby Brahmana-hood was attained by Visvamitra and other kings? The list of Gotras of Kaufika clan given in w. 91-97 is incomplete (dot ML P. A Study, p -409).
verses.hindi: ऋषिगणस्तदा प्रोक्‍्तं न दृष्टो (ष्ठा) वायुदेवता । इति चिन्तयतां तेषामणुमात्रस्तु दृष्टवान्ू और कक्षीवान--ये तेंतीस अंगिर वंशीय श्रेष्ठ ऋषि हैं, जो सब के सब मंत्रकर्ता हैं। अब कश्यप वेशीय ऋषियों को सुनिये ।९८-१०२। कश्यप, वत्सार, विधभ्रम, रैभ्य, अप्तित और देवल-ये छः कश्यप वंशीय ब्रद्यगादी ऋषि हैं। अति, अचिसन, व्यामावान् निष्ठर, बुद्धिमात् वल्यूतक तथा पूर्वातिथि-ये अन्नि वंशीय मंत्रकर्ता महर्षि कहे गये हैं । है ऋषिगण ! वशिष्ठ, शक्ति, पराशर, इन्दुप्रमति, भरद्वसु, मेत्रावरुण,
verses.wordMeaning: What are the characteristics of Dharma, penance and learning whereby Brahmana-hood was attained by Visvamitra and other kings? The list of Gotras of Kaufika clan given in w. 91-97 is incomplete (dot ML P. A Study, p -409).
verses.commentary: Sense: What are the characteristics of Dharma, penance and learning whereby Brahmana-hood was attained by Visvamitra and other kings? The list of Gotras of Kaufika clan given in w. 91-97 is incomplete (dot ML P. A Study, p -409).

verses.sanskrit: उवाच मधुरां वाणीं मेघगम्भीरनिस्वनाम् । किमर्थं बोधितो ब्रह्मन् समर्थैर् वः सुरासुरैः
verses.transliteration: uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ meghagambhīranisvanām / kimarthaṃ bodhito brahman samarthair vaḥ surāsuraiḥ
verses.translation: Thus requested, he ( Sula ) spoke these meaningful words: A sinful soul, a base man, may give charitable gifts to Brahmanas after proclaiming his intention to perform righteous deeds to the people out of hypocrisy. An uncontrol¬ led man overwhelmed by passion and delusion may perform severe Japas and in the end may give charitable gifts for the purpose of sanctifying himslf. But these charitable gifts offered by him do not yield fruits. The charitable gifts of a wicked- souled man indulging in violence, do not stay (i.e. do not yield fruits) even if he engaged himself in holy rites. Similarly the Danas offered by one who has amassed wealth by painful
verses.hindi: और कुण्डिन--ये सात ऋषि ब्रह्मक्षेत्र के नित्रासी कहे गये हैं। यह) ब्रह्मक्षेत्र तीथं लोक पितामह ब्रह्मा द्वारा सेवित परम पवित्र कुरुक्षेत्र में अवस्थित है, प्राचीन काल में स्त्रयं ब्रह्मा जी ने इस महातीर्थ का निर्माण किया था ।१०३-१०७। उस परम पवित्र तीर्थ में एक बार देवताओं, ऋषियों, तथा मुनियों का विराट सम गम था। उस अबसर पर ब्रह्मा जी ने यह प्रश्न उपस्थित किया कि वायु देवता कहाँ देखे जाते हैं ?
verses.wordMeaning: Thus requested, he ( Sula ) spoke these meaningful words: A sinful soul, a base man, may give charitable gifts to Brahmanas after proclaiming his intention to perform righteous deeds to the people out of hypocrisy.…

verses.sanskrit: ब्रह्मोवाच: तालमेघभयात्कृष्ण सम्प्राप्तास् तव मन्दिरम् । न वध्यः कस्यचित् पापस्तालमेघो जनार्दन
verses.transliteration: brahmovāca: tālameghabhayātkṛṣṇa samprāptās tava mandiram / na vadhyaḥ kasyacit pāpastālamegho janārdana
verses.translation: Riches acquired by just (proper) means must be gifted to pious, deserving persons. If one performs; Tajnas and makes charitable gifts without harbouring any specific desire in his mind, he attains the fruits of that Dana. His; Dana results in happiness. One attains enjoyment through Dana and goes Th in; an evidence of social mobility in ancient India.
verses.hindi: आप लोग बतलाइये  ऋषियों ने कहा, हम लोगों ने तो वायु देवता का दर्शन नहीं किया है। इस प्रकार की बात चीत चल रही थी कि इसी बीच एक अणु दिखलाई पड़ा । वह अणु एक पुर के रूप में परिणत +एते सप्तषंय इत्यारभ्य विधेया ब्राह्मणस्य त्वित्यन्तग्रन्थ: क. ग. डः. पुस्तकेषु नास्ति । +इदमर्ध नास्ति घ पुस्तके।  धनुश्चिह्वान्तगंतग्रन्थ: ख. पुस्तके नास्ति । १. यहाँ से अगले प्रष्ठ पर /” चिह्न तक का पाठ कई गमृल पुस्तकों में नहीं है ।
verses.wordMeaning: Riches acquired by just (proper) means must be gifted to pious, deserving persons. If one performs; Tajnas and makes charitable gifts without harbouring any specific desire in his mind, he attains the fruits of that Dana. His; Dana results in happiness.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Riches acquired by just (proper) means must be gifted to pious, deserving persons. If one performs; Tajnas and makes charitable gifts without harbouring any specific desire in his mind, he attains the fruits of that Dana. His; Dana results in happiness.…

verses.sanskrit: त्वमेव जहि तं दुष्टं मृत्युं यास्यति नान्यथा
verses.transliteration: tvameva jahi taṃ duṣṭaṃ mṛtyuṃ yāsyati nānyathā
verses.translation: Bhargavyoma in Bd. P. Sutahotra's successors were three extremely righteous ones, viz. KaSa, Sala and lord Gjrtsamada.
verses.hindi: एकोनषष्टितमो5घ्याय: ४८५
verses.wordMeaning: Bhargavyoma in Bd. P. Sutahotra's successors were three extremely righteous ones, viz. KaSa, Sala and lord Gjrtsamada.
verses.commentary: Sense: Bhargavyoma in Bd. P. Sutahotra's successors were three extremely righteous ones, viz. KaSa, Sala and lord Gjrtsamada.

verses.sanskrit: श्रीकृष्ण उवाच: स्वस्थानं गम्यतां देवाः स्वकीयां लभत प्रजाम् । दुष्टात्मानं हनिष्यामि तालमेघं महाबलम्
verses.transliteration: śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca: svasthānaṃ gamyatāṃ devāḥ svakīyāṃ labhata prajām / duṣṭātmānaṃ haniṣyāmi tālameghaṃ mahābalam
verses.translation: Sunaka was the son of Grtsamada and his son was Saunaka. In his race Brahmanas, Vaisyas and Sudras were born as a result of their diverse Karmans. O Brahmana, Salas son was Arsti$ena and Caranta was liis son. The Saunakas and the Arstisenas were Brahmanas endowed with qualities characteristic of Ksatriyas. Kasa's sons were Kasaya, Rasta and Dirghatapas.
verses.hindi: शुद्रास्तद्द्वगुणास्तत्र स्थापिता मातरिश्वना । तानुवाच ततो देवो मातरिश्वा महाविभुः पूथं मज्भूक्तिकर्तारों मन्नाम्ता ख्यातिसाप्नुथ । द्वय॑ दूत नु प्रत्येक हिजान्भजत भो हिजाः..
verses.wordMeaning: Sunaka was the son of Grtsamada and his son was Saunaka. In his race Brahmanas, Vaisyas and Sudras were born as a result of their diverse Karmans. O Brahmana, Salas son was Arsti$ena and Caranta was liis son.…

verses.transliteration: sthānaṃ bruvantu me devā vasedyatra sa dānavaḥ

verses.sanskrit: देवा ऊचुः । हिमाचलगुहायां स वसते दानवेश्वरः । चतुर्विंशतिसाहस्रैः कन्याभिः परिवारितः
verses.transliteration: devā ūcuḥ / himācalaguhāyāṃ sa vasate dānaveśvaraḥ / caturviṃśatisāhasraiḥ kanyābhiḥ parivāritaḥ
verses.translation: As stated at the end of the last chapter, this chapter describes the race of Ayu who ruled at Kasi. Dhanvantari, the famous physician-king, the founder of the systematic science of Ayurveda was bom in Ayu's lineage. Hence the title specifically refers to him in preference to his forebears. Ksatravrddha in Bd. P. A line is missing here. Bd. P. supplies the names of the remaining three sons, viz. Rambha, Raji and Anenas (Bd.P. Op. Cit. v. 2).
verses.hindi: गोत्रजायाश्च नंवेद्यं तथाकार्य प्रथव्पृथक् । चतस्नरः सुभगास्तत्र कुययुः कुण्डनमादरात् अस्पां नान्याधिकारो5स्ति सज्जने मत्य॑पुड्धवाः। षद् स्थानानि च मन्नास्ना दृष्ट्वा पूतो भवेञ्यर: ।)

verses.sanskrit: तुरङ्गैः स्यन्दनैः कृष्ण संख्या तस्य न विद्यते । नटा नानाविधास्तत्र असंख्यातगुणा हरे
verses.transliteration: turaṅgaiḥ syandanaiḥ kṛṣṇa saṃkhyā tasya na vidyate / naṭā nānāvidhāstatra asaṃkhyātaguṇā hare
verses.translation: How was Dhanvantari, a god, born among human O Brahmanas, may the origin of Dhanvantari be heard.
verses.hindi: देवत्रयाणामादेशाद्धर्मसंक्षणाय च । यत्र रुद्रः स्थिरश्चा5षसीद्विक्षु सर्वासु सूरतिमान्
verses.wordMeaning: How was Dhanvantari, a god, born among human O Brahmanas, may the origin of Dhanvantari be heard.
verses.commentary: Sense: How was Dhanvantari, a god, born among human O Brahmanas, may the origin of Dhanvantari be heard.

verses.transliteration: dviradāḥ parvatākārā hayāśca dviradopamāḥ / mahābalo vasettatra gīrvāṇabhayadāyakaḥ
verses.translation: He was born prior to everyone. 1 He was enveloped in a halo of glory all round. On seeing him with perfectly shaped limbs, (gods) stood surprised and said, "You are Aja (the unborn) ". Heivie he is remembered as Aja. verses.hindi: वाडादित्यश्च देवेश: स्थापितो वायुना तदा। फामदः सर्वंदः सुर्यो प्रभ्रोशः प्रतापबान् १२० दिखाई पड़ने लगा जिसका वायुपुर नाम पड़ा। उस समय उस विस्तृत वायुपुर में अठारह सहख ब्राह्मणों का निवास स्थान निर्मित हुआ था । परम प्रभावश्ञाली वायु देवता ने ब्राह्मणों की संख्या से ट्विगुणित संख्या में शूद्रों की स्थापना की और उन सब से कहा कि तुम सब लोग मेरे भक्त हो और मेरे ही नाम से तुम सब ख्याति प्राप्त करोगे, कतः तुम प्रत्येक दो व्यक्ति ब्राह्मणों की अनुचर वृत्ति स्वीकार कर उनकी सेवा करते
