verses.transliteration: śrāddhaṃ tatraiva yo bhaktyā kurvīta nṛpanandana / pitarastasya tṛpyanti yāvadābhūtasamplavam
verses.translation: The state of being the object of knowledge (Visayaiva) and of not being so ( Avisayatva ) are proclaimed (as the characteris¬ tics) of Ksetra and Kfetrajna. Brahma should be known as Aoisaya (not object of knowledge, the knower) and Ksetra is called Visaya (object of knowledge)*. Ksetra is presided over by Ksetrajna and so is said to be for his sake. Since the bodies are many, the Sarlrin (the embo¬ died soul) is remembered as many. These souls are stationed without any arrangement (avyuhat) and are unmixed (a-sahkardt) like luminaries. Since there is the perception of happiness and sorrow severally in the When the withdrawal of those different beings sets in, that is brought about naturally after the lapse of a great deal of period. At that time the passion for sustenance of the worlds of the self-born god Brahma recedes, along with all the residents of Brahma's heaven. Then the attachment for the sustenance of those resi¬ ding (in meditation) in Atman recedes and they begin to see defects therein of their contemporaries. Then their (sense of) detachment is aroused and it dispels their Atma-vada (egotism). Bhoj'ya (object of Now they dwell in the Atman alone. They arc quiescent and endowed with (true) vision. All of them are pure, free from blemish and in conscious or unconscious stage. It is proclaimed that they attain complete absolution there itself and they do not return to Sarhsara since they are devoid of Gunas (state of nirgunatva ) and the sense of identity with the body (niratmatva). Thus the process of dissolution by the Self-born Brahma through Prakrti has been recounted. In this Prasarhyama (final curbing and restraint) the Karanas (organs of activity) of all living beings differ. Thus is the curbing of the Tattvas (Principles) along with that of the Karanas. This Tattvaprasamyama is remembered as capable of repetition. Dharma and Adharma, penance, perfect knowledge, the auspicious, the inauspicious, truth, falsehood, superiority, inferiority, happiness, sorrow, likes, dislikes—all these are mere attributes of one who has gone* (i.e. who has attained salvation). The merits and demerits of living beings that have been stabilised in Prakrti, are declared to lie unmanifested. The same merits and demerits (in different situations) join this body or the next. Dharma and Adharma (virtue and sin) are merely two qualities of creatures. They flourish in the form of the body along with the organs of sense ( Karam ) of creatures. The sentient Gunas (i.e. Sattva etc.) presided over by Ksetrajfia get dissolved during the primary creation and secondary creation in the world. The creatures come into con¬ tact or get separated from their Karanas (organs of activity) and they move about (i.e. undergo worldly existence and suffer¬ ing)- The Vrttis (proclivities, causes of activities) are three¬ fold according as they are of the nature of Sattva, Rajas or The (attribute) Sattva of the divine nature is conducive to attain the upper part (heaven) and Tamas is of the nature of (falling off) to the lower part (hell). The activiser In all the worlds, within all the living beings these All living creatures do not understand the reality due to their being overwhelmed by Tamas. But not realising the Tattva (Reality), they are fettered in three ways. He is bound by three types of bondages: These are the three types of bondage due to ignora¬ nce. The following are the usual defects (due to them)—Seeing permanence in what is transcient; perception of happiness in what actually is the cause of misery; feeling of possessiveness in what does not belong to one; and decisive knowledge of purity in what is impure. Those who have these mental defects have the defects of knowledge through misapprehension. The cessation of attachment (. Raga ) and hatred ( Dvesa ) is called knowledge. Ignorance is the root-cause of Tamas. Rajas has two-fold Karman (the auspicious and inauspicious) as its result. The resumption of the physical body once again is the result of Karmas. Thus great misery begins to function. The various sins committed by ears, eyes, skin, tongue and nose are the causes of the rebirth and misery. A man with a craving is said to be a Bala (an imma¬ ture or ignorant person). As a result of actions committed by himself, the individual soul goes round and round there only (in the Samsara) like the bull yoked to the oil-pressing machine. Hence it is taught that gross ignorance is the cause of all miseries. Realising that it is the sole enemy one shall endea¬ vour to acquire knowledge. One renounces {tyajate*) everything by perfect know¬ ledge. As a result of renunciation the intellect becomes detached, one becomes pure as a result of detachment; the pure one be¬ comes liberated by means of Sattva Guna. Henceforth I shall explain Raga (passion and attach¬ ment) that overwhelms living beings. Due to this attachment, It is the attachment to worldly pleasures that is declar¬ er as the cause of births. In all the physical worlds beginning with 3-aimi and ending with the immobile beings, this attach¬ ment ahne is the cause of birth and that is the result of ignorance. Hence one shall avoid ignorance. If one does not accept the words of sages as authority nor has regard for good manners as practised by virtuous and respectable men: if one is opposed to the discipline of (four) castes and stages in life; and if a man is antagonistic to wise men and scriptural injunctions—that is the cause of rebirth in lower species. There are various kinds of tortures in remaining (or taking birth) among the six kinds of lower animals. There is complete obstruction in the matter of cause and object of knowledge (?). The entire non-attainment of Ativarya (glory and pros- perity) is in the nature of Pratighata (obstacle) (to the desires). Thus the four types of Tamasa proclivities of the living beings etc. have been recounted. Bondage is for one who is fettered to it (the worldy Devoid of any Sarhbandha (contact) and in a state of Thus the characteristic features of perfect knowledge and liberation have been succinctly explained. That liberation is declared by those who see truth. The first one is the separation from worldly impres¬ sions, thanks to perfect knowledge. The second one is due to destruction of passion (passionate attachment) whereby the liberated soul attains Kaivalya, because even the Linga Sarira (the subtle inner body) is absent. Through Kaivalya he becomes Niranjana (unsullied). By not being sullied, he becomes Suddha (pure). In this state of liberation there is no guide or leader. The third type of cause of liberation is by the destruction of Tfsna (thirst) (for enjoyment). The liberated souls do not experience misery caused by the obstacle to the worldly objects of desired melody etc. These eight things caused by Prakfti adhere to the Ksetrajiias. They are called Gunas and Matras (the three Gunas and the five Tanmatras ). One should practice non-hatred and absence of attach¬ ment to the five Visayas (objects of sensual enjoyment) of both divine and human nature, after seeing the defects therein. One should avoid heart-burn, pleasure and dejectedness. By having recourse to non-attachment the embodied soul be¬ comes free from Mamatva (the feeling of my-ness i.e. possessive¬ ness). He should decide in his mind (intellect) that (the worldly existence) is non-eternal, inauspicious and conducive to misery. Then with Sattvic traits he should perform pure activities. When the attachment to worldly objects of pleasure becomes firm, he becomes able to see defects and blemishes entirely. Verses 87-92 describe the process of death.

verses.translation: Due to the chilliness, the virulently excited Vayu (life breath) pierces the centres of Pranas (vital airs), cuts off vulnerable parts of the body and rises up. It is the breath stationed in the abodes of vital airs of all living beings. By contraction, Jfiana (consciousness and knowledge) becomes covered up and the activities are enshroud¬ ed. The Jiva (the individual soul) being bereaved of the supporting body, is induced by its own actions committed be¬ fore. It then dislodges the Pranas from the eight limbs. (In the end) abandoning the body.it ceases to have breathing activity. Being abandoned by the vital airs thus, the person is called "Dead". This is something like this. When someone holds the glow-worm in his hand and goes about here and there he too is visible in its light. He who kills it, though a carrier (of the glow-worm) ceases to be a carrier (leader). The third, viz. the elimination of thirst or covetous¬ ness is spoken as the characteristic of liberation. It is the (result of) observation of defects in five objects of sensual pleasure such as sound and others. Absence of hatred, absence of intense attachment, avoidance of pleasure and agony (about objects of pleasure)—these are the dissolutions of the eight Prakrtis (primary essences which evolved the whole Universe). All the eight Prakrtis mentioned before should be known in order, beginning with Avyakta (the Unmanifest) and endmg with BHUas (Elements). These are called the dissolution of the Prakrtis. Those who follow the rigorous discipline of the four castes and stages of life and those who do not go contrary to The eight groups of Devas (and their abodes) are those Those who stay in those abodes do not experience the misery due to the obstacle to the achievement of such desired objects as sweet melody etc. These are the eight Prak r ta forms in ord-.r. They come into contact with the Ksetrajnas They are of the nature of the three Gunas and five Tanmatras People do not see with their eyes the clouds distinct from the water therein in the course of the rainy season. (Similarly ordinary people do not see the individual soul. They can only infer.) y After realising categories ending with Avjakta (the Unmanifest) and what is presided over by the Kselrajna, he be¬ comes pure and becomes liberated through knowledge. When the truth is realized, the principle that was obscure comes out. But in different bodies that have completely ceased to exist, the Karana (the individual soul) differs from the Avyakta and the Jrianin. One who is completely liberated from the body in the form of Gunas as well as Prana etc. does not take up another body, just as sprout never comes out when seed is burnt. Due to knowledge he becomes enlightened and pure of the four DaSas (conditions). He follows the Prakrti. They say that Prakrti is the reality, while Vikaras (its evolutes) are unreal. Its Sad-bhava (apparent? existence) should be known as Anria (unreal). Sadbhava (State of being existent) is called Salya (Reality). Satya (Brahman) is without name and form. x They called Ksetrajna" as possessing name and form. Because he knows (thoroughly) the Ksetra (the field i.e. the body) he is called Ksetrajna. Ksetrajna is auspicious because of the perception of Ksetra. Ksetrajna is remembered. Hence it is mentioned as Ksetra by those who know it. Ksetra is seen to be without intelli¬ gence but Ksetrajna is always endowed with intelligence. Those who know Ksetra call it so because of its Ksayana (destruction), Karana (being created), Ksalatrdna (protection from wound), Bhojyalva (state of being what is eaten or enjoyed) and Visayalva (state of being the object). All categories beginning with Mahat, ending with VtSesa possess variety of forms and they are characterised as Vikara (an evolute, change). Hence they arc peculiar (Vila- ksana). Hence verily Aksara (imperishable) approaches the / Kfara (perishable) I. * 3. That evolute ( Vikara ) is called Ksara as it wastes away and perishes. 4 Happiness, misery, delusion are called Bhojya (that which is to be experienced). It is Visaya (object of enjoyment) as it is insentient. That which has the opposite quality 5 * * * * is remem¬ bered as Vibhu. It is called Aksara (imperishable) for the following reasons: It does not waste away (na ksiyate). It does not perish ( na ksarati). Evolutes spread from it. It is not diminished. Since it lies in Pur (puri anuSele ) it is called Purusa. The term Purusa is derived also as follows: Since it is Purafira- tynyika that is the Pratyayi (the knower) of the Pura (Body), it is cailed so. He is other than what can be called existent, non¬ existent, bound, liberated, mobile, stable. As he is devoid of any cause, he cannot be specified (by any of these terms). 1 Since he is very pure, he cannot be indicated specifi¬ cally. Since he is full of bliss, it is of equal vision. Since he is the cause (Karin) of Atmapralyaya (the knowledge of Atman), no causal expression applies to it 2 (?) It can be imagined or in¬ ferred. Those who perceive thus are not deluded. When he sees the knower who is quiescent in regard to all objects, who is of the nature of Vision, and who is the only one to be pointed out among the visible and invisible objects, his emancipation (uplift) takes place. After having realised this great Being, the perfect knower attains quiescence (calmness). He, the perfect knower, does not see the separateness in the effect, cause, the physical objects of intellect etc., that is in contact or severed, and him who is dead or alive. 3 The causal Atman controls that Atman (the individual soul) by means of his own self. He abides in the Prakrti, in its cause and in his own Atman. He exists. He does not exist. He is he or he is another. He is here or he is hereafter. He has oneness or separateness. He is Ksetrajna or Purusa. He possesses Atman or he is devoid of Atman. He is sentient or non-sentient. He is a doer or non-doer. He is the enjoyer or he is only the enjoyed. On realizing the unsullied Ksetrajna, there is no further return to Sariisara. It is called Avdey n (inexpressibe) be¬ cause it cannot be described by means of logic or by arguments it cannot be grasped. It is (called) Apratarkya (that which cannot be argued about) because it cannot be conceived. After attaining that Bd.P. v. 95 reads: juuldjnanavivarjilah 'He is a knower, devoid of ignorance*. Abetter reading. Bd. P. v. 98 reads anyunam vdpyahetukam 'not deficient and not caused— spontaneous*. Some lines in the text mixed up. When the Ksctrajha is free from Gunas, when it is pure, quiescent, unsullied, exhausted, devoid of both happi¬ ness and misery, when it is checked and attains calmness and when it becomes Niralmaka (devoid of ego?), there is neither Vdcyatva (state of being expressed) nor Avacyatva (the state of not being expressed) (?) These two, annihilation and creation are manifest and unmanifest. Purusa creates and swallows (the entire world). Everything functions again with the Ksetrajna presiding over. At its end, it consciously resorts to the Adhisthana (substratum). Their mutual contact is known as being brought about by SadharmyavxiA Vaidharmya (similarity and dissimilarity). The Samyoga (contact) of the great Purusa is beginningless.* As long as creation and subsidiary creation last Prakrti keeps Purusa restrained and stays: At the outset it functions unintelligently but in favour of it. Its function is for the sake of Purusa. This creation and dissolution are effected by Pradhana as well as by Is'vara. But it is beginningless and endless. Prakrti approaches the Universe even while terrifying it with the feeling of identification. Thus the third creation of Prakrti characterised by Helu (cause) has been recounted. One who strictly adheres to it becomes liberated as mentioned by poets (seers). Thus three types of dissolution have been recounted

verses.sanskrit: यस्तत्र स्नाति वै भक्त्या जितक्रोधो जितेन्द्रियः । एकादश्यां सिते पक्षे मधुना स्नापयेच्छिवम्
verses.transliteration: yastatra snāti vai bhaktyā jitakrodho jitendriyaḥ / ekādaśyāṃ site pakṣe madhunā snāpayecchivam
verses.translation: He who knows this holy creation of Rsis through Varuna becomes long-lived and meritorious. He becomes Puri¬ fied and attains excellent happiness. By listening to this and retaining this (in memory) he becomes free from all sins.
verses.hindi: सब स्त्रियों को देख कर स्वयम्भू ब्रह्मा जी का वी पृथ्वी पर स्खलित हो गया । ब्रह्मषि के भाव से प्रभावित निद्चिचत विधान के कारण पितामह ने प्रथ्वी पर स्खलित अपने बीये को घृत की भाँति ख्ुवा पर रख कर भन्‍्त्रों का विधिवत् उच्चारण कर हवन कर दिया। प्रजापति ते इस प्रकार अनेक जीव-समूहों की सृष्टि की । लोक में परम तेजोमय, किस्तु पृथ्वी पर गिर पड़ने के कारण कुछ क्षीण तेज वाले उस वीर्य से सत्तव गुण,
verses.wordMeaning: He who knows this holy creation of Rsis through Varuna becomes long-lived and meritorious. He becomes Puri¬ fied and attains excellent happiness. By listening to this and retaining this (in memory) he becomes free from all sins.
verses.commentary: Sense: He who knows this holy creation of Rsis through Varuna becomes long-lived and meritorious. He becomes Puri¬ fied and attains excellent happiness. By listening to this and retaining this (in memory) he becomes free from all sins.

verses.sanskrit: श्राद्धं तत्रैव यो भक्त्या पित्ःणामथ दापयेत् । स याति परमं स्थानं बलभद्रवचो यथा
verses.transliteration: śrāddhaṃ tatraiva yo bhaktyā pitḥṇāmatha dāpayet / sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ balabhadravaco yathā
verses.translation: Then all the sages spoke to Romaharsaria: "When the sixth Prajasarga (creation of the subjects) of Caksusa Manu had been dissolved, the creation of Vaivasvata Manu began to function (How did it take place?)."
verses.hindi: रजोगुण एवं तमोगुणमय सृष्टि डत्पन्न हुई। इन उपयुक्त तीनों गुणों से सम्पन्न वह तेज आकाश-मण्डल में देदीप्यमान हुआ । तमोगुणमय तेजस्विता के कारण सभी जीवसमूह उत्पन्न हुए ।३१०१४॥ जिस समय ब्रह्मा ने घत के पात्र में अपने वीये को लेकर अग्ति में हवन किया उस समय उनके कर्मज पुत्रों की उत्पत्ति हुई । अग्नि में वीयें के हवन कर देने पर महृषियों का प्रादुर्भाव हुआ, सातों ऋषियों के शरीर उज्ज्वल एवं देदीप्यमान थे, तथा बालकों के सभी गुण उनमें पाये जाते थे  पहली बार अग्नि में बीये के हवन करते पर लपटों से कवि (भूगु) निकले । इस प्रकार ज्वाला का भेदन कर निकलते हुये कवि को देखकर हिरण्यगर्भ बक्ला ने कहा, यतः अग्नि ज्वाला से प्रकट होते समय तुमने 'भूगु' इस प्रकार का उच्चारण किया है, अतः तुम्हारा नाम भी भूगु हुआ ।३५-३७। इस प्रकार अग्नि ज्वाला का भेदत कर प्रादुभूत होने वाले उस ब्रह्मरषि
verses.wordMeaning: Then all the sages spoke to Romaharsaria: "When the sixth Prajasarga (creation of the subjects) of Caksusa Manu had been dissolved, the creation of Vaivasvata Manu began to function (How did it take place?)."
verses.commentary: Sense: Then all the sages spoke to Romaharsaria: "When the sixth Prajasarga (creation of the subjects) of Caksusa Manu had been dissolved, the creation of Vaivasvata Manu began to function (How did it take place?)."

verses.sanskrit: ॥ इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डे रेवाखण्डे संकर्षणतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनं नामैकाधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ॥ र्क्व् अध्याय १०२ मार्कण्डेय उवाच: मन्मथेशं ततो गच्छेत् सर्वदेवनमस्कृतम् । स्नानमात्रान्नरो राजन्यमलोकं न पश्यति
verses.transliteration: || iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe revākhaṇḍe saṃkarṣaṇatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃ nāmaikādhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ || rkv adhyāya 102 mārkaṇḍeya uvāca: manmatheśaṃ tato gacchet sarvadevanamaskṛtam / snānamātrānnaro rājanyamalokaṃ na paśyati
verses.translation: OSuta, a great narrative has been recounted by Your Holiness. * 1 You have narrated the wonderful deeds of all subjects along with Planus, of JDevas along with sages, of Pitrs Gandharvas, Bhutas (goblins), Pisacas (ghosts)/ serpents', Raksasas, Daityas, Danavas, Yaksas and birds. Their Vidhi- supported decision of their Dharmas and their excellent and fine births have been narrated in wonderful stories. Being narrated to us in your sweet voice (or in charmingly polished words), O son of Suta, it rendered pleasure to our ears and minds for ever till the end of the creation of living beings. After having thus propitiated and honoured Suta, all the great sages, the performers of the Salra (sacrifice) asked him ibout the process of creative function. 2 "O highly intelligent Suta, how does creation re¬ On being thus requested, SutaLomaharsana again began to narrate the process of creation. The speech of sages shows that this must be the last chapter. They have duly honoured Suta. They performed Avabhrtha bath and went to heaven (42). The review of the contents, Phalairuti and the genealogy of teachers who handed down the text of this Purana—all these confirm the above conclusion.

verses.sanskrit: अनपत्या या च नारी स्नायाद् वै पाण्डुनन्दन । पुत्रं सा लभते पार्थ सत्यसङ्घं दृढव्रतम्
verses.transliteration: anapatyā yā ca nārī snāyād vai pāṇḍunandana / putraṃ sā labhate pārtha satyasaṅghaṃ dṛḍhavratam
verses.translation: Dissolution of the Universe and its recreation form an important characteristic ( Laksapa ) of a Purana. As the topic of recreation of the Brahmanda was not properly dealt in previous chapters,. it is taken here to fulfil the PaftcalaksaQa criterion. "I shall recount to you how the creation functions (again). The order of the creation should be known (to occur) as (it took place) before. I shall mention what is seen and what can be inferred. I shall mention cogent arguments. From it (the principle of creative function), all words recede without reaching it along with the mind (i.e. the mind cannot conceive it, the words cannot express it). Just as the unmanifest is invisible and incomprehensi¬ ble, (the objects of creation too) are invisible and incomprehen¬ sible. When the Vikdrai (evolutes) become dissolved they are seen nowhere. The Gunas attain equilibrium and the created things recede. Pradhana stands on a similar footing with Purusas. The Dharmas and the Adharmas of living beings too merge in Avyakla (the Unmanifest).
verses.hindi: ५५४ क्‍ वायुपुराणम् तथेति समनुज्ञातों महादेवः स्वयंभुवा । पुत्रत्वे कल्पयामास सहादेवस्तथा भृगुम् ॥

verses.sanskrit: तत्र स्नात्वा नरो राजञ्छुचिः प्रयतमानसः । उपोष्य रजनीमेकां गोसहस्रफलं लभेत्
verses.transliteration: tatra snātvā naro rājañchuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ / upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
verses.translation: Their Dharma of the nature of Sattva gets settled in the Guna of Sattva, while Adharma of the nature of Tamas (darkness) abides in the Guna Tamas. These two Gunas arc devoid of distinction when the Gunas are in the state of equilibrium. In all the functions of Pradhana the activities will be backed by the intellect. The Ksetrajna will preside over those Gunas without the (intermediary) intellect. Thus the Pura (physical body) will be attained through Abhimana (the act of identification). When it becomes necessary to function both 1 the Ksetra and Ksetrajna begin to interact mutually; they become united together in the relationship of Bhojya (that which has to be enjoyed) and Bhoktr (the enjoyer). The only refuge for them is the Avyakta. Stabilised in the state of equilibrium, the group of Gunas become presided over by the Ksetrajna (at the time of the beginning of creation) and then their equilibrium is upset. Then both Ksetra and Ksetrajna reach the state of

verses.sanskrit: कामिकं तीर्थराजं तु तादृशं न भविष्यति । त्रिरात्रं कुरुते राजन्स गोलक्षफलं लभेत्
verses.transliteration: kāmikaṃ tīrtharājaṃ tu tādṛśaṃ na bhaviṣyati / trirātraṃ kurute rājansa golakṣaphalaṃ labhet
verses.translation: The twcntyfour principles of the nature of Gunas beginning with Mahat and ending with Viiefa (which are called Vikaras) attain the Ksetrajna, Pradhana and Purusa. Then in the Brahmanda (the Cosmic Egg) Isvara will be born (manifest) first. He will be the lord of all living beings, of the entire knowable universe. He is Siva. He is the overlord of all liberated souls. He is the great Brahma of the nature of Brahman. He is the primordial lord and it is said that his manifestation is for the sake of blessing Pradhana. Ksetra and Ksetrajna are self-born and beginning¬ less. They are remembered as subtle. Their union is beginningless. They are aware of all Ksetras. They are joined together without the intermediation of intellect ( AbuddhipQrvakam ) like Matoka (mosquito) and Udumbara tree. They are stationed bcginninglessly and in¬ conceivably like water and fish.
verses.hindi: एवमस्त्विति सोः्प्युक्तो ब्रह्मणा सदसस्पतिः । तस्मादडगिरसश्रवापि आग्नेया इति नः भुतम्ू षटकृत्वस्तु पुनः शुक्ने ब्रह्मणा लोककारिणा  हुते समभवं॑स्तत्न षड्ब्रह्माण इति श्रुतिः ३४३

verses.sanskrit: तत्र नृत्यं प्रकर्तव्यं तुष्यते परमेश्वरः । गीतवादित्रनिर्घोषै रात्रौ जागरणेन च
verses.transliteration: tatra nṛtyaṃ prakartavyaṃ tuṣyate parameśvaraḥ / gītavāditranirghoṣai rātrau jāgaraṇena ca
verses.translation: The creation functions again as it had functioned before. The Ajna (non-knowing) Prakrti transforms itself into the universe functioning through its Gunas, viz. Rajas, Sattva and Tamas. At the time of the functioning (of Prakrti) the Ksetrajna human beings are overwhelmed by Rajas Guna and attain the (benefit of) the principles of Mahat, Ahamkara etc. ending with Visesa and the sense organs. Then the Gunas reach their end (?) God Brahma is of truthful conception. While he was meditating on the Sat, the Gunas Rajas, Sattva and Tamas though mutually dissimilar became manifest as caused by the Sat (the existent). Ksetrajhas (knowers of the Ksetra or body) are ever produced both at the beginning and at the end. Abhimanins [Atmans who identify themselves) become born with instruments of actions readily achieved. All beings are produced from the Aoyakla (Unmanifest) at the outset itself, who had been Sadhakas (spiritual aspirants) or non-Sadhakas (?) All of them undergoing the process of worldly existence along with their Sthanas (abodes) and Prakaranas (contexts?), attain their effects and arc born again and again.
verses.hindi: अहं तृतीय इत्यथंस्तस्मादत्रिः स कीत्यंते। केशेश्व निशितेभूतः पुलस्त्यस्तेन स स्मृतः ४४५ केशलम्बेः समुद्मृतस्तस्मात्त पुलहः स्मृतः । बसुमध्यात्समुत्पन्नो वसुमान्वसुधाश्रयः
verses.wordMeaning: The creation functions again as it had functioned before. The Ajna (non-knowing) Prakrti transforms itself into the universe functioning through its Gunas, viz. Rajas, Sattva and Tamas.…
verses.commentary: Sense: The creation functions again as it had functioned before. The Ajna (non-knowing) Prakrti transforms itself into the universe functioning through its Gunas, viz. Rajas, Sattva and Tamas.…

verses.sanskrit: एरण्ड्यां च महादेवो दृष्टो मे मन्मथेश्वरः । किं समर्थो यमो रुष्टो भद्रो भद्राणि पश्यति
verses.transliteration: eraṇḍyāṃ ca mahādevo dṛṣṭo me manmatheśvaraḥ / kiṃ samartho yamo ruṣṭo bhadro bhadrāṇi paśyati
verses.translation: Dharma and Adhanna are solely of the nature of quality. They begin (give rise to) each other through boons and blessings. All are equal for the purpose of creation. It is at the beginning of creation that they undergo transformation. The Gunas rush to him and hence it is liked by him. The Ksetrajhas attain again and again only those qualities which they had in the previous creation. Being created again and again they attain only them. Qualities of violent or non-violent temperament, softness or cruelty, virtuousness or sinful nature, truthfulness or falsehood—had already been conceived by them (in the former creation); they attain them again and hence they appeal to them. It is through Gunas that the multiplicity and diversity in the great Bhutas (elements), in the sense-objects and in physical forms as well as the separation of living beings take place. Thus I have recounted briefly to you the subsequent creation. Now I shall briefly recount the birth (manifestation) of Brahma. 1
verses.hindi: वसिष्ठ इति तत्त्वज्ञेः प्रोच्यते ब्रह्मवादिभिः । इत्येते ब्रह्मण: पुत्राः मानसाः षण्सहय:ः अतः यह ब्रद्याषि मेरा पुत्र हो । जब “यह भृगु मेरा ही पुत्र हो' । ऐसा शिवजी ने प्रकट किया। तदनन्तर स्वयम्भू ने कहा कि ऐसा ही होगा । तब शिव ने भृगु को अपने पुत्र रूप में स्वीकार किथा । इसी कारणवश भृगु गोत्र में उत्पन्न होनिवाले वरुण वंशीय कहलाते हैं, वे प्रभु भूगु भगवान् श्विव को सनन्‍्तान हुए। तदन्तर भगवान् ब्रह्मा ने पुनः द्वितीय बार वीय॑ को यज्ञाग्नि के अंगार के ऊपर भाहुति डाला जिससे उन अंगरारों पर अड्चों प्रत्यंगों
verses.wordMeaning: Dharma and Adhanna are solely of the nature of quality. They begin (give rise to) each other through boons and blessings. All are equal for the purpose of creation. It is at the beginning of creation that they undergo transformation.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Dharma and Adhanna are solely of the nature of quality. They begin (give rise to) each other through boons and blessings. All are equal for the purpose of creation. It is at the beginning of creation that they undergo transformation.…

verses.sanskrit: कामेन स्थापितः शम्भुरेतस्मात् कामदो नृप । सोपानः स्वर्गमार्गस्य पृथिव्यां मन्मथेश्वरः
verses.transliteration: kāmena sthāpitaḥ śambhuretasmāt kāmado nṛpa / sopānaḥ svargamārgasya pṛthivyāṃ manmatheśvaraḥ
verses.translation: From that Avyakta (unmanifest) cause which is eternal one and of thenature of Sat and Asat (existence and non-existence) Mahesvara (the great Lord) is born through Pradhana and Purusa. With the appellation 'Brahma', he becomes the evolver. He creates the worlds once again of the nature of (i.e. characteri¬ sed by) Abhimana (referring all objects to the self) and Gunas (Sattva etc.). Ahamkara (Cosmic Ego) is born of Mahat (the cosmic intellect) and Bhutas are born of it (Ahamkara). Suta narrates the recreation of the Universe by bringing in Puranic deities like Mahesvara and Brahma and synthesizing the Sarikhya and Puranic accounts. The ramifications of these are extensive. I have re¬ counted to you in accordance with my intellect and in the manner I have heard it, formerly. Know them in the same manner." The sages living in the Naimisa forest heard the story of the origin, maintenance and destruction of the worlds and then finished the holy ablution of Avabhrtha in the Satra. They became pure and attained the meritorious world. 1
verses.hindi: समेत अंगिरा ऋषि प्रादृंभूत हुए ।२८-४०। ब्रह्मा की इस अभिनव सम्भूति को श्रकट हुआ देख अग्नि ने कहा, ब्रह्मन् ! मैंने तुम्हारे दिये हुये बीयें को धारण किया था, भरत: यहू दूसरा पुत्र मेरा हो । सभा में प्रधान के पद पर समासीय ब्रह्मा ने अग्ति की प्रार्थना का अनुमोदन किया कि ऐसा ही हो। यही कारण है कि अंगिरा गोत्रवाले अग्नि गोत्रीय भी कहे जाते हैं--ऐसा हमने सुना है। तदनन्तरः लोकसष्टिकर्त्ता ब्रह्मा ने छः बार अग्नि
verses.wordMeaning: From that Avyakta (unmanifest) cause which is eternal one and of thenature of Sat and Asat (existence and non-existence) Mahesvara (the great Lord) is born through Pradhana and Purusa. With the appellation 'Brahma', he becomes the evolver.…

verses.transliteration: viśeṣaścātra sandhyāyāṃ śrāddhadāne ca bhārata / annadānena rājendra kīrtitaṃ phalamuttamam
verses.translation: In the same manner, you worship duly Devatas (deities) etc., take the valedictory bath ( Avabhrtha ) after the sacrifice and become pure. At the end ofjife be contented (that you have done your duty), abandon bodies, attain the meritorious world and proceed (to enjoy) as you please. All the residents of the Naimisa forest, the performers of the Satra went to heaven after taking the ablution, Avabhrtha on the conclusion of the sacrifice. O excellent Brahmana, in the same manner you will also go to heaven at the end of your life after performing the various kinds of sacrifices and taking the Avabhrtha bath in the end. The Wind-god himself who is engaged in the welfare of the worlds, has narrated this popular Parana consisting of the four Padas 2 (sections), viz. Prakriya is the first section, where the story is taken up (the other sections are) Anusahga, Upodgliata and Upasamhara. lie narrated it to the sages after going to their Satra in the Naimisa forest. verses.transliteration: etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ tava bhaktyā tu bhārata / pṛthivyāṃ sāgarāntāyāṃ prakhyāto manmatheśvaraḥ
verses.translation: Conclusion of the Satra (sacrificial session) and the completion of the narration of the Purana synchronised. The author exhorts the later audience of the Purana to perform sacrifices and go to heaven just as the sages in Naimisaranya did formerly. A brief review of the main Padas (Sections) of the Purana. The scholarly Brahmana who listens to or narrates or teaches this ancient Itihasa rejoices in the worlds of Mahendra for eternal years. * 1 2 After attaining Sdyujya with Brahman along with Brahma he becomes liberated. Eulogising those Prajapatis, the famous noble-souled lords of earth,* he attains the status of Brahman. 3 4 Verses 48-57 contain the Phala-Sruti of listening to or narrating this Purana. MS. Kha used by A. (Anandas'rama edition) contains the following additional verses:
verses.hindi: १. पीछे उत्पन्न होनेवाले छः पुत्रों में अनि की क्रम संख्या तीसरी ही थी ।
verses.wordMeaning: Conclusion of the Satra (sacrificial session) and the completion of the narration of the Purana synchronised. The author exhorts the later audience of the Purana to perform sacrifices and go to heaven just as the sages in Naimisaranya did formerly.…

verses.sanskrit: गोदानं पाण्डवश्रेष्ठ त्रयोदश्यां प्रकारयेत् । चैत्रे मासि सिते पक्षे तत्र गत्वा जितेन्द्रियः
verses.transliteration: godānaṃ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭha trayodaśyāṃ prakārayet / caitre māsi site pakṣe tatra gatvā jitendriyaḥ
verses.translation: A. records the following additional verses from the same (Kha) MS. after the words Brahmabhuydya gacchati: They are translated from p 421 of A edition as follows: This Purana narrated by Kfsna Dvaipayana, the ex¬ pounder of Biahman (Vedas), is conducive to wealth, fame, longevity and great merit. It is on a par with the Vedas. He who extols the fame of the lords of Manvantaras, of the Devas and sages endowed with enormous wealth and splendour, is released from all sins. He shall attain great merit. A scholar wdio always narrates this on every festive occasions, snakes off his sins, conquers heaven and becomes capable of being merged in Brahman. If one at the time of Sraddha recites a section of this (Purana) to Brahmanas, it ultimately passes on to Pitrs bestow¬ ing everything desired and everlasting benefit.
verses.hindi: लोकस्य संस्थानकरास्तेरिमा बधिताः प्रजा: । प्रजापतय इत्येवं पठचनन्‍्ते ब्रह्मणः सुताः ४८ अपरे पितरो नाम एतरेव सहषिभिः । उत्पादिता ऋषिगणाः सप्त लोकेषु विश्वुताः ॥४ ६ आत्रेयाश्व गणाः प्रोक्ताः पितु्णां लोकविश्वुताः ५० एते समासतस्तात पुरंब तु गुणास्त्रयः । असुर्ताश्व॒ प्रकाशाश्व ज्योतिष्मन्तश्व विशुता: १५१ तेषां राजा यमो देवों यमैविहतकल्मषः । अपरे प्रजानां पतयस्ताञ्शुणुध्वमतन्द्रिताः

verses.sanskrit: रात्रौ जागरणं कृत्वा देवस्याग्रे नृपोत्तम । दीपं भक्त्या घृतेनैव देवस्याग्रे निवेदयेत्
verses.transliteration: rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā devasyāgre nṛpottama / dīpaṃ bhaktyā ghṛtenaiva devasyāgre nivedayet
verses.translation: The word Purana is derived thus.' puva anciuti ilipuranam, i.e. that which has been established in ancient times. He who knows this derivation becomes liberated from all sins. Those men of the three higher castes who listen to this Purana and turn their attention to virtuous activities, rejoice in heaven for as many crores of years as there are hair- pores in the skin. After attaining Sayujya (absorption) with Brahman they rejoice along with Devas. Brahma handed over to Matarisvan 1 (Wind-god) this sacred text of the ancient Purana which dispels all sins, which is holy and meritorious and which is conducive to fame. From him it was acquired by Usanas, and Bfhaspati secured it from him. Thereafter, Brhaspati narrated it to Savitr. Savitr recounted it to Mj-tyu and Mrtyu handed it over to Indra. Indra narrated it to Vasistha and he taught it to Sarasvata. Verses 58-66 give the genealogy of teachers who handed down the Purana up to Suta, the present narrator.

verses.sanskrit: स्त्र्यथ वा पुरुषो वापि सममेतत्फलं स्मृतम्
verses.transliteration: stryatha vā puruṣo vāpi samametatphalaṃ smṛtam
verses.translation: Trnabindu narrated it to Daksa and Daksa taught Sakti. Even as he was in the womb, Parasara heard this from Thus the words uttered by Brahma, the first prece¬ ptor, were mentioned by me to my son Amitabuddhi (of un¬ measured intellect); it is narrated orally by (a line of preceptors) of whom Brahma was the first. Preceptors should be earnestly bowed down to by learned men. This story is conducive to wealth, fame and longevity. It is meritorious and achieves all objects (of desire). It destroys sins. This must always be regularly listened to by Brahmanas. This sacred story should not be mentioned to an impure person, a sinner, nor to a disciple who has not put in at least a year's disciplined student life. Nor should it be men¬ tioned to one who never pays heed, nor to one who is not a scholar, nor to one who has no son, nor to one who is inimical. With great mental purity, I bow down to Brahma, 1 the first Mahesvara whose source of origin, they say, is Avyakta This salutation to Mahadeva who is identified with the Primordial Puru?a shows that it is a Saiva Purana. The Maiigalacarana of this Purana pays obeisance to Lord Siva.
verses.hindi: जाता भस्मव्यपोहिन्यां ब्रह्मषिगणसंमता: । वेखानसा मुनिगणास्तपःश्रुतपरायणा: सब लोक की सन्‍्तान वृद्धि करनेवाले हैं, ओर इन्हीं लोगों ने प्रजाओं की बृद्धि की है। इसी कारण ब्रह्मा के ये पुत्र गण प्रजापति कह कर पुकारे जाते हैं। इन्हीं महृषियों द्वारा दूसरे पितर नामक लोकविख्यात ऋषिगण भी उत्पन्न हुए ।४६-४८। वे लोक-प्रसिद्ध सात पितरगण मारीच, भागंव, आडिःमरस पौलस्त्य, पौलह, वाशिष्ठ और आत्रेय के माम से विख्यात हैं । है तात ! सक्षेप में इन पितर गणों का वर्णन कर

verses.sanskrit: ईश्वर उवाच: शृणु देवि परं गुह्यं नाख्यातं कस्यचिन्मया । रेवायाश्चोत्तरे कूले तीर्थं परमशोभनम् । भ्रूणहत्याहरं देवि कामदं पुत्रवर्धनम्
verses.transliteration: īśvara uvāca: śṛṇu devi paraṃ guhyaṃ nākhyātaṃ kasyacinmayā / revāyāścottare kūle tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam / bhrūṇahatyāharaṃ devi kāmadaṃ putravardhanam
verses.translation: The holy rites and duties (Dharma) of those with and without attachment, those of ascetics, the religious students, householders, forest-hermits, women and Sudras have been particularly explained by you. Similarly the rites and duties of Brabmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas and the mixed castes have been recounted. You have described the big rivers Ganga and others. Many kinds of Yajnas, holy rites and penances have been explained in those Puranas. Many kinds of religious gifts, all kinds of Tamos (restraints and holy observances), the duties of Yoga, Samkhya and Bhagavata (pertaining to the holy devotee of the lord) have been explained in them. The paths of devo¬ tion, knowledge, and detachment have been explained. The procedures for the Upasand (special forms of worship) with water and wind (i.c. such as Pranayama where the breath is control¬ led) by those whose minds have been purified by holy rites, have been mentioned.
verses.hindi: उत्पत्ति हुई, रोमछिद्रों से अन्यान्य ऋषियों की उत्पत्ति हुई, इसी प्रकार स्वेद एवं मल से भी कुछ प्रजापतियों की उत्पत्ति हुई। ५६-५८। उसके स्वर से दारुण मास, निर्यास (?) पक्षों की संधियाँ, वत्सर दिन रात एवं
verses.wordMeaning: The holy rites and duties (Dharma) of those with and without attachment, those of ascetics, the religious students, householders, forest-hermits, women and Sudras have been particularly explained by you. Similarly the rites and duties of Brabmanas, Ksatriyas,…
verses.commentary: Sense: The holy rites and duties (Dharma) of those with and without attachment, those of ascetics, the religious students, householders, forest-hermits, women and Sudras have been particularly explained by you. Similarly the rites and duties of Brabmanas, Ksatriyas,…

verses.sanskrit: पार्वत्युवाच: कथयस्व महादेव तीर्थं परमशोभनम् । भ्रूणहत्याहरं कस्मात्कामदं स्वर्गदर्शनम्
verses.transliteration: pārvatyuvāca: kathayasva mahādeva tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam / bhrūṇahatyāharaṃ kasmātkāmadaṃ svargadarśanam
verses.translation: The systems (of philosophy and devotion), the Brahma (pertaining to Brahma), Saiva (that of Siva), Vaisnava (that of Vi§nu)j Saura (that of the Sun), Sakta (that of Sakti, the goddess), Arhata* (that of Arhat, Jina), the six systems of philosophy and the materialistic philosophy—all these and many other things have been explained in the Puranas.
verses.hindi: दारुणा हि रुते मासा निर्यासाः पक्षसंधयः । वत्सरा ये त्वहोरात्राः पित्र (5यं ) ज्योतिश्व दारुणम् आदिसानस्य लोकस्य ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मसमुझ्भूवः  सर्वकामदमित्याहुस्तत्र कन्यामुदाहरन् ६६२ ब्रह्मा सुरगुरुस्तत्र त्रिश्शै: संप्रसोदर्ति । इसे वे जनयिष्यन्ति प्रजा: सर्वाः प्रजेश्वरा: ६३ सर्वे प्रजानां पतयः सर्वे चापि तपस्विनः । तत्प्रसादादिमॉल्लोकान्धारय्रेयुरिसा: क्रिया: ६४ हंढू संवर्धधामास तव तेजो विवर्धनम् । देवेधु बेदविद्वांसः सर्वे राजषंयस्तथा ६५
verses.wordMeaning: The systems (of philosophy and devotion), the Brahma (pertaining to Brahma), Saiva (that of Siva), Vaisnava (that of Vi§nu)j Saura (that of the Sun), Sakta (that of Sakti, the goddess), Arhata* (that of Arhat, Jina),…
verses.commentary: Sense: The systems (of philosophy and devotion), the Brahma (pertaining to Brahma), Saiva (that of Siva), Vaisnava (that of Vi§nu)j Saura (that of the Sun), Sakta (that of Sakti, the goddess), Arhata* (that of Arhat, Jina),…

verses.sanskrit: ईश्वर उवाच: अत्रिर्नाम महादेवि मानसो ब्रह्मणः सुतः । अग्निहोत्ररतो नित्यं देवतातिथिपूजकः
verses.transliteration: īśvara uvāca: atrirnāma mahādevi mānaso brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ / agnihotrarato nityaṃ devatātithipūjakaḥ
verses.translation: It is not known whether there is or not anything be- yond tills that is excellent and worth knowing.
verses.hindi: वेदमन्त्रपरा: सर्वे प्रजापतिगुणो दबा: । अनन्तं ब्रह्म सत्यं च तपश्च परम भुवि
verses.wordMeaning: It is not known whether there is or not anything be- yond tills that is excellent and worth knowing.
verses.commentary: Sense: It is not known whether there is or not anything be- yond tills that is excellent and worth knowing.

verses.sanskrit: सोमसंस्थाश्च सप्तैव कृता विप्रेण पार्वति । अनसूयेति विख्याता भार्या तस्य गुणान्विता
verses.transliteration: somasaṃsthāśca saptaiva kṛtā vipreṇa pārvati / anasūyeti vikhyātā bhāryā tasya guṇānvitā
verses.translation: Could it be that Vyasa or you, holy sir, are hiding any¬ thing? Please clear our doubts in this respect, since you are a complete Pauranika (knower of Puranas).
verses.hindi: सर्वे हि बयमेते च तथ्थव प्रसव: प्रभो । ब्रह्म च ब्राह्मणाश्चेव लोकाश्चेव चराचराः ६७ मरीचिमादित: कृत्वा देवाश्च ऋषिभि: सह । अपत्यानीह संचिन्त्य तेउपत्यं फामयामहे तस्मिन्यज्ञ महाभागा देवाश्च ऋषिभिः सह । एतह्वंशसमुद्भुताः स्थानकालाभिमानिनः ६९ न च तेनव रूपेण स्थापयेयुरिमा: प्रजा: । युगादिनिधनाश्चेब स्थापयेयुरिमाः प्रजा:
verses.wordMeaning: Could it be that Vyasa or you, holy sir, are hiding any¬ thing? Please clear our doubts in this respect, since you are a complete Pauranika (knower of Puranas).
verses.commentary: Sense: Could it be that Vyasa or you, holy sir, are hiding any¬ thing? Please clear our doubts in this respect, since you are a complete Pauranika (knower of Puranas).

verses.sanskrit: पतिव्रता पतिप्राणा पत्युः कार्यहिते रता । एवं याति ततः काले न पुत्रा न च पुत्रिका
verses.transliteration: pativratā patiprāṇā patyuḥ kāryahite ratā / evaṃ yāti tataḥ kāle na putrā na ca putrikā
verses.translation: O Saunaka, listen. I shall explain this intricate pro¬ blem. This is a great secret of divine nature. It should not be mentioned (to anyone and everyone), so say (the sages).
verses.hindi: पितरगणों की दाहुण ज्योति का प्रादुर्भाव हुआ । रोौद्र को लोहित कहा जाता है, लोहित को कनक नाम से भी स्मरण किया गया है, उसी को मैत्र भी जानना चाहिए, धृम पश् माने गये हैं ।५९-६०। उसकी देह- युति से रुद्र तथा आदित्यगणों का समुद्भव हुआ  अडगारों से दिव्य एवं मानुष क़्योतियों का उद्भव हुआ  इस प्रकार ब्रह्म से समुद्भत भगवान् ब्रह्मा इस लोकसृष्टि के आदिमकर्त्ता एवं पूल पुरुष म!ने गये हैं ।
verses.wordMeaning: O Saunaka, listen. I shall explain this intricate pro¬ blem. This is a great secret of divine nature. It should not be mentioned (to anyone and everyone), so say (the sages).
verses.commentary: Sense: O Saunaka, listen. I shall explain this intricate pro¬ blem. This is a great secret of divine nature. It should not be mentioned (to anyone and everyone), so say (the sages).

verses.sanskrit: अपराह्णे महादेवि सुखासीनौ तु सुन्दरि । वदन्तौ सुखदुःखानि पूर्ववृत्तानि यानि च
verses.transliteration: aparāhṇe mahādevi sukhāsīnau tu sundari / vadantau sukhaduḥkhāni pūrvavṛttāni yāni ca
verses.translation: After writing the scory of the Puranas wherein all the meanings of the Vcdic passages have been included, Vyasa, son of Parasara, thought thus in his mind. 1 2
verses.hindi: उनको सब मनोरथों का देनेवाला कहा जाता है। उस महायज्ञ के अवसर पर कन्या की बातचीत के सिलसिले में ऋषियों और ब्रह्मा से इस प्रकार वार्तालाप हुआ। मरीचि ऋषि को अग्रुआ बनाकर सभी ऋषियों एवं प्रजाओं की सृष्टि का कार्य सम्पन्न करेंगे, आपकी क॒पा से ये सभी प्रजापति तथा परम तपस्वी हैं और सभी लोकों को धारण (पालन) करने में समक्ष तथा क्रियानिष्ठ हैं ।६१०६४। तुम्हारे तेश की अभिवद्धि करनेवाले द्न्द्वात्मक भाव की वृद्धि हो गई । देवताओं में वेदों के जाननेवाले ये राजथिंगण, वेदिकमंत्र पराबण एवं प्रजापति के समस्त गुणों से समलंकृत हैं। इस पृथ्वी तल पर एक ब्रह्म ही अनन्त, सत्य एवं परम तप
verses.wordMeaning: After writing the scory of the Puranas wherein all the meanings of the Vcdic passages have been included, Vyasa, son of Parasara, thought thus in his mind. 1 2
verses.commentary: Sense: After writing the scory of the Puranas wherein all the meanings of the Vcdic passages have been included, Vyasa, son of Parasara, thought thus in his mind. 1 2

verses.sanskrit: अत्रिरुवाच: सौम्ये शुभे प्रिये कान्ते चारुसर्वाङ्गसुन्दरि । विद्याविनयसम्पन्ने पद्मपत्रनिभेक्षणे
verses.transliteration: atriruvāca: saumye śubhe priye kānte cārusarvāṅgasundari / vidyāvinayasampanne padmapatranibhekṣaṇe
verses.translation: c 'The duties of the different castes and stages of life have been clearly explained by me. Different paths leading to salvation without infringing the Vedic injunctions have been mentioned by me.
verses.hindi: साध्य है। ये और हम सभी तुम्हारी ही सन्‍्तानें है, इस जगत में ब्रह्म, ब्राह्मण एवं चराचर लोक सब कुछ तुमसे प्रदुर्भूत हुए हैं, हम सभी सन्‍्तान की कामना करते हैं ।६५-६८। इस प्रकार उस महायज्ञ में महा- भाग्यशाली देवगणों ने ऋषियों के साथ ब्रह्मा से प्राथंना की । इन्हीं उपयुक्त ऋषियों एवं देवताओं के वंश में स्थान एवं काल का निर्धारण करनेवाली सन्‍्तानें उत्पन्न हुईं । उन लोगों ने फिर कह्दा, ये प्रजापतिमण इसी
verses.wordMeaning: c 'The duties of the different castes and stages of life have been clearly explained by me. Different paths leading to salvation without infringing the Vedic injunctions have been mentioned by me.
verses.commentary: Sense: c 'The duties of the different castes and stages of life have been clearly explained by me. Different paths leading to salvation without infringing the Vedic injunctions have been mentioned by me.

verses.sanskrit: पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाकारे पृथुश्रोणिभरालसे । न त्वया सदृशी नारी त्रैलोक्ये सचराचरे
verses.transliteration: pūrṇacandranibhākāre pṛthuśroṇibharālase / na tvayā sadṛśī nārī trailokye sacarācare
verses.translation: In my decisions (incorporated) in the {Brahma siilra), the (alleged) distinction between Jiva (individual soul), Isvara and Brahman has been completely refuted. Brahman the supreme soul has been explained on the basis of Vedic passages, cogent arguments and deliberations.
verses.hindi: ततो5ब्रवील्लोकगुरु: परमित्यविचारयन् । एवं देवा विनिश्चित्य मया सृष्ठा न संशय: ॥। तेषां भूगोः कीतंयिष्ये वंश पूर्व महात्मन: । विस्तरेणा55नृपुर्र्या च॒ प्रथमस्य प्रजापते ७२
verses.wordMeaning: In my decisions (incorporated) in the {Brahma siilra), the (alleged) distinction between Jiva (individual soul), Isvara and Brahman has been completely refuted. Brahman the supreme soul has been explained on the basis of Vedic passages, cogent arguments and deliberations.
verses.commentary: Sense: In my decisions (incorporated) in the {Brahma siilra), the (alleged) distinction between Jiva (individual soul), Isvara and Brahman has been completely refuted. Brahman the supreme soul has been explained on the basis of Vedic passages, cogent arguments and deliberations.

verses.sanskrit: रतिपुत्रफला नारी पठ्यते वेदवादिभिः । पुत्रहीनस्य यत्सौख्यं तत्सौख्यं मम सुन्दरि
verses.transliteration: ratiputraphalā nārī paṭhyate vedavādibhiḥ / putrahīnasya yatsaukhyaṃ tatsaukhyaṃ mama sundari
verses.translation: Mention of Jainism and non-mention of Buddhism shows that Buddhism had either disappeared from India at that time or the inclusion of the Buddha as an incarnation of Visnu was probably regarded a sufficient ground not to mention it as a separate system of philosophy. I believe in the first alternative (disappearance of Buddhism on a large scale).
verses.hindi: भृगोस्त्वजनयहिव्या काव्यं वेदबिदां वरम् । देवासुराणासाचार्य शुक्र कविसुत॑ ग्रहम् ..
verses.wordMeaning: Mention of Jainism and non-mention of Buddhism shows that Buddhism had either disappeared from India at that time or the inclusion of the Buddha as an incarnation of Visnu was probably regarded a sufficient ground not to mention it as a separate system of philosophy.…
verses.commentary: Sense: Mention of Jainism and non-mention of Buddhism shows that Buddhism had either disappeared from India at that time or the inclusion of the Buddha as an incarnation of Visnu was probably regarded a sufficient ground not to mention it as a separate system of philosophy.…

verses.sanskrit: यथाहं न तथा पुत्रः समर्थः सर्वकर्मसु । पुन्नामनरकाद्भद्रे जातमात्रेण सुन्दरि
verses.transliteration: yathāhaṃ na tathā putraḥ samarthaḥ sarvakarmasu / punnāmanarakādbhadre jātamātreṇa sundari
verses.translation: Gf. Bh. 4.26-31 and the subsequent two chapters 5 & 6. That episode in the Bh. P. is the basis of this episode of Vyasa's dejection. The mention of Brahma Sutras shows that at the time of this Purana the authors of the Mahabliarata, the Puranas and the Brahma sutra were believed to be one si nglc individual called Krsna Dvaipayana Vyasa.
verses.hindi: स शुक्रश्वोशना ख्यातः स्मृतः काव्योषपि नामतः । पितृणां मानसी कन्या सोमपानां यशस्विनो ॥ ब्राह्मण तेजसा युक्तः स जातो ब्रह्मवित्तम: । तस्थामेव तु चत्वारः पुत्रा: शुक्स्य जज्ञिरे...
verses.wordMeaning: Gf. Bh. 4.26-31 and the subsequent two chapters 5 & 6. That episode in the Bh. P. is the basis of this episode of Vyasa's dejection. The mention of Brahma Sutras shows that at the time of this Purana the authors of the Mahabliarata,…
verses.commentary: Sense: Gf. Bh. 4.26-31 and the subsequent two chapters 5 & 6. That episode in the Bh. P. is the basis of this episode of Vyasa's dejection. The mention of Brahma Sutras shows that at the time of this Purana the authors of the Mahabliarata,…

verses.sanskrit: पतन्तं रक्षयेद्देवि महापातकिनं यदि । महाघोरे गता वापि दुष्टकर्मपितामहाः
verses.transliteration: patantaṃ rakṣayeddevi mahāpātakinaṃ yadi / mahāghore gatā vāpi duṣṭakarmapitāmahāḥ
verses.translation: Those who strictly adhere to the injunctions of the Vedas, perform holy rites only for the sake of Brahman They are free from desires and sins. They perform the holy rites dedicating the fruit thereof to the greatest soul.
verses.hindi: त्वष्टा बरूत्री द्वावेती शण्डामकों च तावभो । ते तदा5वित्यसंकाशा ब्रह्मकल्पा: प्रभावतः.
verses.wordMeaning: Those who strictly adhere to the injunctions of the Vedas, perform holy rites only for the sake of Brahman They are free from desires and sins. They perform the holy rites dedicating the fruit thereof to the greatest soul.
verses.commentary: Sense: Those who strictly adhere to the injunctions of the Vedas, perform holy rites only for the sake of Brahman They are free from desires and sins. They perform the holy rites dedicating the fruit thereof to the greatest soul.

verses.sanskrit: तद्धरन्ति सुपुत्राश्च वैतरण्यां गतानपि । पुत्रेण लोकाञ्जयति पौत्रेण परमा गतिः
verses.transliteration: taddharanti suputrāśca vaitaraṇyāṃ gatānapi / putreṇa lokāñjayati pautreṇa paramā gatiḥ
verses.translation: That Brahman is the greatest. It is pure. It has neither beginning nor end. It is free from ailments. It is eternal and omnipresent. It is steady like the summit of a mountain. It is devoid of deception. It pervades all sense organs but is im- perceivable. It is devoid of sense-organs that are the creations ofPrakrti. It is undeflected by Dik (Space) and Kdla (Time) etc. It is eternal. It is pure consciousness. It is unchanging.
verses.hindi: रठजन:ः प्ृथुरश्मिश्न विद्वान्यस्य बृहद्गिरा:। वरूत्रिणः सता हतते ब्रहिष्ठा: सुरयाजकाः ७८ इज्याधमंबिनाशार्थ मनुमेत्याम्ययोजयन् । निरस्यमान वे धर्म दृष्ट्वेन्द्रो मनुभब्रवीत् ७६ अपने रूप में (बिना स्त्री के) प्रजाओं का विस्तार तो कर नहीं सकते, इनकी प्रजाएं बुगारम्भ से लेकर युगान्त तक स्थित रहनेवाली होगी ।' ऐसी बातें सुनकर लोकपितामह ब्रह्मा ने बिना कुछ विशेष विचार किये ही उत्तर दिया, निस्संदेह इन्हीं सब बातों का निश्चय करके मैंने पहले देवताओं की सृष्टि की है । ये मह॒ब्रिगण जो आप लोगों के वंश में उत्पन्न होनेवाले हैं, उनमें से स्वेप्रथम महात्मा भृगु के वंश का वर्णन विस्तारपूर्वंक क्रमश: कर
verses.wordMeaning: That Brahman is the greatest. It is pure. It has neither beginning nor end. It is free from ailments. It is eternal and omnipresent. It is steady like the summit of a mountain. It is devoid of deception. It pervades all sense organs but is im- perceivable.…
verses.commentary: Sense: That Brahman is the greatest. It is pure. It has neither beginning nor end. It is free from ailments. It is eternal and omnipresent. It is steady like the summit of a mountain. It is devoid of deception. It pervades all sense organs but is im- perceivable.…

verses.sanskrit: अथ पुत्रस्य पौत्रेण प्रगच्छेद् ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् । नास्ति पुत्रसमो बन्धुरिह लोके परत्र च
verses.transliteration: atha putrasya pautreṇa pragacched brahma śāśvatam / nāsti putrasamo bandhuriha loke paratra ca
verses.translation: The whole universe is super-imposed on it like the
verses.hindi: रहा हूं, जो कि प्रथम प्रजापति हैं। उन महात्मा भूगु की दो सत्कुलोत्पन्न कल्याणी स्त्रियाँ थीं, जिनमें एक हिरण्यकशिपु की कन्या थी जिसका“ दिव्या नाम विख्यात है, दूसरी परमसुन्दरी प्रलोम की कन्या थी, जिसका पौलोमी नाम था ।६९-७३। दिव्या ने भगु के संयोग से वेदशानियाँ में सर्वेश्रेष्ठ, देवताओं एवं असूरों के आचायें, कविपुत्र, सुप्रसिद्ध ग्रह शुक्र को उत्पन्त किया। . वे झुक्र उशनता एवं काव्य नाम से भी विख्यात
verses.wordMeaning: The whole universe is super-imposed on it like the
verses.commentary: Sense: The whole universe is super-imposed on it like the

verses.sanskrit: अहश्च मध्यरात्रे च चिन्तयानस्य सर्वदा । शुष्यन्ति मम गात्राणि ग्रीष्मे नद्युदकं यथा
verses.transliteration: ahaśca madhyarātre ca cintayānasya sarvadā / śuṣyanti mama gātrāṇi grīṣme nadyudakaṃ yathā
verses.translation: The Nigamas (Vedas) declare,'Everything is Brahman There is no multiplicity'. It is from Brahman that the crores of Brahmarnjas (Cosmic Eggs) are created and dissolved.
verses.hindi: हैं। शुक्र की पत्ती एवं सोम पान करनेवाले पितरों की यशस्विनी मो नामक कन्या ने चार पुत्रों को उत्पन्न किया ।७४-७६। वे शुक्राचार्थ ब्रह्मतेन से समलंकृत एवं ब्रह्मज्ञानियों में श्रेष्ठ थे। उस पत्नी में शुक्र के चार पुत्र उपन्‍्न हुए, जो त्वष्टा और वरुत्री तथा दण्ड एवं अमक के नाम से विख्यात हैं। शुक्र के प्रभाव से वे पुत्र ब्रहा के समान तेजस्वी तथा आदित्य के समान थे । तिनमें से वरुत्री के रझजन, प्रुथुरदिम और विद्वान बृहद््गिरा नामक ब्रह्मपरायण पुत्र हुए, जो सभी देवताओं के पुरोहित हुए । एक बार यज्ञ एवं धरम के विनाश के लिये इन शुत्रपुत्रों ने मनु से अपने तकंपूर्ण मतों कों निवेदित किया । धर्म कों नष्ट होते देख इन्द्र ने मनु
verses.wordMeaning: The Nigamas (Vedas) declare,'Everything is Brahman There is no multiplicity'. It is from Brahman that the crores of Brahmarnjas (Cosmic Eggs) are created and dissolved.
verses.commentary: Sense: The Nigamas (Vedas) declare,'Everything is Brahman There is no multiplicity'. It is from Brahman that the crores of Brahmarnjas (Cosmic Eggs) are created and dissolved.

verses.sanskrit: अनसूयोवाच: यत्त्वया शोचितं विप्र तत्सर्वं शोचयाम्यहम् । तवोद्वेगकरं यच्च तन्मे दहति चेतसि
verses.transliteration: anasūyovāca: yattvayā śocitaṃ vipra tatsarvaṃ śocayāmyaham / tavodvegakaraṃ yacca tanme dahati cetasi
verses.translation: This Adhyasavada shows that this chapter was written in the post- Sankara period. See v. 39 below.
verses.hindi: भ््पर्द वायुपुराणमभ्
verses.wordMeaning: This Adhyasavada shows that this chapter was written in the post- Sankara period. See v. 39 below.
verses.commentary: Sense: This Adhyasavada shows that this chapter was written in the post- Sankara period. See v. 39 below.

verses.sanskrit: येन पुत्रा भविष्यन्ति आयुष्मन्तो गुणान्विताः । तत्कार्यं च समीक्षस्व येन तुष्येत् प्रजापतिः
verses.transliteration: yena putrā bhaviṣyanti āyuṣmanto guṇānvitāḥ / tatkāryaṃ ca samīkṣasva yena tuṣyet prajāpatiḥ
verses.translation: The dissolution and creation of all the worlds depend upon the Unmesa (opening) and jYimesa (closing) of Brah¬ man. 1 The great Sakti (the divine goddess of power) is station- ed with the support of Brahman.
verses.hindi: एतेरेव तु काम त्वां प्रापयिष्यासि याजनम् । श्रुत्वेन्द्रस्य तु तद्ाक्‍्यं तस्माहेशादपाक़्मतू.. च० सुष्कप देवदेवस्य वेद्यां वे दक्षिण ततः
verses.wordMeaning: The dissolution and creation of all the worlds depend upon the Unmesa (opening) and jYimesa (closing) of Brah¬ man. 1 The great Sakti (the divine goddess of power) is station- ed with the support of Brahman.
verses.commentary: Sense: The dissolution and creation of all the worlds depend upon the Unmesa (opening) and jYimesa (closing) of Brah¬ man. 1 The great Sakti (the divine goddess of power) is station- ed with the support of Brahman.

verses.sanskrit: अत्रिरुवाच: तपस्तप्तं मया भद्रे जातमात्रेण दुष्करम् । व्रतोपवासनियमैः शाकाहारेण सुन्दरि
verses.transliteration: atriruvāca: tapastaptaṃ mayā bhadre jātamātreṇa duṣkaram / vratopavāsaniyamaiḥ śākāhāreṇa sundari
verses.translation: The universe is in it. It originates from Brahman. It is Brahman itself. It is due to the ignorance of Brahman that the universe appears. When Brahman is realised there is no universe.
verses.hindi: एवं वरूत्रिणः पुत्रा इन्द्रेण निहताः पुरा। यजन्यां देवयानी च शुक्रस्य दुहिताइभवत् ८४
verses.wordMeaning: The universe is in it. It originates from Brahman. It is Brahman itself. It is due to the ignorance of Brahman that the universe appears. When Brahman is realised there is no universe.
verses.commentary: Sense: The universe is in it. It originates from Brahman. It is Brahman itself. It is due to the ignorance of Brahman that the universe appears. When Brahman is realised there is no universe.

verses.sanskrit: क्षीणदेहस्तु तिष्ठामि ह्यशक्तो ऽहं महाव्रते । तेन शोचामि चात्मानं रहस्यं कथितं मया
verses.transliteration: kṣīṇadehastu tiṣṭhāmi hyaśakto 'haṃ mahāvrate / tena śocāmi cātmānaṃ rahasyaṃ kathitaṃ mayā
verses.translation: The universe is explained as Asalya (unreal), Ja<fa (insentient), Duhkha (cause of misery) and Auaslu (unreal, un¬ substantial). The opposite of it is Saccidamndamurti— the embodiment of existence, knowledge and bliss.
verses.hindi: विश्वरूपानुजश्रापि विश्वकर्मा यमः स्मृतः ८५ भगोस्तु भुगवो देवा जज्ञिरे दुवादशा55त्मजाः । देव्यां तान्सुषुबे सर्वान्काव्यश्चेवा55तमजान्प्रभुः
verses.wordMeaning: The universe is explained as Asalya (unreal), Ja<fa (insentient), Duhkha (cause of misery) and Auaslu (unreal, un¬ substantial). The opposite of it is Saccidamndamurti— the embodiment of existence, knowledge and bliss.
verses.commentary: Sense: The universe is explained as Asalya (unreal), Ja<fa (insentient), Duhkha (cause of misery) and Auaslu (unreal, un¬ substantial). The opposite of it is Saccidamndamurti— the embodiment of existence, knowledge and bliss.

verses.sanskrit: अनसूयोवाच: भर्तुः पतिव्रता नारी रतिपुत्रविवर्धिनी । त्रिवर्गसाधना सा च श्लाघ्या च विदुषां जने
verses.transliteration: anasūyovāca: bhartuḥ pativratā nārī ratiputravivardhinī / trivargasādhanā sā ca ślāghyā ca viduṣāṃ jane
verses.translation: It is called Vifva when the individual soul is in the wakeful state. It is remembered as Taijasa when the individual is in a state of dream. It is called Prajna when the individual soul is in the state of dreamless slumber. 2 It persists in all the states.
verses.hindi: इत्येते भुगवो देवा: स्मृता द्वादश याज्ञिका: । पौलोम्यजनयत्पुत्न॑ ब्रह्मिष्ठं बसिनं विभुम् 'पैदद
verses.wordMeaning: It is called Vifva when the individual soul is in the wakeful state. It is remembered as Taijasa when the individual is in a state of dream. It is called Prajna when the individual soul is in the state of dreamless slumber. 2 It persists in all the states.
verses.commentary: Sense: It is called Vifva when the individual soul is in the wakeful state. It is remembered as Taijasa when the individual is in a state of dream. It is called Prajna when the individual soul is in the state of dreamless slumber. 2 It persists in all the states.

verses.sanskrit: जपस्तपस्तीर्थयात्रा मृडेज्यामन्त्रसाधनम् । देवताराधनं चैव स्त्रीशूद्रपतनानि षट्
verses.transliteration: japastapastīrthayātrā mṛḍejyāmantrasādhanam / devatārādhanaṃ caiva strīśūdrapatanāni ṣaṭ
verses.translation: It is the eye of eyes. It is the ear of ears. It is the Tvac (skin, i.e, organ of touch) of all Tvacs. It is the tongue of tongues. They consider it the Prana (vital breath) of Pranas.
verses.hindi: से कहा कि मैं इन्हीं लोगों के द्वारा तुमसे यज्ञ करवाऊँगा। इन्द्र की बातें सुनकर वे लोग वहाँ से पलायन कर गये ।७७०८०। उन लोगों के छिप जाने पर उनकी धर्मंपत्नी चेतना को पुरस्कारों से प्रलोभित कर इन्द्र ने अनुगसन किया। तदनस्तर इन्द्र के विमाद्यार्थ यदन करते हुए वे यति (संन्यास्री) वेश में उसी स्थान पर पुनः आये, वहाँ पथ उन दुरात्माओं को आया देख इन्द्र ने संहार कर दिया और स्वयं देबदेव के यज्ञ को दक्षिण वेदी पय शयन किया । वहाँ पर शाला में रहनेवात्रे गीदज्ञों ओर कुत्तों द्वारा भक्षण करते समय उन बरुत्रीपत्नों के शिर गिरकर खजूर के रूप में परिणत हुए। इस प्रकार प्राचोन काल में वसरुत्री के पुत्रों का इन्द्र द्वारा संहार किया गया । यजनी ( जयन्ती ) नामक पत्नी में शुक्र की पुत्री देवयानी की उत्पत्ति हुई ।5१-५४। विरोचन की कन्या यशोधरा में त्वष्टा के तीन शिरवाले विश्वरूप एवं उनके अनुज महान्
verses.wordMeaning: It is the eye of eyes. It is the ear of ears. It is the Tvac (skin, i.e, organ of touch) of all Tvacs. It is the tongue of tongues. They consider it the Prana (vital breath) of Pranas.
verses.commentary: Sense: It is the eye of eyes. It is the ear of ears. It is the Tvac (skin, i.e, organ of touch) of all Tvacs. It is the tongue of tongues. They consider it the Prana (vital breath) of Pranas.

verses.sanskrit: ईदृशं तु महादोषं स्त्रीणां तु व्रतसाधने । वदन्ति मुनयः सर्वे यथोक्तं वेदभाषितम्
verses.transliteration: īdṛśaṃ tu mahādoṣaṃ strīṇāṃ tu vratasādhane / vadanti munayaḥ sarve yathoktaṃ vedabhāṣitam
verses.translation: Human beings are incapable of knowing precisely and attaining it by means of intellect, worldly knowledge, vital breath or physical activity for ever.
verses.hindi: यशस्वी विश्वकर्मा की यमज (जुड़वा) उत्पत्ति हुई। भुगु के बारह पुत्र उत्पस्त हुए जो भृगुगणदेव के नाम से प्रसिद्ध हैं। भगवान् काव्य ने देवी में उन सभी आत्मजों को उत्पन्न किया । जिनके नाम भुवन, भावन, अन्य, अन्यायत, क्रतु, श्रवा, मूर्धा, व्यजय, व्यश्रुष, प्रसव, अज एवं अधिपति स्मरण किये गये हैं। ये बारह भूगुपुत्र बारह याज्ञिक देवगणों के नाम से विख्यात हैं ।५५-८७३। पुलोमा की पुत्री पौलोमी ने ब्रह्मनिष्ठ
verses.wordMeaning: Human beings are incapable of knowing precisely and attaining it by means of intellect, worldly knowledge, vital breath or physical activity for ever.
verses.commentary: Sense: Human beings are incapable of knowing precisely and attaining it by means of intellect, worldly knowledge, vital breath or physical activity for ever.

verses.sanskrit: अनुज्ञाता त्वया ब्रह्मंस् तपस् तप्स्यामि दुष्करम् । पुत्रार्थित्वं समुद्दिश्य तोषयामि सुरोत्तमान्
verses.transliteration: anujñātā tvayā brahmaṃs tapas tapsyāmi duṣkaram / putrārthitvaṃ samuddiśya toṣayāmi surottamān
verses.translation: Just as snake (is misconceived as such) in the rope, mirage as water in the desert, and blueness in the sky is super¬ imposed due to ignorance, so also the non-existing universe is superimposed on Brahman and hence it simply appears to exist.
verses.hindi: जितेरिद्रिय परम प्रभावशाली पृन्र को उत्पन्न किय। । किसी कठोर कर्म के कारण पौलोमी का वह गर्भ आठवें हृदमर्ध नास्ति क. पुस्तके ।
verses.wordMeaning: Just as snake (is misconceived as such) in the rope, mirage as water in the desert, and blueness in the sky is super¬ imposed due to ignorance, so also the non-existing universe is superimposed on Brahman and hence it simply appears to exist.
verses.commentary: Sense: Just as snake (is misconceived as such) in the rope, mirage as water in the desert, and blueness in the sky is super¬ imposed due to ignorance, so also the non-existing universe is superimposed on Brahman and hence it simply appears to exist.

verses.sanskrit: अत्रिरुवाच: साधु साधु महाप्राज्ञे मम संतोषकारिणि । आज्ञाता त्वं मया भद्रे पुत्रार्थं तप आश्रय
verses.transliteration: atriruvāca: sādhu sādhu mahāprājñe mama saṃtoṣakāriṇi / ājñātā tvaṃ mayā bhadre putrārthaṃ tapa āśraya
verses.translation: The vast sky appears to be different inasmuch as it is restricted by jars etc. Similarly the Jiva is the restricted form of the all-pervading soul, restricted through the karya (product e.g. the physical body).
verses.hindi: तस्य तुर्वो ऋषिजेशे ऊरू भित्वा महायशा: । ओवंश्रा5:सोद्चीकस्तु दोप्ता्निसद्शप्रभः ६६२
verses.wordMeaning: The vast sky appears to be different inasmuch as it is restricted by jars etc. Similarly the Jiva is the restricted form of the all-pervading soul, restricted through the karya (product e.g. the physical body).
verses.commentary: Sense: The vast sky appears to be different inasmuch as it is restricted by jars etc. Similarly the Jiva is the restricted form of the all-pervading soul, restricted through the karya (product e.g. the physical body).

verses.sanskrit: देवतानां मनुष्याणां पित्ःणामनृणो भवे । न भार्यासदृशो बन्धुस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विद्यते
verses.transliteration: devatānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ pitḥṇāmanṛṇo bhave / na bhāryāsadṛśo bandhustriṣu lokeṣu vidyate
verses.translation: A partial quotation from Vasugupta's Spanda-Karika 1, but attributes this creation and destruction of the Universe to Siva's Para Sakti—an attempt to adapt aTrika Saiva concept and adopt it in Kevalddvaita.
verses.hindi: जमनाह्ृष्णवस्याग्नेजंमदग्निरजायत । रेणका जमदर्नेस्तु शक्नतुल्यपराक्तमम् ॥॥ ब्रह्मक्षत्रमयं राम सुषुवेडसिततेजसम् ६४ औवस्या5इसी त्पुत्रशतं जमदग्निपुरोगमम् । तेषां पुत्रसहस्नाणि भागंवाणां परस्परात् ६५ देवाश्वाडरिरसो मुख्यास्त्विषुमन्तो महौजसः ६७
verses.wordMeaning: A partial quotation from Vasugupta's Spanda-Karika 1, but attributes this creation and destruction of the Universe to Siva's Para Sakti—an attempt to adapt aTrika Saiva concept and adopt it in Kevalddvaita.
verses.commentary: Sense: A partial quotation from Vasugupta's Spanda-Karika 1, but attributes this creation and destruction of the Universe to Siva's Para Sakti—an attempt to adapt aTrika Saiva concept and adopt it in Kevalddvaita.

verses.sanskrit: तेन देवाः प्रशंसन्ति न भार्यासदृशं सुखम् । सन्मुखे मन्मुखाः पुत्राः विलोमे तु पराङ्मुखाः
verses.transliteration: tena devāḥ praśaṃsanti na bhāryāsadṛśaṃ sukham / sanmukhe manmukhāḥ putrāḥ vilome tu parāṅmukhāḥ
verses.translation: The terras Taijasa, Prajna etc. used here are of Upani$adic antiquity {vide Mantfukya U , 10 and 11).
verses.hindi: मास में व्याधिग्रस्त होकर गिर पड़ा, अतः च्यवन (गिर जाने) के कारण उसका च्यवन नाम पड़ा और प्रचेतस से चेतन हुआ। प्राचेतस च्यवन के क्रीध से पुरुषदाज ने अध्वाको'"”“““ (?) उन भृगु पुत्र च्यबन ने सुकन्या नामक अपनी धमंपत्नी में सत्पुरुषों द्वारा परम सम्मानतीय आत्मवान् और दधीच नामक दो पुत्रों को उत्पन्न किया । सरस्वती में दधीच के संयोग से सारस्वत नामक पुत्र की उत्पत्ति हुई। नहुष की पुत्री महाभाग्य-
verses.wordMeaning: The terras Taijasa, Prajna etc. used here are of Upani$adic antiquity {vide Mantfukya U , 10 and 11).
verses.commentary: Sense: The terras Taijasa, Prajna etc. used here are of Upani$adic antiquity {vide Mantfukya U , 10 and 11).

verses.sanskrit: तेन भार्यां प्रशंसन्ति सदेवासुरमानुषाः । महाव्रते महाप्राज्ञे सत्त्ववति शुभेक्षणे
verses.transliteration: tena bhāryāṃ praśaṃsanti sadevāsuramānuṣāḥ / mahāvrate mahāprājñe sattvavati śubhekṣaṇe
verses.translation: Verses 4-1-55 show the influence of the Radha- Krsna cult or Bhagavatism.
verses.hindi: शालिनी रुची आत्मवान् की पत्नी थी ।८८-९१॥ आत्मवान् के ऋषि उरू नामक महायशस्वी पुत्र जंधाओं को फाड़कर उत्पन्न हुआ। उस उवे का पृत्र ऋचीक हुआ जो भ्रज्वलित अग्ति के समान परम तेजस्वी था । ऋचीक मुनि की सत्यवती नामक स्त्री में जमदर्ति ऋषि उत्पन्न हुए। भृगु कृत रुद्र ओर विष्णु के चर में विपयंय हो जाने के कारण वेष्णव अग्नि के रुद्र अंश के भक्षण के कारण ज॑मदग्नि ऋषि उत्पन्न हुए । जमदग्नि के संयोग से रेणुका ने इस्द्र के समान पराक्रमी, परम तेजस्वी ब्रह्मनल से संयुक्त परशुराम को उत्पन्त किया । उव के पुत्र ऋचीक के एक सौ पुत्र थे, जिनमें जमदग्नि सबसे बड़े थे। उन सौ पुत्रों के एक सहस्र पुत्र हुए। उन सभी भगुवंशीय ऋषियों के वंशज परस्पर अन्यान्य ऋषियों के वंशजों से बाह्य विवाहादि कार्यों में योग्य माने गये हैं। वत्स, विश्व, अश्विषेण, पाण्ड, पथ्य, और शौतक--इन सात गोत्रों
verses.wordMeaning: Verses 4-1-55 show the influence of the Radha- Krsna cult or Bhagavatism.
verses.commentary: Sense: Verses 4-1-55 show the influence of the Radha- Krsna cult or Bhagavatism.

verses.sanskrit: तपस्तपस्व शीघ्रं त्वं पुत्रार्थं तु ममाज्ञया । एतद्वाक्यावसाने तु साष्टाङ्गं प्रणताब्रवीत्
verses.transliteration: tapastapasva śīghraṃ tvaṃ putrārthaṃ tu mamājñayā / etadvākyāvasāne tu sāṣṭāṅgaṃ praṇatābravīt
verses.translation: He sports in the world called Goloka which is Brah¬ man itself, the Cil alone, free from difference and Gunas. I have heard it so.
verses.hindi: में भागवगण विभक्त भाने जाते हैं ।९२-९६। अरब अग्नि के पुत्र, परम बुद्धिमान् अंग्रिरा के वंश का वृत्तान्त सुनिये, जिसके गोत्र में परम तेजस्वी भारद्वाज, गौतम, एवं इषुमानू नामक मुख्य देवगण उत्पन्न हुए हैं।
verses.wordMeaning: He sports in the world called Goloka which is Brah¬ man itself, the Cil alone, free from difference and Gunas. I have heard it so.
verses.commentary: Sense: He sports in the world called Goloka which is Brah¬ man itself, the Cil alone, free from difference and Gunas. I have heard it so.

verses.sanskrit: त्वत्प्रसादेन विप्रेन्द्र सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयाम् । हंसलीलागतिः सा च मृगाक्षी वरवर्णिनी
verses.transliteration: tvatprasādena viprendra sarvānkāmānavāpnuyām / haṃsalīlāgatiḥ sā ca mṛgākṣī varavarṇinī
verses.translation: There is nothing greater than He as mentioned in Nigamas and Agamas. Still the Vedas say that he is beyond and greater than Aksara.
verses.hindi: ५६० द वायुपुराणम् सुरूपा चेव मारोची कार्दमी च तथा स्व॒राट । पथ्या व सानवी कन्या तिस्रो भारयस्त्वथर्वणः ॥
verses.wordMeaning: There is nothing greater than He as mentioned in Nigamas and Agamas. Still the Vedas say that he is beyond and greater than Aksara.
verses.commentary: Sense: There is nothing greater than He as mentioned in Nigamas and Agamas. Still the Vedas say that he is beyond and greater than Aksara.

verses.sanskrit: नियमस्था ततो भूत्वा सम्प्राप्ता नर्मदां नदीम् । शिवस्वेदोद्भवां देवीं सर्वपापप्रणाशनीम्
verses.transliteration: niyamasthā tato bhūtvā samprāptā narmadāṃ nadīm / śivasvedodbhavāṃ devīṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanīm
verses.translation: The lord who is the resident of Goloka is called greater than Aksara. Who is this always spoken by the Vedas as beyond even that?
verses.hindi: अथवंणस्तु दायादास्तासु जाता: कुलोद्बहाः । उत्पन्ना महता चंव तपसा भावितात्मनामू
verses.wordMeaning: The lord who is the resident of Goloka is called greater than Aksara. Who is this always spoken by the Vedas as beyond even that?
verses.commentary: Sense: The lord who is the resident of Goloka is called greater than Aksara. Who is this always spoken by the Vedas as beyond even that?

verses.sanskrit: यस्या दर्शनमात्रेण नश्यते पापसञ्चयः । स्नानमात्रेण वै यस्या अश्वमेधफलं लभेत्
verses.transliteration: yasyā darśanamātreṇa naśyate pāpasañcayaḥ / snānamātreṇa vai yasyā aśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet
verses.translation: How is the special meaning, that which is indicated by the words of the Vedas to be known? Is the text of the Veda to be interpi eted otherwise as it implies more than recorded in words (?)
verses.hindi: बहस्पतिः सुरूपाया गोतभः सुषुवे स्व॒राद् । अवन्ध्यं वामदेव च उतथ्यसुशिजं तथा ११०० धिष्णु: पुत्रस्तु पथ्यायां संबतेंश्चंव मानसः । घिचित्तश्र तथा यस्‍्य शरद्ांश्वाप्युतथ्यज: अशिजो दी्घंतमा बृह॒दुत्थो वामदेवज: । धिष्णोः पुत्र: सुधन्वान ऋषभश्न सुधन्वन: १०२
verses.wordMeaning: How is the special meaning, that which is indicated by the words of the Vedas to be known? Is the text of the Veda to be interpi eted otherwise as it implies more than recorded in words (?)
verses.commentary: Sense: How is the special meaning, that which is indicated by the words of the Vedas to be known? Is the text of the Veda to be interpi eted otherwise as it implies more than recorded in words (?)

verses.sanskrit: ये पिबन्ति महादेवि श्रद्दधानाः पयः शुभम् । सोमपानेन तत्तुल्यं नात्र कार्या विचारणा
verses.transliteration: ye pibanti mahādevi śraddadhānāḥ payaḥ śubham / somapānena tattulyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
verses.translation: Vyasa, the son of Satyavatl, became doubtful as to the meaning of the Sruti. He pondered over it for a long time. He could not understand it precisely.
verses.hindi: . रथकारः स्मृता देवा ऋषयो ये परिश्रुता: । बृहस्पतेयंबीयांसो विश्वुते: सुमहायशाः १०३ अडुगिरसस्तु संवर्तो देवानड्रिरसः शुणु । बृहस्पतेयवीयांसो देवा ह्याड्भिरसः स्मृताः
verses.wordMeaning: Vyasa, the son of Satyavatl, became doubtful as to the meaning of the Sruti. He pondered over it for a long time. He could not understand it precisely.
verses.commentary: Sense: Vyasa, the son of Satyavatl, became doubtful as to the meaning of the Sruti. He pondered over it for a long time. He could not understand it precisely.

verses.sanskrit: ये स्मरन्ति दिवा रात्रौ योजनानां शतैरपि । मुच्यन्ते सर्वपापेभ्यो रुद्रलोकं प्रयान्ति ते
verses.transliteration: ye smaranti divā rātrau yojanānāṃ śatairapi / mucyante sarvapāpebhyo rudralokaṃ prayānti te
verses.translation: Even after deliberating (long) the sage did not arrive at the decisive meaning of the Vedic passage. The Veda is Narayana himself, where even great sages (poets) become confounded.
verses.hindi: अयस्यस्तु उतथ्यश्व वामदेवस्तथोसिज: । भारद्वाजाः शांकृतिका गाग्यंकाण्वरथीतराः आड़्िरस अथर्वा की मरीचि नन्दिनी सुरूपा, कर्दम पुत्री स्वराद तथा मनुकल्या पथ्या नामक तीन स्त्रियाँ थीं, उनमें होनेवाली सन्ततियों का विवरण बतला रहा हूं, अथर्वा के वंशोद्धारक उन उत्तराधिकारियों का, जो परम पूजनीय अंगिरा की परम तपस्या के फलस्वरूप उत्पन्न हुए थे, वर्णन कर रहा हूँ, सुरूपा में बृहस्पति का जन्म हुआ, स्वराट् ने गौतम को जन्म दिया +६७-६६ टै। अवन्ध्य, वामदेव, उशिज उतथ्य ओर
verses.wordMeaning: Even after deliberating (long) the sage did not arrive at the decisive meaning of the Vedic passage. The Veda is Narayana himself, where even great sages (poets) become confounded.
verses.commentary: Sense: Even after deliberating (long) the sage did not arrive at the decisive meaning of the Vedic passage. The Veda is Narayana himself, where even great sages (poets) become confounded.

verses.sanskrit: नर्मदायाः समीपे तु तावुभौ योजनद्वये । न पश्यन्ति यमं तत्र ये मृता वरवर्णिनि
verses.transliteration: narmadāyāḥ samīpe tu tāvubhau yojanadvaye / na paśyanti yamaṃ tatra ye mṛtā varavarṇini
verses.translation: Still he underwent great distress of the heart. Then he thought: 'Whom shall I approach? What shall I do?
verses.hindi: धिष्ण ये पथ्या में उत्पन्न हुए, ऑर संबर्त तथा विचित्त उसके मानस पुत्र हुए। उतथ्य के पुत्र शरह्वान हुए । उशिज के पुत्र दीघंतमा तथा वामदेब के पुत्र बृहदुत्थ हुए । धिष्णु के पुत्र सुधन्वा ओर सुधन्वा का पृत्र ऋषय हुआ । और ऋषय के रथकार नामक देवगण तथा परम विख्यात ऋषिगण पूत्र रूप में हुए । बृहस्पति के पुत्र महान यशस्वी एवं परम विख्यात भारद्वाज हुए ।१००-१०३। आउज्लिरस के संवर्त नामक जो पूत्र थे उनकी संततियाँ
verses.wordMeaning: Still he underwent great distress of the heart. Then he thought: 'Whom shall I approach? What shall I do?
verses.commentary: Sense: Still he underwent great distress of the heart. Then he thought: 'Whom shall I approach? What shall I do?

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तदुत्तरे कूले एरण्ड्याः सङ्गमे शुभे । नियमस्था विशालाक्षी शाकाहारेण सुन्दरि
verses.transliteration: tatastaduttare kūle eraṇḍyāḥ saṅgame śubhe / niyamasthā viśālākṣī śākāhāreṇa sundari
verses.translation: I do not see anyone in this world who is omniscient and who sees everything.' After not knowing anyone in the world who could clear his doubts he went to a cave in Meru and performed a great penance. There was a beautiful forest there. Although there was blinding darkness within, the rocks shed a golden brilliance everywhere.
verses.hindi: देवगणों में परिगणित हैं, उत आंगिरस गोत्रीय देवताओं का विवरण सुनिये। बृहस्पति के छोटे भाई वे आंगिरस गोत्रीय देवगण माने जाते हैं। वे आंगिरस गोत्रीय देवणण सुरूपा के औरस पुत्र रूप में उत्पन्न हुए थे  उनकी संख्या दस है तथा उनके नाम औरस, आंयु, दनु, दक्ष, दर्भ, प्राण, हविष्मान्, हंविष्णु क्रु ओर सत्य है । अयस्य, उतथ्य, वामदेव, भारद्वाज गोजोय शांकृतिक, गाग्य, काण्व, रथीतर, मुद्गल, विष्णुवृद्ध, हरित, वायव, भारद्वाज गोत्रीय भाक्ष, आर्षभ और किभय--पये पनद्रह अंगिरा के गमोनीय हैं, जो अन्यान्य ऋषियों के गोत्रों स विवाहादि सम्बन्धों में अंगीकार किये गये हैं। अंगिरा के गोत्र में उत्पन्‍्न होनेवालों की संख्या
verses.wordMeaning: I do not see anyone in this world who is omniscient and who sees everything.' After not knowing anyone in the world who could clear his doubts he went to a cave in Meru and performed a great penance. There was a beautiful forest there.…
verses.commentary: Sense: I do not see anyone in this world who is omniscient and who sees everything.' After not knowing anyone in the world who could clear his doubts he went to a cave in Meru and performed a great penance. There was a beautiful forest there.…

verses.sanskrit: तोषयन्ती त्रींश्च देवाञ्छुभैः स्तोत्रैर् व्रतैस्तथा । ग्रीष्मेषु च महादेवि पञ्चाग्निं साधयेत् ततः
verses.transliteration: toṣayantī trīṃśca devāñchubhaiḥ stotrair vrataistathā / grīṣmeṣu ca mahādevi pañcāgniṃ sādhayet tataḥ
verses.translation: The forest was resonant with the chirping sounds of the birds among the groves of the different trees and creepers. It was devoid of the sufferings due to hunger, thirst, fear, anger, distress and dejection. Ponds and tanks beautified with lotuses abounded there. Their banks were set with golden slabs on which the birds moved about. It was served by the winds wafting the fragrance from the lotuses. It was devoid of beasts of prey. It was frequented by animalshaving auspicious nature. The place was devoid of crowds of people. It was embellished
verses.hindi: फश्यपः सवितुविद्वांस्तेन स ब्रह्मण: समः । मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु ब्रह्मणांड्शेन जायते
verses.wordMeaning: The forest was resonant with the chirping sounds of the birds among the groves of the different trees and creepers. It was devoid of the sufferings due to hunger, thirst, fear, anger, distress and dejection. Ponds and tanks beautified with lotuses abounded there.…
verses.commentary: Sense: The forest was resonant with the chirping sounds of the birds among the groves of the different trees and creepers. It was devoid of the sufferings due to hunger, thirst, fear, anger, distress and dejection. Ponds and tanks beautified with lotuses abounded there.…

verses.sanskrit: वर्षाकाले चार्द्रवासाश्चरेच्चान्द्रायणानि च । हेमन्ते तु ततः प्राप्ते तोयमध्ये वसेत्सदा
verses.transliteration: varṣākāle cārdravāsāścareccāndrāyaṇāni ca / hemante tu tataḥ prāpte toyamadhye vasetsadā
verses.translation: The sage entered that cave. After attaining full con¬ trol over his mind, posture and urge for food, he meditated on the four Vedas with great concentration.
verses.hindi: “हाश्चेकसा हि विज्ञेया वाइसनः कश्य उच्यते । कश्यं मद्यं स्मृतं विप्रेः कश्यपानात्तु कश्यप: करोति नाम यद्वाचो वा क्रमुदाहृतम् । दक्षाभिशप्तः कुपितः कश्यपस्तेन सोभवत्
verses.wordMeaning: The sage entered that cave. After attaining full con¬ trol over his mind, posture and urge for food, he meditated on the four Vedas with great concentration.
verses.commentary: Sense: The sage entered that cave. After attaining full con¬ trol over his mind, posture and urge for food, he meditated on the four Vedas with great concentration.
